papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central technique for compressing large deep learning models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teachers' performance. Across vision, language, speech, and recommendation tasks, researchers combine KD with architectural compression, pre-training, privacy mechanisms, and data-free approaches to address inference cost, dataset availability, and domain-specific challenges. Empirical work shows that careful choices about what to transfer (logits, features, layers), how to train teachers and students, and how to incorporate task or data constraints strongly determine final student quality.

papers_seen.author: Riley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is not merely a model-compression trick but a central, practical paradigm for deploying high-performance deep and NLP models under real-world constraints. KD can compress large pre-trained models into lightweight students, transfer inductive biases, improve robustness and generalization, enable low-precision and privacy-aware deployments, and adapt to data- or compute-limited settings. Effective distillation couples soft-label transfer with representation-level alignment, task-aware architecture choices, and complementary techniques (quantization, pruning, augmentation). However, KD must be applied carefully: teacher–student mismatches, bias transfer, domain shift, and limited-data regimes require method choices such as feature mimicking, teacher ensembles, teacher-free objectives, or fairness-aware augmentations. The result is a flexible toolkit that—when combined with architectural and data strategies—makes high-quality, efficient models feasible for production NLP and deep-learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Morales
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Practical Tool for Compressing and Adapting Deep and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated approach for producing smaller models that retain much of the performance and useful behavior of larger teachers. KD supports a spectrum of deployment goals — reduced latency and memory, domain adaptation, privacy-aware training, and robustness improvements — and works best when combined with complementary techniques (e.g., layer mapping, feature matching, synthetic-data generation, pruning, or quantization). However, KD is not a universal solution: outcomes depend on teacher quality, what signals are transferred, data fidelity, and design choices that align distilled knowledge to the downstream task. Practical adoption therefore requires principled pipeline choices and awareness of KD failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Murillo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Pragmatic Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students across modalities and tasks. KD reliably reduces inference cost and memory while preserving much of teacher performance, but it is not a turnkey solution: its success depends on design choices about what to transfer, how to handle data limitations, and how to combine distillation with complementary compression and fairness-preserving techniques. I argue that KD should be treated as a central component of a model-compression pipeline — one that is combined with architecture-aware methods, data and curriculum strategies, and explicit checks for robustness, privacy, and bias — to achieve deployable, efficient, and responsible models in practice.

papers_seen.author: Chandler
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Task-Aware Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for turning large, high-performing deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD succeeds by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone, and when combined with complementary techniques (architecture search, pruning, quantization, data augmentation, and multi-teacher curricula) it enables substantial reductions in inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance. However, KD is context-sensitive: choices about what to transfer (logits, features, relational signals), how to produce or augment training data, and how to align teacher and student architectures determine outcomes. Effective deployment therefore treats KD as a central tool in compression pipelines but tailors the pipeline to task constraints, data availability, and robustness/fairness goals.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Understanding and Improving Lexical Choice in Non-Autoregressive Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is essential for training non-autoregressive translation (NAT) models by reducing the complexity of the raw data with an autoregressive teacher model. In this study, we empirically show that as a side effect of this training, the lexical choice errors on low-frequency words are propagated to the NAT model from the teacher model. To alleviate this problem, we propose to expose the raw data to NAT models to restore the useful information of low-frequency words, which are missed in the distilled data. To this end, we introduce an extra Kullback-Leibler divergence term derived by comparing the lexical choice of NAT model and that embedded in the raw data. Experimental results across language pairs and model architectures demonstrate the effectiveness and universality of the proposed approach. Extensive analyses confirm our claim that our approach improves performance by reducing the lexical choice errors on low-frequency words. Encouragingly, our approach pushes the SOTA NAT performance on the WMT14 English-German and WMT16 Romanian-English datasets up to 27.8 and 33.8 BLEU points, respectively. The source code will be released.

papers_seen.author: Mcclain
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation from Internal Representations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is typically conducted by training a small model (the student) to mimic a large and cumbersome model (the teacher). The idea is to compress the knowledge from the teacher by using its output probabilities as soft-labels to optimize the student. However, when the teacher is considerably large, there is no guarantee that the internal knowledge of the teacher will be transferred into the student; even if the student closely matches the soft-labels, its internal representations may be considerably different. This internal mismatch can undermine the generalization capabilities originally intended to be transferred from the teacher to the student. In this paper, we propose to distill the internal representations of a large model such as BERT into a simplified version of it. We formulate two ways to distill such representations and various algorithms to conduct the distillation. We experiment with datasets from the GLUE benchmark and consistently show that adding knowledge distillation from internal representations is a more powerful method than only using soft-label distillation.

papers_seen.author: Bowman
papers_seen.title: TRILLsson: Distilled Universal Paralinguistic Speech Representations
papers_seen.abstract: Recent advances in self-supervision have dramatically improved the quality of speech representations. However, deployment of state-of-the-art embedding models on devices has been restricted due to their limited public availability and large resource footprint. Our work addresses these issues by publicly releasing a collection of paralinguistic speech models that are small and near state-of-the-art performance. Our approach is based on knowledge distillation, and our models are distilled on public data only. We explore different architectures and thoroughly evaluate our models on the Non-Semantic Speech (NOSS) benchmark. Our largest distilled model is less than 15% the size of the original model (314MB vs 2.2GB), achieves over 96% the accuracy on 6 of 7 tasks, and is trained on 6.5% the data. The smallest model is 1% in size (22MB) and achieves over 90% the accuracy on 6 of 7 tasks. Our models outperform the open source Wav2Vec 2.0 model on 6 of 7 tasks, and our smallest model outperforms the open source Wav2Vec 2.0 on both emotion recognition tasks despite being 7% the size.

papers_seen.author: Spears
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of techniques for transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models so that high performance can be retained under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. Across modalities KD spans simple soft-target matching to richer transfers of internal features, attention, or relational structure, and it is usually combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and careful data strategies (real, public, synthetic, or data-free). Empirical results show large reductions in model size and inference cost with modest accuracy loss in many settings, but success depends on choices of what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, how to handle limited or private data, and how to preserve robustness and fairness under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Diaz
papers_seen.title: Model Compression with Two-stage Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation for Web Question Answering System
papers_seen.abstract: Deep pre-training and fine-tuning models (such as BERT and OpenAI GPT) have demonstrated excellent results in question answering areas. However, due to the sheer amount of model parameters, the inference speed of these models is very slow. How to apply these complex models to real business scenarios becomes a challenging but practical problem. Previous model compression methods usually suffer from information loss during the model compression procedure, leading to inferior models compared with the original one. To tackle this challenge, we propose a Two-stage Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation (TMKD for short) method for web Question Answering system. We first develop a general Q\&A distillation task for student model pre-training, and further fine-tune this pre-trained student model with multi-teacher knowledge distillation on downstream tasks (like Web Q\&A task, MNLI, SNLI, RTE tasks from GLUE), which effectively reduces the overfitting bias in individual teacher models, and transfers more general knowledge to the student model. The experiment results show that our method can significantly outperform the baseline methods and even achieve comparable results with the original teacher models, along with substantial speedup of model inference.

papers_seen.author: Harris
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students while retaining much of the teacher's behavior. A growing literature shows KD can act via soft-target matching, intermediate representation transfer, attention- or relation-based losses, self-distillation, online and data-free variants, and can be combined with pruning, layer-skipping, quantization, or architecture search. KD delivers strong empirical gains across modalities (vision, language, recommendation, and graphs) when its signal, data strategy, and optimization schedule are chosen to match the deployment constraints. Important open issues remain — handling rare or low-frequency behaviors, adapting across domains and heterogeneous architectures, and operating under strict privacy or data-availability constraints — but pragmatic pipelines that mix KD with complementary compression tools offer the most reliable path to deployable compact models.

papers_seen.author: Walters
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and inductive biases from large teacher models to smaller student models so they can meet real-world constraints (latency, memory, privacy). Methods vary by what is transferred (soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention, relational signals), how data are used or synthesized, and whether distillation is combined with other compression tools or automated search. Empirically, KD often preserves much of teacher performance while enabling substantial reductions in size and inference cost, but practical success depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity, addressing data or privacy limits, and adapting teachers or objectives to propagate desired properties such as robustness and generalization.

papers_seen.author: Kennedy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of teacher performance. KD encompasses techniques that transfer predictive behavior (soft logits), intermediate representations, and relational or structural signals; it can be combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet latency and memory constraints. Practical deployments extend KD to privacy-preserving, federated, and data-poor scenarios, and leverage online or multi-teacher protocols. Empirical and theoretical work highlights clear strengths in producing compact models for NLP and vision, while also identifying limits related to optimization, teacher imperfection, data mismatch, and distributional shifts that must be addressed by careful engineering and complementary compression strategies.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques reduce the size, memory, and inference cost of large neural networks by transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models. Across tasks and modalities—classification, detection, generative modeling, retrieval, and NLP—research has developed logits-based, feature-based, and task-adapted distillation strategies, multi-teacher and ensemble approaches, privacy- and communication-conscious protocols for distributed settings, and teacher-optimization/meta-learning variants. These methods trade off fidelity to teacher behavior with student capacity, expose failure modes (e.g., transfer of low-frequency lexical mistakes or overfitting of student features), and introduce remedies such as selective sample distillation, feature projectors, adversarially-informed samples, and staged or multi-teacher curricula. While KD consistently improves compact models compared to training from scratch and enables deployment on resource-constrained platforms, open issues remain in robustness, task-specific alignment, and distillation under data heterogeneity.

papers_seen.author: Maddox
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Tool for Compression, Bias Transfer, and Robust Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is more than a model compression trick: it is a practical mechanism for transferring inductive biases, regularizing students, enabling privacy- and data-constrained deployments, and adapting architectures or modalities. When paired with complementary techniques—data augmentation, curriculum schedules, teacher ensembles, or generative replay—KD consistently narrows the gap between compact students and large teachers while addressing real-world constraints such as limited labeled data, compute, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Jacobs
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Across vision and language tasks KD encompasses soft-target matching, intermediate feature and layer-wise alignment, adversarial and data-free generation, and task-aware layer mapping. Empirical evidence shows KD enables substantial reductions in latency and memory while often preserving or improving generalization, but success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, and how to handle limited or absent original training data. Practical deployments combine KD with complementary compression methods and careful data or curriculum design to balance accuracy, robustness, and resource constraints.

papers_seen.author: Bowers
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, efficient students by transferring behavioral and representational knowledge from teacher models. A rich family of distillation techniques—ranging from soft-target (logit) matching to intermediate feature imitation, layer-mapping, projector-based transforms, and meta-learned teachers—enables practical trade-offs between accuracy, latency, and deployability across vision and language tasks. Practical success depends on choosing appropriate distillation signals, adapting teacher behavior to student capacity, and addressing data or deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Kelley
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performance models into smaller, deployable students by transferring useful behavior or representations. Across vision, language, generative, and graph domains, KD operates via multiple signals (soft logits, intermediate features, relational or ensemble knowledge) and is typically combined with complementary techniques such as pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation, and data strategies. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can both convey additional task signal and act as a regularizer that improves student generalization relative to training from scratch, but its effectiveness depends on choices about what to transfer, data availability or synthesis, teacher quality, and deployment constraints. Practical use requires tailoring distillation recipes to student capacity and application-specific constraints (latency, privacy, domain shift), and open problems remain around optimization mismatches, rare-token or low-frequency behavior, and privacy-sensitive or heterogeneous-data settings.

papers_seen.author: Roberts
papers_seen.title: Improving the Interpretability of Deep Neural Networks with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep Neural Networks have achieved huge success at a wide spectrum of applications from language modeling, computer vision to speech recognition. However, nowadays, good performance alone is not sufficient to satisfy the needs of practical deployment where interpretability is demanded for cases involving ethics and mission critical applications. The complex models of Deep Neural Networks make it hard to understand and reason the predictions, which hinders its further progress. To tackle this problem, we apply the Knowledge Distillation technique to distill Deep Neural Networks into decision trees in order to attain good performance and interpretability simultaneously. We formulate the problem at hand as a multi-output regression problem and the experiments demonstrate that the student model achieves significantly better accuracy performance (about 1\% to 5\%) than vanilla decision trees at the same level of tree depth. The experiments are implemented on the TensorFlow platform to make it scalable to big datasets. To the best of our knowledge, we are the first to distill Deep Neural Networks into vanilla decision trees on multi-class datasets.

papers_seen.author: Duncan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practically essential approach for compressing large neural models so they can be deployed under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. By transferring learned behavior from teachers to students, KD enables many deployment trade-offs while remaining compatible with complementary techniques (e.g., quantization, pruning, architecture search). However, to be robust and broadly useful in real systems, distillation must go beyond naive soft-label matching: effective pipelines combine logits with internal representation transfer, task- and layer-aware selection of signals, appropriate data strategies, and attention to distributional heterogeneity and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Carpenter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Practical, and Responsible Tool for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, widely applicable method for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. KD shines when combined with complementary compression techniques and data strategies, but its reliability depends on careful choices about what is transferred, how teachers and students are aligned, and how data or robustness constraints are handled. I argue KD should be treated as a central instrument in compression pipelines, used with explicit engineering and ethical practices to manage its limits.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: AutoGAN-Distiller: Searching to Compress Generative Adversarial Networks
papers_seen.abstract: The compression of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) has lately drawn attention, due to the increasing demand for deploying GANs into mobile devices for numerous applications such as image translation, enhancement and editing. However, compared to the substantial efforts to compressing other deep models, the research on compressing GANs (usually the generators) remains at its infancy stage. Existing GAN compression algorithms are limited to handling specific GAN architectures and losses. Inspired by the recent success of AutoML in deep compression, we introduce AutoML to GAN compression and develop an AutoGAN-Distiller (AGD) framework. Starting with a specifically designed efficient search space, AGD performs an end-to-end discovery for new efficient generators, given the target computational resource constraints. The search is guided by the original GAN model via knowledge distillation, therefore fulfilling the compression. AGD is fully automatic, standalone (i.e., needing no trained discriminators), and generically applicable to various GAN models. We evaluate AGD in two representative GAN tasks: image translation and super resolution. Without bells and whistles, AGD yields remarkably lightweight yet more competitive compressed models, that largely outperform existing alternatives. Our codes and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/TAMU-VITA/AGD.

papers_seen.author: Cortez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach that enables deployment of large deep models by training smaller students to retain much of teacher performance. KD supports a wide range of transfer signals (logits, features, attention), training protocols (multi-stage, multi-teacher, federated), and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design). When applied carefully and combined with appropriate data, alignment, and robustness strategies, KD yields substantial runtime and memory savings with modest accuracy loss, making it central to production model compression in NLP and related domains.

papers_seen.author: Harrell
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques have become central tools to deploy high-capacity deep models in latency-, memory-, privacy-, and compute-constrained settings. Across vision, language, graph, and multimodal domains, practitioners use teacher-student training, feature-level transfer, data-free distillation, and hybrid pipelines that combine pruning or architecture search with distillation. Work in this area balances fidelity to teacher models, robustness, and efficiency, and explores trade-offs such as reliance on original training data, communication overhead in federated settings, and the benefits of designing students or student-friendly teachers. The literature shows repeated success of KD when tailored to the task and constraints, while also revealing limitations under severe data heterogeneity or adversarial settings.

papers_seen.author: Hicks
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Adaptation: Teaching to Adapt
papers_seen.abstract: Domain adaptation is crucial in many real-world applications where the distribution of the training data differs from the distribution of the test data. Previous Deep Learning-based approaches to domain adaptation need to be trained jointly on source and target domain data and are therefore unappealing in scenarios where models need to be adapted to a large number of domains or where a domain is evolving, e.g. spam detection where attackers continuously change their tactics.   To fill this gap, we propose Knowledge Adaptation, an extension of Knowledge Distillation (Bucilua et al., 2006; Hinton et al., 2015) to the domain adaptation scenario. We show how a student model achieves state-of-the-art results on unsupervised domain adaptation from multiple sources on a standard sentiment analysis benchmark by taking into account the domain-specific expertise of multiple teachers and the similarities between their domains.   When learning from a single teacher, using domain similarity to gauge trustworthiness is inadequate. To this end, we propose a simple metric that correlates well with the teacher's accuracy in the target domain. We demonstrate that incorporating high-confidence examples selected by this metric enables the student model to achieve state-of-the-art performance in the single-source scenario.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Context-Sensitive Path to Compact Deep Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic framework for compressing large, high-performing deep models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students. Far from a single recipe, KD encompasses soft-target matching, feature and layer alignment, contrastive and self-supervised variants, and teacher-free or data-scarce regimes. When paired with complementary techniques (pruning, architecture adaptation, projectors, and data strategies), KD enables strong trade-offs between latency, memory, and fidelity — but its success depends on matching the distillation signals, optimization schedule, and data assumptions to the deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques reduce computation, memory and latency of large deep models by transferring information from high-capacity "teacher" models to smaller "student" models. A range of approaches have been developed: soft-target (logit) distillation, feature- and layer-wise matching, data-augmentation and data-free synthesis, multi-teacher and curriculum strategies, and teacher-aware or teacher-training modifications. These methods are applied across modalities (NLP, vision, multimodal) and settings (limited data, federated or resource-constrained deployments), and combine naturally with quantization and low-precision inference. Empirical and theoretical work shows gains arise both from conveying inter-class similarities (dark knowledge) and from the regularization effect of softened targets; more recent work focuses on selecting or synthesizing the most useful knowledge for a given student and task.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression methods aim to transfer performance and representational properties from large, expensive models to smaller, efficient ones. Across tasks in vision, language, graph learning, and generative modeling, researchers have developed strategies that extend beyond matching final logits: layer-wise and representation matching, many-to-many layer alignment, data-free distillation, private/distilled deployment, multi-teacher and self-distillation schemes, and task-adaptive compression. These approaches trade off fidelity, privacy, and computational cost, and they have been shown to enable real-world deployment of pretrained language models and other deep systems while revealing open challenges in distribution shift, heterogeneous data, and preserving inductive biases.

papers_seen.author: Alvarado
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques compress large neural networks into smaller, faster models for practical deployment. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD succeeds through multiple mechanisms — not solely by copying a stronger teacher — enabling many practical variants (logit-based soft targets, feature- and layer-level matching, multi-teacher and online schemes, data-free and privacy-preserving protocols). Effective application depends on choosing what and how to transfer, handling data or device constraints, and combining distillation with other compression tools. Key limitations include optimization dynamics, distribution shift for synthetic data, and heterogeneity in federated or privacy-sensitive settings; current research points toward deeper study of representation transfer, optimization effects, and task-aware distillation pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applied strategy to transfer information from large or specialized teacher models into smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained student models. In practice KD has been used to compress pretrained language models, speed up inference in structured models, enable multimodal generation, improve low-precision networks, and scale training across data-parallel workers. Research spans theoretical analyses of why distillation works, empirical studies of failure modes (e.g., propagation of teacher errors), and practical training recipes (including online and self-distillation variants) that balance fidelity to the teacher with student capacity and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Owens
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses capability from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. It encompasses methods that transfer final outputs, intermediate representations, relational structure, or training curricula, and it is applied across modalities (vision, language, scene synthesis, and optimization tasks). KD delivers practical gains in inference speed, memory footprint, and often generalization or robustness when paired with complementary techniques (data augmentation, architecture design, and adversarial training), but its success depends on choices about what is transferred, how data are used or synthesized, and how teacher and student capacities are aligned.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers behavior from large teacher models into smaller student models to reduce latency, memory, and computation while retaining much of the teacher's performance. Across vision, language, and graph domains, KD has been applied as logit matching, intermediate-feature alignment, adversarial transfer, and data- or task-aware synthesis. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD often acts both as a source of extra task signal and as a regularizer; practical systems combine KD with pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation, and data strategies to meet deployment constraints. Important open issues include data heterogeneity, teacher–student capacity mismatch, privacy-preserving releases, and closing remaining gaps in robustness and domain generalization.

papers_seen.author: Phillips
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation transfers knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models so students retain much of the teacher’s performance while reducing inference cost, memory, and latency. The literature has expanded from simple soft-label matching to a broad toolbox that includes intermediate-feature and attention matching, self-distillation, multi-teacher schemes, data-free and zero-shot approaches, curriculum and sample-selection strategies, and combinations with pruning/quantization or architecture search. Empirical work shows that careful choices about what to transfer, how to align architectures, and how to handle data or privacy constraints determine success; outstanding challenges include optimization dynamics, distribution shift, rare-token behaviors, and guaranteeing robust or fair behavior after compression.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Imperative for Deploying Large NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained models have driven major NLP advances but are often impractical for real-world deployment because of size, latency, privacy, and data-distribution constraints. Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression strategies enable retaining most of a large model's performance while producing models that meet latency, memory, and regulatory requirements. Effective KD encompasses diverse techniques — task-adaptive compression, feature mimicking, data-free distillation, teacher meta-learning, privacy-aware distillation, and distributed/continual distillation — which together form a practical toolkit for making state-of-the-art NLP useful at scale.

papers_seen.author: Bowers
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, efficient students by transferring behavioral and representational knowledge from teacher models. A rich family of distillation techniques—ranging from soft-target (logit) matching to intermediate feature imitation, layer-mapping, projector-based transforms, and meta-learned teachers—enables practical trade-offs between accuracy, latency, and deployability across vision and language tasks. Practical success depends on choosing appropriate distillation signals, adapting teacher behavior to student capacity, and addressing data or deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical, Versatile Path to Compact and Generalizable Deep Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical suite of techniques that enable deployment of powerful deep models in resource-constrained or privacy-sensitive settings. Across modalities and tasks, KD compresses capacity while retaining much of the teacher's performance, and when combined with representation-level matching, data augmentation, curriculum strategies, meta-learning, or architecture-aware search it can also improve generalization, robustness, and cross-device inclusivity. KD is therefore not merely a model-compression trick but a broadly applicable framework for transferring structure, relational signals, and inductive biases from expensive models into efficient students for real-world use.

papers_seen.author: Patterson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Effective, Flexible, and Context-Sensitive
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, widely applicable approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When used thoughtfully—matching what is transferred to student capacity, combining logits- and feature-level objectives, and integrating complementary techniques like low-precision numerics or architectural redesign—KD consistently yields compact models that approach teacher performance while reducing inference cost. However, KD is not a one-size-fits-all solution: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints such as privacy or heterogeneity, so practitioners must adapt KD components and pipelines to the task and environment.

papers_seen.author: Mckay
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques have become central to deploying high-performance deep models in resource-constrained settings. Research has produced diverse approaches that transfer information from larger "teacher" models to smaller "student" models via softened outputs, intermediate feature supervision, layer-wise alignment, module replacement, data augmentation, and data-free synthesis. These methods have been applied across modalities (vision, speech, language, multi-modal), combined with quantization and architecture search, and adapted for settings with limited or private data. Empirical and theoretical work highlights why distillation can improve generalization, how inductive biases or teacher strength influence transfer, and practical strategies to make students more robust and efficient. Challenges remain in aligning heterogeneous architectures, preserving task-relevant representations, and designing principled distillation objectives for varied downstream tasks.

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP — Promise, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from larger teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. When paired with representation-level objectives, data strategies (including synthetic or privacy-preserving generation), and architecture-aware design, KD routinely yields models that meet latency, memory, and deployment constraints while retaining much of teacher performance. Success is engineering-dependent: the distillation signal, student capacity and pre-training, data availability, and explicit mitigation for harms such as bias or distributional fragility determine whether compressed models meet real-world needs.

papers_seen.author: Cortez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach that enables deployment of large deep models by training smaller students to retain much of teacher performance. KD supports a wide range of transfer signals (logits, features, attention), training protocols (multi-stage, multi-teacher, federated), and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design). When applied carefully and combined with appropriate data, alignment, and robustness strategies, KD yields substantial runtime and memory savings with modest accuracy loss, making it central to production model compression in NLP and related domains.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression methods provide practical mechanisms to convert large, high-performing deep models into smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained students suitable for real-world deployment. Across vision, speech, and NLP, practitioners use KD to trade off capacity and efficiency while aiming to preserve task performance, often in combination with complementary techniques such as quantization, pruning, or architecture adaptation. Success depends on aligning teacher signals, student capacity, data strategy, and optimization schedules; remaining challenges include handling domain shift, preserving rare-token behavior, and operating under privacy or data-limited settings.

papers_seen.author: Green
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and internal information from teacher models. Across vision, language, graph, and detection tasks, distillation techniques range from matching softened output distributions to aligning intermediate features or relational structures, and they are frequently combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) and data strategies (augmentation, synthetic-data or no-data approaches). Continued progress centers on principled transfer objectives, data-aware workflows, and integration with other compression primitives to produce deployable, robust compact models.

papers_seen.author: Rivera
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of techniques for transferring behavior from large teacher models into smaller, faster students so models can be deployed under compute, memory, privacy, and latency constraints. Distillation methods vary in what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, relational or ensemble outputs), how training data are used (original, augmented, synthesized, or absent), and how distillation is combined with orthogonal compression strategies (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical results show KD can preserve substantial teacher performance when pipelines are tailored to student capacity, data availability, and deployment needs; open challenges remain around robustness, fairness, domain shift, and data- or privacy-limited settings.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation with Progressive Refinement of Targets
papers_seen.abstract: The generalization capability of deep neural networks has been substantially improved by applying a wide spectrum of regularization methods, e.g., restricting function space, injecting randomness during training, augmenting data, etc. In this work, we propose a simple yet effective regularization method named progressive self-knowledge distillation (PS-KD), which progressively distills a model's own knowledge to soften hard targets (i.e., one-hot vectors) during training. Hence, it can be interpreted within a framework of knowledge distillation as a student becomes a teacher itself. Specifically, targets are adjusted adaptively by combining the ground-truth and past predictions from the model itself. We show that PS-KD provides an effect of hard example mining by rescaling gradients according to difficulty in classifying examples. The proposed method is applicable to any supervised learning tasks with hard targets and can be easily combined with existing regularization methods to further enhance the generalization performance. Furthermore, it is confirmed that PS-KD achieves not only better accuracy, but also provides high quality of confidence estimates in terms of calibration as well as ordinal ranking. Extensive experimental results on three different tasks, image classification, object detection, and machine translation, demonstrate that our method consistently improves the performance of the state-of-the-art baselines. The code is available at https://github.com/lgcnsai/PS-KD-Pytorch.

papers_seen.author: Daniel
papers_seen.title: Data-Free Adversarial Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge Distillation (KD) has made remarkable progress in the last few years and become a popular paradigm for model compression and knowledge transfer. However, almost all existing KD algorithms are data-driven, i.e., relying on a large amount of original training data or alternative data, which is usually unavailable in real-world scenarios. In this paper, we devote ourselves to this challenging problem and propose a novel adversarial distillation mechanism to craft a compact student model without any real-world data. We introduce a model discrepancy to quantificationally measure the difference between student and teacher models and construct an optimizable upper bound. In our work, the student and the teacher jointly act the role of the discriminator to reduce this discrepancy, when a generator adversarially produces some "hard samples" to enlarge it. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed data-free method yields comparable performance to existing data-driven methods. More strikingly, our approach can be directly extended to semantic segmentation, which is more complicated than classification, and our approach achieves state-of-the-art results. Code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/VainF/Data-Free-Adversarial-Distillation.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Practical, and Composable Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students that remain useful for deployment in resource-constrained or data-limited settings. KD works across modalities and deployment scenarios when combined with complementary compression techniques and careful design choices. To realize its benefits practitioners should treat KD as a component of a compression pipeline: design student-friendly teachers, choose what to transfer (logits, features, layers) based on task needs, address data constraints with augmentation or data-free methods, and pair distillation with pruning, quantization, or architecture search to meet latency and memory goals.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: What We Know
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical suite of techniques that transfers information from large teacher models to smaller students to enable efficient deployment. In practice KD spans matching teacher outputs (soft logits), aligning intermediate representations, specialized layer- and channel-level transfers, and workflows that combine distillation with pruning, quantization, or synthetic-data strategies. KD delivers substantial reductions in compute, memory, and latency while often improving student generalization, but its success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity, and how to handle data or domain shifts. Open issues include robustness under distributional heterogeneity, preserving rare-token or fine-grained behavior in sequence models, and distillation without original training data.

papers_seen.author: Cochran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Uses, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations. Across vision, language, speech, graph, and multimodal tasks, a family of techniques—soft-label matching, feature and attention imitation, layer mapping, multi-teacher and curriculum schemes, and data-free or privacy-aware protocols—enables students to recover much of teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints. Practical success depends on task- and deployment-aware choices (distilled signal, student capacity, data availability, and augmentation), and remaining challenges include robustness to distribution shift, preservation of rare-token or fine-grained behaviors, and distillation under privacy or data-scarce conditions.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible, and empirically validated family of methods for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When applied thoughtfully—using richer targets than logits, aligning intermediate representations, and combining with complementary techniques such as pruning, quantization, or architecture search—KD routinely enables substantial reductions in latency, memory, and energy while preserving much of a teacher's performance. KD also adapts to constrained settings (few-shot, federated, or data-free) and supports robustness and domain adaptation when pipelines are designed to match task and deployment constraints. Realizing KD's full value requires principled choices about what to transfer, how to generate or select distillation data, and how to align teacher and student capacity.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Practical Principles for Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, production-ready approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, faster ones while retaining much of their performance. KD techniques span teacher design, student-teacher layer mapping, multi-teacher and ensemble strategies, data-aware and data-free workflows, and scalable/online training protocols. When combined with task-aware selection and domain adaptation, distillation enables effective deployment of high-performing models under latency, memory, and heterogeneous-device constraints.

papers_seen.author: Lin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, faster student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. KD is applied across modalities and deployment contexts to reduce inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance. Practical KD pipelines combine choice of distillation target, teacher and student preparation, data strategies, and complementary compression methods to meet constraints such as latency, memory, privacy, and domain shift. While KD is highly effective in many settings, it has known limits—capacity mismatch, distributional heterogeneity, and transferred biases—that require careful method and evaluation design.

papers_seen.author: Rocha
papers_seen.title: Few Shot Network Compression via Cross Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Model compression has been widely adopted to obtain light-weighted deep neural networks. Most prevalent methods, however, require fine-tuning with sufficient training data to ensure accuracy, which could be challenged by privacy and security issues. As a compromise between privacy and performance, in this paper we investigate few shot network compression: given few samples per class, how can we effectively compress the network with negligible performance drop? The core challenge of few shot network compression lies in high estimation errors from the original network during inference, since the compressed network can easily over-fits on the few training instances. The estimation errors could propagate and accumulate layer-wisely and finally deteriorate the network output. To address the problem, we propose cross distillation, a novel layer-wise knowledge distillation approach. By interweaving hidden layers of teacher and student network, layer-wisely accumulated estimation errors can be effectively reduced.The proposed method offers a general framework compatible with prevalent network compression techniques such as pruning. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that cross distillation can significantly improve the student network's accuracy when only a few training instances are available.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation for Practical NLP Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical, flexible pathway to deploy high-performing deep learning and NLP models under real-world constraints. By transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or inductive biases from large or multi-modal teachers to smaller students, distillation enables task- and domain-specific compression, faster inference, privacy-preserving distributed training, and architectural simplification. Effective distillation requires methods that match the target deployment needs—task-awareness, layer alignment, careful use of data augmentation and teacher ensembles, and scaling strategies for large datasets and distributed settings. When designed deliberately, distillation yields compressed models that retain much of the teacher's capability while meeting latency, size, and privacy requirements.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, practical strategy for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students in deep learning and NLP. KD is versatile—operating at the level of logits, features, or layers—and integrates naturally with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and with data-constrained or privacy-sensitive deployments. When applied with attention to what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to manage data, KD yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance; however, careful design is required to address optimization, distribution-shift, and low-frequency phenomena.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Distilling portable Generative Adversarial Networks for Image Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been widely used in various image-to-image translation tasks, they can be hardly applied on mobile devices due to their heavy computation and storage cost. Traditional network compression methods focus on visually recognition tasks, but never deal with generation tasks. Inspired by knowledge distillation, a student generator of fewer parameters is trained by inheriting the low-level and high-level information from the original heavy teacher generator. To promote the capability of student generator, we include a student discriminator to measure the distances between real images, and images generated by student and teacher generators. An adversarial learning process is therefore established to optimize student generator and student discriminator. Qualitative and quantitative analysis by conducting experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method can learn portable generative models with strong performance.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical, flexible approach for turning large, high-performing deep and pretrained NLP models into smaller, faster models suitable for real-world deployment. The literature shows KD operates via multiple signals (soft targets, intermediate features, attention or relational structure), multiple workflows (data-driven, data-free, multi-stage, multi-teacher), and often in combination with orthogonal compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical work demonstrates that properly designed distillation pipelines can recover most of a teacher's utility in a much smaller footprint, but success depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity, addressing data limitations and privacy constraints, and engineering choices such as layer mapping, augmentation, and progressive or curriculum-driven training.

papers_seen.author: Maddox
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Tool for Compression, Bias Transfer, and Robust Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is more than a model compression trick: it is a practical mechanism for transferring inductive biases, regularizing students, enabling privacy- and data-constrained deployments, and adapting architectures or modalities. When paired with complementary techniques—data augmentation, curriculum schedules, teacher ensembles, or generative replay—KD consistently narrows the gap between compact students and large teachers while addressing real-world constraints such as limited labeled data, compute, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Mechanisms, Variants, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, more deployable students by transferring information beyond hard labels. Across modalities and settings, KD methods range from matching teacher soft targets (logits) to aligning intermediate representations, combining multiple teachers, synthesizing training data when originals are unavailable, and integrating with other compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Practical distillation must balance student capacity, the form of transferred knowledge, data availability and privacy constraints, and optimization strategies to produce compact models that preserve accuracy, robustness, and deployment requirements.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: BERT Learns to Teach: Knowledge Distillation with Meta Learning
papers_seen.abstract: We present Knowledge Distillation with Meta Learning (MetaDistil), a simple yet effective alternative to traditional knowledge distillation (KD) methods where the teacher model is fixed during training. We show the teacher network can learn to better transfer knowledge to the student network (i.e., learning to teach) with the feedback from the performance of the distilled student network in a meta learning framework. Moreover, we introduce a pilot update mechanism to improve the alignment between the inner-learner and meta-learner in meta learning algorithms that focus on an improved inner-learner. Experiments on various benchmarks show that MetaDistil can yield significant improvements compared with traditional KD algorithms and is less sensitive to the choice of different student capacity and hyperparameters, facilitating the use of KD on different tasks and models.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Extract the Knowledge of Graph Neural Networks and Go Beyond it: An Effective Knowledge Distillation Framework
papers_seen.abstract: Semi-supervised learning on graphs is an important problem in the machine learning area. In recent years, state-of-the-art classification methods based on graph neural networks (GNNs) have shown their superiority over traditional ones such as label propagation. However, the sophisticated architectures of these neural models will lead to a complex prediction mechanism, which could not make full use of valuable prior knowledge lying in the data, e.g., structurally correlated nodes tend to have the same class. In this paper, we propose a framework based on knowledge distillation to address the above issues. Our framework extracts the knowledge of an arbitrary learned GNN model (teacher model), and injects it into a well-designed student model. The student model is built with two simple prediction mechanisms, i.e., label propagation and feature transformation, which naturally preserves structure-based and feature-based prior knowledge, respectively. In specific, we design the student model as a trainable combination of parameterized label propagation and feature transformation modules. As a result, the learned student can benefit from both prior knowledge and the knowledge in GNN teachers for more effective predictions. Moreover, the learned student model has a more interpretable prediction process than GNNs. We conduct experiments on five public benchmark datasets and employ seven GNN models including GCN, GAT, APPNP, SAGE, SGC, GCNII and GLP as the teacher models. Experimental results show that the learned student model can consistently outperform its corresponding teacher model by 1.4% - 4.7% on average. Code and data are available at https://github.com/BUPT-GAMMA/CPF
