papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Design Principles
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely applicable approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. KD achieves favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-offs across modalities when practitioners choose what form of teacher knowledge to transfer, how to map layers and representations, and how to handle limited or private data. However, KD is not plug-and-play: outcomes depend heavily on teacher quality, distilled signals, data availability, and task-specific constraints. Thoughtful combination of feature-level objectives, task-aware layer selection, data-synthesis or privacy-preserving queries, and targeted curricula yields robust compressed models ready for real-world deployment.

papers_seen.author: Liu
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Strategy for Compressing NLP Models: Benefits, Limits, and Practical Recipes
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable ones. In NLP, KD enables retaining much of the teacher model's linguistic capability while reducing storage and inference cost. Effective compression with KD requires more than mimicking final outputs: it benefits from aligning internal representations, task-aware layer mapping, and handling data or privacy constraints with synthetic or metadata-driven techniques. However, KD is not a panacea — distributional heterogeneity, privacy, and mismatches between teacher and student capacity pose real limits that must be mitigated by careful method design and evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Across vision, speech, and language tasks, KD has expanded from simple logit matching to a rich toolbox including feature- and layer-level imitation, self- and progressive-distillation, ensemble compression, data-free or zero-shot approaches, and federated protocols. Empirical work shows KD can yield compact models that retain much of teacher performance while reducing inference cost, but practical success depends on design choices about what to transfer, how to supply or synthesize data, and how to handle teacher–student mismatches and optimization challenges.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: AutoGAN-Distiller: Searching to Compress Generative Adversarial Networks
papers_seen.abstract: The compression of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) has lately drawn attention, due to the increasing demand for deploying GANs into mobile devices for numerous applications such as image translation, enhancement and editing. However, compared to the substantial efforts to compressing other deep models, the research on compressing GANs (usually the generators) remains at its infancy stage. Existing GAN compression algorithms are limited to handling specific GAN architectures and losses. Inspired by the recent success of AutoML in deep compression, we introduce AutoML to GAN compression and develop an AutoGAN-Distiller (AGD) framework. Starting with a specifically designed efficient search space, AGD performs an end-to-end discovery for new efficient generators, given the target computational resource constraints. The search is guided by the original GAN model via knowledge distillation, therefore fulfilling the compression. AGD is fully automatic, standalone (i.e., needing no trained discriminators), and generically applicable to various GAN models. We evaluate AGD in two representative GAN tasks: image translation and super resolution. Without bells and whistles, AGD yields remarkably lightweight yet more competitive compressed models, that largely outperform existing alternatives. Our codes and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/TAMU-VITA/AGD.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Mitigating Gender Bias in Distilled Language Models via Counterfactual Role Reversal
papers_seen.abstract: Language models excel at generating coherent text, and model compression techniques such as knowledge distillation have enabled their use in resource-constrained settings. However, these models can be biased in multiple ways, including the unfounded association of male and female genders with gender-neutral professions. Therefore, knowledge distillation without any fairness constraints may preserve or exaggerate the teacher model's biases onto the distilled model. To this end, we present a novel approach to mitigate gender disparity in text generation by learning a fair model during knowledge distillation. We propose two modifications to the base knowledge distillation based on counterfactual role reversal$\unicode{x2014}$modifying teacher probabilities and augmenting the training set. We evaluate gender polarity across professions in open-ended text generated from the resulting distilled and finetuned GPT$\unicode{x2012}$2 models and demonstrate a substantial reduction in gender disparity with only a minor compromise in utility. Finally, we observe that language models that reduce gender polarity in language generation do not improve embedding fairness or downstream classification fairness.

papers_seen.author: Barnes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practical Patterns, and Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses high-capacity teacher models into smaller student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Across vision and language, distillation strategies—matching logits, internal features, attention or relational structure, or using synthetic or public data—enable large reductions in model size and latency while preserving much of teacher performance. Practical deployments combine distillation with other compression tools, online or distributed training regimes, and privacy-aware variants, but face persistent challenges in aligning internal representations, retaining robustness and fairness, and operating under data or resource constraints.

papers_seen.author: Lin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, faster student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. KD is applied across modalities and deployment contexts to reduce inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance. Practical KD pipelines combine choice of distillation target, teacher and student preparation, data strategies, and complementary compression methods to meet constraints such as latency, memory, privacy, and domain shift. While KD is highly effective in many settings, it has known limits—capacity mismatch, distributional heterogeneity, and transferred biases—that require careful method and evaluation design.

papers_seen.author: Wong
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Principled Path to Efficient, Adaptable, and Responsible NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is not merely a compression trick but a general framework that enables smaller or specialized models to inherit useful behaviors from larger teachers while controlling generalization, efficiency, and social impact. When combined with layer-wise and representation-level matching, task-aware architecture search, thoughtful input augmentation, and deployment-aware protocols, KD supports high-performance, resource-frugal NLP systems that can be adapted to heterogeneous devices and sensitive application contexts.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: MEAL: Multi-Model Ensemble via Adversarial Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Often the best performing deep neural models are ensembles of multiple base-level networks. Unfortunately, the space required to store these many networks, and the time required to execute them at test-time, prohibits their use in applications where test sets are large (e.g., ImageNet). In this paper, we present a method for compressing large, complex trained ensembles into a single network, where knowledge from a variety of trained deep neural networks (DNNs) is distilled and transferred to a single DNN. In order to distill diverse knowledge from different trained (teacher) models, we propose to use adversarial-based learning strategy where we define a block-wise training loss to guide and optimize the predefined student network to recover the knowledge in teacher models, and to promote the discriminator network to distinguish teacher vs. student features simultaneously. The proposed ensemble method (MEAL) of transferring distilled knowledge with adversarial learning exhibits three important advantages: (1) the student network that learns the distilled knowledge with discriminators is optimized better than the original model; (2) fast inference is realized by a single forward pass, while the performance is even better than traditional ensembles from multi-original models; (3) the student network can learn the distilled knowledge from a teacher model that has arbitrary structures. Extensive experiments on CIFAR-10/100, SVHN and ImageNet datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our MEAL method. On ImageNet, our ResNet-50 based MEAL achieves top-1/5 21.79%/5.99% val error, which outperforms the original model by 2.06%/1.14%. Code and models are available at: https://github.com/AaronHeee/MEAL

papers_seen.author: Wheeler
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Cornerstone for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically proven approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation), task-aware design, and careful teacher selection or training, KD can yield compact models that retain much of the original performance. However, successful deployment requires attention to data heterogeneity, fairness, and robustness limitations.

papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: Effective Knowledge Distillation: Representation, Selection, and Practical Constraints
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach to compress and adapt large deep models for deployment in resource- or privacy-constrained settings. Effective distillation goes beyond matching teacher logits: transferring internal representations, choosing which teacher signals to trust, and accommodating deployment constraints (limited data, communication, low-precision hardware) are all decisive. I argue that the most reliable distillation pipelines combine representation-level objectives, selective/sample-aware strategies, and engineering choices that address privacy and efficiency, yielding compact students that retain teacher strengths across NLP, vision, and graph domains.

papers_seen.author: Charles
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, broadly applicable approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers information from high-capacity teachers to compact students via outputs, intermediate representations, or relational signals, and integrates naturally with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and deployment workflows (on-device inference, federated learning, and data-limited regimes). While KD reliably improves efficiency while preserving much of teacher performance, robust application requires careful choices about what signals to transfer, how to handle imperfect teachers and low-frequency behaviors, and how to combine KD with data strategies and architecture design to meet real-world constraints.

papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: Reinforced Multi-Teacher Selection for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: In natural language processing (NLP) tasks, slow inference speed and huge footprints in GPU usage remain the bottleneck of applying pre-trained deep models in production. As a popular method for model compression, knowledge distillation transfers knowledge from one or multiple large (teacher) models to a small (student) model. When multiple teacher models are available in distillation, the state-of-the-art methods assign a fixed weight to a teacher model in the whole distillation. Furthermore, most of the existing methods allocate an equal weight to every teacher model. In this paper, we observe that, due to the complexity of training examples and the differences in student model capability, learning differentially from teacher models can lead to better performance of student models distilled. We systematically develop a reinforced method to dynamically assign weights to teacher models for different training instances and optimize the performance of student model. Our extensive experimental results on several NLP tasks clearly verify the feasibility and effectiveness of our approach.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Recommendations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile method for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD works across modalities (vision, language, graphs, and generative models) by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from teachers to students. When applied thoughtfully—selecting appropriate distillation signals, aligning internal representations, and integrating complementary compression techniques—KD reliably yields compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is not a plug-and-play cure: its success depends on teacher quality, data strategy, optimization choices, and architecture alignment, so practitioners should pair KD with task-aware curricula, representation-level objectives, and other compression tools to realize robust deployment.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. The approach spans simple soft-target matching to feature- and layer-level imitation, and it is commonly combined with other compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture simplification) and data strategies (public or synthesized data, selective sampling). KD routinely improves compact models over training from scratch and enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, but its effectiveness depends on design choices about what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, how to prepare data, and how to mitigate teacher imperfections and distributional shift.

papers_seen.author: Jackson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad family of techniques for transferring information from large, often expensive teacher models to smaller, cheaper student models so they retain much of the teacher's performance while reducing inference cost. KD methods operate at different levels (logits, intermediate features, modules or entire architectures) and are applied across domains including vision, speech, NLP and federated settings. Contemporary work has advanced new losses, layer-alignment strategies, module-replacement schemes, robustness-aware procedures, and analyses that clarify when and why distillation helps. Important practical challenges remain around heterogeneous data, strong teachers, and preserving properties such as robustness, generalization across distributions, and multimodal capability.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Central Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely applicable method for compressing large models into smaller, deployable ones across NLP and other deep learning domains. KD preserves much of teacher performance while enabling faster inference, smaller footprints, and flexible deployment; however, it has failure modes related to data dependence, teacher quality, and rare-token fidelity. Effective use of KD therefore treats it as a toolbox—combining multi-teacher schedules, data-aware augmentation, representation-level objectives, and privacy-aware protocols—to produce robust, task-appropriate compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Hickman
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques aim to transfer the predictive power of large, expensive models into smaller, faster models while retaining performance. Approaches vary from matching teacher outputs (soft labels) to aligning intermediate representations, leveraging data augmentation or synthesized data when real data are limited, and jointly optimizing architecture and distillation losses for task-adaptive compression. Advances address student–teacher capacity gaps, multi-teacher transfer, and domain or data scarcity; remaining challenges include transferring internal structure efficiently, generalization under distribution shifts, and designing teacher models that are optimized for downstream distillation.

papers_seen.author: Nguyen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Small-footprint Highway Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning has significantly advanced state-of-the-art of speech recognition in the past few years. However, compared to conventional Gaussian mixture acoustic models, neural network models are usually much larger, and are therefore not very deployable in embedded devices. Previously, we investigated a compact highway deep neural network (HDNN) for acoustic modelling, which is a type of depth-gated feedforward neural network. We have shown that HDNN-based acoustic models can achieve comparable recognition accuracy with much smaller number of model parameters compared to plain deep neural network (DNN) acoustic models. In this paper, we push the boundary further by leveraging on the knowledge distillation technique that is also known as {\it teacher-student} training, i.e., we train the compact HDNN model with the supervision of a high accuracy cumbersome model. Furthermore, we also investigate sequence training and adaptation in the context of teacher-student training. Our experiments were performed on the AMI meeting speech recognition corpus. With this technique, we significantly improved the recognition accuracy of the HDNN acoustic model with less than 0.8 million parameters, and narrowed the gap between this model and the plain DNN with 30 million parameters.

papers_seen.author: Adkins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, broadly applicable strategy for shrinking large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students. KD can reproduce much of a teacher's task performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints; it also integrates naturally with complementary techniques (pretraining, data augmentation, multi-teacher supervision, and progressive module replacement). Realizing KD's full value in production requires attention to optimization gaps, dataset mismatch, and the risk of propagating teacher biases, and benefits from targeted extensions—feature-level objectives, adversarially-informed sample selection, and staged or progressive compression strategies.

papers_seen.author: Kim
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, flexible approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When paired with representation-aware objectives, careful pre-training of compact models, and safeguards for robustness and privacy, KD enables production-ready reductions in latency, memory, and energy while retaining much of a teacher's performance. I argue that KD should be treated as a central tool in model-compression pipelines, not as a single recipe but as a family of methods to be combined with task-aware design choices for reliable deployment.

papers_seen.author: Valencia
papers_seen.title: Practical and Robust Knowledge Distillation for Deployable Deep Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a central tool for compressing large deep models so they can be deployed under latency, memory, and power constraints. Beyond matching teacher output probabilities, modern distillation should transfer internal structure, be tailored to domain and modality differences, and integrate with quantization, privacy, and data-limited settings. When applied with methods that address representation mismatch, optimization challenges, and curriculum of supervisory signals, distillation enables small models that approach teacher performance while meeting real-world deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Ware
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, flexible, and production-ready family of techniques that enables large deep and language models to be compressed into smaller, faster, and more deployable students. When combined with complementary methods—representation matching, multi-teacher or online schemes, synthetic or data-free generation, and hardware-aware compression—KD delivers strong efficiency gains while preserving much of teacher performance. However, KD is not a universal solution: its success depends on careful pipeline design to address capacity mismatch, dataset or domain heterogeneity, privacy constraints, and the risk of transferring or amplifying teacher biases.

papers_seen.author: Shaw
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Practical Tool for Model Compression in NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, versatile approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of their performance. KD works across modalities and tasks, and its effectiveness depends on matching distillation techniques to data and deployment constraints. When combined with careful model and data design, KD enables practical deployment of advanced models under latency, memory, and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Brennan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as the most practical and widely applicable approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students for vision, language, and other modalities. When applied thoughtfully — selecting what to transfer (logits, features, attention), designing teacher-student pairs, and combining KD with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, data synthesis) — distillation recovers much of a teacher’s performance while meeting real-world latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD also serves beyond compression as a regularizer that can improve robustness and generalization, but it is not a panacea: capacity mismatch, domain shift, optimization differences, and risks of transferring biases or vulnerability must be managed through targeted practices and evaluations.

papers_seen.author: Roberts
papers_seen.title: Improving the Interpretability of Deep Neural Networks with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep Neural Networks have achieved huge success at a wide spectrum of applications from language modeling, computer vision to speech recognition. However, nowadays, good performance alone is not sufficient to satisfy the needs of practical deployment where interpretability is demanded for cases involving ethics and mission critical applications. The complex models of Deep Neural Networks make it hard to understand and reason the predictions, which hinders its further progress. To tackle this problem, we apply the Knowledge Distillation technique to distill Deep Neural Networks into decision trees in order to attain good performance and interpretability simultaneously. We formulate the problem at hand as a multi-output regression problem and the experiments demonstrate that the student model achieves significantly better accuracy performance (about 1\% to 5\%) than vanilla decision trees at the same level of tree depth. The experiments are implemented on the TensorFlow platform to make it scalable to big datasets. To the best of our knowledge, we are the first to distill Deep Neural Networks into vanilla decision trees on multi-class datasets.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation in Practical Model Compression for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a niche training trick into a broad, practically necessary toolkit for compressing large deep models for deployment in resource-constrained settings. KD variants enable compressing Transformer-based and convolutional architectures, transferring useful inductive biases, operating with limited or no access to original training data, and even addressing downstream concerns such as fairness. At the same time, KD has limitations in certain distributed or heterogeneous-data settings that require complementary methods or careful protocol design. A targeted combination of task-aware layer-wise methods, feature-level mimicking, adversarial/data-free generation, and attention to distributional heterogeneity yields the best practical results for NLP and other deep learning applications.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: The Case for Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Model Compression in NLP and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable ones while retaining much of their performance. Across NLP, speech, vision-language, and multimodal tasks, distillation techniques—including self-distillation, layer-wise/task-aware distillation, and teacher adaptation—enable substantial reductions in model size and compute with limited accuracy loss. KD is complementary to other compression strategies (e.g., pruning and architecture search) and benefits from careful choices in intermediate-target selection, data augmentation, and teacher-student alignment. When combined thoughtfully with task adaptation and hardware-aware techniques, KD unlocks feasible deployment of advanced models in resource-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical, flexible approach for turning large, high-performing deep and pretrained NLP models into smaller, faster models suitable for real-world deployment. The literature shows KD operates via multiple signals (soft targets, intermediate features, attention or relational structure), multiple workflows (data-driven, data-free, multi-stage, multi-teacher), and often in combination with orthogonal compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical work demonstrates that properly designed distillation pipelines can recover most of a teacher's utility in a much smaller footprint, but success depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity, addressing data limitations and privacy constraints, and engineering choices such as layer mapping, augmentation, and progressive or curriculum-driven training.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques transfer predictive behavior and internal structure from larger teacher models to smaller student models to reduce computation, memory, and latency while preserving performance. The literature documents a spectrum of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention or channel maps, and relational signals), a variety of optimization and architectural practices (layer mapping, projectors, multi-stage training, and student-friendly teacher design), and deployment workflows for constrained settings (data-free, federated, and domain-adaptive distillation). Empirical and theoretical work highlights multiple mechanisms that make KD effective (regularization via soft targets, representation alignment, and optimization/inductive-bias transfer), while also identifying persistent challenges such as aligning heterogeneous architectures, preserving low-frequency behavior, and selecting what and when to transfer. Practical recommendations center on matching distillation signals to student capacity, using feature- or layer-aware objectives when internal alignment matters, and combining KD with complementary compression techniques for robust deployment.

papers_seen.author: Patterson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Effective, Flexible, and Context-Sensitive
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, widely applicable approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When used thoughtfully—matching what is transferred to student capacity, combining logits- and feature-level objectives, and integrating complementary techniques like low-precision numerics or architectural redesign—KD consistently yields compact models that approach teacher performance while reducing inference cost. However, KD is not a one-size-fits-all solution: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints such as privacy or heterogeneity, so practitioners must adapt KD components and pipelines to the task and environment.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Path to Compact, Deployable Deep Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, flexible set of techniques for transferring behavior from large, expensive teacher models into smaller, faster students. In deep learning and NLP, KD enables practical deployment by reducing latency, memory, and power requirements while retaining much of teacher performance. Effective application requires: (1) combining KD with domain-aware pretraining of compact models, (2) adapting distillation to data-constrained or privacy-sensitive settings, and (3) integrating architectural and optimization improvements (e.g., feature projectors, mixed-precision) to close remaining gaps. When applied thoughtfully, KD is a key tool for making state-of-the-art models useful in real-world, resource-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Calderon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained deep models deliver strong performance across vision and language tasks but are often too large or slow for real-world deployment. Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression strategies provide practical ways to transfer behavior from high-capacity teacher models to smaller students, enabling reduced storage, faster inference, and deployment on constrained devices. Research has developed a range of KD formulations—logit-level supervision, intermediate representation matching, layer mapping, multi-teacher fusion, and data-free distillation—alongside empirical and theoretical analyses that explain when and why distillation helps. The literature also shows KD’s effectiveness in NLP for compressing models like BERT into lightweight architectures without additional data, and highlights open challenges such as heterogeneous teachers, data privacy, and preserving task-specific inductive biases.

papers_seen.author: Adkins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, broadly applicable strategy for shrinking large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students. KD can reproduce much of a teacher's task performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints; it also integrates naturally with complementary techniques (pretraining, data augmentation, multi-teacher supervision, and progressive module replacement). Realizing KD's full value in production requires attention to optimization gaps, dataset mismatch, and the risk of propagating teacher biases, and benefits from targeted extensions—feature-level objectives, adversarially-informed sample selection, and staged or progressive compression strategies.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Compressing GANs using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been used in several machine learning tasks such as domain transfer, super resolution, and synthetic data generation. State-of-the-art GANs often use tens of millions of parameters, making them expensive to deploy for applications in low SWAP (size, weight, and power) hardware, such as mobile devices, and for applications with real time capabilities. There has been no work found to reduce the number of parameters used in GANs. Therefore, we propose a method to compress GANs using knowledge distillation techniques, in which a smaller "student" GAN learns to mimic a larger "teacher" GAN. We show that the distillation methods used on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and Celeb-A datasets can compress teacher GANs at ratios of 1669:1, 58:1, and 87:1, respectively, while retaining the quality of the generated image. From our experiments, we observe a qualitative limit for GAN's compression. Moreover, we observe that, with a fixed parameter budget, compressed GANs outperform GANs trained using standard training methods. We conjecture that this is partially owing to the optimization landscape of over-parameterized GANs which allows efficient training using alternating gradient descent. Thus, training an over-parameterized GAN followed by our proposed compression scheme provides a high quality generative model with a small number of parameters.

papers_seen.author: Walters
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and inductive biases from large teacher models to smaller student models so they can meet real-world constraints (latency, memory, privacy). Methods vary by what is transferred (soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention, relational signals), how data are used or synthesized, and whether distillation is combined with other compression tools or automated search. Empirically, KD often preserves much of teacher performance while enabling substantial reductions in size and inference cost, but practical success depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity, addressing data or privacy limits, and adapting teachers or objectives to propagate desired properties such as robustness and generalization.

papers_seen.author: Rocha
papers_seen.title: Few Shot Network Compression via Cross Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Model compression has been widely adopted to obtain light-weighted deep neural networks. Most prevalent methods, however, require fine-tuning with sufficient training data to ensure accuracy, which could be challenged by privacy and security issues. As a compromise between privacy and performance, in this paper we investigate few shot network compression: given few samples per class, how can we effectively compress the network with negligible performance drop? The core challenge of few shot network compression lies in high estimation errors from the original network during inference, since the compressed network can easily over-fits on the few training instances. The estimation errors could propagate and accumulate layer-wisely and finally deteriorate the network output. To address the problem, we propose cross distillation, a novel layer-wise knowledge distillation approach. By interweaving hidden layers of teacher and student network, layer-wisely accumulated estimation errors can be effectively reduced.The proposed method offers a general framework compatible with prevalent network compression techniques such as pruning. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that cross distillation can significantly improve the student network's accuracy when only a few training instances are available.

papers_seen.author: Rivera
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of techniques for transferring behavior from large teacher models into smaller, faster students so models can be deployed under compute, memory, privacy, and latency constraints. Distillation methods vary in what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, relational or ensemble outputs), how training data are used (original, augmented, synthesized, or absent), and how distillation is combined with orthogonal compression strategies (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical results show KD can preserve substantial teacher performance when pipelines are tailored to student capacity, data availability, and deployment needs; open challenges remain around robustness, fairness, domain shift, and data- or privacy-limited settings.

papers_seen.author: Kennedy
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques transfer information from larger teacher models to smaller student models to reduce inference cost while preserving performance. The literature identifies several methodological families — soft-label/logit matching, intermediate representation or feature mimicking, layer-wise and many-to-many layer alignment, multi-teacher and online protocols, and data-free/synthetic-data strategies — and shows that KD often works best when combined with complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and when adapted to the task and deployment constraints. Empirical work demonstrates strong gains across vision, language, graph, and multimodal domains, while practical deployment raises challenges in data availability, teacher-student architecture mismatch, robustness, and privacy in federated or distributed settings.

papers_seen.author: Cortez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach that enables deployment of large deep models by training smaller students to retain much of teacher performance. KD supports a wide range of transfer signals (logits, features, attention), training protocols (multi-stage, multi-teacher, federated), and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design). When applied carefully and combined with appropriate data, alignment, and robustness strategies, KD yields substantial runtime and memory savings with modest accuracy loss, making it central to production model compression in NLP and related domains.

papers_seen.author: Allison
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a core strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable ones by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from teacher models to students. The field has diversified from logits-only matching to richer targets (intermediate features, attention maps, relational signals), multiple training regimes (data-free, online, federated, multi-teacher), and task-aware techniques that address capacity mismatch and deployment constraints. KD is widely applicable across modalities (vision, speech, multimodal, graphs, NLP) and is most effective when combined with data- and architecture-aware practices, but practical limits remain around representation alignment, rare-token behavior, privacy, and domain transfer.

papers_seen.author: Galvan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Design-Sensitive Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely applicable approach for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. When implemented thoughtfully—choosing what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, and which data and augmentation strategies to use—KD can recover much of a teacher’s performance while substantially reducing inference cost and memory. However, distillation also has limits: it can propagate teacher biases, struggle with low-data or low-capacity students, and requires complementary techniques (e.g., layer mapping, pruning, or synthetic-data schemes) and careful evaluation to meet real-world deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Context-Sensitive Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and widely applicable method for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search, or data augmentation), and when adapted to task and data constraints, KD enables large reductions in size and latency while retaining much of a teacher's performance. At the same time, KD’s success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how teachers and students are matched, and how to handle domain shift or limited data.

papers_seen.author: Freeman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. When applied thoughtfully — choosing appropriate distillation signals, handling data constraints, and combining KD with complementary techniques — KD can recover most of a teacher's performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy requirements. However, KD is not a panacea: its success depends on student capacity, representation alignment, optimization schedules, and careful mitigation of teacher biases and distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Whitehead
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models to reduce computation, memory, and latency while retaining much of the original performance. KD encompasses a family of techniques — matching soft outputs, aligning intermediate representations, using multi-stage or curriculum schemes, and combining distillation with other compression methods — and is widely used for deploying models in resource-constrained or privacy-sensitive settings. Success depends on matching distillation objectives and data strategies to deployment goals and student capacity.

papers_seen.author: Lawrence
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge From a Deep Pose Regressor Network
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a novel method to distill knowledge from a deep pose regressor network for efficient Visual Odometry (VO). Standard distillation relies on "dark knowledge" for successful knowledge transfer. As this knowledge is not available in pose regression and the teacher prediction is not always accurate, we propose to emphasize the knowledge transfer only when we trust the teacher. We achieve this by using teacher loss as a confidence score which places variable relative importance on the teacher prediction. We inject this confidence score to the main training task via Attentive Imitation Loss (AIL) and when learning the intermediate representation of the teacher through Attentive Hint Training (AHT) approach. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work which successfully distill the knowledge from a deep pose regression network. Our evaluation on the KITTI and Malaga dataset shows that we can keep the student prediction close to the teacher with up to 92.95% parameter reduction and 2.12x faster in computation time.

papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: Private Model Compression via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The soaring demand for intelligent mobile applications calls for deploying powerful deep neural networks (DNNs) on mobile devices. However, the outstanding performance of DNNs notoriously relies on increasingly complex models, which in turn is associated with an increase in computational expense far surpassing mobile devices' capacity. What is worse, app service providers need to collect and utilize a large volume of users' data, which contain sensitive information, to build the sophisticated DNN models. Directly deploying these models on public mobile devices presents prohibitive privacy risk. To benefit from the on-device deep learning without the capacity and privacy concerns, we design a private model compression framework RONA. Following the knowledge distillation paradigm, we jointly use hint learning, distillation learning, and self learning to train a compact and fast neural network. The knowledge distilled from the cumbersome model is adaptively bounded and carefully perturbed to enforce differential privacy. We further propose an elegant query sample selection method to reduce the number of queries and control the privacy loss. A series of empirical evaluations as well as the implementation on an Android mobile device show that RONA can not only compress cumbersome models efficiently but also provide a strong privacy guarantee. For example, on SVHN, when a meaningful $(9.83,10^{-6})$-differential privacy is guaranteed, the compact model trained by RONA can obtain 20$\times$ compression ratio and 19$\times$ speed-up with merely 0.97% accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Hall
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large models by transferring useful information from one or more teacher models to a smaller student model, enabling faster inference, lower memory use, and domain- or deployment-specific adaptation. Research has developed multiple distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational signals), teacher-management strategies (ensembles, multi-teacher weighting, teacher-training), data strategies (data-aware curricula, data-free synthesis), and complementary techniques (projector layers, adversarial objectives, curriculum schedules). Empirical work shows that careful selection of what to transfer and how to align teacher and student—balanced with attention to optimization dynamics and data constraints—produces compact models that preserve much of the teacher’s performance while meeting real-world latency, privacy, and robustness requirements.

papers_seen.author: Garrison
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly adopted approach to compress large neural models into smaller, faster students for deployment in resource- and privacy-constrained settings. A rich set of practical variants has emerged — from matching teacher logits to aligning intermediate representations, multi-teacher and self-distillation schemes, and data-free or synthesized-data approaches — and KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression methods and deployment-aware design. Remaining challenges include optimization mismatch between teacher and student, distribution shift, rare-token or low-frequency behavior degradation, and the potential transfer of teacher biases; addressing these requires task-aware choices about what to transfer, how to build students and teachers, and how to handle limited or private data.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Compressing Visual-linguistic Model via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite exciting progress in pre-training for visual-linguistic (VL) representations, very few aspire to a small VL model. In this paper, we study knowledge distillation (KD) to effectively compress a transformer-based large VL model into a small VL model. The major challenge arises from the inconsistent regional visual tokens extracted from different detectors of Teacher and Student, resulting in the misalignment of hidden representations and attention distributions. To address the problem, we retrain and adapt the Teacher by using the same region proposals from Student's detector while the features are from Teacher's own object detector. With aligned network inputs, the adapted Teacher is capable of transferring the knowledge through the intermediate representations. Specifically, we use the mean square error loss to mimic the attention distribution inside the transformer block and present a token-wise noise contrastive loss to align the hidden state by contrasting with negative representations stored in a sample queue. To this end, we show that our proposed distillation significantly improves the performance of small VL models on image captioning and visual question answering tasks. It reaches 120.8 in CIDEr score on COCO captioning, an improvement of 5.1 over its non-distilled counterpart; and an accuracy of 69.8 on VQA 2.0, a 0.8 gain from the baseline. Our extensive experiments and ablations confirm the effectiveness of VL distillation in both pre-training and fine-tuning stages.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applied strategy to transfer information from large or specialized teacher models into smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained student models. In practice KD has been used to compress pretrained language models, speed up inference in structured models, enable multimodal generation, improve low-precision networks, and scale training across data-parallel workers. Research spans theoretical analyses of why distillation works, empirical studies of failure modes (e.g., propagation of teacher errors), and practical training recipes (including online and self-distillation variants) that balance fidelity to the teacher with student capacity and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information beyond hard labels. Over the past decade this has grown from simple logit-matching into a toolkit that includes internal representation alignment, layer-mapping strategies, data and privacy-aware procedures, adversarial and robustness-aware objectives, online and distributed schemes, and methods tailored for specific architectures such as pre-trained language models. Distillation often recovers much of a teacher’s performance when deliberately designed (choice of signals, data, and architecture), but it faces limits from optimization difficulties, capacity mismatch, distributional shift, and the risk of transferring undesirable teacher behaviors such as bias. Practical success therefore depends on combining multiple transfer signals, handling data constraints, and adapting both teacher and student to the deployment context.

papers_seen.author: Ibarra
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Composable Path for Compressing Deep and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, versatile technique for transferring behavior from large teacher models into smaller student models to reduce latency, memory, and power requirements while retaining much of the teacher's performance. KD works across modalities and tasks, but its practical success depends on choices about what signal to transfer, how to supply or synthesize training data, and how to combine distillation with complementary compression methods. When applied thoughtfully within a wider compression pipeline, KD enables deployable models for resource-constrained and privacy-sensitive settings.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure. Across vision and language tasks KD supports deployment to resource-constrained devices, data-scarce regimes, and domain adaptation. Effective distillation combines teacher-to-student signal design (soft outputs, features, attention or relational cues), data strategies (augmentation, synthetic or online generation), and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture modification). While KD often produces strong size–performance tradeoffs, practical success depends on addressing capacity mismatch, domain shift, and signal selection so the student can absorb the teacher’s knowledge.

papers_seen.author: Charles
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, broadly applicable approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers information from high-capacity teachers to compact students via outputs, intermediate representations, or relational signals, and integrates naturally with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and deployment workflows (on-device inference, federated learning, and data-limited regimes). While KD reliably improves efficiency while preserving much of teacher performance, robust application requires careful choices about what signals to transfer, how to handle imperfect teachers and low-frequency behaviors, and how to combine KD with data strategies and architecture design to meet real-world constraints.

papers_seen.author: Alvarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Challenges, and Trends
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques aim to produce smaller, faster models that retain much of the predictive power of larger teachers. Across modalities (vision, language, speech, graphs, and generation), practitioners balance trade-offs among accuracy, efficiency, data availability, privacy, and fairness. Recent work extends classical logits-based distillation with feature- and layer-level objectives, projector modules, adversarial data generation for data-free settings, multi-teacher and meta-learned teachers, and privacy-aware perturbations. Empirical and theoretical analyses highlight both practical gains and persistent issues—optimization barriers that prevent perfect teacher matching, data-mismatch effects, and modality-specific alignment problems—guiding current best practices for deploying distilled models in resource- and privacy-constrained scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Extract the Knowledge of Graph Neural Networks and Go Beyond it: An Effective Knowledge Distillation Framework
papers_seen.abstract: Semi-supervised learning on graphs is an important problem in the machine learning area. In recent years, state-of-the-art classification methods based on graph neural networks (GNNs) have shown their superiority over traditional ones such as label propagation. However, the sophisticated architectures of these neural models will lead to a complex prediction mechanism, which could not make full use of valuable prior knowledge lying in the data, e.g., structurally correlated nodes tend to have the same class. In this paper, we propose a framework based on knowledge distillation to address the above issues. Our framework extracts the knowledge of an arbitrary learned GNN model (teacher model), and injects it into a well-designed student model. The student model is built with two simple prediction mechanisms, i.e., label propagation and feature transformation, which naturally preserves structure-based and feature-based prior knowledge, respectively. In specific, we design the student model as a trainable combination of parameterized label propagation and feature transformation modules. As a result, the learned student can benefit from both prior knowledge and the knowledge in GNN teachers for more effective predictions. Moreover, the learned student model has a more interpretable prediction process than GNNs. We conduct experiments on five public benchmark datasets and employ seven GNN models including GCN, GAT, APPNP, SAGE, SGC, GCNII and GLP as the teacher models. Experimental results show that the learned student model can consistently outperform its corresponding teacher model by 1.4% - 4.7% on average. Code and data are available at https://github.com/BUPT-GAMMA/CPF

papers_seen.author: Orr
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information beyond hard labels. KD has evolved from simple soft-target matching into a flexible toolkit that includes intermediate-representation alignment, self- and multi-teacher schemes, data-free and online protocols, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Practical application of KD requires matching the distilled signals and workflows to student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints; addressing failure modes such as transferred biases or poor handling of low-frequency phenomena; and integrating distillation into a broader compression pipeline to meet latency, memory, and privacy goals.

papers_seen.author: Koch
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques aim to transfer useful knowledge from larger, expensive models to smaller, more efficient ones so that deployed systems retain high performance under resource constraints. Approaches span logit-level supervision, feature- and layer-level matching, progressive module replacement, and data-augmentation or data-free strategies. Applications include compressing large language models, accelerating inference on edge devices, enabling multi-task and federated learning, and improving robustness or generalization. Practical deployments often combine KD with quantization, architecture design, or task-aware selection of teacher signals to balance fidelity and efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Bowman
papers_seen.title: TRILLsson: Distilled Universal Paralinguistic Speech Representations
papers_seen.abstract: Recent advances in self-supervision have dramatically improved the quality of speech representations. However, deployment of state-of-the-art embedding models on devices has been restricted due to their limited public availability and large resource footprint. Our work addresses these issues by publicly releasing a collection of paralinguistic speech models that are small and near state-of-the-art performance. Our approach is based on knowledge distillation, and our models are distilled on public data only. We explore different architectures and thoroughly evaluate our models on the Non-Semantic Speech (NOSS) benchmark. Our largest distilled model is less than 15% the size of the original model (314MB vs 2.2GB), achieves over 96% the accuracy on 6 of 7 tasks, and is trained on 6.5% the data. The smallest model is 1% in size (22MB) and achieves over 90% the accuracy on 6 of 7 tasks. Our models outperform the open source Wav2Vec 2.0 model on 6 of 7 tasks, and our smallest model outperforms the open source Wav2Vec 2.0 on both emotion recognition tasks despite being 7% the size.

papers_seen.author: Murillo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Pragmatic Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students across modalities and tasks. KD reliably reduces inference cost and memory while preserving much of teacher performance, but it is not a turnkey solution: its success depends on design choices about what to transfer, how to handle data limitations, and how to combine distillation with complementary compression and fairness-preserving techniques. I argue that KD should be treated as a central component of a model-compression pipeline — one that is combined with architecture-aware methods, data and curriculum strategies, and explicit checks for robustness, privacy, and bias — to achieve deployable, efficient, and responsible models in practice.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, widely applicable strategy for producing compact, deployable models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. KD works across modalities and deployment constraints, and supports extensions for data-free, federated, and privacy-sensitive settings. However, realizing KD’s full potential requires careful choices about what signals to transfer (logits, features, relational signals), how to align teacher and student architectures, and how to mitigate transferred harms such as bias or degraded rare-token behavior. When combined with complementary methods (augmentation, layer-aware mapping, multi-teacher ensembles, or differential-privacy mechanisms), KD becomes a flexible core of effective compression pipelines for real-world NLP and deep-learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Practical Recommendations for NLP and Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely applicable approach to compress large deep models into smaller, deployable ones. Across language models, speech encoders, and vision systems, distillation reduces model size and inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance. However, success is not automatic: distillation interacts with dataset availability, model heterogeneity, optimization dynamics, robustness, and fairness. Careful choices of what to transfer (logits, features, layer-wise representations), how to handle missing data, and how to address heterogeneous or privacy-sensitive settings are essential for reliable compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Rhodes
papers_seen.title: Why Knowledge Distillation Is Central to Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic and versatile route to compressing large models into smaller, deployable ones while preserving much of their performance. Across domains and deployment constraints—multi-task learning, low-resource devices, federated settings, data-free scenarios, and generative or detection tasks—KD enables targeted transfer of behavior, representations, and robustness. However, realizing KD's potential requires task-aware choices: which teacher(s) to use, what intermediate signals to mimic, how to select or synthesize training samples, and whether to incorporate adversarial or ensemble strategies. When combined with appropriate pre-training, selective sample strategies, and representation-level objectives, KD produces compact models that are accurate, efficient, and more widely deployable than large models alone.

papers_seen.author: Gaines
papers_seen.title: AdaBERT: Task-Adaptive BERT Compression with Differentiable Neural Architecture Search
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained language models such as BERT have shown their effectiveness in various natural language processing tasks. However, the huge parameter size makes them difficult to be deployed in real-time applications that require quick inference with limited resources. Existing methods compress BERT into small models while such compression is task-independent, i.e., the same compressed BERT for all different downstream tasks. Motivated by the necessity and benefits of task-oriented BERT compression, we propose a novel compression method, AdaBERT, that leverages differentiable Neural Architecture Search to automatically compress BERT into task-adaptive small models for specific tasks. We incorporate a task-oriented knowledge distillation loss to provide search hints and an efficiency-aware loss as search constraints, which enables a good trade-off between efficiency and effectiveness for task-adaptive BERT compression. We evaluate AdaBERT on several NLP tasks, and the results demonstrate that those task-adaptive compressed models are 12.7x to 29.3x faster than BERT in inference time and 11.5x to 17.0x smaller in terms of parameter size, while comparable performance is maintained.

papers_seen.author: Burton
papers_seen.title: Efficient Transformer-based Large Scale Language Representations using Hardware-friendly Block Structured Pruning
papers_seen.abstract: Pre-trained large-scale language models have increasingly demonstrated high accuracy on many natural language processing (NLP) tasks. However, the limited weight storage and computational speed on hardware platforms have impeded the popularity of pre-trained models, especially in the era of edge computing. In this work, we propose an efficient transformer-based large-scale language representation using hardware-friendly block structure pruning. We incorporate the reweighted group Lasso into block-structured pruning for optimization. Besides the significantly reduced weight storage and computation, the proposed approach achieves high compression rates. Experimental results on different models (BERT, RoBERTa, and DistilBERT) on the General Language Understanding Evaluation (GLUE) benchmark tasks show that we achieve up to 5.0x with zero or minor accuracy degradation on certain task(s). Our proposed method is also orthogonal to existing compact pre-trained language models such as DistilBERT using knowledge distillation, since a further 1.79x average compression rate can be achieved on top of DistilBERT with zero or minor accuracy degradation. It is suitable to deploy the final compressed model on resource-constrained edge devices.

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP — Promise, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from larger teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. When paired with representation-level objectives, data strategies (including synthetic or privacy-preserving generation), and architecture-aware design, KD routinely yields models that meet latency, memory, and deployment constraints while retaining much of teacher performance. Success is engineering-dependent: the distillation signal, student capacity and pre-training, data availability, and explicit mitigation for harms such as bias or distributional fragility determine whether compressed models meet real-world needs.
