papers_seen.author: Duncan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practically essential approach for compressing large neural models so they can be deployed under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. By transferring learned behavior from teachers to students, KD enables many deployment trade-offs while remaining compatible with complementary techniques (e.g., quantization, pruning, architecture search). However, to be robust and broadly useful in real systems, distillation must go beyond naive soft-label matching: effective pipelines combine logits with internal representation transfer, task- and layer-aware selection of signals, appropriate data strategies, and attention to distributional heterogeneity and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Mitchell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Practical Tool for Compressing and Adapting Deep and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated technique for producing compact models that retain much of the performance and useful behavior of larger teachers. When integrated with complementary methods — such as progressive module replacement, data-free synthesis, adversarially-aware training, and task- or domain-aware curricula — KD supports deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints and enables domain adaptation and robustness improvements. However, KD is not a panacea: its success depends on teacher quality, the choice of distillation signal, data strategies, and careful pipeline design to preserve robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Cook
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Benefits, Limits, and Engineering Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile foundation for compressing deep and language models: it enables much smaller, faster students to capture substantial teacher performance while supporting deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD excels when combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and careful engineering (choice of transferred signals, data augmentation, teacher selection). However, KD is not a plug-and-play solution: it can propagate teacher imperfections, struggle with rare-token or low-frequency behaviors, and face difficulties under heterogeneous or privacy-constrained data regimes. Treating KD as the central tool in a compression pipeline — but one that requires task-aware design and diagnostics — yields the best practical outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Calderon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained deep models deliver strong performance across vision and language tasks but are often too large or slow for real-world deployment. Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression strategies provide practical ways to transfer behavior from high-capacity teacher models to smaller students, enabling reduced storage, faster inference, and deployment on constrained devices. Research has developed a range of KD formulations—logit-level supervision, intermediate representation matching, layer mapping, multi-teacher fusion, and data-free distillation—alongside empirical and theoretical analyses that explain when and why distillation helps. The literature also shows KD’s effectiveness in NLP for compressing models like BERT into lightweight architectures without additional data, and highlights open challenges such as heterogeneous teachers, data privacy, and preserving task-specific inductive biases.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers behavior from large teacher models into smaller student models to reduce latency, memory, and computation while retaining much of the teacher's performance. Across vision, language, and graph domains, KD has been applied as logit matching, intermediate-feature alignment, adversarial transfer, and data- or task-aware synthesis. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD often acts both as a source of extra task signal and as a regularizer; practical systems combine KD with pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation, and data strategies to meet deployment constraints. Important open issues include data heterogeneity, teacher–student capacity mismatch, privacy-preserving releases, and closing remaining gaps in robustness and domain generalization.

papers_seen.author: Daniel
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models to reduce compute, memory, and latency while preserving task performance. Across vision, speech, and language tasks, KD has been adapted into many forms—soft-target matching, intermediate representation alignment, attention and relational transfers, multi-teacher ensembles, online distillation, and task-adaptive pipelines—and combined with orthogonal compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to enable deployment in resource-constrained or privacy-sensitive settings. Empirical work shows KD often recovers most of a teacher's utility in a much smaller footprint, but success depends on teacher quality, the choice of distilled signals, data availability and domain shift, and robustness and privacy constraints. The field continues to refine objectives, layer-mapping strategies, and workflows that make distillation effective across modalities and large pretrained models in practical deployments.

papers_seen.author: Hickman
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques aim to transfer the predictive power of large, expensive models into smaller, faster models while retaining performance. Approaches vary from matching teacher outputs (soft labels) to aligning intermediate representations, leveraging data augmentation or synthesized data when real data are limited, and jointly optimizing architecture and distillation losses for task-adaptive compression. Advances address student–teacher capacity gaps, multi-teacher transfer, and domain or data scarcity; remaining challenges include transferring internal structure efficiently, generalization under distribution shifts, and designing teacher models that are optimized for downstream distillation.

papers_seen.author: Rios
papers_seen.title: Improving Neural Topic Models using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Topic models are often used to identify human-interpretable topics to help make sense of large document collections. We use knowledge distillation to combine the best attributes of probabilistic topic models and pretrained transformers. Our modular method can be straightforwardly applied with any neural topic model to improve topic quality, which we demonstrate using two models having disparate architectures, obtaining state-of-the-art topic coherence. We show that our adaptable framework not only improves performance in the aggregate over all estimated topics, as is commonly reported, but also in head-to-head comparisons of aligned topics.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: What is known about Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques provide practical ways to transfer predictive capacity from larger teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained student models. The field encompasses simple soft-target matching as well as richer forms of transfer such as intermediate representation alignment, attention- or feature-level matching, multi-stage and multi-teacher pipelines, self-distillation, and data- or privacy-aware variants. Empirical work shows distilled students can approach teacher performance while offering large gains in latency, memory, and deployability; theoretical and empirical analyses emphasize mechanisms including soft-target regularization, representational alignment, and optimization dynamics. Practical success depends on careful choices of what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, how to use data (including synthetic or public data), and how to address robustness, fairness, and distributional shifts.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Practical Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable ones. When paired with task-aware objectives, data strategies (including data-free synthesis), and complementary compression techniques, KD can preserve much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Effective use of KD requires deliberate choices about what to transfer, which data to use or synthesize, and how to align teacher and student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Mcmillan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression for NLP: Strengths, Limits, and a Recipe for Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is the most practical and widely adopted strategy for compressing large NLP models into smaller, deployable students. When applied thoughtfully—matching soft outputs, aligning intermediate representations, using task-aware layer mapping, and addressing data or privacy constraints—KD recovers most of a teacher’s performance while enabling large reductions in storage, latency, and power. However, effective deployment requires recognizing and mitigating limits such as capacity mismatch, distributional heterogeneity, and the risk of transferring teacher biases.

papers_seen.author: Diaz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, broadly applicable approach to compressing large models for deployment in resource-constrained settings. KD enables model-size and compute reductions while preserving task performance, and it integrates naturally with other compression techniques, privacy-preserving releases, federated and heterogeneous-device training, and domain/continual adaptation. However, its success depends on careful choices: how teacher signals are generated and weighted, which data (or synthetic/meta-data) drive distillation, and how KD interacts with data heterogeneity and fairness constraints. When combined with complementary methods (pruning, architecture search, data augmentation, selective sample weighting), KD yields efficient models that retain much of the teacher’s capabilities across vision, generative, and language tasks.

papers_seen.author: Mueller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a central, pragmatic approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD delivers strong empirical gains across domains by transferring soft outputs, intermediate representations, or task-specific behaviors from teachers to students. Its strengths are practical: it supports deployment on constrained hardware, enables multi-teacher and cross-model transfer, and integrates with other compression tools. At the same time, KD is not a plug-and-play solution: theoretical and empirical work shows limits under data heterogeneity, imperfect teachers, and mismatched architectures, so KD must be applied with task-aware choices (signal type, layer alignment, teacher selection, and curricula) and often combined with complementary methods to realize reliable, high-fidelity compression.

papers_seen.author: Pena
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, production-oriented paradigm for turning large, high-performing models into smaller, faster students suitable for deployment. Beyond pure compression, KD can act as a regularizer and a mechanism for transferring internal representations, enabling trade-offs among accuracy, latency, privacy, and robustness. Effective KD pipelines combine multiple signals (soft targets, intermediate features, attention maps), data strategies (including data-free synthesis), and deployment-aware techniques (privacy-preserving queries, architecture adaptation). I argue that KD should be treated as the central, organizing method in any practical compression workflow, but that realizing its benefits requires task-aware choices about what to transfer and how to mitigate known failure modes such as teacher–student mismatch and degraded modeling of rare phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Hahn
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression strategies are widely used to produce smaller, faster models by transferring knowledge from larger or ensemble teachers to compact students. These techniques span supervised distillation, self-distillation, data-free and adversarial approaches, layer- and task-aware mappings, and distributed/online schemes. Empirical work shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance across modalities (classification, detection, generation, and language tasks) while enabling practical deployment; theoretical and practical challenges remain around data dependence, teacher imperfection, robustness, and optimal student–teacher alignment.

papers_seen.author: Adkins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, broadly applicable strategy for shrinking large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students. KD can reproduce much of a teacher's task performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints; it also integrates naturally with complementary techniques (pretraining, data augmentation, multi-teacher supervision, and progressive module replacement). Realizing KD's full value in production requires attention to optimization gaps, dataset mismatch, and the risk of propagating teacher biases, and benefits from targeted extensions—feature-level objectives, adversarially-informed sample selection, and staged or progressive compression strategies.

papers_seen.author: Joyce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers behavior from large teacher models into smaller students to reduce inference cost while retaining much of the teacher's capability. KD is flexible: it can match logits, intermediate representations, attention maps, or relational signals; it can be combined with augmentation, architecture search, pruning, or task adaptation; and it can operate with or without original training data. When applied with careful choices about what to transfer, how to align representations, and how to address data or optimization mismatches, KD enables practical deployment of compact models across vision, language, and multimodal tasks. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a central component of any compression strategy and summarizes concrete practices to maximize its effectiveness and mitigate known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Caldwell
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer information from larger, expensive teacher models to smaller, deployable students to reduce inference cost while preserving much of the teacher’s behavior. Across modalities and tasks, KD methods vary by the form of transferred signal (soft targets, intermediate features, attention maps, or module behaviors), training setting (offline, online, federated, or data-free), and complementary techniques (architecture design, pruning, quantization, and data augmentation). Practical success depends on aligning teacher and student inputs/representations, selecting appropriate distillation objectives for the task and data regime, and mitigating distributional or token-frequency artifacts introduced during distillation. This synthesis summarizes major approaches, empirical findings, limitations, and practical strategies for applying KD in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Distilling portable Generative Adversarial Networks for Image Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been widely used in various image-to-image translation tasks, they can be hardly applied on mobile devices due to their heavy computation and storage cost. Traditional network compression methods focus on visually recognition tasks, but never deal with generation tasks. Inspired by knowledge distillation, a student generator of fewer parameters is trained by inheriting the low-level and high-level information from the original heavy teacher generator. To promote the capability of student generator, we include a student discriminator to measure the distances between real images, and images generated by student and teacher generators. An adversarial learning process is therefore established to optimize student generator and student discriminator. Qualitative and quantitative analysis by conducting experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method can learn portable generative models with strong performance.

papers_seen.author: Valdez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Pragmatic Tool for Compressing Deep and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is not merely one technique among many for model compression: when applied thoughtfully it is a central, practical lever for producing small, fast models that retain much of the performance, robustness, and task-specific behavior of large teachers. Best practice couples KD with representation-level supervision, teacher-student co-design, data and privacy strategies, and complementary compression methods so that compact models meet real-world latency, memory and heterogeneity constraints.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: A Closer Look at Deep Learning Heuristics: Learning rate restarts, Warmup and Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The convergence rate and final performance of common deep learning models have significantly benefited from heuristics such as learning rate schedules, knowledge distillation, skip connections, and normalization layers. In the absence of theoretical underpinnings, controlled experiments aimed at explaining these strategies can aid our understanding of deep learning landscapes and the training dynamics. Existing approaches for empirical analysis rely on tools of linear interpolation and visualizations with dimensionality reduction, each with their limitations. Instead, we revisit such analysis of heuristics through the lens of recently proposed methods for loss surface and representation analysis, viz., mode connectivity and canonical correlation analysis (CCA), and hypothesize reasons for the success of the heuristics. In particular, we explore knowledge distillation and learning rate heuristics of (cosine) restarts and warmup using mode connectivity and CCA. Our empirical analysis suggests that: (a) the reasons often quoted for the success of cosine annealing are not evidenced in practice; (b) that the effect of learning rate warmup is to prevent the deeper layers from creating training instability; and (c) that the latent knowledge shared by the teacher is primarily disbursed to the deeper layers.

papers_seen.author: Murillo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Pragmatic Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students across modalities and tasks. KD reliably reduces inference cost and memory while preserving much of teacher performance, but it is not a turnkey solution: its success depends on design choices about what to transfer, how to handle data limitations, and how to combine distillation with complementary compression and fairness-preserving techniques. I argue that KD should be treated as a central component of a model-compression pipeline — one that is combined with architecture-aware methods, data and curriculum strategies, and explicit checks for robustness, privacy, and bias — to achieve deployable, efficient, and responsible models in practice.

papers_seen.author: May
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a suite of methods for transferring information from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller student models so they can be deployed under compute, memory, and privacy constraints. KD encompasses matching teacher outputs, aligning intermediate representations, online and multi-teacher workflows, and data-aware or data-free strategies. Empirically KD often yields compact students that approach teacher performance and can improve generalization, but practical success hinges on teacher-student alignment, data strategy, and addressing robustness and distribution-shift issues. Open directions include distillation without original data, preserving fine-grained sequence behavior, and adapting KD to heterogeneous or privacy-sensitive settings.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Show, Attend and Distill:Knowledge Distillation via Attention-based Feature Matching
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation extracts general knowledge from a pre-trained teacher network and provides guidance to a target student network. Most studies manually tie intermediate features of the teacher and student, and transfer knowledge through pre-defined links. However, manual selection often constructs ineffective links that limit the improvement from the distillation. There has been an attempt to address the problem, but it is still challenging to identify effective links under practical scenarios. In this paper, we introduce an effective and efficient feature distillation method utilizing all the feature levels of the teacher without manually selecting the links. Specifically, our method utilizes an attention-based meta-network that learns relative similarities between features, and applies identified similarities to control distillation intensities of all possible pairs. As a result, our method determines competent links more efficiently than the previous approach and provides better performance on model compression and transfer learning tasks. Further qualitative analyses and ablative studies describe how our method contributes to better distillation. The implementation code is available at github.com/clovaai/attention-feature-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Trade-offs, and Practical Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) trains compact student models by transferring information from larger teacher models, enabling deployment under computation, memory, or latency constraints. Across vision, speech, language, and recommendation systems, KD takes many forms — logit matching, feature mimicking, ensemble compression, and data-free synthesis — and is often combined with model pruning, architectural simplification, or curriculum strategies. Effective distillation requires choices about what to transfer (soft targets vs. intermediate features), how to supply or synthesize data, and how to schedule or regularize training; these choices shape outcomes in accuracy, robustness, interpretability, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Explaining Knowledge Distillation by Quantifying the Knowledge
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a method to interpret the success of knowledge distillation by quantifying and analyzing task-relevant and task-irrelevant visual concepts that are encoded in intermediate layers of a deep neural network (DNN). More specifically, three hypotheses are proposed as follows. 1. Knowledge distillation makes the DNN learn more visual concepts than learning from raw data. 2. Knowledge distillation ensures that the DNN is prone to learning various visual concepts simultaneously. Whereas, in the scenario of learning from raw data, the DNN learns visual concepts sequentially. 3. Knowledge distillation yields more stable optimization directions than learning from raw data. Accordingly, we design three types of mathematical metrics to evaluate feature representations of the DNN. In experiments, we diagnosed various DNNs, and above hypotheses were verified.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: AutoGAN-Distiller: Searching to Compress Generative Adversarial Networks
papers_seen.abstract: The compression of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) has lately drawn attention, due to the increasing demand for deploying GANs into mobile devices for numerous applications such as image translation, enhancement and editing. However, compared to the substantial efforts to compressing other deep models, the research on compressing GANs (usually the generators) remains at its infancy stage. Existing GAN compression algorithms are limited to handling specific GAN architectures and losses. Inspired by the recent success of AutoML in deep compression, we introduce AutoML to GAN compression and develop an AutoGAN-Distiller (AGD) framework. Starting with a specifically designed efficient search space, AGD performs an end-to-end discovery for new efficient generators, given the target computational resource constraints. The search is guided by the original GAN model via knowledge distillation, therefore fulfilling the compression. AGD is fully automatic, standalone (i.e., needing no trained discriminators), and generically applicable to various GAN models. We evaluate AGD in two representative GAN tasks: image translation and super resolution. Without bells and whistles, AGD yields remarkably lightweight yet more competitive compressed models, that largely outperform existing alternatives. Our codes and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/TAMU-VITA/AGD.

papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: Ensemble Knowledge Distillation for CTR Prediction
papers_seen.abstract: Recently, deep learning-based models have been widely studied for click-through rate (CTR) prediction and lead to improved prediction accuracy in many industrial applications. However, current research focuses primarily on building complex network architectures to better capture sophisticated feature interactions and dynamic user behaviors. The increased model complexity may slow down online inference and hinder its adoption in real-time applications. Instead, our work targets at a new model training strategy based on knowledge distillation (KD). KD is a teacher-student learning framework to transfer knowledge learned from a teacher model to a student model. The KD strategy not only allows us to simplify the student model as a vanilla DNN model but also achieves significant accuracy improvements over the state-of-the-art teacher models. The benefits thus motivate us to further explore the use of a powerful ensemble of teachers for more accurate student model training. We also propose some novel techniques to facilitate ensembled CTR prediction, including teacher gating and early stopping by distillation loss. We conduct comprehensive experiments against 12 existing models and across three industrial datasets. Both offline and online A/B testing results show the effectiveness of our KD-based training strategy.

papers_seen.author: Bush
papers_seen.title: Practical and Principled Knowledge Distillation for NLP: Task-aware, Teacher-aware, and System-level Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical pillar for compressing large deep and language models into deployable, efficient students. When applied thoughtfully—aligning distilled information to the downstream task, designing or adapting teachers with student constraints in mind, and combining KD with complementary compression techniques—KD can recover much of the teacher's capability while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is not a panacea: optimization difficulties, dataset mismatch, and distributional issues can limit gains unless addressed explicitly. A principled KD pipeline therefore includes task-aware selection of distilled signals, teacher-student co-design, and system-level techniques (pruning/quantization or data-free synthesis) to achieve robust, efficient models for production NLP settings.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Context-Sensitive Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and widely applicable method for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search, or data augmentation), and when adapted to task and data constraints, KD enables large reductions in size and latency while retaining much of a teacher's performance. At the same time, KD’s success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how teachers and students are matched, and how to handle domain shift or limited data.

papers_seen.author: Hahn
papers_seen.title: PKD: General Distillation Framework for Object Detectors via Pearson Correlation Coefficient
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation(KD) is a widely-used technique to train compact models in object detection. However, there is still a lack of study on how to distill between heterogeneous detectors. In this paper, we empirically find that better FPN features from a heterogeneous teacher detector can help the student although their detection heads and label assignments are different. However, directly aligning the feature maps to distill detectors suffers from two problems. First, the difference in feature magnitude between the teacher and the student could enforce overly strict constraints on the student. Second, the FPN stages and channels with large feature magnitude from the teacher model could dominate the gradient of distillation loss, which will overwhelm the effects of other features in KD and introduce much noise. To address the above issues, we propose to imitate features with Pearson Correlation Coefficient to focus on the relational information from the teacher and relax constraints on the magnitude of the features. Our method consistently outperforms the existing detection KD methods and works for both homogeneous and heterogeneous student-teacher pairs. Furthermore, it converges faster. With a powerful MaskRCNN-Swin detector as the teacher, ResNet-50 based RetinaNet and FCOS achieve 41.5% and 43.9% mAP on COCO2017, which are 4.1\% and 4.8\% higher than the baseline, respectively.

papers_seen.author: Riley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is not merely a model-compression trick but a central, practical paradigm for deploying high-performance deep and NLP models under real-world constraints. KD can compress large pre-trained models into lightweight students, transfer inductive biases, improve robustness and generalization, enable low-precision and privacy-aware deployments, and adapt to data- or compute-limited settings. Effective distillation couples soft-label transfer with representation-level alignment, task-aware architecture choices, and complementary techniques (quantization, pruning, augmentation). However, KD must be applied carefully: teacher–student mismatches, bias transfer, domain shift, and limited-data regimes require method choices such as feature mimicking, teacher ensembles, teacher-free objectives, or fairness-aware augmentations. The result is a flexible toolkit that—when combined with architectural and data strategies—makes high-quality, efficient models feasible for production NLP and deep-learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical, Careful, and Multifaceted Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, widely applicable approach to compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. When applied thoughtfully, KD enables deployment under resource, latency, and privacy constraints; supports domain adaptation and vocabulary specialization; and can be combined with other compression techniques. However, its success depends on careful choices about what to transfer (logits vs. features), how to align layers and representations, how to generate or augment data for distillation, and how to mitigate propagated errors or biases from teachers.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Learning Compact Metrics for MT
papers_seen.abstract: Recent developments in machine translation and multilingual text generation have led researchers to adopt trained metrics such as COMET or BLEURT, which treat evaluation as a regression problem and use representations from multilingual pre-trained models such as XLM-RoBERTa or mBERT. Yet studies on related tasks suggest that these models are most efficient when they are large, which is costly and impractical for evaluation. We investigate the trade-off between multilinguality and model capacity with RemBERT, a state-of-the-art multilingual language model, using data from the WMT Metrics Shared Task. We present a series of experiments which show that model size is indeed a bottleneck for cross-lingual transfer, then demonstrate how distillation can help addressing this bottleneck, by leveraging synthetic data generation and transferring knowledge from one teacher to multiple students trained on related languages. Our method yields up to 10.5% improvement over vanilla fine-tuning and reaches 92.6% of RemBERT's performance using only a third of its parameters.

papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: A Practical, Multifaceted Position on Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a central, practical tool for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a multifaceted framework—combining soft-label supervision, intermediate representation matching, data- and task-aware training, and architecture-aware design—distillation reliably yields compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints. However, distillation must be applied carefully: teacher imperfections, low-frequency token behavior, data scarcity, and domain shifts can undermine student quality unless addressed via targeted strategies such as exposing raw data, tailoring teacher signals, and integrating complementary compression methods. With careful engineering and principled choices about what and how to transfer, distillation enables high-performing, efficient models across vision and language tasks.

papers_seen.author: Rios
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques transform large, high-performing models into smaller or more usable forms while attempting to retain performance. Methods range from transferring soft targets to matching intermediate representations, to data-free and federated protocols that address privacy and communication constraints. These approaches have been applied across computer vision, speech, and natural language tasks and are used both for deployment efficiency and for secondary goals such as interpretability or domain generalization.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques have matured into a diverse set of approaches that trade off capacity, latency, and privacy to deploy high-performing deep models in constrained settings. Methods operate at different places in the training pipeline: compressing via soft-targets, transferring intermediate representations, searching or adapting compact architectures, or avoiding access to original data. Work across modalities (vision, language, graphs, generative models, and medical imaging) shows that careful choice of what to transfer (logits, relations, feature directions, layer mappings) and how to transfer it (attention, contrastive alignment, adversarial generators, or task-aware filters) determines final student performance. Practical concerns such as domain adaptation, federated and heterogeneous-device settings, and data augmentation interact strongly with distillation design choices. The literature suggests a clear pattern: representation-level and layer-aware transfers often outperform naive logits-only approaches for structured or pre-trained models, while teacher-free, data-free, and communication-efficient variants enable distillation under realistic deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: Private Model Compression via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The soaring demand for intelligent mobile applications calls for deploying powerful deep neural networks (DNNs) on mobile devices. However, the outstanding performance of DNNs notoriously relies on increasingly complex models, which in turn is associated with an increase in computational expense far surpassing mobile devices' capacity. What is worse, app service providers need to collect and utilize a large volume of users' data, which contain sensitive information, to build the sophisticated DNN models. Directly deploying these models on public mobile devices presents prohibitive privacy risk. To benefit from the on-device deep learning without the capacity and privacy concerns, we design a private model compression framework RONA. Following the knowledge distillation paradigm, we jointly use hint learning, distillation learning, and self learning to train a compact and fast neural network. The knowledge distilled from the cumbersome model is adaptively bounded and carefully perturbed to enforce differential privacy. We further propose an elegant query sample selection method to reduce the number of queries and control the privacy loss. A series of empirical evaluations as well as the implementation on an Android mobile device show that RONA can not only compress cumbersome models efficiently but also provide a strong privacy guarantee. For example, on SVHN, when a meaningful $(9.83,10^{-6})$-differential privacy is guaranteed, the compact model trained by RONA can obtain 20$\times$ compression ratio and 19$\times$ speed-up with merely 0.97% accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Figueroa
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly adopted family of techniques for compressing high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, or inductive biases. Across vision, language, and multimodal tasks, KD methods aim to preserve teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and compute. Practical pipelines combine distillation with architecture adaptations, data strategies, and complementary compression (pruning, quantization) and must address failure modes related to data mismatch, rare-token fidelity, teacher–student capacity gaps, and privacy or domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Larson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer information from larger teacher models to smaller students to reduce inference cost, memory, and latency while preserving performance. Methods extend beyond matching soft output logits to include intermediate feature/representation matching, layer-wise alignment, adversarial or curriculum-driven sample selection, and data-free or privacy-aware synthesis. Distillation is widely applicable across modalities (vision, speech, language, multimodal) and use cases (on-device deployment, federated learning, low-precision inference), but success depends on careful choices about which signals to transfer, how to handle data availability or heterogeneity, and how to align teacher and student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Harrell
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques have become central tools to deploy high-capacity deep models in latency-, memory-, privacy-, and compute-constrained settings. Across vision, language, graph, and multimodal domains, practitioners use teacher-student training, feature-level transfer, data-free distillation, and hybrid pipelines that combine pruning or architecture search with distillation. Work in this area balances fidelity to teacher models, robustness, and efficiency, and explores trade-offs such as reliance on original training data, communication overhead in federated settings, and the benefits of designing students or student-friendly teachers. The literature shows repeated success of KD when tailored to the task and constraints, while also revealing limitations under severe data heterogeneity or adversarial settings.

papers_seen.author: Bush
papers_seen.title: Multi-Label Image Classification via Knowledge Distillation from Weakly-Supervised Detection
papers_seen.abstract: Multi-label image classification is a fundamental but challenging task towards general visual understanding. Existing methods found the region-level cues (e.g., features from RoIs) can facilitate multi-label classification. Nevertheless, such methods usually require laborious object-level annotations (i.e., object labels and bounding boxes) for effective learning of the object-level visual features. In this paper, we propose a novel and efficient deep framework to boost multi-label classification by distilling knowledge from weakly-supervised detection task without bounding box annotations. Specifically, given the image-level annotations, (1) we first develop a weakly-supervised detection (WSD) model, and then (2) construct an end-to-end multi-label image classification framework augmented by a knowledge distillation module that guides the classification model by the WSD model according to the class-level predictions for the whole image and the object-level visual features for object RoIs. The WSD model is the teacher model and the classification model is the student model. After this cross-task knowledge distillation, the performance of the classification model is significantly improved and the efficiency is maintained since the WSD model can be safely discarded in the test phase. Extensive experiments on two large-scale datasets (MS-COCO and NUS-WIDE) show that our framework achieves superior performances over the state-of-the-art methods on both performance and efficiency.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically proven toolkit for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students across vision and NLP. KD preserves much of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and communication costs, and it integrates naturally with feature-level matching, data-free synthesis, online and federated protocols, and teacher-design strategies. However, its effectiveness depends on what is distilled (logits, features, attention), data availability and domain match, teacher–student capacity alignment, and objectives like robustness, privacy, and fairness. Real-world deployment requires matching distillation techniques to constraints and explicitly addressing robustness, bias, and data-privacy tradeoffs.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Reframing Knowledge Distillation: Beyond Strong Teachers to Regularization, Representations, and Practical Variants
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful tool for compressing deep models, but its benefits arise from multiple mechanisms beyond mere imitation of a stronger teacher. Empirical and theoretical work indicates that distillation combines regularization effects of soft targets, representational alignment, and optimization dynamics; these insights motivate a broader set of practical strategies (teacher-free or data-free distillation, feature-based objectives, contrastive and adversarial losses, ensembles, and co-training of teacher/student) to obtain compact models that generalize well. This paper argues that practitioners should select KD variants depending on data availability, deployment constraints, and the nature of the task, and that future research should prioritize understanding optimization and representation transfer rather than treating teacher capacity as the sole determinant of success.

papers_seen.author: Lawrence
papers_seen.title: Practical Benefits and Cautions of Knowledge Distillation for NLP Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach to compressing large deep and language models into smaller, faster models suitable for deployment. When applied thoughtfully—using techniques such as data augmentation, multi-teacher training, teacher optimization, or data-free procedures—KD can preserve much of the teacher's utility while reducing inference cost and memory. However, distillation can transfer or amplify undesirable properties of teachers (e.g., biases), and its success depends on choices like which teacher knowledge to transfer and which training samples to use. I argue KD is a powerful tool for NLP model compression but must be combined with targeted strategies for robustness, fairness, privacy, and sample selection to realize its full benefits in practice.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Imperative for Deploying Large NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained models have driven major NLP advances but are often impractical for real-world deployment because of size, latency, privacy, and data-distribution constraints. Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression strategies enable retaining most of a large model's performance while producing models that meet latency, memory, and regulatory requirements. Effective KD encompasses diverse techniques — task-adaptive compression, feature mimicking, data-free distillation, teacher meta-learning, privacy-aware distillation, and distributed/continual distillation — which together form a practical toolkit for making state-of-the-art NLP useful at scale.

papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Trade-offs, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or ensemble knowledge. The approach spans simple logit/soft-label matching to feature- and layer-level objectives, multi-teacher pipelines, teacher-free variants, and combinations with architecture search, pruning and data-synthesis. Empirical and theoretical work shows distillation yields substantial efficiency gains with careful design, but also exposes limits from optimization, data heterogeneity, and capacity mismatch. Practical deployment therefore balances what to transfer, how to adapt the student architecture, and whether data or privacy constraints require specialized protocols.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible paradigm for producing compact models that meet real-world constraints while preserving much of the performance of large teachers. When properly designed, KD extends beyond matching soft labels to include feature- and layer-level transfers, pre-training of small architectures, multi-stage curricula, and coordination with architecture search and other compression techniques. Careful attention to data, teacher–student capacity, and deployment objectives turns KD from a heuristic into a reliable engineering approach for compressing deep and NLP models.

papers_seen.author: Bright
papers_seen.title: Towards Practical Lipreading with Distilled and Efficient Models
papers_seen.abstract: Lipreading has witnessed a lot of progress due to the resurgence of neural networks. Recent works have placed emphasis on aspects such as improving performance by finding the optimal architecture or improving generalization. However, there is still a significant gap between the current methodologies and the requirements for an effective deployment of lipreading in practical scenarios. In this work, we propose a series of innovations that significantly bridge that gap: first, we raise the state-of-the-art performance by a wide margin on LRW and LRW-1000 to 88.5% and 46.6%, respectively using self-distillation. Secondly, we propose a series of architectural changes, including a novel Depthwise Separable Temporal Convolutional Network (DS-TCN) head, that slashes the computational cost to a fraction of the (already quite efficient) original model. Thirdly, we show that knowledge distillation is a very effective tool for recovering performance of the lightweight models. This results in a range of models with different accuracy-efficiency trade-offs. However, our most promising lightweight models are on par with the current state-of-the-art while showing a reduction of 8.2x and 3.9x in terms of computational cost and number of parameters, respectively, which we hope will enable the deployment of lipreading models in practical applications.

papers_seen.author: Valencia
papers_seen.title: Practical and Robust Knowledge Distillation for Deployable Deep Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a central tool for compressing large deep models so they can be deployed under latency, memory, and power constraints. Beyond matching teacher output probabilities, modern distillation should transfer internal structure, be tailored to domain and modality differences, and integrate with quantization, privacy, and data-limited settings. When applied with methods that address representation mismatch, optimization challenges, and curriculum of supervisory signals, distillation enables small models that approach teacher performance while meeting real-world deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Arroyo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Scenarios, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques reduce the computational and storage footprint of large neural networks by transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller students. Approaches span matching outputs (soft labels), transferring intermediate representations (feature or layer-wise distillation), adapting teacher selection and weighting, and operating under constraints such as missing original data, privacy, or multi-modal inputs. Practical work on language models, vision-language systems, and other domains highlights gains from task-aware selection of distilled information, architectural adapters between teacher and student, and advanced training schemes (e.g., adversarial sample generation, meta-learning of teachers). Empirical results and surveys show KD is versatile: it improves student accuracy over training from scratch, enables deployment in resource-constrained settings, and can be extended to preserve privacy and support domain adaptation, while theoretical and empirical analyses clarify when and why distillation helps and what challenges remain.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Understanding BERT Rankers Under Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep language models such as BERT pre-trained on large corpus have given a huge performance boost to the state-of-the-art information retrieval ranking systems. Knowledge embedded in such models allows them to pick up complex matching signals between passages and queries. However, the high computation cost during inference limits their deployment in real-world search scenarios. In this paper, we study if and how the knowledge for search within BERT can be transferred to a smaller ranker through distillation. Our experiments demonstrate that it is crucial to use a proper distillation procedure, which produces up to nine times speedup while preserving the state-of-the-art performance.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high‑capacity models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, or structural inductive biases from teachers. A spectrum of methods—logit/soft‑label matching, feature- and layer-wise imitation, attention and relation transfer, ensemble-to-singleton distillation, self-distillation, and data‑free synthesis—has been developed to meet deployment goals such as latency reduction, privacy, domain adaptation, and robustness. Empirical and applied work in NLP, vision, speech, and graph domains shows that carefully chosen distilled signals, teacher designs, and training protocols allow compact models to approach teacher performance, though challenges remain around domain shift, low-frequency phenomena, and preserving fairness and privacy in compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Variants, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses or transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller students by providing richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. Across vision, speech, graph, and language tasks, KD appears to work through a mix of mechanisms — soft targets acting as regularizers, matching intermediate representations, and reducing effective data complexity — and can be combined with data augmentation, privacy-preserving noise, and architecture-aware projectors. Practical research highlights trade-offs related to teacher quality, which samples to transfer, robustness, and device heterogeneity; current methods address these by selective sample transfer, contrastive or feature-level alignment, adversarial objectives, and pre-training compact students before distillation. Key open directions include principled selection of distilled samples, theoretical characterization of when distilled soft targets help versus hurt, and integrating KD with pruning and other compression approaches for deployment on constrained devices.

papers_seen.author: Mcmillan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression for NLP: Strengths, Limits, and a Recipe for Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is the most practical and widely adopted strategy for compressing large NLP models into smaller, deployable students. When applied thoughtfully—matching soft outputs, aligning intermediate representations, using task-aware layer mapping, and addressing data or privacy constraints—KD recovers most of a teacher’s performance while enabling large reductions in storage, latency, and power. However, effective deployment requires recognizing and mitigating limits such as capacity mismatch, distributional heterogeneity, and the risk of transferring teacher biases.

papers_seen.author: Rocha
papers_seen.title: Few Shot Network Compression via Cross Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Model compression has been widely adopted to obtain light-weighted deep neural networks. Most prevalent methods, however, require fine-tuning with sufficient training data to ensure accuracy, which could be challenged by privacy and security issues. As a compromise between privacy and performance, in this paper we investigate few shot network compression: given few samples per class, how can we effectively compress the network with negligible performance drop? The core challenge of few shot network compression lies in high estimation errors from the original network during inference, since the compressed network can easily over-fits on the few training instances. The estimation errors could propagate and accumulate layer-wisely and finally deteriorate the network output. To address the problem, we propose cross distillation, a novel layer-wise knowledge distillation approach. By interweaving hidden layers of teacher and student network, layer-wisely accumulated estimation errors can be effectively reduced.The proposed method offers a general framework compatible with prevalent network compression techniques such as pruning. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that cross distillation can significantly improve the student network's accuracy when only a few training instances are available.

papers_seen.author: Nunez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical but Engineering-Dependent Route to Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile set of methods for transferring behavior from large teacher models to smaller students, enabling reduced inference cost and deployment on constrained devices. KD can match final outputs or internal representations and is often combined with complementary compression techniques; however, its success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align architectures, and how to handle data and optimization mismatches. I argue that KD should be treated as an essential, task-aware component of compression pipelines rather than a plug-and-play solution, and I offer practical directions to maximize its benefits while mitigating common failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Mckay
papers_seen.title: MixKD: Towards Efficient Distillation of Large-scale Language Models
papers_seen.abstract: Large-scale language models have recently demonstrated impressive empirical performance. Nevertheless, the improved results are attained at the price of bigger models, more power consumption, and slower inference, which hinder their applicability to low-resource (both memory and computation) platforms. Knowledge distillation (KD) has been demonstrated as an effective framework for compressing such big models. However, large-scale neural network systems are prone to memorize training instances, and thus tend to make inconsistent predictions when the data distribution is altered slightly. Moreover, the student model has few opportunities to request useful information from the teacher model when there is limited task-specific data available. To address these issues, we propose MixKD, a data-agnostic distillation framework that leverages mixup, a simple yet efficient data augmentation approach, to endow the resulting model with stronger generalization ability. Concretely, in addition to the original training examples, the student model is encouraged to mimic the teacher's behavior on the linear interpolation of example pairs as well. We prove from a theoretical perspective that under reasonable conditions MixKD gives rise to a smaller gap between the generalization error and the empirical error. To verify its effectiveness, we conduct experiments on the GLUE benchmark, where MixKD consistently leads to significant gains over the standard KD training, and outperforms several competitive baselines. Experiments under a limited-data setting and ablation studies further demonstrate the advantages of the proposed approach.

papers_seen.author: Hensley
papers_seen.title: Apprentice: Using Knowledge Distillation Techniques To Improve Low-Precision Network Accuracy
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning networks have achieved state-of-the-art accuracies on computer vision workloads like image classification and object detection. The performant systems, however, typically involve big models with numerous parameters. Once trained, a challenging aspect for such top performing models is deployment on resource constrained inference systems - the models (often deep networks or wide networks or both) are compute and memory intensive. Low-precision numerics and model compression using knowledge distillation are popular techniques to lower both the compute requirements and memory footprint of these deployed models. In this paper, we study the combination of these two techniques and show that the performance of low-precision networks can be significantly improved by using knowledge distillation techniques. Our approach, Apprentice, achieves state-of-the-art accuracies using ternary precision and 4-bit precision for variants of ResNet architecture on ImageNet dataset. We present three schemes using which one can apply knowledge distillation techniques to various stages of the train-and-deploy pipeline.

papers_seen.author: Zamora
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, cheaper students by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations. The family of KD methods includes soft-target (logit) matching, feature- and layer-wise alignment, relational and module-level transfer, data-free or zero-shot synthesis, and integration with architecture search or federated training. Practical deployments balance what is transferred with student capacity, data availability, privacy constraints, and device heterogeneity; empirical work shows KD often preserves much of teacher performance while enabling lower latency, smaller models, and domain specialization, but open challenges remain around robustness, domain shift, and principled selection of distilled signals.
