papers_seen.author: Wheeler
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Cornerstone for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically proven approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation), task-aware design, and careful teacher selection or training, KD can yield compact models that retain much of the original performance. However, successful deployment requires attention to data heterogeneity, fairness, and robustness limitations.

papers_seen.author: Taylor
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller models by transferring predictive and representational information from teachers to students. Across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks, KD enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Practical pipelines combine soft-target matching, representation-level imitation, architecture-aware design and search, and data strategies (including data-free or privacy-preserving synthesis). While KD often recovers much of a teacher's performance and can enable students that are substantially faster and smaller, success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align representations, and how to manage data and teacher quality; important open problems remain in robustness, domain shift, and theoretical explanation.

papers_seen.author: Moran
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of methods for transferring predictive capacity from larger teacher models into smaller, more efficient students so models can be deployed under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. Research over the past decade has expanded simple logit-matching into a rich set of variants—feature and layer alignment, progressive module replacement, self-distillation, data-free synthesis, and privacy-aware ensembles—making KD a cornerstone of modern model-compression toolkits.

papers_seen.author: Maldonado
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge by Mimicking Features
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a popular method to train efficient networks ("student") with the help of high-capacity networks ("teacher"). Traditional methods use the teacher's soft logits as extra supervision to train the student network. In this paper, we argue that it is more advantageous to make the student mimic the teacher's features in the penultimate layer. Not only the student can directly learn more effective information from the teacher feature, feature mimicking can also be applied for teachers trained without a softmax layer. Experiments show that it can achieve higher accuracy than traditional KD. To further facilitate feature mimicking, we decompose a feature vector into the magnitude and the direction. We argue that the teacher should give more freedom to the student feature's magnitude, and let the student pay more attention on mimicking the feature direction. To meet this requirement, we propose a loss term based on locality-sensitive hashing (LSH). With the help of this new loss, our method indeed mimics feature directions more accurately, relaxes constraints on feature magnitudes, and achieves state-of-the-art distillation accuracy. We provide theoretical analyses of how LSH facilitates feature direction mimicking, and further extend feature mimicking to multi-label recognition and object detection.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Power, Limits, and Practical Recipes
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central, pragmatic approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. When combined with complementary techniques and careful engineering it can deliver substantial reductions in model size and latency while retaining much of teacher performance. However, KD is not a drop-in cure: success depends on choices about what to transfer (logits, features, relations), how to prepare teachers and students, how to handle data scarcity or privacy constraints, and how to preserve robustness and fairness. This essay argues that KD should be treated as a flexible core of compression pipelines, and it summarizes practical strategies and caveats for effective, responsible deployment.

papers_seen.author: Hurst
papers_seen.title: Contemporary Approaches and Applications of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques transfer information from larger, more costly models to smaller, deployable models. Modern work expands beyond simple soft-label matching to include distillation of internal representations, feature-level imitation, privacy-preserving and data-free strategies, task-adaptive compression, and adaptations to specialized architectures (e.g., GANs, detectors, and transformers). These methods aim to preserve accuracy, robustness, and efficiency (compute, memory, or communication) while enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices or in privacy-sensitive and distributed settings.

papers_seen.author: Kidd
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable approach for compressing large deep learning models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students. Modern KD goes beyond matching logits: it includes feature- and representation-level transfers, multi-teacher and self-distillation strategies, and workflows that integrate augmentation, data-free synthesis, pruning, and quantization to meet latency, memory, and privacy requirements. Practical success depends on matching distillation technique to deployment objectives, careful design of layer mappings and loss terms, attention to teacher quality and data availability, and combinations with other compression tools to preserve robustness and generalization.

papers_seen.author: Walton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential, Practical Strategy for Compressing Deep Models in NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques are indispensable for deploying high-capacity deep and language models in resource-constrained settings. By transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teachers to smaller students, practitioners can achieve large reductions in model size and latency while retaining most task performance. However, realizing these gains reliably requires attention to what is transferred (logits, features, relations), how teachers and data are chosen, and hardware- or deployment-aware compression strategies.

papers_seen.author: Allen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practical Principles, and Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques transfer knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models so that compact systems approach teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints. Work across vision and NLP shows that effective compression combines multiple strategies — soft-label matching, intermediate representation alignment, architecture-aware design, data- and privacy-aware workflows, and adversarial or ensemble consolidation — and that practical gains depend on addressing representation mismatch, optimization dynamics, and task or domain shifts. This synthesis summarizes prevailing methods, empirical patterns, and recurring trade-offs relevant for practitioners aiming to deploy efficient models in resource- or data-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models so they meet real-world constraints on latency, memory, and deployment. Across vision, language, generative, and structured prediction tasks, KD has been adapted from simple soft-label matching into a rich toolbox that includes intermediate-layer supervision, multi-teacher schedules, student-aware teacher training, data- and augmentation-aware pipelines, and combinations with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). When applied with attention to student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints, KD reliably improves size–performance trade-offs, but its success depends on careful signal selection, teacher–student alignment, and strategies to mitigate capacity mismatch, distribution shift, and transferred teacher artifacts.

papers_seen.author: Caldwell
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer information from larger, expensive teacher models to smaller, deployable students to reduce inference cost while preserving much of the teacher’s behavior. Across modalities and tasks, KD methods vary by the form of transferred signal (soft targets, intermediate features, attention maps, or module behaviors), training setting (offline, online, federated, or data-free), and complementary techniques (architecture design, pruning, quantization, and data augmentation). Practical success depends on aligning teacher and student inputs/representations, selecting appropriate distillation objectives for the task and data regime, and mitigating distributional or token-frequency artifacts introduced during distillation. This synthesis summarizes major approaches, empirical findings, limitations, and practical strategies for applying KD in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Daniels
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, faster students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. Methods range from matching softened logits to imitating internal representations, attention maps, or channel-wise activations, and can be combined with quantization, low-precision numerics, architecture-aware design, and data- or teacher-aware training regimes. In practice, distillation is a multifaceted toolkit that must be tailored to deployment goals (latency, memory, domain adaptation, privacy, robustness), and remaining challenges include principled sample selection, representation alignment across heterogeneous architectures, and preserving robustness and fairness under compression.

papers_seen.author: Bright
papers_seen.title: Towards Practical Lipreading with Distilled and Efficient Models
papers_seen.abstract: Lipreading has witnessed a lot of progress due to the resurgence of neural networks. Recent works have placed emphasis on aspects such as improving performance by finding the optimal architecture or improving generalization. However, there is still a significant gap between the current methodologies and the requirements for an effective deployment of lipreading in practical scenarios. In this work, we propose a series of innovations that significantly bridge that gap: first, we raise the state-of-the-art performance by a wide margin on LRW and LRW-1000 to 88.5% and 46.6%, respectively using self-distillation. Secondly, we propose a series of architectural changes, including a novel Depthwise Separable Temporal Convolutional Network (DS-TCN) head, that slashes the computational cost to a fraction of the (already quite efficient) original model. Thirdly, we show that knowledge distillation is a very effective tool for recovering performance of the lightweight models. This results in a range of models with different accuracy-efficiency trade-offs. However, our most promising lightweight models are on par with the current state-of-the-art while showing a reduction of 8.2x and 3.9x in terms of computational cost and number of parameters, respectively, which we hope will enable the deployment of lipreading models in practical applications.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Task-Aware Path to Model Compression in NLP and Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a flexible and practical framework for compressing large models and transferring capabilities to smaller ones. When applied thoughtfully — using layer-aware alignment, attention-guided feature matching, dynamic multi-teacher strategies, and privacy- or deployment-aware protocols — distillation enables substantial speedups, reduced footprint, and cross-modal or cross-device applicability with small drops (or even gains) in task performance. Distillation is not a plug-and-play cure: optimization challenges, teacher-student mismatch, and task-specific redundancy mean methods must be adapted to the target architecture and data regime to realize consistent benefits.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Unifying Heterogeneous Classifiers with Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: In this paper, we study the problem of unifying knowledge from a set of classifiers with different architectures and target classes into a single classifier, given only a generic set of unlabelled data. We call this problem Unifying Heterogeneous Classifiers (UHC). This problem is motivated by scenarios where data is collected from multiple sources, but the sources cannot share their data, e.g., due to privacy concerns, and only privately trained models can be shared. In addition, each source may not be able to gather data to train all classes due to data availability at each source, and may not be able to train the same classification model due to different computational resources. To tackle this problem, we propose a generalisation of knowledge distillation to merge HCs. We derive a probabilistic relation between the outputs of HCs and the probability over all classes. Based on this relation, we propose two classes of methods based on cross-entropy minimisation and matrix factorisation, which allow us to estimate soft labels over all classes from unlabelled samples and use them in lieu of ground truth labels to train a unified classifier. Our extensive experiments on ImageNet, LSUN, and Places365 datasets show that our approaches significantly outperform a naive extension of distillation and can achieve almost the same accuracy as classifiers that are trained in a centralised, supervised manner.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Insights, and Practical Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large models into smaller, faster ones by transferring information from a teacher to a student. It has been applied across supervised, self-supervised, multimodal and domain-adaptation settings to reduce inference cost while retaining much of the teacher's performance. Progress includes direct soft-target matching, feature- and relation-based imitation, self- and progressive-distillation strategies, and task- or domain-aware adaptations. Empirical work highlights both the power of KD to produce efficient models for deployment and important practical considerations—such as the value of pre-training, the role of data augmentation and sample selection, and computational bottlenecks—that shape effective distillation regimes. Despite advances, optimization mismatches, teacher–student capacity differences, and data-domain shift remain active challenges guiding current research and practice.

papers_seen.author: Shields
papers_seen.title: What is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high‑capacity teacher models into smaller, faster student models by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. The technique encompasses matching softened output distributions, aligning intermediate representations and attention maps, synthesizing or reusing data when originals are unavailable, and co‑designing compact architectures. KD is flexible and widely applicable across modalities (language, vision, multimodal, and generative models) and is most effective when combined with complementary compression strategies and task‑aware choices about what and how to transfer. Success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data regime, and the match between teacher and student architectures; open challenges include domain shift, robustness, fairness, and theoretical understanding of when and why distillation works.

papers_seen.author: Osborne
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, more efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and internal knowledge. Across vision and language tasks, KD is used to reduce inference cost, enable deployment on resource-constrained devices, and retain performance through techniques that go beyond matching final outputs—including intermediate representation imitation, data-aware training, multi-teacher strategies, and teacher-free or data-free approaches. Empirical work demonstrates both consistent gains and important failure modes (e.g., loss of low-frequency lexical information or sensitivity to domain shift), motivating refinements such as internal representation distillation, curriculum or sample selection, data augmentation choices, and dynamic teacher weighting. Open challenges remain in understanding what components of teacher knowledge most benefit students, how to handle heterogeneity between teacher and student architectures, and how to distill effectively without access to original training data.

papers_seen.author: Hicks
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large models into smaller ones by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or other structural knowledge from teacher(s) to student(s). Approaches range from classic logit-matching to feature- and channel-wise transfer, multi-teacher schemes, self-distillation, data-free adversarial methods, and adaptations for distributed or heterogeneous settings. Empirical work shows that properly designed distillation can preserve much of teacher performance while greatly reducing size and latency; practical success depends on choices like what form of knowledge to transfer, whether and how to augment or synthesize data, and how to handle heterogeneous compute or domain shifts.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Channel Distillation: Channel-Wise Attention for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is to transfer the knowledge from the data learned by the teacher network to the student network, so that the student has the advantage of less parameters and less calculations, and the accuracy is close to the teacher. In this paper, we propose a new distillation method, which contains two transfer distillation strategies and a loss decay strategy. The first transfer strategy is based on channel-wise attention, called Channel Distillation (CD). CD transfers the channel information from the teacher to the student. The second is Guided Knowledge Distillation (GKD). Unlike Knowledge Distillation (KD), which allows the student to mimic each sample's prediction distribution of the teacher, GKD only enables the student to mimic the correct output of the teacher. The last part is Early Decay Teacher (EDT). During the training process, we gradually decay the weight of the distillation loss. The purpose is to enable the student to gradually control the optimization rather than the teacher. Our proposed method is evaluated on ImageNet and CIFAR100. On ImageNet, we achieve 27.68% of top-1 error with ResNet18, which outperforms state-of-the-art methods. On CIFAR100, we achieve surprising result that the student outperforms the teacher. Code is available at https://github.com/zhouzaida/channel-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central technique for compressing large deep learning models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teachers' performance. Across vision, language, speech, and recommendation tasks, researchers combine KD with architectural compression, pre-training, privacy mechanisms, and data-free approaches to address inference cost, dataset availability, and domain-specific challenges. Empirical work shows that careful choices about what to transfer (logits, features, layers), how to train teachers and students, and how to incorporate task or data constraints strongly determine final student quality.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Linkless Link Prediction via Relational Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have shown exceptional performance in the task of link prediction. Despite their effectiveness, the high latency brought by non-trivial neighborhood data dependency limits GNNs in practical deployments. Conversely, the known efficient MLPs are much less effective than GNNs due to the lack of relational knowledge. In this work, to combine the advantages of GNNs and MLPs, we start with exploring direct knowledge distillation (KD) methods for link prediction, i.e., predicted logit-based matching and node representation-based matching. Upon observing direct KD analogs do not perform well for link prediction, we propose a relational KD framework, Linkless Link Prediction (LLP), to distill knowledge for link prediction with MLPs. Unlike simple KD methods that match independent link logits or node representations, LLP distills relational knowledge that is centered around each (anchor) node to the student MLP. Specifically, we propose rank-based matching and distribution-based matching strategies that complement each other. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LLP boosts the link prediction performance of MLPs with significant margins, and even outperforms the teacher GNNs on 7 out of 8 benchmarks. LLP also achieves a 70.68x speedup in link prediction inference compared to GNNs on the large-scale OGB dataset.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Extensions, and Practical Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a core approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. Research over the past decade has expanded KD from simple teacher–student logit matching to a rich set of strategies that address data availability, privacy, distributed settings, architecture mismatches, and task-specific compression needs. Advances include data-free and zero-shot distillation, federated and privacy-aware distillation, representational and layer-mapping techniques for pre-trained language models, and practical combinations with quantization and architecture search to enable deployment on resource-constrained devices.

papers_seen.author: Parsons
papers_seen.title: Curriculum Learning for Dense Retrieval Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Recent work has shown that more effective dense retrieval models can be obtained by distilling ranking knowledge from an existing base re-ranking model. In this paper, we propose a generic curriculum learning based optimization framework called CL-DRD that controls the difficulty level of training data produced by the re-ranking (teacher) model. CL-DRD iteratively optimizes the dense retrieval (student) model by increasing the difficulty of the knowledge distillation data made available to it. In more detail, we initially provide the student model coarse-grained preference pairs between documents in the teacher's ranking and progressively move towards finer-grained pairwise document ordering requirements. In our experiments, we apply a simple implementation of the CL-DRD framework to enhance two state-of-the-art dense retrieval models. Experiments on three public passage retrieval datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed framework.

papers_seen.author: Owens
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses capability from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. It encompasses methods that transfer final outputs, intermediate representations, relational structure, or training curricula, and it is applied across modalities (vision, language, scene synthesis, and optimization tasks). KD delivers practical gains in inference speed, memory footprint, and often generalization or robustness when paired with complementary techniques (data augmentation, architecture design, and adversarial training), but its success depends on choices about what is transferred, how data are used or synthesized, and how teacher and student capacities are aligned.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Distilling the Knowledge of BERT for Sequence-to-Sequence ASR
papers_seen.abstract: Attention-based sequence-to-sequence (seq2seq) models have achieved promising results in automatic speech recognition (ASR). However, as these models decode in a left-to-right way, they do not have access to context on the right. We leverage both left and right context by applying BERT as an external language model to seq2seq ASR through knowledge distillation. In our proposed method, BERT generates soft labels to guide the training of seq2seq ASR. Furthermore, we leverage context beyond the current utterance as input to BERT. Experimental evaluations show that our method significantly improves the ASR performance from the seq2seq baseline on the Corpus of Spontaneous Japanese (CSJ). Knowledge distillation from BERT outperforms that from a transformer LM that only looks at left context. We also show the effectiveness of leveraging context beyond the current utterance. Our method outperforms other LM application approaches such as n-best rescoring and shallow fusion, while it does not require extra inference cost.

papers_seen.author: Carr
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Cornerstone for Compressing Deep Models in NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, versatile mechanism for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable ones in NLP and related modalities. When paired with targeted choices—what signals to transfer (logits versus features), how to align layers, teacher design, and data strategies—KD preserves much of the teacher’s capability while reducing compute, memory, and latency. However, KD is not a universal remedy: its success depends on optimization details, data availability, and careful engineering to handle distribution shift, rare behaviors, and student–teacher mismatches.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure. Across vision and language tasks KD supports deployment to resource-constrained devices, data-scarce regimes, and domain adaptation. Effective distillation combines teacher-to-student signal design (soft outputs, features, attention or relational cues), data strategies (augmentation, synthetic or online generation), and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture modification). While KD often produces strong size–performance tradeoffs, practical success depends on addressing capacity mismatch, domain shift, and signal selection so the student can absorb the teacher’s knowledge.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Unifying Paradigm for Compression, Adaptation, and Robust Training
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be considered not merely as a compression trick but as a general and practical training paradigm. Across modalities and tasks, KD transfers information about function, structure, and uncertainty from one model (or ensemble) to another, enabling smaller, faster, or more adaptable models while improving generalization, interpretability, and domain transfer. Success depends on how teacher knowledge is selected, represented, and combined with data-side techniques; thoughtful design choices (layer mapping, sample selection, augmentation, and teacher trust) determine whether KD yields compression, robustness, or better task-specific performance.

papers_seen.author: Arnold
papers_seen.title: Does Knowledge Distillation Really Work?
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular technique for training a small student network to emulate a larger teacher model, such as an ensemble of networks. We show that while knowledge distillation can improve student generalization, it does not typically work as it is commonly understood: there often remains a surprisingly large discrepancy between the predictive distributions of the teacher and the student, even in cases when the student has the capacity to perfectly match the teacher. We identify difficulties in optimization as a key reason for why the student is unable to match the teacher. We also show how the details of the dataset used for distillation play a role in how closely the student matches the teacher -- and that more closely matching the teacher paradoxically does not always lead to better student generalization.

papers_seen.author: Mills
papers_seen.title: Why Knowledge Distillation Should Be the Central Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, adaptable technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of their performance. When combined with careful pre-training of compact architectures, representation-level transfer, augmentation or synthesized data, and orthogonal compression methods (pruning, quantization), KD delivers strong trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy. However, realizing those gains in practice requires attention to optimization dynamics, data availability, privacy, and known failure modes (e.g., low-frequency token degradation), and so KD should be applied as part of an integrated, responsible compression pipeline.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation with Progressive Refinement of Targets
papers_seen.abstract: The generalization capability of deep neural networks has been substantially improved by applying a wide spectrum of regularization methods, e.g., restricting function space, injecting randomness during training, augmenting data, etc. In this work, we propose a simple yet effective regularization method named progressive self-knowledge distillation (PS-KD), which progressively distills a model's own knowledge to soften hard targets (i.e., one-hot vectors) during training. Hence, it can be interpreted within a framework of knowledge distillation as a student becomes a teacher itself. Specifically, targets are adjusted adaptively by combining the ground-truth and past predictions from the model itself. We show that PS-KD provides an effect of hard example mining by rescaling gradients according to difficulty in classifying examples. The proposed method is applicable to any supervised learning tasks with hard targets and can be easily combined with existing regularization methods to further enhance the generalization performance. Furthermore, it is confirmed that PS-KD achieves not only better accuracy, but also provides high quality of confidence estimates in terms of calibration as well as ordinal ranking. Extensive experimental results on three different tasks, image classification, object detection, and machine translation, demonstrate that our method consistently improves the performance of the state-of-the-art baselines. The code is available at https://github.com/lgcnsai/PS-KD-Pytorch.

papers_seen.author: Rocha
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practical Trends
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques aim to transfer predictive power from large teacher models into smaller, faster, or more private student models while retaining most of the original performance. Work across vision and language has expanded KD beyond simple logit matching into data-centric methods (augmentation and mixup), layer- and representation-level transfers, task-adaptive architecture search, data-free and privacy-aware distillation, and unified pipelines that combine pruning or structural compression with distillation. The field blends empirical engineering (speed/size trade-offs) with emerging theoretical analyses that help explain when and why distillation helps.

papers_seen.author: Carpenter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Practical, and Responsible Tool for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, widely applicable method for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. KD shines when combined with complementary compression techniques and data strategies, but its reliability depends on careful choices about what is transferred, how teachers and students are aligned, and how data or robustness constraints are handled. I argue KD should be treated as a central instrument in compression pipelines, used with explicit engineering and ethical practices to manage its limits.

papers_seen.author: Mayo
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques aim to transfer the predictive power of large, expensive models into smaller, faster models suitable for deployment, domain adaptation, or constrained hardware. Research has explored matching output distributions, aligning internal representations, module-replacement strategies, data-augmented or data-free distillation, robustness-aware objectives, and task-aware selection of transferable knowledge. Empirical work spans language models (including BERT), reading comprehension, retrieval/ranking, and vision tasks, demonstrating trade-offs between compression ratio, accuracy retention, robustness, and required access to teacher training data. Best practices emphasize careful choice of distillation signal (logits, attention, hidden activations), augmentation or synthesis of training examples when data are scarce, and filtering or adapting teacher knowledge to the student’s capacity and target task.

papers_seen.author: Keith
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression techniques transfer capability from large teacher models into smaller, deployable students to reduce inference cost, memory, and energy while preserving much of task performance. The literature shows a spectrum of methods — from soft-target matching to representation-level alignment, progressive module replacement, and data-free or adversarial sample synthesis — and emphasizes that distillation is most effective when combined with careful student initialization, architecture-aware alignment, and complementary compression methods. Practical success depends on choices about what signals to transfer, how to supply or synthesize training data, and how to align teacher and student capacities; open challenges include optimization dynamics, domain shift, privacy, and robustness under rare phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical and Flexible Path to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large models into smaller, faster ones while retaining much of their performance. Beyond simple teacher-student logit matching, effective KD approaches exploit feature-level mimicking, task-aware layer selection, meta-learned teachers, online distillation for large-scale training, and task-adaptive model search. When applied thoughtfully — choosing the right supervision signal (logits vs. features), shaping teacher behavior to be student-friendly, and matching distillation to deployment constraints — KD can deliver strong accuracy-efficiency trade-offs across vision and language tasks, improve robustness, and enable practical deployment of pretrained models in resource-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: On Representation Knowledge Distillation for Graph Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a learning paradigm for boosting resource-efficient graph neural networks (GNNs) using more expressive yet cumbersome teacher models. Past work on distillation for GNNs proposed the Local Structure Preserving loss (LSP), which matches local structural relationships defined over edges across the student and teacher's node embeddings. This paper studies whether preserving the global topology of how the teacher embeds graph data can be a more effective distillation objective for GNNs, as real-world graphs often contain latent interactions and noisy edges. We propose Graph Contrastive Representation Distillation (G-CRD), which uses contrastive learning to implicitly preserve global topology by aligning the student node embeddings to those of the teacher in a shared representation space. Additionally, we introduce an expanded set of benchmarks on large-scale real-world datasets where the performance gap between teacher and student GNNs is non-negligible. Experiments across 4 datasets and 14 heterogeneous GNN architectures show that G-CRD consistently boosts the performance and robustness of lightweight GNNs, outperforming LSP (and a global structure preserving variant of LSP) as well as baselines from 2D computer vision. An analysis of the representational similarity among teacher and student embedding spaces reveals that G-CRD balances preserving local and global relationships, while structure preserving approaches are best at preserving one or the other. Our code is available at https://github.com/chaitjo/efficient-gnns

papers_seen.author: Beck
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses larger teacher models into smaller student models by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. Approaches include matching softened logits, aligning intermediate representations or attention maps, mapping or projecting teacher layers to student layers, and operating in offline, online, federated, or data-free regimes. Distillation is commonly combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and task-aware data strategies. Practical success depends on choosing which signals to transfer, aligning teacher and student capacity, managing data or privacy constraints, and designing curricula or multi-stage pipelines that reflect deployment needs. While distillation routinely produces compact models that retain much of teacher performance, open challenges remain in representation mismatch, amplifying teacher biases, and ensuring robustness and fairness under compression.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible, and empirically validated family of methods for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When applied thoughtfully—using richer targets than logits, aligning intermediate representations, and combining with complementary techniques such as pruning, quantization, or architecture search—KD routinely enables substantial reductions in latency, memory, and energy while preserving much of a teacher's performance. KD also adapts to constrained settings (few-shot, federated, or data-free) and supports robustness and domain adaptation when pipelines are designed to match task and deployment constraints. Realizing KD's full value requires principled choices about what to transfer, how to generate or select distillation data, and how to align teacher and student capacity.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge distillation from multi-modal to mono-modal segmentation networks
papers_seen.abstract: The joint use of multiple imaging modalities for medical image segmentation has been widely studied in recent years. The fusion of information from different modalities has demonstrated to improve the segmentation accuracy, with respect to mono-modal segmentations, in several applications. However, acquiring multiple modalities is usually not possible in a clinical setting due to a limited number of physicians and scanners, and to limit costs and scan time. Most of the time, only one modality is acquired. In this paper, we propose KD-Net, a framework to transfer knowledge from a trained multi-modal network (teacher) to a mono-modal one (student). The proposed method is an adaptation of the generalized distillation framework where the student network is trained on a subset (1 modality) of the teacher's inputs (n modalities). We illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in brain tumor segmentation with the BraTS 2018 dataset. Using different architectures, we show that the student network effectively learns from the teacher and always outperforms the baseline mono-modal network in terms of segmentation accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Beyond Soft Labels: A Practical Position on Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a crucial technique for shrinking large deep models to meet real-world latency, memory and privacy constraints while retaining much of their performance. However, naive distillation that only matches teacher soft-labels is often insufficient. A more reliable strategy combines distillation of internal representations and features, task- or domain-adaptive compression, and architecture-aware search or adaptation. When applied with care — addressing optimization issues, data or privacy limits, and mismatch between teacher and student capacities — distillation enables compact, fast models that approach teacher performance across speech, NLP and vision tasks.

papers_seen.author: Rhodes
papers_seen.title: Lifelong Language Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: It is challenging to perform lifelong language learning (LLL) on a stream of different tasks without any performance degradation comparing to the multi-task counterparts. To address this issue, we present Lifelong Language Knowledge Distillation (L2KD), a simple but efficient method that can be easily applied to existing LLL architectures in order to mitigate the degradation. Specifically, when the LLL model is trained on a new task, we assign a teacher model to first learn the new task, and pass the knowledge to the LLL model via knowledge distillation. Therefore, the LLL model can better adapt to the new task while keeping the previously learned knowledge. Experiments show that the proposed L2KD consistently improves previous state-of-the-art models, and the degradation comparing to multi-task models in LLL tasks is well mitigated for both sequence generation and text classification tasks.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: A Closer Look at Deep Learning Heuristics: Learning rate restarts, Warmup and Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The convergence rate and final performance of common deep learning models have significantly benefited from heuristics such as learning rate schedules, knowledge distillation, skip connections, and normalization layers. In the absence of theoretical underpinnings, controlled experiments aimed at explaining these strategies can aid our understanding of deep learning landscapes and the training dynamics. Existing approaches for empirical analysis rely on tools of linear interpolation and visualizations with dimensionality reduction, each with their limitations. Instead, we revisit such analysis of heuristics through the lens of recently proposed methods for loss surface and representation analysis, viz., mode connectivity and canonical correlation analysis (CCA), and hypothesize reasons for the success of the heuristics. In particular, we explore knowledge distillation and learning rate heuristics of (cosine) restarts and warmup using mode connectivity and CCA. Our empirical analysis suggests that: (a) the reasons often quoted for the success of cosine annealing are not evidenced in practice; (b) that the effect of learning rate warmup is to prevent the deeper layers from creating training instability; and (c) that the latent knowledge shared by the teacher is primarily disbursed to the deeper layers.

papers_seen.author: Bright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Solution for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible approach to compressing large neural models for deployment and domain-specialization. Beyond simple teacher-to-student label matching, modern KD techniques transfer intermediate representations, exploit synthetic or augmented data, operate without original training data, and incorporate privacy or distributed-training constraints. These variants enable retaining much of the teacher performance while reducing inference cost, supporting domain adaptation, improving generalization under limited-data regimes, and meeting privacy or latency requirements for real-world systems.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: R2L: Distilling Neural Radiance Field to Neural Light Field for Efficient Novel View Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Recent research explosion on Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) shows the encouraging potential to represent complex scenes with neural networks. One major drawback of NeRF is its prohibitive inference time: Rendering a single pixel requires querying the NeRF network hundreds of times. To resolve it, existing efforts mainly attempt to reduce the number of required sampled points. However, the problem of iterative sampling still exists. On the other hand, Neural Light Field (NeLF) presents a more straightforward representation over NeRF in novel view synthesis -- the rendering of a pixel amounts to one single forward pass without ray-marching. In this work, we present a deep residual MLP network (88 layers) to effectively learn the light field. We show the key to successfully learning such a deep NeLF network is to have sufficient data, for which we transfer the knowledge from a pre-trained NeRF model via data distillation. Extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world scenes show the merits of our method over other counterpart algorithms. On the synthetic scenes, we achieve 26-35x FLOPs reduction (per camera ray) and 28-31x runtime speedup, meanwhile delivering significantly better (1.4-2.8 dB average PSNR improvement) rendering quality than NeRF without any customized parallelism requirement.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Revisiting Knowledge Distillation via Label Smoothing Regularization
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge Distillation (KD) aims to distill the knowledge of a cumbersome teacher model into a lightweight student model. Its success is generally attributed to the privileged information on similarities among categories provided by the teacher model, and in this sense, only strong teacher models are deployed to teach weaker students in practice. In this work, we challenge this common belief by following experimental observations: 1) beyond the acknowledgment that the teacher can improve the student, the student can also enhance the teacher significantly by reversing the KD procedure; 2) a poorly-trained teacher with much lower accuracy than the student can still improve the latter significantly. To explain these observations, we provide a theoretical analysis of the relationships between KD and label smoothing regularization. We prove that 1) KD is a type of learned label smoothing regularization and 2) label smoothing regularization provides a virtual teacher model for KD. From these results, we argue that the success of KD is not fully due to the similarity information between categories from teachers, but also to the regularization of soft targets, which is equally or even more important.   Based on these analyses, we further propose a novel Teacher-free Knowledge Distillation (Tf-KD) framework, where a student model learns from itself or manuallydesigned regularization distribution. The Tf-KD achieves comparable performance with normal KD from a superior teacher, which is well applied when a stronger teacher model is unavailable. Meanwhile, Tf-KD is generic and can be directly deployed for training deep neural networks. Without any extra computation cost, Tf-KD achieves up to 0.65\% improvement on ImageNet over well-established baseline models, which is superior to label smoothing regularization.

papers_seen.author: Cook
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Benefits, Limits, and Engineering Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile foundation for compressing deep and language models: it enables much smaller, faster students to capture substantial teacher performance while supporting deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD excels when combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and careful engineering (choice of transferred signals, data augmentation, teacher selection). However, KD is not a plug-and-play solution: it can propagate teacher imperfections, struggle with rare-token or low-frequency behaviors, and face difficulties under heterogeneous or privacy-constrained data regimes. Treating KD as the central tool in a compression pipeline — but one that requires task-aware design and diagnostics — yields the best practical outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression methods provide practical mechanisms to convert large, high-performing deep models into smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained students suitable for real-world deployment. Across vision, speech, and NLP, practitioners use KD to trade off capacity and efficiency while aiming to preserve task performance, often in combination with complementary techniques such as quantization, pruning, or architecture adaptation. Success depends on aligning teacher signals, student capacity, data strategy, and optimization schedules; remaining challenges include handling domain shift, preserving rare-token behavior, and operating under privacy or data-limited settings.

papers_seen.author: Parsons
papers_seen.title: Curriculum Learning for Dense Retrieval Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Recent work has shown that more effective dense retrieval models can be obtained by distilling ranking knowledge from an existing base re-ranking model. In this paper, we propose a generic curriculum learning based optimization framework called CL-DRD that controls the difficulty level of training data produced by the re-ranking (teacher) model. CL-DRD iteratively optimizes the dense retrieval (student) model by increasing the difficulty of the knowledge distillation data made available to it. In more detail, we initially provide the student model coarse-grained preference pairs between documents in the teacher's ranking and progressively move towards finer-grained pairwise document ordering requirements. In our experiments, we apply a simple implementation of the CL-DRD framework to enhance two state-of-the-art dense retrieval models. Experiments on three public passage retrieval datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed framework.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Graph-less Neural Networks: Teaching Old MLPs New Tricks via Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are popular for graph machine learning and have shown great results on wide node classification tasks. Yet, they are less popular for practical deployments in the industry owing to their scalability challenges incurred by data dependency. Namely, GNN inference depends on neighbor nodes multiple hops away from the target, and fetching them burdens latency-constrained applications. Existing inference acceleration methods like pruning and quantization can speed up GNNs by reducing Multiplication-and-ACcumulation (MAC) operations, but the improvements are limited given the data dependency is not resolved. Conversely, multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs) have no graph dependency and infer much faster than GNNs, even though they are less accurate than GNNs for node classification in general. Motivated by these complementary strengths and weaknesses, we bring GNNs and MLPs together via knowledge distillation (KD). Our work shows that the performance of MLPs can be improved by large margins with GNN KD. We call the distilled MLPs Graph-less Neural Networks (GLNNs) as they have no inference graph dependency. We show that GLNNs with competitive accuracy infer faster than GNNs by 146X-273X and faster than other acceleration methods by 14X-27X. Under a production setting involving both transductive and inductive predictions across 7 datasets, GLNN accuracies improve over stand-alone MLPs by 12.36% on average and match GNNs on 6/7 datasets. Comprehensive analysis shows when and why GLNNs can achieve competitive accuracies to GNNs and suggests GLNN as a handy choice for latency-constrained applications.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques transfer information from large teacher models to smaller student models to reduce inference cost and enable deployment in resource-constrained settings. A diverse set of KD variants—matching soft logits, aligning intermediate representations, synthesizing or reusing data, or adapting student architectures—has been developed. These methods are applied across modalities and combine effectively with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to achieve favorable size/accuracy trade-offs. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to generate or select training data, and how to align teacher and student architectures; open challenges include robust transfer under domain shift, privacy constraints, and heterogeneous deployment environments.

papers_seen.author: Green
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and internal information from teacher models. Across vision, language, graph, and detection tasks, distillation techniques range from matching softened output distributions to aligning intermediate features or relational structures, and they are frequently combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) and data strategies (augmentation, synthetic-data or no-data approaches). Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, how to supply or synthesize training data, and how to mitigate capacity, distributional, and bias-related limits. Continued progress centers on principled transfer objectives, data-aware workflows, and integration with other compression primitives to produce deployable, robust compact models.

papers_seen.author: Cortez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach that enables deployment of large deep models by training smaller students to retain much of teacher performance. KD supports a wide range of transfer signals (logits, features, attention), training protocols (multi-stage, multi-teacher, federated), and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design). When applied carefully and combined with appropriate data, alignment, and robustness strategies, KD yields substantial runtime and memory savings with modest accuracy loss, making it central to production model compression in NLP and related domains.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques aim to transfer predictive performance and internal representations from large, expensive teacher models to smaller, faster student models. Work in this area spans theoretical analyses, practical compression recipes for language and vision models, approaches that avoid access to original training data, and methods that target robustness, privacy, or device heterogeneity. The field balances trade-offs among student capacity, teacher imperfection, data availability, and downstream task requirements, producing a range of techniques—logit-level distillation, layer-wise and module-level matching, progressive replacement, data-free generation, and combined compression with low-precision numerics—that are evaluated across tasks from BERT compression to multimodal and 3D detection. This synthesis summarizes prevailing methods, motivations, and recurring challenges emerging from recent literature.

papers_seen.author: Gibson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression methods transfer predictive behavior and internal representations from larger or more informed teacher models into smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained students. These methods are applied to reduce latency and memory, enable deployment on heterogeneous or private devices, and to retain teacher performance through tailored losses, intermediate-feature matching, multi-stage pipelines, and combinations with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Empirical work shows KD succeeds across modalities (language, vision, multimodal, and generative models) when design choices — what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and which data to use — are matched to the task and constraints. Ongoing challenges include distilling rare-token behaviors, handling severe data heterogeneity, ensuring privacy and fairness, and automating student architecture design.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models so they meet real-world constraints on latency, memory, and deployment. Across vision, language, generative, and structured prediction tasks, KD has been adapted from simple soft-label matching into a rich toolbox that includes intermediate-layer supervision, multi-teacher schedules, student-aware teacher training, data- and augmentation-aware pipelines, and combinations with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). When applied with attention to student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints, KD reliably improves size–performance trade-offs, but its success depends on careful signal selection, teacher–student alignment, and strategies to mitigate capacity mismatch, distribution shift, and transferred teacher artifacts.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Recommendations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile method for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD works across modalities (vision, language, graphs, and generative models) by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from teachers to students. When applied thoughtfully—selecting appropriate distillation signals, aligning internal representations, and integrating complementary compression techniques—KD reliably yields compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is not a plug-and-play cure: its success depends on teacher quality, data strategy, optimization choices, and architecture alignment, so practitioners should pair KD with task-aware curricula, representation-level objectives, and other compression tools to realize robust deployment.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large or ensemble models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior and/or internal structure. Across vision and NLP, practitioners use KD to reduce latency and memory, adapt models to new domains, enable privacy- or data-constrained deployments, and condense ensembles into single deployable models. Effective distillation blends choices about what to transfer (soft targets, features, layers), how to pretrain or adapt compact architectures, and how to handle limited or sensitive data. While KD often preserves much of a teacher’s performance, achieving robust, fair, and domain-appropriate students requires careful design of teachers, student architectures, and distillation signals.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: What Makes a "Good" Data Augmentation in Knowledge Distillation -- A Statistical Perspective
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a general neural network training approach that uses a teacher model to guide the student model. Existing works mainly study KD from the network output side (e.g., trying to design a better KD loss function), while few have attempted to understand it from the input side. Especially, its interplay with data augmentation (DA) has not been well understood. In this paper, we ask: Why do some DA schemes (e.g., CutMix) inherently perform much better than others in KD? What makes a "good" DA in KD? Our investigation from a statistical perspective suggests that a good DA scheme should reduce the covariance of the teacher-student cross-entropy. A practical metric, the stddev of teacher's mean probability (T. stddev), is further presented and well justified empirically. Besides the theoretical understanding, we also introduce a new entropy-based data-mixing DA scheme, CutMixPick, to further enhance CutMix. Extensive empirical studies support our claims and demonstrate how we can harvest considerable performance gains simply by using a better DA scheme in knowledge distillation.
