papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Variants, and Practical Insights
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models into smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained student models. KD methods range from soft-label (logit) matching to feature- and layer-level imitation, self-distillation, multi-teacher schemes, and data- or privacy-aware variants that synthesize or reuse surrogate data. Applied across vision, speech, recommender systems, and NLP, KD supports deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints while enabling domain adaptation and robustness-focused objectives. Practical success depends on careful choices about what signals to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, how to handle limited or private data, and how to combine distillation with complementary compression methods.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: Understanding Knowledge Distillation in Non-autoregressive Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Non-autoregressive machine translation (NAT) systems predict a sequence of output tokens in parallel, achieving substantial improvements in generation speed compared to autoregressive models. Existing NAT models usually rely on the technique of knowledge distillation, which creates the training data from a pretrained autoregressive model for better performance. Knowledge distillation is empirically useful, leading to large gains in accuracy for NAT models, but the reason for this success has, as of yet, been unclear. In this paper, we first design systematic experiments to investigate why knowledge distillation is crucial to NAT training. We find that knowledge distillation can reduce the complexity of data sets and help NAT to model the variations in the output data. Furthermore, a strong correlation is observed between the capacity of an NAT model and the optimal complexity of the distilled data for the best translation quality. Based on these findings, we further propose several approaches that can alter the complexity of data sets to improve the performance of NAT models. We achieve the state-of-the-art performance for the NAT-based models, and close the gap with the autoregressive baseline on WMT14 En-De benchmark.

papers_seen.author: Adkins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, broadly applicable strategy for shrinking large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students. KD can reproduce much of a teacher's task performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints; it also integrates naturally with complementary techniques (pretraining, data augmentation, multi-teacher supervision, and progressive module replacement). Realizing KD's full value in production requires attention to optimization gaps, dataset mismatch, and the risk of propagating teacher biases, and benefits from targeted extensions—feature-level objectives, adversarially-informed sample selection, and staged or progressive compression strategies.

papers_seen.author: Decker
papers_seen.title: Practical and Principled Knowledge Distillation for Compressing NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature and versatile approach for compressing large deep learning and NLP models into smaller, faster students while preserving much of the teacher’s performance. Effective compression in practice requires matching the distillation technique to the deployment objective: using self-distillation or multi-teacher strategies to extract richer supervisory signals, combining KD with architecture search or pruning for task-specific efficiency, applying appropriate soft/hard label mixing informed by bias–variance tradeoffs, and controlling data and privacy considerations during distillation. When these elements are combined, KD can deliver substantial runtime and memory savings with minimal accuracy loss, making it central to deploying modern NLP systems under resource constraints.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Extract the Knowledge of Graph Neural Networks and Go Beyond it: An Effective Knowledge Distillation Framework
papers_seen.abstract: Semi-supervised learning on graphs is an important problem in the machine learning area. In recent years, state-of-the-art classification methods based on graph neural networks (GNNs) have shown their superiority over traditional ones such as label propagation. However, the sophisticated architectures of these neural models will lead to a complex prediction mechanism, which could not make full use of valuable prior knowledge lying in the data, e.g., structurally correlated nodes tend to have the same class. In this paper, we propose a framework based on knowledge distillation to address the above issues. Our framework extracts the knowledge of an arbitrary learned GNN model (teacher model), and injects it into a well-designed student model. The student model is built with two simple prediction mechanisms, i.e., label propagation and feature transformation, which naturally preserves structure-based and feature-based prior knowledge, respectively. In specific, we design the student model as a trainable combination of parameterized label propagation and feature transformation modules. As a result, the learned student can benefit from both prior knowledge and the knowledge in GNN teachers for more effective predictions. Moreover, the learned student model has a more interpretable prediction process than GNNs. We conduct experiments on five public benchmark datasets and employ seven GNN models including GCN, GAT, APPNP, SAGE, SGC, GCNII and GLP as the teacher models. Experimental results show that the learned student model can consistently outperform its corresponding teacher model by 1.4% - 4.7% on average. Code and data are available at https://github.com/BUPT-GAMMA/CPF

papers_seen.author: Suarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Path to Compact Deep Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, practical approach for turning large, high-performing deep models into smaller, faster models suitable for real-world deployment. Beyond pure compression, KD serves as a flexible training paradigm that can be combined with pre-training, privacy-preserving workflows, and architecture-aware mimicry to preserve task performance while meeting latency, memory, and device constraints. A pragmatic KD pipeline aligns the choice of distillation signal, teacher design, student pretraining, and data strategy to the deployment context.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical, flexible approach for turning large, high-performing deep and pretrained NLP models into smaller, faster models suitable for real-world deployment. The literature shows KD operates via multiple signals (soft targets, intermediate features, attention or relational structure), multiple workflows (data-driven, data-free, multi-stage, multi-teacher), and often in combination with orthogonal compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical work demonstrates that properly designed distillation pipelines can recover most of a teacher's utility in a much smaller footprint, but success depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity, addressing data limitations and privacy constraints, and engineering choices such as layer mapping, augmentation, and progressive or curriculum-driven training.

papers_seen.author: Ortiz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Context-Sensitive Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic strategy for compressing large deep and NLP models into compact, deployable students. Rather than a single recipe, KD functions as a toolbox: it can transfer softened outputs, intermediate representations, attention maps, or relational signals; be combined with architecture search, pruning, or quantization; and operate with or without original training data. KD delivers substantial reductions in size and latency with modest performance loss when methods and signals are chosen to match student capacity, task requirements, and deployment constraints. However, KD is context-sensitive: success depends on handling teacher–student mismatch, robustness and fairness concerns, data availability, and optimization choices. The most reliable pipelines therefore combine multiple distillation signals, data-aware strategies, and targeted remedies for limits such as bias transfer and rare-token degradation.

papers_seen.author: Henson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal knowledge. Across vision, language, and generative domains, methods range from matching teacher soft targets to aligning intermediate representations, synthesizing surrogate data when originals are unavailable, and coordinating multi-teacher or online protocols. Practical pipelines commonly combine distillation with pruning, quantization, or architecture search to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Effectiveness depends on student capacity, the choice of distilled signals, data availability, and attention to robustness and fairness; these trade-offs guide ongoing research and engineering practice.

papers_seen.author: Aguirre
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques transfer information from large, high-capacity teacher models to smaller student models to reduce model size, latency, and deployment cost while retaining much of the teacher's utility. Methods vary in what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, ensembles), how training data is used or synthesized, and whether distillation is combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Across vision and NLP tasks, distillation enables practical deployment of compact models but requires careful handling of representation mismatch, data availability, optimization schedules, and potential amplification of teacher errors or biases.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible paradigm for producing compact models that meet real-world constraints while preserving much of the performance of large teachers. When properly designed, KD extends beyond matching soft labels to include feature- and layer-level transfers, pre-training of small architectures, multi-stage curricula, and coordination with architecture search and other compression techniques. Careful attention to data, teacher–student capacity, and deployment objectives turns KD from a heuristic into a reliable engineering approach for compressing deep and NLP models.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge distillation from multi-modal to mono-modal segmentation networks
papers_seen.abstract: The joint use of multiple imaging modalities for medical image segmentation has been widely studied in recent years. The fusion of information from different modalities has demonstrated to improve the segmentation accuracy, with respect to mono-modal segmentations, in several applications. However, acquiring multiple modalities is usually not possible in a clinical setting due to a limited number of physicians and scanners, and to limit costs and scan time. Most of the time, only one modality is acquired. In this paper, we propose KD-Net, a framework to transfer knowledge from a trained multi-modal network (teacher) to a mono-modal one (student). The proposed method is an adaptation of the generalized distillation framework where the student network is trained on a subset (1 modality) of the teacher's inputs (n modalities). We illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in brain tumor segmentation with the BraTS 2018 dataset. Using different architectures, we show that the student network effectively learns from the teacher and always outperforms the baseline mono-modal network in terms of segmentation accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Graph-less Neural Networks: Teaching Old MLPs New Tricks via Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are popular for graph machine learning and have shown great results on wide node classification tasks. Yet, they are less popular for practical deployments in the industry owing to their scalability challenges incurred by data dependency. Namely, GNN inference depends on neighbor nodes multiple hops away from the target, and fetching them burdens latency-constrained applications. Existing inference acceleration methods like pruning and quantization can speed up GNNs by reducing Multiplication-and-ACcumulation (MAC) operations, but the improvements are limited given the data dependency is not resolved. Conversely, multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs) have no graph dependency and infer much faster than GNNs, even though they are less accurate than GNNs for node classification in general. Motivated by these complementary strengths and weaknesses, we bring GNNs and MLPs together via knowledge distillation (KD). Our work shows that the performance of MLPs can be improved by large margins with GNN KD. We call the distilled MLPs Graph-less Neural Networks (GLNNs) as they have no inference graph dependency. We show that GLNNs with competitive accuracy infer faster than GNNs by 146X-273X and faster than other acceleration methods by 14X-27X. Under a production setting involving both transductive and inductive predictions across 7 datasets, GLNN accuracies improve over stand-alone MLPs by 12.36% on average and match GNNs on 6/7 datasets. Comprehensive analysis shows when and why GLNNs can achieve competitive accuracies to GNNs and suggests GLNN as a handy choice for latency-constrained applications.

papers_seen.author: Bush
papers_seen.title: Multi-Label Image Classification via Knowledge Distillation from Weakly-Supervised Detection
papers_seen.abstract: Multi-label image classification is a fundamental but challenging task towards general visual understanding. Existing methods found the region-level cues (e.g., features from RoIs) can facilitate multi-label classification. Nevertheless, such methods usually require laborious object-level annotations (i.e., object labels and bounding boxes) for effective learning of the object-level visual features. In this paper, we propose a novel and efficient deep framework to boost multi-label classification by distilling knowledge from weakly-supervised detection task without bounding box annotations. Specifically, given the image-level annotations, (1) we first develop a weakly-supervised detection (WSD) model, and then (2) construct an end-to-end multi-label image classification framework augmented by a knowledge distillation module that guides the classification model by the WSD model according to the class-level predictions for the whole image and the object-level visual features for object RoIs. The WSD model is the teacher model and the classification model is the student model. After this cross-task knowledge distillation, the performance of the classification model is significantly improved and the efficiency is maintained since the WSD model can be safely discarded in the test phase. Extensive experiments on two large-scale datasets (MS-COCO and NUS-WIDE) show that our framework achieves superior performances over the state-of-the-art methods on both performance and efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Recent Findings
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information from teacher models. Across vision, language, and cross-modal tasks, KD is used both as a stand-alone compression method and in combination with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Practical strategies include logit (soft-label) matching, feature-level imitation, multi-teacher schemes, and data- or label-synthesis when original training data are unavailable. Empirical work shows that distillation can recover most of a teacher's performance while enabling much smaller and faster models, but outcomes depend strongly on choices such as teacher quality, the form of distilled signals, augmentation and synthetic-data generation, and whether low-precision or domain-specific constraints apply.

papers_seen.author: Hamilton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, adaptable approach for compressing large deep models into compact students that meet real-world constraints on latency, memory, and deployment. When matched to task needs and combined with representation-aware objectives, data strategies, and robustness or privacy-aware adaptations, KD enables small models to retain much of teachers' performance across modalities. However, KD is context-sensitive: teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and the chosen distillation signal determine outcomes. A pragmatic pipeline blends logit and feature matching, targeted data augmentation or synthesis, and complementary compression methods to achieve robust, efficient deployment.

papers_seen.author: Hahn
papers_seen.title: PKD: General Distillation Framework for Object Detectors via Pearson Correlation Coefficient
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation(KD) is a widely-used technique to train compact models in object detection. However, there is still a lack of study on how to distill between heterogeneous detectors. In this paper, we empirically find that better FPN features from a heterogeneous teacher detector can help the student although their detection heads and label assignments are different. However, directly aligning the feature maps to distill detectors suffers from two problems. First, the difference in feature magnitude between the teacher and the student could enforce overly strict constraints on the student. Second, the FPN stages and channels with large feature magnitude from the teacher model could dominate the gradient of distillation loss, which will overwhelm the effects of other features in KD and introduce much noise. To address the above issues, we propose to imitate features with Pearson Correlation Coefficient to focus on the relational information from the teacher and relax constraints on the magnitude of the features. Our method consistently outperforms the existing detection KD methods and works for both homogeneous and heterogeneous student-teacher pairs. Furthermore, it converges faster. With a powerful MaskRCNN-Swin detector as the teacher, ResNet-50 based RetinaNet and FCOS achieve 41.5% and 43.9% mAP on COCO2017, which are 4.1\% and 4.8\% higher than the baseline, respectively.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Design Principles
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely applicable approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. KD achieves favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-offs across modalities when practitioners choose what form of teacher knowledge to transfer, how to map layers and representations, and how to handle limited or private data. However, KD is not plug-and-play: outcomes depend heavily on teacher quality, distilled signals, data availability, and task-specific constraints. Thoughtful combination of feature-level objectives, task-aware layer selection, data-synthesis or privacy-preserving queries, and targeted curricula yields robust compressed models ready for real-world deployment.

papers_seen.author: Hahn
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression strategies are widely used to produce smaller, faster models by transferring knowledge from larger or ensemble teachers to compact students. These techniques span supervised distillation, self-distillation, data-free and adversarial approaches, layer- and task-aware mappings, and distributed/online schemes. Empirical work shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance across modalities (classification, detection, generation, and language tasks) while enabling practical deployment; theoretical and practical challenges remain around data dependence, teacher imperfection, robustness, and optimal student–teacher alignment.

papers_seen.author: Abbott
papers_seen.title: Compressing Deep Graph Neural Networks via Adversarial Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep graph neural networks (GNNs) have been shown to be expressive for modeling graph-structured data. Nevertheless, the over-stacked architecture of deep graph models makes it difficult to deploy and rapidly test on mobile or embedded systems. To compress over-stacked GNNs, knowledge distillation via a teacher-student architecture turns out to be an effective technique, where the key step is to measure the discrepancy between teacher and student networks with predefined distance functions. However, using the same distance for graphs of various structures may be unfit, and the optimal distance formulation is hard to determine. To tackle these problems, we propose a novel Adversarial Knowledge Distillation framework for graph models named GraphAKD, which adversarially trains a discriminator and a generator to adaptively detect and decrease the discrepancy. Specifically, noticing that the well-captured inter-node and inter-class correlations favor the success of deep GNNs, we propose to criticize the inherited knowledge from node-level and class-level views with a trainable discriminator. The discriminator distinguishes between teacher knowledge and what the student inherits, while the student GNN works as a generator and aims to fool the discriminator. To our best knowledge, GraphAKD is the first to introduce adversarial training to knowledge distillation in graph domains. Experiments on node-level and graph-level classification benchmarks demonstrate that GraphAKD improves the student performance by a large margin. The results imply that GraphAKD can precisely transfer knowledge from a complicated teacher GNN to a compact student GNN.

papers_seen.author: Harrell
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques have become central tools to deploy high-capacity deep models in latency-, memory-, privacy-, and compute-constrained settings. Across vision, language, graph, and multimodal domains, practitioners use teacher-student training, feature-level transfer, data-free distillation, and hybrid pipelines that combine pruning or architecture search with distillation. Work in this area balances fidelity to teacher models, robustness, and efficiency, and explores trade-offs such as reliance on original training data, communication overhead in federated settings, and the benefits of designing students or student-friendly teachers. The literature shows repeated success of KD when tailored to the task and constraints, while also revealing limitations under severe data heterogeneity or adversarial settings.

papers_seen.author: Chapman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, faster students by transferring useful predictive behavior, representations, or inductive biases. A diverse set of distillation strategies—matching soft logits, aligning intermediate features or attention maps, self-distillation, multi-teacher schemes, data-free synthesis, and task-aware adaptations—has been developed to preserve performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Practice-oriented work emphasizes matching the distillation technique to the task, addressing data or privacy limits via synthetic examples or adversarial generation, and combining distillation with architecture and optimization adjustments to close remaining gaps. Empirical successes across language, vision, speech, graphs, and ranking systems show substantial speed and size improvements, though limits remain around distribution shift, teacher–student mismatch, and heterogeneous or federated data settings.

papers_seen.author: Hicks
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large models into smaller ones by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or other structural knowledge from teacher(s) to student(s). Approaches range from classic logit-matching to feature- and channel-wise transfer, multi-teacher schemes, self-distillation, data-free adversarial methods, and adaptations for distributed or heterogeneous settings. Empirical work shows that properly designed distillation can preserve much of teacher performance while greatly reducing size and latency; practical success depends on choices like what form of knowledge to transfer, whether and how to augment or synthesize data, and how to handle heterogeneous compute or domain shifts.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Tool for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a flexible, high-impact way to compress large models into smaller, efficient ones while retaining most task performance. Modern KD methods extend beyond matching final logits to include layer- and feature-level imitation, task-aware selection of distilled information, data-free or few-shot regimes, and multi-teacher or self-distillation strategies. When combined with architecture-aware compression or search, KD enables task-adaptive, privacy-conscious, and efficient deployment of deep models in real-world NLP and vision applications.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: Improved Feature Distillation via Projector Ensemble
papers_seen.abstract: In knowledge distillation, previous feature distillation methods mainly focus on the design of loss functions and the selection of the distilled layers, while the effect of the feature projector between the student and the teacher remains under-explored. In this paper, we first discuss a plausible mechanism of the projector with empirical evidence and then propose a new feature distillation method based on a projector ensemble for further performance improvement. We observe that the student network benefits from a projector even if the feature dimensions of the student and the teacher are the same. Training a student backbone without a projector can be considered as a multi-task learning process, namely achieving discriminative feature extraction for classification and feature matching between the student and the teacher for distillation at the same time. We hypothesize and empirically verify that without a projector, the student network tends to overfit the teacher's feature distributions despite having different architecture and weights initialization. This leads to degradation on the quality of the student's deep features that are eventually used in classification. Adding a projector, on the other hand, disentangles the two learning tasks and helps the student network to focus better on the main feature extraction task while still being able to utilize teacher features as a guidance through the projector. Motivated by the positive effect of the projector in feature distillation, we propose an ensemble of projectors to further improve the quality of student features. Experimental results on different datasets with a series of teacher-student pairs illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

papers_seen.author: Cohen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Strategy for Model Compression and Adaptation in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible approach to produce compact models that retain much of the performance of larger models. Beyond simple compression, KD can transfer inductive biases, enable domain adaptation and vocabulary specialization, support privacy-preserving and federated scenarios, work without access to original data, and improve robustness and feature quality when carefully applied. When combined with targeted techniques — feature mimicking, weighted soft labels, projector layers, or adversarial robustness objectives — KD becomes a unifying toolkit to meet latency, capacity, and privacy constraints in real-world NLP and deep learning deployments.

papers_seen.author: Marshall
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely used approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Across modalities, KD transfers predictive behavior and internal representations using a variety of targets and protocols (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, multi-stage or online schemes) and composes well with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, and how to handle data or privacy constraints. KD enables many deployment goals (reduced latency/memory, domain adaptation, privacy-aware training), but its effectiveness is limited by optimization dynamics, teacher–student mismatch, distribution shift for synthetic data, and the potential transfer of undesirable biases.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Central Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely applicable method for compressing large models into smaller, deployable ones across NLP and other deep learning domains. KD preserves much of teacher performance while enabling faster inference, smaller footprints, and flexible deployment; however, it has failure modes related to data dependence, teacher quality, and rare-token fidelity. Effective use of KD therefore treats it as a toolbox—combining multi-teacher schedules, data-aware augmentation, representation-level objectives, and privacy-aware protocols—to produce robust, task-appropriate compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression techniques have become central tools for reducing the computational and memory footprint of large neural networks while retaining much of their performance. Work in this area has diversified beyond the original teacher-to-student soft-label matching to include self-distillation, online and distributed distillation, feature- and representation-level transfer, multi-teacher selection, and data-augmentation-aware distillation. These methods are applied across modalities (vision, speech, NLP, and graphs) and contexts (domain adaptation, continual learning, large-scale training, and on-device deployment), yielding a range of practical trade-offs between accuracy, latency, and model size. Current advances emphasize richer forms of knowledge (internal representations, relational signals), adaptive teacher weighting, and training-time strategies that improve student generalization, but challenges remain in reliably transferring rare-word or low-frequency behavior, aligning heterogeneous architectures, and scaling distillation to extremely large datasets and models.

papers_seen.author: Waller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core of Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible technique for compressing large models into smaller, deployable ones for deep learning and NLP. When applied as part of an integrated compression pipeline it reduces inference cost and memory while retaining much of teacher performance. Achieving robust, fair, and private deployments requires combining KD with architecture-aware design, appropriate data strategies (including data-free alternatives), careful choice of distilled signals, and systematic evaluation of robustness and bias.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, widely applicable strategy for producing compact, deployable models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. KD works across modalities and deployment constraints, and supports extensions for data-free, federated, and privacy-sensitive settings. However, realizing KD’s full potential requires careful choices about what signals to transfer (logits, features, relational signals), how to align teacher and student architectures, and how to mitigate transferred harms such as bias or degraded rare-token behavior. When combined with complementary methods (augmentation, layer-aware mapping, multi-teacher ensembles, or differential-privacy mechanisms), KD becomes a flexible core of effective compression pipelines for real-world NLP and deep-learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Ray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Multifaceted, Practical Engine for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best understood not as a single trick of copying a stronger model but as a multifaceted training paradigm that can compress, regularize, and adapt models for deployment. When practitioners choose the right distillation signals (soft targets, intermediate features, attention mappings), tailor objectives to data and privacy constraints, and combine KD with complementary techniques (architecture-aware design, quantization, data synthesis), they can produce compact students that approach teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and robustness requirements. Effective use of KD requires attention to representation alignment, optimization schedules, and the constraints of the deployment setting.

papers_seen.author: Russell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. As a practical compression primitive it integrates naturally with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data-synthesis techniques to meet deployment constraints across vision, language, speech, and graph domains. KD is not a plug-and-play cure—its success depends on what signals are transferred, how teacher and student are aligned, and how data or privacy constraints are handled—but when designed carefully it delivers an effective balance of accuracy, robustness, and efficiency for production systems.

papers_seen.author: Frost
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, versatile approach for turning large pre-trained models into smaller, deployable ones. By transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from teachers to students, KD enables substantial reductions in size and inference cost while retaining much of the original performance. Practical KD pipelines combine choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to supplement distillation with complementary compression and data strategies. Despite clear practical benefits, KD requires careful method selection to handle capacity mismatch, data scarcity, distribution shift, and risks of transferring teacher biases; a disciplined pipeline and evaluation strategy are therefore essential for reliable deployment.

papers_seen.author: Hawkins
papers_seen.title: A Fast Knowledge Distillation Framework for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: While Knowledge Distillation (KD) has been recognized as a useful tool in many visual tasks, such as supervised classification and self-supervised representation learning, the main drawback of a vanilla KD framework is its mechanism, which consumes the majority of the computational overhead on forwarding through the giant teacher networks, making the entire learning procedure inefficient and costly. ReLabel, a recently proposed solution, suggests creating a label map for the entire image. During training, it receives the cropped region-level label by RoI aligning on a pre-generated entire label map, allowing for efficient supervision generation without having to pass through the teachers many times. However, as the KD teachers are from conventional multi-crop training, there are various mismatches between the global label-map and region-level label in this technique, resulting in performance deterioration. In this study, we present a Fast Knowledge Distillation (FKD) framework that replicates the distillation training phase and generates soft labels using the multi-crop KD approach, while training faster than ReLabel since no post-processes such as RoI align and softmax operations are used. When conducting multi-crop in the same image for data loading, our FKD is even more efficient than the traditional image classification framework. On ImageNet-1K, we obtain 79.8% with ResNet-50, outperforming ReLabel by ~1.0% while being faster. On the self-supervised learning task, we also show that FKD has an efficiency advantage. Our project page: http://zhiqiangshen.com/projects/FKD/index.html, source code and models are available at: https://github.com/szq0214/FKD.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature and flexible approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable ones. When combined with careful choices—such as pre-training compact students, data-free distillation for privacy, adaptive multi-teacher strategies, feature-level imitation, and teacher-side learning—KD can deliver strong task performance with much smaller inference cost. However, KD is not a panacea: optimization gaps between teacher and student, propagation of teacher biases, and dataset mismatches can limit gains unless explicitly addressed. A pragmatic KD pipeline therefore integrates algorithmic innovations and fairness/optimization checks to realize both efficiency and reliable behavior in production NLP and deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Bush
papers_seen.title: Practical and Principled Knowledge Distillation for NLP: Task-aware, Teacher-aware, and System-level Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical pillar for compressing large deep and language models into deployable, efficient students. When applied thoughtfully—aligning distilled information to the downstream task, designing or adapting teachers with student constraints in mind, and combining KD with complementary compression techniques—KD can recover much of the teacher's capability while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is not a panacea: optimization difficulties, dataset mismatch, and distributional issues can limit gains unless addressed explicitly. A principled KD pipeline therefore includes task-aware selection of distilled signals, teacher-student co-design, and system-level techniques (pruning/quantization or data-free synthesis) to achieve robust, efficient models for production NLP settings.

papers_seen.author: Carney
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from a heuristic for shrinking large models into a broad set of techniques that enable smaller, faster, and often more robust or interpretable models for deep learning and NLP. Empirical and conceptual work shows KD operates through multiple mechanisms — soft-target regularization, transfer of internal representations, and optimization/inductive-bias alignment — and that design choices about what to transfer, how to supply training data, and how to reconcile teacher imperfections with student capacity determine success. KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and careful engineering (data selection, projectors, curriculum), but persistent challenges remain in heterogeneous architectures, data-limited or privacy-sensitive settings, and rare-token behavior.

papers_seen.author: Calderon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained deep models deliver strong performance across vision and language tasks but are often too large or slow for real-world deployment. Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression strategies provide practical ways to transfer behavior from high-capacity teacher models to smaller students, enabling reduced storage, faster inference, and deployment on constrained devices. Research has developed a range of KD formulations—logit-level supervision, intermediate representation matching, layer mapping, multi-teacher fusion, and data-free distillation—alongside empirical and theoretical analyses that explain when and why distillation helps. The literature also shows KD’s effectiveness in NLP for compressing models like BERT into lightweight architectures without additional data, and highlights open challenges such as heterogeneous teachers, data privacy, and preserving task-specific inductive biases.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: The Case for Knowledge Distillation: Versatile Compression for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and powerful approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, more efficient ones. Beyond simple size reduction, KD enables transfer of capabilities across modalities, supports domain adaptation, improves deployment in resource-constrained or privacy-sensitive settings, and can be adapted to distributed training. However, benefits are not automatic: careful design of teacher-student alignment, training data, and distillation objectives is required to preserve task performance and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Harrell
papers_seen.title: No One Left Behind: Inclusive Federated Learning over Heterogeneous Devices
papers_seen.abstract: Federated learning (FL) is an important paradigm for training global models from decentralized data in a privacy-preserving way. Existing FL methods usually assume the global model can be trained on any participating client. However, in real applications, the devices of clients are usually heterogeneous, and have different computing power. Although big models like BERT have achieved huge success in AI, it is difficult to apply them to heterogeneous FL with weak clients. The straightforward solutions like removing the weak clients or using a small model to fit all clients will lead to some problems, such as under-representation of dropped clients and inferior accuracy due to data loss or limited model representation ability. In this work, we propose InclusiveFL, a client-inclusive federated learning method to handle this problem. The core idea of InclusiveFL is to assign models of different sizes to clients with different computing capabilities, bigger models for powerful clients and smaller ones for weak clients. We also propose an effective method to share the knowledge among multiple local models with different sizes. In this way, all the clients can participate in the model learning in FL, and the final model can be big and powerful enough. Besides, we propose a momentum knowledge distillation method to better transfer knowledge in big models on powerful clients to the small models on weak clients. Extensive experiments on many real-world benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in learning accurate models from clients with heterogeneous devices under the FL framework.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Mitigating Gender Bias in Distilled Language Models via Counterfactual Role Reversal
papers_seen.abstract: Language models excel at generating coherent text, and model compression techniques such as knowledge distillation have enabled their use in resource-constrained settings. However, these models can be biased in multiple ways, including the unfounded association of male and female genders with gender-neutral professions. Therefore, knowledge distillation without any fairness constraints may preserve or exaggerate the teacher model's biases onto the distilled model. To this end, we present a novel approach to mitigate gender disparity in text generation by learning a fair model during knowledge distillation. We propose two modifications to the base knowledge distillation based on counterfactual role reversal$\unicode{x2014}$modifying teacher probabilities and augmenting the training set. We evaluate gender polarity across professions in open-ended text generated from the resulting distilled and finetuned GPT$\unicode{x2012}$2 models and demonstrate a substantial reduction in gender disparity with only a minor compromise in utility. Finally, we observe that language models that reduce gender polarity in language generation do not improve embedding fairness or downstream classification fairness.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. KD variants—soft-target matching, intermediate-representation matching, self- and online-distillation, and data-free (zero-shot) synthesis—enable latency, memory, and privacy gains across vision and language tasks. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: its success depends on what signals are distilled, teacher quality, data availability or synthesis, and pipeline choices (layer mapping, curricula, and complementary compression). I argue KD should be treated as the central component of compression pipelines, applied with task-aware design and combined with other methods to manage its limitations and maximize deployment utility.

papers_seen.author: Sanchez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Evidence, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical approach for compressing large neural networks by training smaller student models to reproduce useful behavior of larger teacher models. Across vision, language, speech and graph settings, KD variants—matching softened teacher logits, aligning intermediate features, adversarial and contrastive objectives, multi-stage or multi-teacher pipelines, and data- or privacy-aware synthesis—enable large reductions in model size and latency while retaining much of teacher performance. Realizing these gains requires task-aware choices about what to transfer, how to map layers between architectures, how to select or synthesize training data, and how to balance regularization from soft targets with student capacity and robustness considerations.

papers_seen.author: House
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Principled, Practical, and Context-Sensitive Toolbox for NLP Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an essential approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable systems. When treated as a flexible framework rather than a single recipe, KD can preserve much of teacher performance while meeting constraints of latency, memory, privacy, and domain heterogeneity. However, its success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to adapt to new domains or architectures, and how to select or synthesize training signals for the student.

papers_seen.author: Ferrell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Powerful, Flexible, but Context-Sensitive for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques are practical, widely applicable tools for shrinking large models and transferring capability to smaller models. KD can preserve performance while reducing inference cost, enable cross-modal and cross-task transfer, and be adapted to constrained settings (few-shot, edge devices). However, KD is not a plug-and-play cure: its benefits depend on what is distilled (logits vs. features vs. internal structure), teacher-student design, data regime, and optimization choices. Careful method design — including feature-based objectives, intermediate-layer alignment, self-distillation or meta-learned teachers, and task-aware curricula — is required to realize robust gains without amplifying teacher errors.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: SEED: Self-supervised Distillation For Visual Representation
papers_seen.abstract: This paper is concerned with self-supervised learning for small models. The problem is motivated by our empirical studies that while the widely used contrastive self-supervised learning method has shown great progress on large model training, it does not work well for small models. To address this problem, we propose a new learning paradigm, named SElf-SupErvised Distillation (SEED), where we leverage a larger network (as Teacher) to transfer its representational knowledge into a smaller architecture (as Student) in a self-supervised fashion. Instead of directly learning from unlabeled data, we train a student encoder to mimic the similarity score distribution inferred by a teacher over a set of instances. We show that SEED dramatically boosts the performance of small networks on downstream tasks. Compared with self-supervised baselines, SEED improves the top-1 accuracy from 42.2% to 67.6% on EfficientNet-B0 and from 36.3% to 68.2% on MobileNet-v3-Large on the ImageNet-1k dataset.

papers_seen.author: Jackson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a primary practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, more efficient ones for deployment in constrained environments. KD techniques range from matching softened output distributions to aligning intermediate representations, transferring relational signals, and operating in data-limited or privacy-sensitive regimes via synthesized or public data. When combined with complementary compression methods (quantization, pruning, architecture search), KD enables substantial reductions in latency and memory while often retaining most of the teacher’s performance. Persistent challenges include understanding the mechanisms of transfer, handling student–teacher capacity mismatch, preserving rare-token or long-tail behaviors, and ensuring robustness and fairness under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques aim to transfer predictive performance and internal representations from large, expensive teacher models to smaller, faster student models. Work in this area spans theoretical analyses, practical compression recipes for language and vision models, approaches that avoid access to original training data, and methods that target robustness, privacy, or device heterogeneity. The field balances trade-offs among student capacity, teacher imperfection, data availability, and downstream task requirements, producing a range of techniques—logit-level distillation, layer-wise and module-level matching, progressive replacement, data-free generation, and combined compression with low-precision numerics—that are evaluated across tasks from BERT compression to multimodal and 3D detection. This synthesis summarizes prevailing methods, motivations, and recurring challenges emerging from recent literature.

papers_seen.author: Schultz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Design Principles
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic and versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD can transfer predictive behavior, intermediate representations, and inductive biases across modalities and architectures, enabling large reductions in latency and memory with modest performance loss when applied thoughtfully. Realizing KD's benefits in production requires attention to what signals are transferred, how teachers and students are aligned, data selection or synthesis strategies, and safeguards for robustness and privacy. KD should be treated as a central component of compression pipelines but combined with complementary techniques and careful evaluation to address its known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Cardenas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable and production-ready approach to compressing large models into smaller, faster models while retaining much of their performance. KD supports multiple transfer targets (soft logits, intermediate features, relational signals) and can be adapted to domain, data, and deployment constraints. When combined with complementary compression techniques and matched to student capacity and data availability, KD yields strong trade-offs between accuracy, latency, and resource usage; however, it requires careful engineering to avoid pitfalls such as representation mismatch, teacher error propagation, and data- or distribution-specific failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Harris
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students while retaining much of the teacher's behavior. A growing literature shows KD can act via soft-target matching, intermediate representation transfer, attention- or relation-based losses, self-distillation, online and data-free variants, and can be combined with pruning, layer-skipping, quantization, or architecture search. KD delivers strong empirical gains across modalities (vision, language, recommendation, and graphs) when its signal, data strategy, and optimization schedule are chosen to match the deployment constraints. Important open issues remain — handling rare or low-frequency behaviors, adapting across domains and heterogeneous architectures, and operating under strict privacy or data-availability constraints — but pragmatic pipelines that mix KD with complementary compression tools offer the most reliable path to deployable compact models.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Design Principles
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely applicable approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. KD achieves favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-offs across modalities when practitioners choose what form of teacher knowledge to transfer, how to map layers and representations, and how to handle limited or private data. However, KD is not plug-and-play: outcomes depend heavily on teacher quality, distilled signals, data availability, and task-specific constraints. Thoughtful combination of feature-level objectives, task-aware layer selection, data-synthesis or privacy-preserving queries, and targeted curricula yields robust compressed models ready for real-world deployment.
