papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation for Practical NLP Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical, flexible pathway to deploy high-performing deep learning and NLP models under real-world constraints. By transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or inductive biases from large or multi-modal teachers to smaller students, distillation enables task- and domain-specific compression, faster inference, privacy-preserving distributed training, and architectural simplification. Effective distillation requires methods that match the target deployment needs—task-awareness, layer alignment, careful use of data augmentation and teacher ensembles, and scaling strategies for large datasets and distributed settings. When designed deliberately, distillation yields compressed models that retain much of the teacher's capability while meeting latency, size, and privacy requirements.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques provide practical routes to deploy large, high-performance neural models in resource- constrained or latency-sensitive settings. Methods vary in what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, relational structure), how training data is used or synthesized, and whether compression is task-agnostic or task-adaptive. In natural language tasks, KD has enabled dramatic size and speed gains for large pretrained models (e.g., BERT) as well as the feasibility of simple architectures that retain most of the original performance. Despite empirical success, challenges remain: choosing what to transfer for maximal utility, constructing or selecting suitable training examples, handling heterogeneous or private data (federated or data-free settings), and designing teacher-student curricula or architectures that improve transfer. Emerging directions include task-adaptive compression, many-to-many layer alignment, multi-teacher and teacher-aware training, and principled approaches to data selection or generation during distillation.

papers_seen.author: Abbott
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Issues
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision, speech, and NLP. Approaches vary from traditional teacher-to-student soft-label transfer to data-free (zero-shot) distillation, online and mutual distillation among peers, meta-learned teachers, and internal-representation matching. Empirical work shows KD can improve student generalization, speed, and footprint but also introduces dataset-specific artifacts (e.g., degraded modeling of low-frequency tokens) and optimization mismatches that require complementary strategies such as exposing raw data, augmentations, adaptive teacher selection, or distillation of intermediate representations. Practical systems (federated or large-scale distributed training) benefit from variants like online or zero-shot distillation to respect privacy and device heterogeneity, while research continues to study why KD works and how to align teacher and student beyond output probabilities.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression seek to transfer performance and desirable properties from large, expensive models to smaller, efficient ones. The literature spans techniques that match outputs (soft labels), intermediate representations, or training dynamics; methods that operate with or without access to original data; and approaches that adapt compression to tasks, modalities, or deployment constraints. Empirical results show that discriminative matching of representations, careful layer mappings, adversarial data synthesis, and task-aware architecture search all improve the trade-offs between size, speed, and accuracy in both vision and language settings. Practical developments also emphasize teacher design, robustness transfer, and strategies for low-data or privacy-constrained scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Walters
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and inductive biases from large teacher models to smaller student models so they can meet real-world constraints (latency, memory, privacy). Methods vary by what is transferred (soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention, relational signals), how data are used or synthesized, and whether distillation is combined with other compression tools or automated search. Empirically, KD often preserves much of teacher performance while enabling substantial reductions in size and inference cost, but practical success depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity, addressing data or privacy limits, and adapting teachers or objectives to propagate desired properties such as robustness and generalization.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Task-Aware Path to Model Compression in NLP and Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a flexible and practical framework for compressing large models and transferring capabilities to smaller ones. When applied thoughtfully — using layer-aware alignment, attention-guided feature matching, dynamic multi-teacher strategies, and privacy- or deployment-aware protocols — distillation enables substantial speedups, reduced footprint, and cross-modal or cross-device applicability with small drops (or even gains) in task performance. Distillation is not a plug-and-play cure: optimization challenges, teacher-student mismatch, and task-specific redundancy mean methods must be adapted to the target architecture and data regime to realize consistent benefits.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central technique for compressing large deep learning models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teachers' performance. Across vision, language, speech, and recommendation tasks, researchers combine KD with architectural compression, pre-training, privacy mechanisms, and data-free approaches to address inference cost, dataset availability, and domain-specific challenges. Empirical work shows that careful choices about what to transfer (logits, features, layers), how to train teachers and students, and how to incorporate task or data constraints strongly determine final student quality.

papers_seen.author: Zuniga
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Composable Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable and practical technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster, and more deployable student models. KD is effective across modalities (vision, speech, language, graphs) and settings (task-specific compression, data-limited or data-free transfer), and its strengths are amplified when combined with complementary methods such as architecture-aware replacement, pruning, low-precision numerics, adaptive teacher design, and careful input-side practices. To realize robust and fair compressed models, practitioners should treat KD as one tool within a pipeline: design student-friendly teachers, account for data constraints, use augmentation and curriculum where helpful, and combine KD with orthogonal compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Orr
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information beyond hard labels. KD has evolved from simple soft-target matching into a flexible toolkit that includes intermediate-representation alignment, self- and multi-teacher schemes, data-free and online protocols, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Practical application of KD requires matching the distilled signals and workflows to student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints; addressing failure modes such as transferred biases or poor handling of low-frequency phenomena; and integrating distillation into a broader compression pipeline to meet latency, memory, and privacy goals.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Confidence-Aware Multi-Teacher Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is initially introduced to utilize additional supervision from a single teacher model for the student model training. To boost the student performance, some recent variants attempt to exploit diverse knowledge sources from multiple teachers. However, existing studies mainly integrate knowledge from diverse sources by averaging over multiple teacher predictions or combining them using other various label-free strategies, which may mislead student in the presence of low-quality teacher predictions. To tackle this problem, we propose Confidence-Aware Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation (CA-MKD), which adaptively assigns sample-wise reliability for each teacher prediction with the help of ground-truth labels, with those teacher predictions close to one-hot labels assigned large weights. Besides, CA-MKD incorporates intermediate layers to stable the knowledge transfer process. Extensive experiments show that our CA-MKD consistently outperforms all compared state-of-the-art methods across various teacher-student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Rice
papers_seen.title: CoReD: Generalizing Fake Media Detection with Continual Representation using Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Over the last few decades, artificial intelligence research has made tremendous strides, but it still heavily relies on fixed datasets in stationary environments. Continual learning is a growing field of research that examines how AI systems can learn sequentially from a continuous stream of linked data in the same way that biological systems do. Simultaneously, fake media such as deepfakes and synthetic face images have emerged as significant to current multimedia technologies. Recently, numerous method has been proposed which can detect deepfakes with high accuracy. However, they suffer significantly due to their reliance on fixed datasets in limited evaluation settings. Therefore, in this work, we apply continuous learning to neural networks' learning dynamics, emphasizing its potential to increase data efficiency significantly. We propose Continual Representation using Distillation (CoReD) method that employs the concept of Continual Learning (CL), Representation Learning (RL), and Knowledge Distillation (KD). We design CoReD to perform sequential domain adaptation tasks on new deepfake and GAN-generated synthetic face datasets, while effectively minimizing the catastrophic forgetting in a teacher-student model setting. Our extensive experimental results demonstrate that our method is efficient at domain adaptation to detect low-quality deepfakes videos and GAN-generated images from several datasets, outperforming the-state-of-art baseline methods.

papers_seen.author: Wolfe
papers_seen.title: Robust and Resource-Efficient Data-Free Knowledge Distillation by Generative Pseudo Replay
papers_seen.abstract: Data-Free Knowledge Distillation (KD) allows knowledge transfer from a trained neural network (teacher) to a more compact one (student) in the absence of original training data. Existing works use a validation set to monitor the accuracy of the student over real data and report the highest performance throughout the entire process. However, validation data may not be available at distillation time either, making it infeasible to record the student snapshot that achieved the peak accuracy. Therefore, a practical data-free KD method should be robust and ideally provide monotonically increasing student accuracy during distillation. This is challenging because the student experiences knowledge degradation due to the distribution shift of the synthetic data. A straightforward approach to overcome this issue is to store and rehearse the generated samples periodically, which increases the memory footprint and creates privacy concerns. We propose to model the distribution of the previously observed synthetic samples with a generative network. In particular, we design a Variational Autoencoder (VAE) with a training objective that is customized to learn the synthetic data representations optimally. The student is rehearsed by the generative pseudo replay technique, with samples produced by the VAE. Hence knowledge degradation can be prevented without storing any samples. Experiments on image classification benchmarks show that our method optimizes the expected value of the distilled model accuracy while eliminating the large memory overhead incurred by the sample-storing methods.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: Less is More: Task-aware Layer-wise Distillation for Language Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Layer-wise distillation is a powerful tool to compress large models (i.e. teacher models) into small ones (i.e., student models). The student distills knowledge from the teacher by mimicking the hidden representations of the teacher at every intermediate layer. However, layer-wise distillation is difficult. Since the student has a smaller model capacity than the teacher, it is often under-fitted. Furthermore, the hidden representations of the teacher contain redundant information that the student does not necessarily need for the target task's learning. To address these challenges, we propose a novel Task-aware layEr-wise Distillation (TED). TED designs task-aware filters to align the hidden representations of the student and the teacher at each layer. The filters select the knowledge that is useful for the target task from the hidden representations. As such, TED reduces the knowledge gap between the two models and helps the student to fit better on the target task. We evaluate TED in two scenarios: continual pre-training and fine-tuning. TED demonstrates significant and consistent improvements over existing distillation methods in both scenarios. Code is available at https://github.com/cliang1453/task-aware-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Abbott
papers_seen.title: Compressing Deep Graph Neural Networks via Adversarial Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep graph neural networks (GNNs) have been shown to be expressive for modeling graph-structured data. Nevertheless, the over-stacked architecture of deep graph models makes it difficult to deploy and rapidly test on mobile or embedded systems. To compress over-stacked GNNs, knowledge distillation via a teacher-student architecture turns out to be an effective technique, where the key step is to measure the discrepancy between teacher and student networks with predefined distance functions. However, using the same distance for graphs of various structures may be unfit, and the optimal distance formulation is hard to determine. To tackle these problems, we propose a novel Adversarial Knowledge Distillation framework for graph models named GraphAKD, which adversarially trains a discriminator and a generator to adaptively detect and decrease the discrepancy. Specifically, noticing that the well-captured inter-node and inter-class correlations favor the success of deep GNNs, we propose to criticize the inherited knowledge from node-level and class-level views with a trainable discriminator. The discriminator distinguishes between teacher knowledge and what the student inherits, while the student GNN works as a generator and aims to fool the discriminator. To our best knowledge, GraphAKD is the first to introduce adversarial training to knowledge distillation in graph domains. Experiments on node-level and graph-level classification benchmarks demonstrate that GraphAKD improves the student performance by a large margin. The results imply that GraphAKD can precisely transfer knowledge from a complicated teacher GNN to a compact student GNN.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Across vision, speech, and language tasks, KD has expanded from simple logit matching to a rich toolbox including feature- and layer-level imitation, self- and progressive-distillation, ensemble compression, data-free or zero-shot approaches, and federated protocols. Empirical work shows KD can yield compact models that retain much of teacher performance while reducing inference cost, but practical success depends on design choices about what to transfer, how to supply or synthesize data, and how to handle teacher–student mismatches and optimization challenges.

papers_seen.author: Davenport
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically proven approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of large teachers. KD methods—ranging from soft-label/logit matching to feature- and relation-level imitation—work across modalities and tasks and integrate naturally with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. However, maximizing KD’s benefits requires deliberate choices about what signals to transfer, how to supply or synthesize data, and how to align teacher and student architectures; left unaddressed, challenges such as representation misalignment, degraded rare-token behavior, and robustness or privacy losses can limit gains.

papers_seen.author: Wong
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Principled Path to Efficient, Adaptable, and Responsible NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is not merely a compression trick but a general framework that enables smaller or specialized models to inherit useful behaviors from larger teachers while controlling generalization, efficiency, and social impact. When combined with layer-wise and representation-level matching, task-aware architecture search, thoughtful input augmentation, and deployment-aware protocols, KD supports high-performance, resource-frugal NLP systems that can be adapted to heterogeneous devices and sensitive application contexts.

papers_seen.author: Gaines
papers_seen.title: AdaBERT: Task-Adaptive BERT Compression with Differentiable Neural Architecture Search
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained language models such as BERT have shown their effectiveness in various natural language processing tasks. However, the huge parameter size makes them difficult to be deployed in real-time applications that require quick inference with limited resources. Existing methods compress BERT into small models while such compression is task-independent, i.e., the same compressed BERT for all different downstream tasks. Motivated by the necessity and benefits of task-oriented BERT compression, we propose a novel compression method, AdaBERT, that leverages differentiable Neural Architecture Search to automatically compress BERT into task-adaptive small models for specific tasks. We incorporate a task-oriented knowledge distillation loss to provide search hints and an efficiency-aware loss as search constraints, which enables a good trade-off between efficiency and effectiveness for task-adaptive BERT compression. We evaluate AdaBERT on several NLP tasks, and the results demonstrate that those task-adaptive compressed models are 12.7x to 29.3x faster than BERT in inference time and 11.5x to 17.0x smaller in terms of parameter size, while comparable performance is maintained.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression strategies enable smaller, faster models to inherit performance from larger teachers by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or ensemble knowledge. Techniques range from logit-based soft-target distillation to feature- and attention-level mimicry, multi-teacher and task-adaptive pipelines, and methods that relax the need for original training data or strong teachers. Across computer vision and natural language processing tasks, distilled students can approach teacher accuracy while drastically reducing parameters and latency; complementary strategies such as careful pre-training of compact models and architecture search further improve trade-offs between efficiency and effectiveness. Key challenges remain in preserving rare-token behavior, aligning heterogeneous teacher–student inputs, and ensuring privacy and robustness during compression.

papers_seen.author: Brennan
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring learned behavior beyond hard labels. Over the past decade KD has evolved from logit-matching to a broad toolkit that includes representation- and feature-level imitation, flexible layer mappings, task-aware architecture search, and strategies for data-limited or deployment-constrained settings. Combining these techniques with careful teacher selection, sample or objective weighting, and deployment-aware choices (e.g., low-precision or privacy-preserving protocols) yields compact models that often retain much of the teacher's utility while meeting latency and resource constraints.

papers_seen.author: Carpenter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Practical, and Responsible Tool for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, widely applicable method for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. KD shines when combined with complementary compression techniques and data strategies, but its reliability depends on careful choices about what is transferred, how teachers and students are aligned, and how data or robustness constraints are handled. I argue KD should be treated as a central instrument in compression pipelines, used with explicit engineering and ethical practices to manage its limits.

papers_seen.author: Adkins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, broadly applicable strategy for shrinking large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students. KD can reproduce much of a teacher's task performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints; it also integrates naturally with complementary techniques (pretraining, data augmentation, multi-teacher supervision, and progressive module replacement). Realizing KD's full value in production requires attention to optimization gaps, dataset mismatch, and the risk of propagating teacher biases, and benefits from targeted extensions—feature-level objectives, adversarially-informed sample selection, and staged or progressive compression strategies.

papers_seen.author: Zuniga
papers_seen.title: Large scale distributed neural network training through online distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Techniques such as ensembling and distillation promise model quality improvements when paired with almost any base model. However, due to increased test-time cost (for ensembles) and increased complexity of the training pipeline (for distillation), these techniques are challenging to use in industrial settings. In this paper we explore a variant of distillation which is relatively straightforward to use as it does not require a complicated multi-stage setup or many new hyperparameters. Our first claim is that online distillation enables us to use extra parallelism to fit very large datasets about twice as fast. Crucially, we can still speed up training even after we have already reached the point at which additional parallelism provides no benefit for synchronous or asynchronous stochastic gradient descent. Two neural networks trained on disjoint subsets of the data can share knowledge by encouraging each model to agree with the predictions the other model would have made. These predictions can come from a stale version of the other model so they can be safely computed using weights that only rarely get transmitted. Our second claim is that online distillation is a cost-effective way to make the exact predictions of a model dramatically more reproducible. We support our claims using experiments on the Criteo Display Ad Challenge dataset, ImageNet, and the largest to-date dataset used for neural language modeling, containing $6\times 10^{11}$ tokens and based on the Common Crawl repository of web data.

papers_seen.author: Farmer
papers_seen.title: The Practical Case for Feature- and Representation-Aware Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile strategy for compressing large models into efficient students while retaining much of their accuracy. Beyond the classical logit-matching formulation, modern KD practices that match internal representations, use tailored projectors or selective sample strategies, and account for deployment constraints (e.g., no access to original data or adversarial threats) yield better student models across modalities and tasks. Combining these advances—feature mimicking, projector ensembles, selective distillation, data-free techniques, and robustness-aware training—produces compact models that are both performant and deployable.

papers_seen.author: Maddox
papers_seen.title: BERT-EMD: Many-to-Many Layer Mapping for BERT Compression with Earth Mover's Distance
papers_seen.abstract: Pre-trained language models (e.g., BERT) have achieved significant success in various natural language processing (NLP) tasks. However, high storage and computational costs obstruct pre-trained language models to be effectively deployed on resource-constrained devices. In this paper, we propose a novel BERT distillation method based on many-to-many layer mapping, which allows each intermediate student layer to learn from any intermediate teacher layers. In this way, our model can learn from different teacher layers adaptively for various NLP tasks. %motivated by the intuition that different NLP tasks require different levels of linguistic knowledge contained in the intermediate layers of BERT. In addition, we leverage Earth Mover's Distance (EMD) to compute the minimum cumulative cost that must be paid to transform knowledge from teacher network to student network. EMD enables the effective matching for many-to-many layer mapping. %EMD can be applied to network layers with different sizes and effectively measures semantic distance between the teacher network and student network. Furthermore, we propose a cost attention mechanism to learn the layer weights used in EMD automatically, which is supposed to further improve the model's performance and accelerate convergence time. Extensive experiments on GLUE benchmark demonstrate that our model achieves competitive performance compared to strong competitors in terms of both accuracy and model compression.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression methods aim to transfer performance and representational properties from large, expensive models to smaller, efficient ones. Across tasks in vision, language, graph learning, and generative modeling, researchers have developed strategies that extend beyond matching final logits: layer-wise and representation matching, many-to-many layer alignment, data-free distillation, private/distilled deployment, multi-teacher and self-distillation schemes, and task-adaptive compression. These approaches trade off fidelity, privacy, and computational cost, and they have been shown to enable real-world deployment of pretrained language models and other deep systems while revealing open challenges in distribution shift, heterogeneous data, and preserving inductive biases.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Practical Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable ones. When paired with task-aware objectives, data strategies (including data-free synthesis), and complementary compression techniques, KD can preserve much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Effective use of KD requires deliberate choices about what to transfer, which data to use or synthesize, and how to align teacher and student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Bowman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practical Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of techniques for transferring knowledge from larger, expensive models (teachers) to smaller, efficient models (students). KD has been applied across vision, language, generative modeling, and privacy-sensitive settings to reduce storage, latency, and energy while attempting to preserve accuracy and desirable properties. Practical approaches range from soft-label matching and feature imitation to many-to-many layer mappings and self-distillation; theoretical work links KD to regularization effects and label smoothing. Despite clear empirical successes in compressing large pretrained language models and vision networks, important challenges remain: students often fail to replicate teachers' internal representations, robustness and fairness do not automatically transfer, and privacy or heterogeneous-data settings impose additional constraints. Ongoing advances focus on richer targets (internal features, layer mappings), alternate training regimes (self- and teacher-free distillation), and task-aware strategies for robust and private compression.

papers_seen.author: Roberts
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Cornerstone for Compressing Deep Models in NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic and broadly applicable strategy for compressing large deep models so they can be deployed under real-world constraints. By transferring predictive behavior or intermediate representations from a high-capacity teacher to a smaller student, KD enables substantial reductions in model size and latency while preserving much of the original performance. When combined with architectural replacements, meta-learning, or task-aware layer matching, KD can be adapted to diverse settings (on-device inference, federated systems, data-scarce environments) and modalities. However, its effectiveness depends on choices such as which signals to transfer, how to handle imperfect teachers, and how to preserve rare or low-frequency behaviors; addressing these challenges is necessary for robust practical adoption.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: Improved Feature Distillation via Projector Ensemble
papers_seen.abstract: In knowledge distillation, previous feature distillation methods mainly focus on the design of loss functions and the selection of the distilled layers, while the effect of the feature projector between the student and the teacher remains under-explored. In this paper, we first discuss a plausible mechanism of the projector with empirical evidence and then propose a new feature distillation method based on a projector ensemble for further performance improvement. We observe that the student network benefits from a projector even if the feature dimensions of the student and the teacher are the same. Training a student backbone without a projector can be considered as a multi-task learning process, namely achieving discriminative feature extraction for classification and feature matching between the student and the teacher for distillation at the same time. We hypothesize and empirically verify that without a projector, the student network tends to overfit the teacher's feature distributions despite having different architecture and weights initialization. This leads to degradation on the quality of the student's deep features that are eventually used in classification. Adding a projector, on the other hand, disentangles the two learning tasks and helps the student network to focus better on the main feature extraction task while still being able to utilize teacher features as a guidance through the projector. Motivated by the positive effect of the projector in feature distillation, we propose an ensemble of projectors to further improve the quality of student features. Experimental results on different datasets with a series of teacher-student pairs illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a practical cornerstone for compressing large deep models into deployable, lower-latency students while retaining much of their predictive capacity. KD methods span simple soft-target matching to feature- and layer-level transfer, and they can operate in constrained settings (limited data, heterogeneous architectures, cross-modal scenarios). However, the effectiveness of KD depends on what is transferred, how teachers and students are matched, and how KD is combined with complementary compression strategies. Careful design—addressing teacher errors, domain shift, data availability, and architecture mismatch—yields compact models that meet real deployment constraints without disproportionate loss in quality.

papers_seen.author: Mcclain
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation from Internal Representations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is typically conducted by training a small model (the student) to mimic a large and cumbersome model (the teacher). The idea is to compress the knowledge from the teacher by using its output probabilities as soft-labels to optimize the student. However, when the teacher is considerably large, there is no guarantee that the internal knowledge of the teacher will be transferred into the student; even if the student closely matches the soft-labels, its internal representations may be considerably different. This internal mismatch can undermine the generalization capabilities originally intended to be transferred from the teacher to the student. In this paper, we propose to distill the internal representations of a large model such as BERT into a simplified version of it. We formulate two ways to distill such representations and various algorithms to conduct the distillation. We experiment with datasets from the GLUE benchmark and consistently show that adding knowledge distillation from internal representations is a more powerful method than only using soft-label distillation.

papers_seen.author: Warner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Model Compression and Adaptation in NLP and Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as a central, practical technique for compressing and adapting large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD is versatile: it transfers predictive behavior, intermediate representations, and ensemble knowledge; supports data-free or privacy-sensitive settings; and can improve robustness and calibration when combined with complementary methods. Realizing KD’s full potential requires matching the distillation recipe to deployment goals and addressing failure modes such as optimization mismatches, bias transfer, and poor handling of low-frequency phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical, Careful, and Multifaceted Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, widely applicable approach to compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. When applied thoughtfully, KD enables deployment under resource, latency, and privacy constraints; supports domain adaptation and vocabulary specialization; and can be combined with other compression techniques. However, its success depends on careful choices about what to transfer (logits vs. features), how to align layers and representations, how to generate or augment data for distillation, and how to mitigate propagated errors or biases from teachers.

papers_seen.author: Spears
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of techniques for transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models so that high performance can be retained under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. Across modalities KD spans simple soft-target matching to richer transfers of internal features, attention, or relational structure, and it is usually combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and careful data strategies (real, public, synthetic, or data-free). Empirical results show large reductions in model size and inference cost with modest accuracy loss in many settings, but success depends on choices of what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, how to handle limited or private data, and how to preserve robustness and fairness under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Ball
papers_seen.title: The Practical Centrality and Limits of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an essential, practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. By transferring richer signals than hard labels—soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, or relational structure—KD enables substantial reductions in latency, memory, and energy while recovering much of a teacher’s performance. Effective deployment treats KD as a component of a broader compression pipeline: select the appropriate distilled signals, align teacher and student architectures, use data-aware or data-free strategies as needed, and combine distillation with pruning, quantization, or architecture-aware pretraining. KD succeeds widely but has known failure modes—teacher imperfections, capacity mismatch, distribution shift, rare-token fidelity loss, and bias transfer—that require principled engineering, diagnostics, and complementary techniques to address.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Is Label Smoothing Truly Incompatible with Knowledge Distillation: An Empirical Study
papers_seen.abstract: This work aims to empirically clarify a recently discovered perspective that label smoothing is incompatible with knowledge distillation. We begin by introducing the motivation behind on how this incompatibility is raised, i.e., label smoothing erases relative information between teacher logits. We provide a novel connection on how label smoothing affects distributions of semantically similar and dissimilar classes. Then we propose a metric to quantitatively measure the degree of erased information in sample's representation. After that, we study its one-sidedness and imperfection of the incompatibility view through massive analyses, visualizations and comprehensive experiments on Image Classification, Binary Networks, and Neural Machine Translation. Finally, we broadly discuss several circumstances wherein label smoothing will indeed lose its effectiveness. Project page: http://zhiqiangshen.com/projects/LS_and_KD/index.html.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses or transfers knowledge from larger or multiple teacher models into smaller or otherwise constrained student models to reduce inference cost while retaining performance. Across computer vision, speech, recommendation, and NLP, KD techniques include matching soft outputs, transferring intermediate features, multi-teacher and staged protocols, and data-free synthesis of surrogate training examples. Practical systems combine KD with pruning or architecture changes, and recent theory helps explain when and why distillation helps. Despite strong empirical gains, challenges remain in handling heterogeneous teachers, data unavailability, task-specific adaptations (e.g., detection, translation), and robustness on low-frequency or out-of-distribution phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: Effective Knowledge Distillation: Representation, Selection, and Practical Constraints
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach to compress and adapt large deep models for deployment in resource- or privacy-constrained settings. Effective distillation goes beyond matching teacher logits: transferring internal representations, choosing which teacher signals to trust, and accommodating deployment constraints (limited data, communication, low-precision hardware) are all decisive. I argue that the most reliable distillation pipelines combine representation-level objectives, selective/sample-aware strategies, and engineering choices that address privacy and efficiency, yielding compact students that retain teacher strengths across NLP, vision, and graph domains.

papers_seen.author: Mckee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Model Compression: Power, Patterns, and Precautions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, flexible approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a toolkit rather than a single recipe, and combined with complementary compression methods and data strategies, KD enables substantial reductions in latency, memory, and energy while retaining much of teacher performance. However, distillation can transfer teacher weaknesses (biases, brittleness, low-frequency errors) and requires careful choices about what to transfer, how to align representations across heterogeneous architectures, and how to handle limited or private data. Practical deployment therefore calls for method selection tailored to task and constraints, plus safeguards for robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing neural models by transferring information from a teacher to a smaller student so the student preserves much of the teacher’s behavior while using less compute, memory, or latency. The literature shows a family of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention or relational signals), multiple training regimes (offline, online/self-distillation, data-free), and many practical integrations (pre-training compact students, combining with pruning/quantization, and curriculum or data selection). Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, availability and selection of data, and deployment constraints; remaining challenges include capacity/optimization mismatch, preserving rare or fine-grained behaviors, and distillation under privacy or data-scarce settings.

papers_seen.author: Rocha
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practical Trends
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques aim to transfer predictive power from large teacher models into smaller, faster, or more private student models while retaining most of the original performance. Work across vision and language has expanded KD beyond simple logit matching into data-centric methods (augmentation and mixup), layer- and representation-level transfers, task-adaptive architecture search, data-free and privacy-aware distillation, and unified pipelines that combine pruning or structural compression with distillation. The field blends empirical engineering (speed/size trade-offs) with emerging theoretical analyses that help explain when and why distillation helps.

papers_seen.author: Gardner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Essential, Versatile, and Context-Sensitive for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable technique for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students that retain much of teacher performance. KD can be applied across modalities and settings to reduce inference cost, enable deployment under resource or privacy constraints, and serve as a core component of broader compression pipelines. However, its effectiveness depends on careful design choices about what to transfer, data regimes, and alignment between teacher and student.

papers_seen.author: Keith
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression techniques transfer capability from large teacher models into smaller, deployable students to reduce inference cost, memory, and energy while preserving much of task performance. The literature shows a spectrum of methods — from soft-target matching to representation-level alignment, progressive module replacement, and data-free or adversarial sample synthesis — and emphasizes that distillation is most effective when combined with careful student initialization, architecture-aware alignment, and complementary compression methods. Practical success depends on choices about what signals to transfer, how to supply or synthesize training data, and how to align teacher and student capacities; open challenges include optimization dynamics, domain shift, privacy, and robustness under rare phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Gibson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression methods transfer predictive behavior and internal representations from larger or more informed teacher models into smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained students. These methods are applied to reduce latency and memory, enable deployment on heterogeneous or private devices, and to retain teacher performance through tailored losses, intermediate-feature matching, multi-stage pipelines, and combinations with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Empirical work shows KD succeeds across modalities (language, vision, multimodal, and generative models) when design choices — what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and which data to use — are matched to the task and constraints. Ongoing challenges include distilling rare-token behaviors, handling severe data heterogeneity, ensuring privacy and fairness, and automating student architecture design.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Across computer vision and NLP, practitioners use KD to reduce inference cost, enable on-device deployment, and adapt large pretrained models to constrained settings. KD techniques vary in what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, attention or relational signals), how training data are handled (real, augmented, synthesized, or none), and how teachers and students are aligned architecturally and procedurally. When design choices are matched to the task and constraints, KD enables substantial compression with modest performance loss; however, challenges remain for heterogeneous architectures, generative tasks, privacy-sensitive settings, and preserving rare-token or low-frequency behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Daniels
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, faster students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. Methods range from matching softened logits to imitating internal representations, attention maps, or channel-wise activations, and can be combined with quantization, low-precision numerics, architecture-aware design, and data- or teacher-aware training regimes. In practice, distillation is a multifaceted toolkit that must be tailored to deployment goals (latency, memory, domain adaptation, privacy, robustness), and remaining challenges include principled sample selection, representation alignment across heterogeneous architectures, and preserving robustness and fairness under compression.

papers_seen.author: Hurst
papers_seen.title: Contemporary Approaches and Applications of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques transfer information from larger, more costly models to smaller, deployable models. Modern work expands beyond simple soft-label matching to include distillation of internal representations, feature-level imitation, privacy-preserving and data-free strategies, task-adaptive compression, and adaptations to specialized architectures (e.g., GANs, detectors, and transformers). These methods aim to preserve accuracy, robustness, and efficiency (compute, memory, or communication) while enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices or in privacy-sensitive and distributed settings.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Trade-offs, and Practical Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) trains compact student models by transferring information from larger teacher models, enabling deployment under computation, memory, or latency constraints. Across vision, speech, language, and recommendation systems, KD takes many forms — logit matching, feature mimicking, ensemble compression, and data-free synthesis — and is often combined with model pruning, architectural simplification, or curriculum strategies. Effective distillation requires choices about what to transfer (soft targets vs. intermediate features), how to supply or synthesize data, and how to schedule or regularize training; these choices shape outcomes in accuracy, robustness, interpretability, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Trade-offs, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or ensemble knowledge. The approach spans simple logit/soft-label matching to feature- and layer-level objectives, multi-teacher pipelines, teacher-free variants, and combinations with architecture search, pruning and data-synthesis. Empirical and theoretical work shows distillation yields substantial efficiency gains with careful design, but also exposes limits from optimization, data heterogeneity, and capacity mismatch. Practical deployment therefore balances what to transfer, how to adapt the student architecture, and whether data or privacy constraints require specialized protocols.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Insights
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques enable deployment of large deep models by transferring knowledge to smaller, faster, or lower-precision models. Existing work spans pre-training compact models, teacher-to-student soft-target transfer, data-free and teacher-free approaches, self-distillation, architecture- and task-specific adaptations, and combinations with quantization or pruning. Empirical results show that distilled students can approach teacher performance across classification, ranking, speech, and generation tasks, while specialized strategies address limited task data, privacy constraints, and heterogeneous deployment settings. Open challenges include handling domain shift, designing teacher-student curricula, and developing universally effective objectives for diverse architectures and tasks.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Distilling portable Generative Adversarial Networks for Image Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been widely used in various image-to-image translation tasks, they can be hardly applied on mobile devices due to their heavy computation and storage cost. Traditional network compression methods focus on visually recognition tasks, but never deal with generation tasks. Inspired by knowledge distillation, a student generator of fewer parameters is trained by inheriting the low-level and high-level information from the original heavy teacher generator. To promote the capability of student generator, we include a student discriminator to measure the distances between real images, and images generated by student and teacher generators. An adversarial learning process is therefore established to optimize student generator and student discriminator. Qualitative and quantitative analysis by conducting experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method can learn portable generative models with strong performance.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical, flexible approach for producing compact neural models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. Across vision and language applications KD has been extended from simple soft-label matching to a wide set of techniques—intermediate-representation transfer, layer-aware alignment, multi-teacher and self-distillation, data-free variants, and adversarial or projector-based feature matching—that enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD both preserves predictive performance and can improve generalization in many settings, while also raising practical challenges such as teacher–student mismatch and degraded modeling of low-frequency phenomena that require targeted mitigations.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques reduce the size, memory, and inference cost of large neural networks by transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models. Across tasks and modalities—classification, detection, generative modeling, retrieval, and NLP—research has developed logits-based, feature-based, and task-adapted distillation strategies, multi-teacher and ensemble approaches, privacy- and communication-conscious protocols for distributed settings, and teacher-optimization/meta-learning variants. These methods trade off fidelity to teacher behavior with student capacity, expose failure modes (e.g., transfer of low-frequency lexical mistakes or overfitting of student features), and introduce remedies such as selective sample distillation, feature projectors, adversarially-informed samples, and staged or multi-teacher curricula. While KD consistently improves compact models compared to training from scratch and enables deployment on resource-constrained platforms, open issues remain in robustness, task-specific alignment, and distillation under data heterogeneity.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Compressing Visual-linguistic Model via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite exciting progress in pre-training for visual-linguistic (VL) representations, very few aspire to a small VL model. In this paper, we study knowledge distillation (KD) to effectively compress a transformer-based large VL model into a small VL model. The major challenge arises from the inconsistent regional visual tokens extracted from different detectors of Teacher and Student, resulting in the misalignment of hidden representations and attention distributions. To address the problem, we retrain and adapt the Teacher by using the same region proposals from Student's detector while the features are from Teacher's own object detector. With aligned network inputs, the adapted Teacher is capable of transferring the knowledge through the intermediate representations. Specifically, we use the mean square error loss to mimic the attention distribution inside the transformer block and present a token-wise noise contrastive loss to align the hidden state by contrasting with negative representations stored in a sample queue. To this end, we show that our proposed distillation significantly improves the performance of small VL models on image captioning and visual question answering tasks. It reaches 120.8 in CIDEr score on COCO captioning, an improvement of 5.1 over its non-distilled counterpart; and an accuracy of 69.8 on VQA 2.0, a 0.8 gain from the baseline. Our extensive experiments and ablations confirm the effectiveness of VL distillation in both pre-training and fine-tuning stages.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large or ensemble teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure. Across vision, language, and multimodal tasks, KD uses a range of targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational signals) and workflows (offline teacher-student, online/self-distillation, multi-teacher curricula, data-free or federated protocols). When combined with architecture search, pruning, or quantization, KD enables deployment of compact models with large gains in latency and memory while often preserving generalization. Practical success depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity, handling data or privacy constraints, and addressing optimization mismatches and distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Jackson
papers_seen.title: Online Knowledge Distillation via Mutual Contrastive Learning for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: The teacher-free online Knowledge Distillation (KD) aims to train an ensemble of multiple student models collaboratively and distill knowledge from each other. Although existing online KD methods achieve desirable performance, they often focus on class probabilities as the core knowledge type, ignoring the valuable feature representational information. We present a Mutual Contrastive Learning (MCL) framework for online KD. The core idea of MCL is to perform mutual interaction and transfer of contrastive distributions among a cohort of networks in an online manner. Our MCL can aggregate cross-network embedding information and maximize the lower bound to the mutual information between two networks. This enables each network to learn extra contrastive knowledge from others, leading to better feature representations, thus improving the performance of visual recognition tasks. Beyond the final layer, we extend MCL to intermediate layers and perform an adaptive layer-matching mechanism trained by meta-optimization. Experiments on image classification and transfer learning to visual recognition tasks show that layer-wise MCL can lead to consistent performance gains against state-of-the-art online KD approaches. The superiority demonstrates that layer-wise MCL can guide the network to generate better feature representations. Our code is publicly avaliable at https://github.com/winycg/L-MCL.

papers_seen.author: Zamora
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, cheaper students by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations. The family of KD methods includes soft-target (logit) matching, feature- and layer-wise alignment, relational and module-level transfer, data-free or zero-shot synthesis, and integration with architecture search or federated training. Practical deployments balance what is transferred with student capacity, data availability, privacy constraints, and device heterogeneity; empirical work shows KD often preserves much of teacher performance while enabling lower latency, smaller models, and domain specialization, but open challenges remain around robustness, domain shift, and principled selection of distilled signals.

papers_seen.author: Riley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is not merely a model-compression trick but a central, practical paradigm for deploying high-performance deep and NLP models under real-world constraints. KD can compress large pre-trained models into lightweight students, transfer inductive biases, improve robustness and generalization, enable low-precision and privacy-aware deployments, and adapt to data- or compute-limited settings. Effective distillation couples soft-label transfer with representation-level alignment, task-aware architecture choices, and complementary techniques (quantization, pruning, augmentation). However, KD must be applied carefully: teacher–student mismatches, bias transfer, domain shift, and limited-data regimes require method choices such as feature mimicking, teacher ensembles, teacher-free objectives, or fairness-aware augmentations. The result is a flexible toolkit that—when combined with architectural and data strategies—makes high-quality, efficient models feasible for production NLP and deep-learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Cohen
papers_seen.title: ALP-KD: Attention-Based Layer Projection for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is considered as a training and compression strategy in which two neural networks, namely a teacher and a student, are coupled together during training. The teacher network is supposed to be a trustworthy predictor and the student tries to mimic its predictions. Usually, a student with a lighter architecture is selected so we can achieve compression and yet deliver high-quality results. In such a setting, distillation only happens for final predictions whereas the student could also benefit from teacher's supervision for internal components.   Motivated by this, we studied the problem of distillation for intermediate layers. Since there might not be a one-to-one alignment between student and teacher layers, existing techniques skip some teacher layers and only distill from a subset of them. This shortcoming directly impacts quality, so we instead propose a combinatorial technique which relies on attention. Our model fuses teacher-side information and takes each layer's significance into consideration, then performs distillation between combined teacher layers and those of the student. Using our technique, we distilled a 12-layer BERT (Devlin et al. 2019) into 6-, 4-, and 2-layer counterparts and evaluated them on GLUE tasks (Wang et al. 2018). Experimental results show that our combinatorial approach is able to outperform other existing techniques.
