papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation for Practical NLP Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical, flexible pathway to deploy high-performing deep learning and NLP models under real-world constraints. By transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or inductive biases from large or multi-modal teachers to smaller students, distillation enables task- and domain-specific compression, faster inference, privacy-preserving distributed training, and architectural simplification. Effective distillation requires methods that match the target deployment needs—task-awareness, layer alignment, careful use of data augmentation and teacher ensembles, and scaling strategies for large datasets and distributed settings. When designed deliberately, distillation yields compressed models that retain much of the teacher's capability while meeting latency, size, and privacy requirements.

papers_seen.author: Rocha
papers_seen.title: Few Shot Network Compression via Cross Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Model compression has been widely adopted to obtain light-weighted deep neural networks. Most prevalent methods, however, require fine-tuning with sufficient training data to ensure accuracy, which could be challenged by privacy and security issues. As a compromise between privacy and performance, in this paper we investigate few shot network compression: given few samples per class, how can we effectively compress the network with negligible performance drop? The core challenge of few shot network compression lies in high estimation errors from the original network during inference, since the compressed network can easily over-fits on the few training instances. The estimation errors could propagate and accumulate layer-wisely and finally deteriorate the network output. To address the problem, we propose cross distillation, a novel layer-wise knowledge distillation approach. By interweaving hidden layers of teacher and student network, layer-wisely accumulated estimation errors can be effectively reduced.The proposed method offers a general framework compatible with prevalent network compression techniques such as pruning. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that cross distillation can significantly improve the student network's accuracy when only a few training instances are available.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, broadly applicable route to compressing large models into smaller, faster ones for deployment in resource- and privacy-constrained settings. When combined with complementary techniques (e.g., architecture-aware design, data augmentation, and privacy mechanisms), KD consistently yields strong accuracy-efficiency trade-offs across modalities. However, realizing those gains requires careful choices about what to transfer (logits, features, attention), how to select or synthesize data, and how to mitigate transferred harms (bias, privacy leakage). This paper argues that KD should be treated as a central, flexible tool for model compression while emphasizing practical design principles and known failure modes that practitioners must address.

papers_seen.author: Novak
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression methods enable transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large, high-capacity teachers to smaller students so models can be deployed under computation, memory, latency, or privacy constraints. The literature shows a spectrum of approaches — from matching softened output distributions to feature- and layer-level imitation, attention-guided alignment, data-free or zero-shot synthesis of training examples, and distributed or privacy-aware protocols — and demonstrates successful applications across vision, speech, recommendation, and many NLP tasks. Practical effectiveness depends on choices of distillation signal, data availability and synthesis, teacher–student architecture alignment, and training curricula; open challenges include handling imperfect teachers, preserving rare or long-tail behaviors, and maintaining robustness under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Mcclain
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation from Internal Representations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is typically conducted by training a small model (the student) to mimic a large and cumbersome model (the teacher). The idea is to compress the knowledge from the teacher by using its output probabilities as soft-labels to optimize the student. However, when the teacher is considerably large, there is no guarantee that the internal knowledge of the teacher will be transferred into the student; even if the student closely matches the soft-labels, its internal representations may be considerably different. This internal mismatch can undermine the generalization capabilities originally intended to be transferred from the teacher to the student. In this paper, we propose to distill the internal representations of a large model such as BERT into a simplified version of it. We formulate two ways to distill such representations and various algorithms to conduct the distillation. We experiment with datasets from the GLUE benchmark and consistently show that adding knowledge distillation from internal representations is a more powerful method than only using soft-label distillation.

papers_seen.author: Cobb
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, faster students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels. Over the past decade KD has evolved from simple soft-target matching to a diverse toolkit that includes intermediate-representation matching, layerwise alignment, multi-teacher and self-distillation, curriculum and augmentation strategies, and privacy- or data-free procedures. When combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) and task-aware choices about what and how to transfer, KD enables practical deployment of high-performing models across modalities while raising open issues in robustness, fairness, and distributional generalization.

papers_seen.author: Doyle
papers_seen.title: DE-RRD: A Knowledge Distillation Framework for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: Recent recommender systems have started to employ knowledge distillation, which is a model compression technique distilling knowledge from a cumbersome model (teacher) to a compact model (student), to reduce inference latency while maintaining performance. The state-of-the-art methods have only focused on making the student model accurately imitate the predictions of the teacher model. They have a limitation in that the prediction results incompletely reveal the teacher's knowledge. In this paper, we propose a novel knowledge distillation framework for recommender system, called DE-RRD, which enables the student model to learn from the latent knowledge encoded in the teacher model as well as from the teacher's predictions. Concretely, DE-RRD consists of two methods: 1) Distillation Experts (DE) that directly transfers the latent knowledge from the teacher model. DE exploits "experts" and a novel expert selection strategy for effectively distilling the vast teacher's knowledge to the student with limited capacity. 2) Relaxed Ranking Distillation (RRD) that transfers the knowledge revealed from the teacher's prediction with consideration of the relaxed ranking orders among items. Our extensive experiments show that DE-RRD outperforms the state-of-the-art competitors and achieves comparable or even better performance to that of the teacher model with faster inference time.

papers_seen.author: Jackson
papers_seen.title: Online Knowledge Distillation via Mutual Contrastive Learning for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: The teacher-free online Knowledge Distillation (KD) aims to train an ensemble of multiple student models collaboratively and distill knowledge from each other. Although existing online KD methods achieve desirable performance, they often focus on class probabilities as the core knowledge type, ignoring the valuable feature representational information. We present a Mutual Contrastive Learning (MCL) framework for online KD. The core idea of MCL is to perform mutual interaction and transfer of contrastive distributions among a cohort of networks in an online manner. Our MCL can aggregate cross-network embedding information and maximize the lower bound to the mutual information between two networks. This enables each network to learn extra contrastive knowledge from others, leading to better feature representations, thus improving the performance of visual recognition tasks. Beyond the final layer, we extend MCL to intermediate layers and perform an adaptive layer-matching mechanism trained by meta-optimization. Experiments on image classification and transfer learning to visual recognition tasks show that layer-wise MCL can lead to consistent performance gains against state-of-the-art online KD approaches. The superiority demonstrates that layer-wise MCL can guide the network to generate better feature representations. Our code is publicly avaliable at https://github.com/winycg/L-MCL.

papers_seen.author: Powell
papers_seen.title: What is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer information from larger, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models so that students retain much of teacher performance while reducing computational cost. The literature characterizes KD methods at multiple granularities (final logits, intermediate features, attention or layer mappings, and module- or task-level transfer), documents practical recipes and failure modes, and explores extensions for data-free settings, robustness, and specialized tasks (e.g., machine translation, detection). Empirical and theoretical work shows KD is a flexible tool that benefits from careful choices in distilled signals, data/augmentation strategies, and teacher-student alignment; however, limitations remain around optimization, low-frequency phenomena, data availability, and architecture mismatch.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. The approach spans simple soft-target matching to feature- and layer-level imitation, and it is commonly combined with other compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture simplification) and data strategies (public or synthesized data, selective sampling). KD routinely improves compact models over training from scratch and enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, but its effectiveness depends on design choices about what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, how to prepare data, and how to mitigate teacher imperfections and distributional shift.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) offers a pragmatic pathway to produce compact, efficient models from large teachers while preserving much of their performance. When thoughtfully combined with complementary techniques—representation-level objectives, architecture-aware student design, data strategies including data-free or privacy-sensitive workflows, and targeted optimization—KD enables deployment under latency, memory, and heterogeneity constraints. However, realizing these gains requires attention to teacher quality, student capacity, optimization dynamics, and data issues; failures and trade-offs are documented and can be managed with targeted practices.

papers_seen.author: Cohen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Strategy for Model Compression and Adaptation in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible approach to produce compact models that retain much of the performance of larger models. Beyond simple compression, KD can transfer inductive biases, enable domain adaptation and vocabulary specialization, support privacy-preserving and federated scenarios, work without access to original data, and improve robustness and feature quality when carefully applied. When combined with targeted techniques — feature mimicking, weighted soft labels, projector layers, or adversarial robustness objectives — KD becomes a unifying toolkit to meet latency, capacity, and privacy constraints in real-world NLP and deep learning deployments.

papers_seen.author: Scott
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques transfer information from larger teacher models into smaller student models to reduce computation, memory, and latency while attempting to preserve predictive performance. The field encompasses a range of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational signals), training workflows (single- and multi-stage, multi-teacher, self-distillation, data-free), and practical integrations with pruning, quantization, and architecture adaptation. Empirical and conceptual work points to several mechanisms that make distillation effective (soft-target regularization, representation alignment, and inductive-bias transfer) and identifies recurring deployment concerns such as architecture mismatch, data availability, domain shift, and robustness. Best practices emphasize matching distillation signals to student capacity, using layer-aware objectives when internal alignment matters, and combining distillation with complementary compression methods for realistic constraints.

papers_seen.author: Robbins
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely used set of techniques to transfer behavior from large "teacher" models to smaller "student" models so they can run with lower latency, memory, and cost while retaining much of the teacher's performance. The field has diversified from simple logit-matching into a broad toolkit that includes feature- and layer-level imitation, multi-teacher and multi-stage pipelines, data-free or synthetic-data approaches, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacities, how to handle data and domain mismatch, and how to address optimization and deployment constraints. Empirical work shows KD often preserves substantial teacher utility across vision and NLP, but theoretical and empirical analyses also highlight optimization limits, capacity- and distribution-mismatch risks, and the importance of pre-training and task-aware design for robust deployment.

papers_seen.author: Hall
papers_seen.title: FedZKT: Zero-Shot Knowledge Transfer towards Resource-Constrained Federated Learning with Heterogeneous On-Device Models
papers_seen.abstract: Federated learning enables multiple distributed devices to collaboratively learn a shared prediction model without centralizing their on-device data. Most of the current algorithms require comparable individual efforts for local training with the same structure and size of on-device models, which, however, impedes participation from resource-constrained devices. Given the widespread yet heterogeneous devices nowadays, in this paper, we propose an innovative federated learning framework with heterogeneous on-device models through Zero-shot Knowledge Transfer, named by FedZKT. Specifically, FedZKT allows devices to independently determine the on-device models upon their local resources. To achieve knowledge transfer across these heterogeneous on-device models, a zero-shot distillation approach is designed without any prerequisites for private on-device data, which is contrary to certain prior research based on a public dataset or a pre-trained data generator. Moreover, this compute-intensive distillation task is assigned to the server to allow the participation of resource-constrained devices, where a generator is adversarially learned with the ensemble of collected on-device models. The distilled central knowledge is then sent back in the form of the corresponding on-device model parameters, which can be easily absorbed on the device side. Extensive experimental studies demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of FedZKT towards on-device knowledge agnostic, on-device model heterogeneity, and other challenging federated learning scenarios, such as heterogeneous on-device data and straggler effects.

papers_seen.author: Chavez
papers_seen.title: Data-Free Knowledge Distillation for Deep Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Recent advances in model compression have provided procedures for compressing large neural networks to a fraction of their original size while retaining most if not all of their accuracy. However, all of these approaches rely on access to the original training set, which might not always be possible if the network to be compressed was trained on a very large dataset, or on a dataset whose release poses privacy or safety concerns as may be the case for biometrics tasks. We present a method for data-free knowledge distillation, which is able to compress deep neural networks trained on large-scale datasets to a fraction of their size leveraging only some extra metadata to be provided with a pretrained model release. We also explore different kinds of metadata that can be used with our method, and discuss tradeoffs involved in using each of them.

papers_seen.author: Rios
papers_seen.title: Improving Neural Topic Models using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Topic models are often used to identify human-interpretable topics to help make sense of large document collections. We use knowledge distillation to combine the best attributes of probabilistic topic models and pretrained transformers. Our modular method can be straightforwardly applied with any neural topic model to improve topic quality, which we demonstrate using two models having disparate architectures, obtaining state-of-the-art topic coherence. We show that our adaptable framework not only improves performance in the aggregate over all estimated topics, as is commonly reported, but also in head-to-head comparisons of aligned topics.

papers_seen.author: Harris
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical, and Composable Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly practical approach for turning large, high-performing models into smaller, efficient models suitable for deployment. Across vision and language tasks, KD enables substantial reductions in parameter count and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance. Its strengths come from flexibility in what to transfer (logits, intermediate features, optimization signals), its compatibility with architecture search and other compression primitives, and its ability to operate under constrained or private-data scenarios. KD is not a one-size-fits-all remedy: practitioners should select KD variants and complementary techniques guided by task requirements, data availability, and deployment constraints to balance fidelity, robustness, and efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Nolan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, or relational structure. Across vision, speech, and natural language tasks, distillation enables large reductions in model size and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance when combined with careful choices of transfer target, student architecture, and complementary compression techniques. Practical success depends on data strategies, layer-matching or projector design, and attention to optimization dynamics and teacher–student capacity mismatch; open problems include principled data synthesis or selection, preserving robustness and fairness, and scaling to heterogeneous or privacy-sensitive deployments.

papers_seen.author: Kidd
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable approach for compressing large deep learning models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students. Modern KD goes beyond matching logits: it includes feature- and representation-level transfers, multi-teacher and self-distillation strategies, and workflows that integrate augmentation, data-free synthesis, pruning, and quantization to meet latency, memory, and privacy requirements. Practical success depends on matching distillation technique to deployment objectives, careful design of layer mappings and loss terms, attention to teacher quality and data availability, and combinations with other compression tools to preserve robustness and generalization.

papers_seen.author: Bentley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Trade-offs, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely used set of techniques for training compact student models that capture much of a larger teacher model's behavior while reducing latency, memory, and energy costs. KD is instantiated through multiple signals (soft targets, intermediate features, relational and layer-wise objectives), often combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture redesign. Empirical work shows KD can yield substantial deployability gains across NLP tasks (ranking, reading comprehension, multi-task models), but its success depends on choices about what is transferred, how data are used or synthesized, and how teacher and student architectures or training schedules are aligned; unresolved issues include optimization mismatch, bias transfer, rare-token fidelity, and robustness under domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Hickman
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques aim to transfer the predictive power of large, expensive models into smaller, faster models while retaining performance. Approaches vary from matching teacher outputs (soft labels) to aligning intermediate representations, leveraging data augmentation or synthesized data when real data are limited, and jointly optimizing architecture and distillation losses for task-adaptive compression. Advances address student–teacher capacity gaps, multi-teacher transfer, and domain or data scarcity; remaining challenges include transferring internal structure efficiently, generalization under distribution shifts, and designing teacher models that are optimized for downstream distillation.

papers_seen.author: Rasmussen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Context-Sensitive Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile toolkit for turning large, expensive models into smaller, deployable ones while retaining much of their predictive power. When applied with attention to what to transfer, how to prepare data, and how to align teacher and student architectures, KD enables effective trade-offs among accuracy, latency, and privacy. However, KD is not a universal solution: its success depends on matching methods to task constraints and combining distillation with complementary compression or robustness techniques where necessary.

papers_seen.author: Bright
papers_seen.title: Towards Practical Lipreading with Distilled and Efficient Models
papers_seen.abstract: Lipreading has witnessed a lot of progress due to the resurgence of neural networks. Recent works have placed emphasis on aspects such as improving performance by finding the optimal architecture or improving generalization. However, there is still a significant gap between the current methodologies and the requirements for an effective deployment of lipreading in practical scenarios. In this work, we propose a series of innovations that significantly bridge that gap: first, we raise the state-of-the-art performance by a wide margin on LRW and LRW-1000 to 88.5% and 46.6%, respectively using self-distillation. Secondly, we propose a series of architectural changes, including a novel Depthwise Separable Temporal Convolutional Network (DS-TCN) head, that slashes the computational cost to a fraction of the (already quite efficient) original model. Thirdly, we show that knowledge distillation is a very effective tool for recovering performance of the lightweight models. This results in a range of models with different accuracy-efficiency trade-offs. However, our most promising lightweight models are on par with the current state-of-the-art while showing a reduction of 8.2x and 3.9x in terms of computational cost and number of parameters, respectively, which we hope will enable the deployment of lipreading models in practical applications.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical, Versatile Path to Compact and Generalizable Deep Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical suite of techniques that enable deployment of powerful deep models in resource-constrained or privacy-sensitive settings. Across modalities and tasks, KD compresses capacity while retaining much of the teacher's performance, and when combined with representation-level matching, data augmentation, curriculum strategies, meta-learning, or architecture-aware search it can also improve generalization, robustness, and cross-device inclusivity. KD is therefore not merely a model-compression trick but a broadly applicable framework for transferring structure, relational signals, and inductive biases from expensive models into efficient students for real-world use.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses or transfers knowledge from larger or multiple teacher models into smaller or otherwise constrained student models to reduce inference cost while retaining performance. Across computer vision, speech, recommendation, and NLP, KD techniques include matching soft outputs, transferring intermediate features, multi-teacher and staged protocols, and data-free synthesis of surrogate training examples. Practical systems combine KD with pruning or architecture changes, and recent theory helps explain when and why distillation helps. Despite strong empirical gains, challenges remain in handling heterogeneous teachers, data unavailability, task-specific adaptations (e.g., detection, translation), and robustness on low-frequency or out-of-distribution phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Richards
papers_seen.title: TextKD-GAN: Text Generation using KnowledgeDistillation and Generative Adversarial Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Text generation is of particular interest in many NLP applications such as machine translation, language modeling, and text summarization. Generative adversarial networks (GANs) achieved a remarkable success in high quality image generation in computer vision,and recently, GANs have gained lots of interest from the NLP community as well. However, achieving similar success in NLP would be more challenging due to the discrete nature of text. In this work, we introduce a method using knowledge distillation to effectively exploit GAN setup for text generation. We demonstrate how autoencoders (AEs) can be used for providing a continuous representation of sentences, which is a smooth representation that assign non-zero probabilities to more than one word. We distill this representation to train the generator to synthesize similar smooth representations. We perform a number of experiments to validate our idea using different datasets and show that our proposed approach yields better performance in terms of the BLEU score and Jensen-Shannon distance (JSD) measure compared to traditional GAN-based text generation approaches without pre-training.

papers_seen.author: Rhodes
papers_seen.title: Why Knowledge Distillation Is Central to Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic and versatile route to compressing large models into smaller, deployable ones while preserving much of their performance. Across domains and deployment constraints—multi-task learning, low-resource devices, federated settings, data-free scenarios, and generative or detection tasks—KD enables targeted transfer of behavior, representations, and robustness. However, realizing KD's potential requires task-aware choices: which teacher(s) to use, what intermediate signals to mimic, how to select or synthesize training samples, and whether to incorporate adversarial or ensemble strategies. When combined with appropriate pre-training, selective sample strategies, and representation-level objectives, KD produces compact models that are accurate, efficient, and more widely deployable than large models alone.

papers_seen.author: Roman
papers_seen.title: Fair Feature Distillation for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: Fairness is becoming an increasingly crucial issue for computer vision, especially in the human-related decision systems. However, achieving algorithmic fairness, which makes a model produce indiscriminative outcomes against protected groups, is still an unresolved problem. In this paper, we devise a systematic approach which reduces algorithmic biases via feature distillation for visual recognition tasks, dubbed as MMD-based Fair Distillation (MFD). While the distillation technique has been widely used in general to improve the prediction accuracy, to the best of our knowledge, there has been no explicit work that also tries to improve fairness via distillation. Furthermore, We give a theoretical justification of our MFD on the effect of knowledge distillation and fairness. Throughout the extensive experiments, we show our MFD significantly mitigates the bias against specific minorities without any loss of the accuracy on both synthetic and real-world face datasets.

papers_seen.author: Morgan
papers_seen.title: Making Knowledge Distillation a Core Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible, and broadly applicable method for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. When paired with representation-level objectives, careful teacher design, and complementary compression techniques (pruning, architecture replacement, or low-precision numerics), KD yields favorable trade-offs between accuracy, latency, and deployability. The method has clear limits (e.g., rare-token behaviors, data or privacy constraints), but these are addressable with multi-stage pipelines, data-centered practices, and task-aware design.

papers_seen.author: Parsons
papers_seen.title: Curriculum Learning for Dense Retrieval Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Recent work has shown that more effective dense retrieval models can be obtained by distilling ranking knowledge from an existing base re-ranking model. In this paper, we propose a generic curriculum learning based optimization framework called CL-DRD that controls the difficulty level of training data produced by the re-ranking (teacher) model. CL-DRD iteratively optimizes the dense retrieval (student) model by increasing the difficulty of the knowledge distillation data made available to it. In more detail, we initially provide the student model coarse-grained preference pairs between documents in the teacher's ranking and progressively move towards finer-grained pairwise document ordering requirements. In our experiments, we apply a simple implementation of the CL-DRD framework to enhance two state-of-the-art dense retrieval models. Experiments on three public passage retrieval datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed framework.

papers_seen.author: Wagner
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation in Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Since deep learning became a key player in natural language processing (NLP), many deep learning models have been showing remarkable performances in a variety of NLP tasks, and in some cases, they are even outperforming humans. Such high performance can be explained by efficient knowledge representation of deep learning models. While many methods have been proposed to learn more efficient representation, knowledge distillation from pretrained deep networks suggest that we can use more information from the soft target probability to train other neural networks. In this paper, we propose a new knowledge distillation method self-knowledge distillation, based on the soft target probabilities of the training model itself, where multimode information is distilled from the word embedding space right below the softmax layer. Due to the time complexity, our method approximates the soft target probabilities. In experiments, we applied the proposed method to two different and fundamental NLP tasks: language model and neural machine translation. The experiment results show that our proposed method improves performance on the tasks.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. The field has broadened from soft-logit matching to include feature- and layer-level alignment, relational and attention-aware transfers, data-free synthesis, adversarially-aware objectives, and curriculum or multi-teacher schemes. Practical success depends on choices about the distillation signal, data availability or synthesis, teacher–student architectural alignment, and training curricula; open challenges include preserving rare or long-tail behaviors, maintaining robustness and privacy, and adapting distillation to domain shifts and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Show, Attend and Distill:Knowledge Distillation via Attention-based Feature Matching
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation extracts general knowledge from a pre-trained teacher network and provides guidance to a target student network. Most studies manually tie intermediate features of the teacher and student, and transfer knowledge through pre-defined links. However, manual selection often constructs ineffective links that limit the improvement from the distillation. There has been an attempt to address the problem, but it is still challenging to identify effective links under practical scenarios. In this paper, we introduce an effective and efficient feature distillation method utilizing all the feature levels of the teacher without manually selecting the links. Specifically, our method utilizes an attention-based meta-network that learns relative similarities between features, and applies identified similarities to control distillation intensities of all possible pairs. As a result, our method determines competent links more efficiently than the previous approach and provides better performance on model compression and transfer learning tasks. Further qualitative analyses and ablative studies describe how our method contributes to better distillation. The implementation code is available at github.com/clovaai/attention-feature-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Wong
papers_seen.title: Embracing the Dark Knowledge: Domain Generalization Using Regularized Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Though convolutional neural networks are widely used in different tasks, lack of generalization capability in the absence of sufficient and representative data is one of the challenges that hinder their practical application. In this paper, we propose a simple, effective, and plug-and-play training strategy named Knowledge Distillation for Domain Generalization (KDDG) which is built upon a knowledge distillation framework with the gradient filter as a novel regularization term. We find that both the ``richer dark knowledge" from the teacher network, as well as the gradient filter we proposed, can reduce the difficulty of learning the mapping which further improves the generalization ability of the model. We also conduct experiments extensively to show that our framework can significantly improve the generalization capability of deep neural networks in different tasks including image classification, segmentation, reinforcement learning by comparing our method with existing state-of-the-art domain generalization techniques. Last but not the least, we propose to adopt two metrics to analyze our proposed method in order to better understand how our proposed method benefits the generalization capability of deep neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Morgan
papers_seen.title: Making Knowledge Distillation a Core Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible, and broadly applicable method for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. When paired with representation-level objectives, careful teacher design, and complementary compression techniques (pruning, architecture replacement, or low-precision numerics), KD yields favorable trade-offs between accuracy, latency, and deployability. The method has clear limits (e.g., rare-token behaviors, data or privacy constraints), but these are addressable with multi-stage pipelines, data-centered practices, and task-aware design.

papers_seen.author: Montgomery
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical, Versatile Path to Model Compression and Responsible Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature and flexible approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster, and often more deployable models. Beyond raw compression, KD can be adapted to meet constraints of privacy, heterogeneous devices, low-precision hardware, and domain or modality shifts. When combined with complementary techniques such as pre-training, layer-level supervision, or ensemble teachers, distillation can retain much of the teacher’s effectiveness while enabling production usage that would otherwise be impractical. This essay argues that KD should be a primary tool in the model-compression toolbox for both research and engineering deployments, and that best results come from tailoring distillation objectives and pipelines to application needs.

papers_seen.author: Caldwell
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer information from larger, expensive teacher models to smaller, deployable students to reduce inference cost while preserving much of the teacher’s behavior. Across modalities and tasks, KD methods vary by the form of transferred signal (soft targets, intermediate features, attention maps, or module behaviors), training setting (offline, online, federated, or data-free), and complementary techniques (architecture design, pruning, quantization, and data augmentation). Practical success depends on aligning teacher and student inputs/representations, selecting appropriate distillation objectives for the task and data regime, and mitigating distributional or token-frequency artifacts introduced during distillation. This synthesis summarizes major approaches, empirical findings, limitations, and practical strategies for applying KD in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Phillips
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation transfers knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models so students retain much of the teacher’s performance while reducing inference cost, memory, and latency. The literature has expanded from simple soft-label matching to a broad toolbox that includes intermediate-feature and attention matching, self-distillation, multi-teacher schemes, data-free and zero-shot approaches, curriculum and sample-selection strategies, and combinations with pruning/quantization or architecture search. Empirical work shows that careful choices about what to transfer, how to align architectures, and how to handle data or privacy constraints determine success; outstanding challenges include optimization dynamics, distribution shift, rare-token behaviors, and guaranteeing robust or fair behavior after compression.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practical Patterns
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information from teachers through softened outputs, intermediate representations, or training dynamics. A range of techniques — including self-distillation, multi-stage curricula, feature alignment, online and adversarial schemes, and combinations with pruning or architecture-aware design — enable favorable trade-offs between accuracy, latency, and resource constraints. Practical success depends on student capacity, the choice of distillation targets, data availability or synthesis, and safeguards for robustness, privacy, and long-tail behavior.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large models by transferring information from a high-capacity teacher to a smaller student, using signals beyond hard labels to preserve generalization while reducing compute and memory. Modern work expands KD beyond soft logits to intermediate features, layer mappings, adversarial and attention-based objectives, and data- or resource-constrained settings. Empirical results across vision, speech and NLP show that tailored distillation strategies can recover much of a teacher's performance in compact models, though challenges remain in data-free scenarios, handling imperfect teachers, and preserving rare-token fidelity in sequence tasks.

papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: Ensemble Knowledge Distillation for CTR Prediction
papers_seen.abstract: Recently, deep learning-based models have been widely studied for click-through rate (CTR) prediction and lead to improved prediction accuracy in many industrial applications. However, current research focuses primarily on building complex network architectures to better capture sophisticated feature interactions and dynamic user behaviors. The increased model complexity may slow down online inference and hinder its adoption in real-time applications. Instead, our work targets at a new model training strategy based on knowledge distillation (KD). KD is a teacher-student learning framework to transfer knowledge learned from a teacher model to a student model. The KD strategy not only allows us to simplify the student model as a vanilla DNN model but also achieves significant accuracy improvements over the state-of-the-art teacher models. The benefits thus motivate us to further explore the use of a powerful ensemble of teachers for more accurate student model training. We also propose some novel techniques to facilitate ensembled CTR prediction, including teacher gating and early stopping by distillation loss. We conduct comprehensive experiments against 12 existing models and across three industrial datasets. Both offline and online A/B testing results show the effectiveness of our KD-based training strategy.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: Less is More: Task-aware Layer-wise Distillation for Language Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Layer-wise distillation is a powerful tool to compress large models (i.e. teacher models) into small ones (i.e., student models). The student distills knowledge from the teacher by mimicking the hidden representations of the teacher at every intermediate layer. However, layer-wise distillation is difficult. Since the student has a smaller model capacity than the teacher, it is often under-fitted. Furthermore, the hidden representations of the teacher contain redundant information that the student does not necessarily need for the target task's learning. To address these challenges, we propose a novel Task-aware layEr-wise Distillation (TED). TED designs task-aware filters to align the hidden representations of the student and the teacher at each layer. The filters select the knowledge that is useful for the target task from the hidden representations. As such, TED reduces the knowledge gap between the two models and helps the student to fit better on the target task. We evaluate TED in two scenarios: continual pre-training and fine-tuning. TED demonstrates significant and consistent improvements over existing distillation methods in both scenarios. Code is available at https://github.com/cliang1453/task-aware-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Marshall
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely used approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Across modalities, KD transfers predictive behavior and internal representations using a variety of targets and protocols (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, multi-stage or online schemes) and composes well with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, and how to handle data or privacy constraints. KD enables many deployment goals (reduced latency/memory, domain adaptation, privacy-aware training), but its effectiveness is limited by optimization dynamics, teacher–student mismatch, distribution shift for synthetic data, and the potential transfer of undesirable biases.

papers_seen.author: Farmer
papers_seen.title: Towards Efficient 3D Object Detection with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite substantial progress in 3D object detection, advanced 3D detectors often suffer from heavy computation overheads. To this end, we explore the potential of knowledge distillation (KD) for developing efficient 3D object detectors, focusing on popular pillar- and voxel-based detectors.In the absence of well-developed teacher-student pairs, we first study how to obtain student models with good trade offs between accuracy and efficiency from the perspectives of model compression and input resolution reduction. Then, we build a benchmark to assess existing KD methods developed in the 2D domain for 3D object detection upon six well-constructed teacher-student pairs. Further, we propose an improved KD pipeline incorporating an enhanced logit KD method that performs KD on only a few pivotal positions determined by teacher classification response, and a teacher-guided student model initialization to facilitate transferring teacher model's feature extraction ability to students through weight inheritance. Finally, we conduct extensive experiments on the Waymo dataset. Our best performing model achieves $65.75\%$ LEVEL 2 mAPH, surpassing its teacher model and requiring only $44\%$ of teacher flops. Our most efficient model runs 51 FPS on an NVIDIA A100, which is $2.2\times$ faster than PointPillar with even higher accuracy. Code is available at \url{https://github.com/CVMI-Lab/SparseKD}.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Highlight Every Step: Knowledge Distillation via Collaborative Teaching
papers_seen.abstract: High storage and computational costs obstruct deep neural networks to be deployed on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation aims to train a compact student network by transferring knowledge from a larger pre-trained teacher model. However, most existing methods on knowledge distillation ignore the valuable information among training process associated with training results. In this paper, we provide a new Collaborative Teaching Knowledge Distillation (CTKD) strategy which employs two special teachers. Specifically, one teacher trained from scratch (i.e., scratch teacher) assists the student step by step using its temporary outputs. It forces the student to approach the optimal path towards the final logits with high accuracy. The other pre-trained teacher (i.e., expert teacher) guides the student to focus on a critical region which is more useful for the task. The combination of the knowledge from two special teachers can significantly improve the performance of the student network in knowledge distillation. The results of experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, SVHN and Tiny ImageNet datasets verify that the proposed knowledge distillation method is efficient and achieves state-of-the-art performance.

papers_seen.author: Osborne
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge from Deep Networks with Applications to Healthcare Domain
papers_seen.abstract: Exponential growth in Electronic Healthcare Records (EHR) has resulted in new opportunities and urgent needs for discovery of meaningful data-driven representations and patterns of diseases in Computational Phenotyping research. Deep Learning models have shown superior performance for robust prediction in computational phenotyping tasks, but suffer from the issue of model interpretability which is crucial for clinicians involved in decision-making. In this paper, we introduce a novel knowledge-distillation approach called Interpretable Mimic Learning, to learn interpretable phenotype features for making robust prediction while mimicking the performance of deep learning models. Our framework uses Gradient Boosting Trees to learn interpretable features from deep learning models such as Stacked Denoising Autoencoder and Long Short-Term Memory. Exhaustive experiments on a real-world clinical time-series dataset show that our method obtains similar or better performance than the deep learning models, and it provides interpretable phenotypes for clinical decision making.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques reduce computation, memory and latency of large deep models by transferring information from high-capacity "teacher" models to smaller "student" models. A range of approaches have been developed: soft-target (logit) distillation, feature- and layer-wise matching, data-augmentation and data-free synthesis, multi-teacher and curriculum strategies, and teacher-aware or teacher-training modifications. These methods are applied across modalities (NLP, vision, multimodal) and settings (limited data, federated or resource-constrained deployments), and combine naturally with quantization and low-precision inference. Empirical and theoretical work shows gains arise both from conveying inter-class similarities (dark knowledge) and from the regularization effect of softened targets; more recent work focuses on selecting or synthesizing the most useful knowledge for a given student and task.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Path to Compact, Deployable Deep Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, flexible set of techniques for transferring behavior from large, expensive teacher models into smaller, faster students. In deep learning and NLP, KD enables practical deployment by reducing latency, memory, and power requirements while retaining much of teacher performance. Effective application requires: (1) combining KD with domain-aware pretraining of compact models, (2) adapting distillation to data-constrained or privacy-sensitive settings, and (3) integrating architectural and optimization improvements (e.g., feature projectors, mixed-precision) to close remaining gaps. When applied thoughtfully, KD is a key tool for making state-of-the-art models useful in real-world, resource-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Rejuvenating Low-Frequency Words: Making the Most of Parallel Data in Non-Autoregressive Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is commonly used to construct synthetic data for training non-autoregressive translation (NAT) models. However, there exists a discrepancy on low-frequency words between the distilled and the original data, leading to more errors on predicting low-frequency words. To alleviate the problem, we directly expose the raw data into NAT by leveraging pretraining. By analyzing directed alignments, we found that KD makes low-frequency source words aligned with targets more deterministically but fails to align sufficient low-frequency words from target to source. Accordingly, we propose reverse KD to rejuvenate more alignments for low-frequency target words. To make the most of authentic and synthetic data, we combine these complementary approaches as a new training strategy for further boosting NAT performance. We conduct experiments on five translation benchmarks over two advanced architectures. Results demonstrate that the proposed approach can significantly and universally improve translation quality by reducing translation errors on low-frequency words. Encouragingly, our approach achieves 28.2 and 33.9 BLEU points on the WMT14 English-German and WMT16 Romanian-English datasets, respectively. Our code, data, and trained models are available at \url{https://github.com/alphadl/RLFW-NAT}.

papers_seen.author: Hahn
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression strategies are widely used to produce smaller, faster models by transferring knowledge from larger or ensemble teachers to compact students. These techniques span supervised distillation, self-distillation, data-free and adversarial approaches, layer- and task-aware mappings, and distributed/online schemes. Empirical work shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance across modalities (classification, detection, generation, and language tasks) while enabling practical deployment; theoretical and practical challenges remain around data dependence, teacher imperfection, robustness, and optimal student–teacher alignment.

papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a flexible, empirically effective route to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of the teacher's performance. KD can be adapted across modalities and constraints—by matching soft logits, intermediate representations, or attention maps; by using ensembles or teacher optimization; and by operating with or without original training data—making it well suited to real-world deployment needs. Because its effectiveness depends on representation alignment, teacher–student design, and data regime, KD is best applied as a component in broader compression pipelines (combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware choices) and selected to fit the target task and constraints.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression strategies enable smaller, faster models to inherit performance from larger teachers by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or ensemble knowledge. Techniques range from logit-based soft-target distillation to feature- and attention-level mimicry, multi-teacher and task-adaptive pipelines, and methods that relax the need for original training data or strong teachers. Across computer vision and natural language processing tasks, distilled students can approach teacher accuracy while drastically reducing parameters and latency; complementary strategies such as careful pre-training of compact models and architecture search further improve trade-offs between efficiency and effectiveness. Key challenges remain in preserving rare-token behavior, aligning heterogeneous teacher–student inputs, and ensuring privacy and robustness during compression.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge distillation from multi-modal to mono-modal segmentation networks
papers_seen.abstract: The joint use of multiple imaging modalities for medical image segmentation has been widely studied in recent years. The fusion of information from different modalities has demonstrated to improve the segmentation accuracy, with respect to mono-modal segmentations, in several applications. However, acquiring multiple modalities is usually not possible in a clinical setting due to a limited number of physicians and scanners, and to limit costs and scan time. Most of the time, only one modality is acquired. In this paper, we propose KD-Net, a framework to transfer knowledge from a trained multi-modal network (teacher) to a mono-modal one (student). The proposed method is an adaptation of the generalized distillation framework where the student network is trained on a subset (1 modality) of the teacher's inputs (n modalities). We illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in brain tumor segmentation with the BraTS 2018 dataset. Using different architectures, we show that the student network effectively learns from the teacher and always outperforms the baseline mono-modal network in terms of segmentation accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Flynn
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Design-Sensitive Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and multifaceted approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When applied with task-aware choices about what to transfer, how to train, and how to supplement distillation with complementary compression methods, KD can preserve most of a teacher's utility while meeting constraints on latency, memory, and privacy. However, KD is not a plug-and-play solution: its success depends on student capacity, the distilled signal, data availability (including data-free regimes), and mitigation of teacher imperfections and distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Across vision, language, graph, and speech tasks, KD variants (logit/soft-target matching, intermediate-feature alignment, relational transfer, multi-stage or multi-teacher schedules, and privacy-aware procedures) enable substantial reductions in inference cost and memory while often preserving most of the teacher's performance. Practical deployments pair KD with pretraining, sample-selection, and complementary compression techniques to meet latency, device, and privacy constraints; however, challenges remain around capacity mismatch, data scarcity, domain shift, and preserving rare or low-frequency behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Carr
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Cornerstone for Compressing Deep Models in NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, versatile mechanism for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable ones in NLP and related modalities. When paired with targeted choices—what signals to transfer (logits versus features), how to align layers, teacher design, and data strategies—KD preserves much of the teacher’s capability while reducing compute, memory, and latency. However, KD is not a universal remedy: its success depends on optimization details, data availability, and careful engineering to handle distribution shift, rare behaviors, and student–teacher mismatches.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques reduce the size, memory, and inference cost of large neural networks by transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models. Across tasks and modalities—classification, detection, generative modeling, retrieval, and NLP—research has developed logits-based, feature-based, and task-adapted distillation strategies, multi-teacher and ensemble approaches, privacy- and communication-conscious protocols for distributed settings, and teacher-optimization/meta-learning variants. These methods trade off fidelity to teacher behavior with student capacity, expose failure modes (e.g., transfer of low-frequency lexical mistakes or overfitting of student features), and introduce remedies such as selective sample distillation, feature projectors, adversarially-informed samples, and staged or multi-teacher curricula. While KD consistently improves compact models compared to training from scratch and enables deployment on resource-constrained platforms, open issues remain in robustness, task-specific alignment, and distillation under data heterogeneity.

papers_seen.author: Archer
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Core, Practical Tool for Compression — Strengths, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical method for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. It succeeds by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone (e.g., softened logits, intermediate representations, or relational signals), and by combining with complementary techniques (pruning, low-precision inference, architecture search, and data augmentation). KD enables substantial reductions in model size and latency while retaining much of teacher performance, but its effectiveness depends on careful choices about what to transfer, which examples to use, and how to adapt teachers and students to deployment constraints. Thoughtful design — including feature-level transfer, curriculum or selective-sample strategies, augmentation, and data-free synthesis when needed — makes KD a practical cornerstone of model compression for deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Powell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable, empirically effective approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. It supports multiple transfer signals (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps), operates with or without original training data, and composes naturally with complementary methods (pre-training of compact models, pruning, quantization, architecture search). KD enables substantial reductions in inference cost while retaining much teacher performance, but it is not a panacea: practitioners must address capacity mismatch, data or distributional heterogeneity, and the risk of transferring undesirable behaviors (biases or adversarial vulnerabilities). A pragmatic deployment pipeline treats KD as one component in a compression strategy, matched to task constraints and combined with targeted mitigations for fairness, robustness, and heterogeneous-data scenarios.
