papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Methods, Theory, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses and transfers knowledge from larger, often ensemble or teacher models into smaller student models to enable efficient deployment and improved generalization under resource constraints. Techniques range from matching final soft outputs to aligning intermediate representations, leveraging self-supervision, adversarial objectives, or curriculum and sample selection strategies. Distillation has been applied across classification, generation, retrieval, speech, and structured prediction, and it also offers avenues to transfer inductive biases, improve robustness, and preserve privacy. Empirical and theoretical work has clarified when distillation helps, what kind of "dark knowledge" is useful, and how regularization-like effects of soft targets can be harnessed even without a superior teacher.

papers_seen.author: Doyle
papers_seen.title: DE-RRD: A Knowledge Distillation Framework for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: Recent recommender systems have started to employ knowledge distillation, which is a model compression technique distilling knowledge from a cumbersome model (teacher) to a compact model (student), to reduce inference latency while maintaining performance. The state-of-the-art methods have only focused on making the student model accurately imitate the predictions of the teacher model. They have a limitation in that the prediction results incompletely reveal the teacher's knowledge. In this paper, we propose a novel knowledge distillation framework for recommender system, called DE-RRD, which enables the student model to learn from the latent knowledge encoded in the teacher model as well as from the teacher's predictions. Concretely, DE-RRD consists of two methods: 1) Distillation Experts (DE) that directly transfers the latent knowledge from the teacher model. DE exploits "experts" and a novel expert selection strategy for effectively distilling the vast teacher's knowledge to the student with limited capacity. 2) Relaxed Ranking Distillation (RRD) that transfers the knowledge revealed from the teacher's prediction with consideration of the relaxed ranking orders among items. Our extensive experiments show that DE-RRD outperforms the state-of-the-art competitors and achieves comparable or even better performance to that of the teacher model with faster inference time.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Survey of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical and flexible approach to compress large models and transfer knowledge across models, modalities, and tasks. Practitioners use KD to produce smaller, faster student models that retain much of a teacher's performance, to regularize training via self-distillation, and to enable multi-task or resource-heterogeneous deployment. Despite strong empirical results across vision, speech, translation, and question answering, distillation exhibits failure modes—e.g., propagation of teacher errors or poor handling of low-frequency phenomena—that motivate variants such as multi-teacher schemes, feature-level objectives, projector layers, and teacher-student co-training. The literature combines empirical recipes and growing theoretical analysis to guide when and how to mix soft teacher signals and hard labels, design teacher architectures, and choose representation vs. logit distillation for best trade-offs between accuracy, efficiency, and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Data Regimes, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a suite of techniques for transferring behavior and representations from larger teacher models into smaller, more efficient students so models can be deployed under latency, memory, or data/privacy constraints. Over the last decade KD has expanded from simple logit-matching into diverse objectives and workflows — including feature- and layer-wise matching, self- and online-distillation, adversarial or data-free synthesis, and task-aware layer mapping — that together form practical compression toolkits across vision and NLP. Effective distillation depends on careful choice of transferred signals, data strategy, and alignment between teacher and student capacity.

papers_seen.author: Munoz
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression methods form a broad set of techniques for transferring information from large or ensemble models into smaller, faster, or more interpretable models. These techniques are applied across modalities (vision, language, multimodal), deployment scenarios (edge devices, federated learning), and objectives (accuracy preservation, efficiency, interpretability, fairness). Advances include theoretical reframings that connect KD to regularization, a range of strategies for aligning outputs and internal representations, methods that restructure or progressively replace model components, and practical systems that enable heterogeneous and privacy-sensitive deployments. Despite clear empirical gains, open problems remain in understanding when and why different distillation targets (soft outputs, internal features, attention maps, module behavior) are most effective, and how to balance compression with robustness and interpretability.

papers_seen.author: Maddox
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Tool for Compression, Bias Transfer, and Robust Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is more than a model compression trick: it is a practical mechanism for transferring inductive biases, regularizing students, enabling privacy- and data-constrained deployments, and adapting architectures or modalities. When paired with complementary techniques—data augmentation, curriculum schedules, teacher ensembles, or generative replay—KD consistently narrows the gap between compact students and large teachers while addressing real-world constraints such as limited labeled data, compute, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Welch
papers_seen.title: Distillation as Default: A Practical Position on Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a necessary and practical core technique for compressing large deep models into deployable, efficient students. When combined with representation-level matching, careful pre-training of compact students, and attention to privacy and deployment constraints, KD preserves much of teacher performance while enabling low-latency, on-device, and federated use. However, naive soft-label matching is insufficient: best practice integrates intermediate-feature supervision, data- and architecture-aware pipelines, and multi-stage or multi-teacher strategies to handle domain shift, rare phenomena, and heterogeneous architectures.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Compressing GANs using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been used in several machine learning tasks such as domain transfer, super resolution, and synthetic data generation. State-of-the-art GANs often use tens of millions of parameters, making them expensive to deploy for applications in low SWAP (size, weight, and power) hardware, such as mobile devices, and for applications with real time capabilities. There has been no work found to reduce the number of parameters used in GANs. Therefore, we propose a method to compress GANs using knowledge distillation techniques, in which a smaller "student" GAN learns to mimic a larger "teacher" GAN. We show that the distillation methods used on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and Celeb-A datasets can compress teacher GANs at ratios of 1669:1, 58:1, and 87:1, respectively, while retaining the quality of the generated image. From our experiments, we observe a qualitative limit for GAN's compression. Moreover, we observe that, with a fixed parameter budget, compressed GANs outperform GANs trained using standard training methods. We conjecture that this is partially owing to the optimization landscape of over-parameterized GANs which allows efficient training using alternating gradient descent. Thus, training an over-parameterized GAN followed by our proposed compression scheme provides a high quality generative model with a small number of parameters.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Insights, and Practical Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large models into smaller, faster ones by transferring information from a teacher to a student. It has been applied across supervised, self-supervised, multimodal and domain-adaptation settings to reduce inference cost while retaining much of the teacher's performance. Progress includes direct soft-target matching, feature- and relation-based imitation, self- and progressive-distillation strategies, and task- or domain-aware adaptations. Empirical work highlights both the power of KD to produce efficient models for deployment and important practical considerations—such as the value of pre-training, the role of data augmentation and sample selection, and computational bottlenecks—that shape effective distillation regimes. Despite advances, optimization mismatches, teacher–student capacity differences, and data-domain shift remain active challenges guiding current research and practice.

papers_seen.author: James
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a heuristic for compressing large models into a broadly applicable set of techniques that enable smaller, faster, and in some cases fairer or more interpretable models. Its effectiveness depends on choices about what to transfer (logits, features, structure), how to prepare training data, and how to reconcile teacher imperfections with student capacity. When these design choices are matched to the task and constraints, KD enables substantial compression with small performance loss and can address privacy and resource limitations.

papers_seen.author: Walsh
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Practical Core of Model Compression — and How to Use It Safely
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, high-impact approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller students suitable for deployment. KD can transfer soft targets, intermediate representations, or training dynamics to produce compact models that preserve much of teacher performance. Effective, production-ready compression treats KD as the central engine but pairs it with complementary techniques (representation alignment, projectors, pruning/quantization, privacy-aware protocols and ensemble or multi-teacher strategies). KD yields strong size–performance tradeoffs in both vision and NLP when engineered for student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints; however, practitioners must also manage limitations such as transferred biases, capacity mismatch, and domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Is Label Smoothing Truly Incompatible with Knowledge Distillation: An Empirical Study
papers_seen.abstract: This work aims to empirically clarify a recently discovered perspective that label smoothing is incompatible with knowledge distillation. We begin by introducing the motivation behind on how this incompatibility is raised, i.e., label smoothing erases relative information between teacher logits. We provide a novel connection on how label smoothing affects distributions of semantically similar and dissimilar classes. Then we propose a metric to quantitatively measure the degree of erased information in sample's representation. After that, we study its one-sidedness and imperfection of the incompatibility view through massive analyses, visualizations and comprehensive experiments on Image Classification, Binary Networks, and Neural Machine Translation. Finally, we broadly discuss several circumstances wherein label smoothing will indeed lose its effectiveness. Project page: http://zhiqiangshen.com/projects/LS_and_KD/index.html.

papers_seen.author: Tran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practical Patterns
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring predictive behavior or intermediate representations. Across vision, speech, and natural language tasks, practitioners apply KD to reduce model size, latency, and resource cost while retaining much of the teacher's performance. Variants of KD extend beyond soft-label matching to feature- and layer-level alignment, multi-teacher and online schemes, cross-modal transfer, and data-limited or privacy-sensitive settings. Effective distillation typically combines careful choice of transfer target, student architecture and pre-training, and complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization). Open challenges include principled data selection or synthesis for distillation, handling imperfect or heterogeneous teachers, preserving robustness and fairness, and scaling distillation to large distributed training scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Suarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Path to Compact Deep Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, practical approach for turning large, high-performing deep models into smaller, faster models suitable for real-world deployment. Beyond pure compression, KD serves as a flexible training paradigm that can be combined with pre-training, privacy-preserving workflows, and architecture-aware mimicry to preserve task performance while meeting latency, memory, and device constraints. A pragmatic KD pipeline aligns the choice of distillation signal, teacher design, student pretraining, and data strategy to the deployment context.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Collaborative Distillation for Ultra-Resolution Universal Style Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Universal style transfer methods typically leverage rich representations from deep Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models (e.g., VGG-19) pre-trained on large collections of images. Despite the effectiveness, its application is heavily constrained by the large model size to handle ultra-resolution images given limited memory. In this work, we present a new knowledge distillation method (named Collaborative Distillation) for encoder-decoder based neural style transfer to reduce the convolutional filters. The main idea is underpinned by a finding that the encoder-decoder pairs construct an exclusive collaborative relationship, which is regarded as a new kind of knowledge for style transfer models. Moreover, to overcome the feature size mismatch when applying collaborative distillation, a linear embedding loss is introduced to drive the student network to learn a linear embedding of the teacher's features. Extensive experiments show the effectiveness of our method when applied to different universal style transfer approaches (WCT and AdaIN), even if the model size is reduced by 15.5 times. Especially, on WCT with the compressed models, we achieve ultra-resolution (over 40 megapixels) universal style transfer on a 12GB GPU for the first time. Further experiments on optimization-based stylization scheme show the generality of our algorithm on different stylization paradigms. Our code and trained models are available at https://github.com/mingsun-tse/collaborative-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses or transfers knowledge from larger or multiple teacher models into smaller or otherwise constrained student models to reduce inference cost while retaining performance. Across computer vision, speech, recommendation, and NLP, KD techniques include matching soft outputs, transferring intermediate features, multi-teacher and staged protocols, and data-free synthesis of surrogate training examples. Practical systems combine KD with pruning or architecture changes, and recent theory helps explain when and why distillation helps. Despite strong empirical gains, challenges remain in handling heterogeneous teachers, data unavailability, task-specific adaptations (e.g., detection, translation), and robustness on low-frequency or out-of-distribution phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Unifying Paradigm for Compression, Adaptation, and Robust Training
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be considered not merely as a compression trick but as a general and practical training paradigm. Across modalities and tasks, KD transfers information about function, structure, and uncertainty from one model (or ensemble) to another, enabling smaller, faster, or more adaptable models while improving generalization, interpretability, and domain transfer. Success depends on how teacher knowledge is selected, represented, and combined with data-side techniques; thoughtful design choices (layer mapping, sample selection, augmentation, and teacher trust) determine whether KD yields compression, robustness, or better task-specific performance.

papers_seen.author: Gilbert
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Composable Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as a central, composable component of model-compression pipelines for deep learning and NLP. KD is versatile—able to transfer logits, intermediate representations, and relational signals—and can be combined with pruning, quantization, architecture redesign, or data-synthesis techniques to produce deployable students that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Its practical success requires matching distilled signals to student capacity, handling data and distributional constraints, and explicitly addressing fairness and robustness concerns. When designed and evaluated carefully, KD enables effective trade-offs between efficiency and task performance across modalities.

papers_seen.author: Mckee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Model Compression: Power, Patterns, and Precautions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, flexible approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a toolkit rather than a single recipe, and combined with complementary compression methods and data strategies, KD enables substantial reductions in latency, memory, and energy while retaining much of teacher performance. However, distillation can transfer teacher weaknesses (biases, brittleness, low-frequency errors) and requires careful choices about what to transfer, how to align representations across heterogeneous architectures, and how to handle limited or private data. Practical deployment therefore calls for method selection tailored to task and constraints, plus safeguards for robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques transfer information from larger, ensemble, or otherwise expensive teacher models into smaller, cheaper student models so that deployed systems meet latency, memory, and power constraints while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. Over the past decade researchers have developed a family of approaches — soft-target matching, intermediate representation and relation matching, online and self-distillation, curriculum and data-aware strategies, and combinations with pruning/quantization or architecture search — that together form a practical toolkit for compressing models used in vision and language tasks. Empirical work shows KD can produce dramatic inference-speed and memory gains with modest accuracy loss when methods are chosen to match task, data, and deployment constraints; important open problems remain around optimization mismatches, robustness to distribution shift, and how best to distill under limited or sensitive data conditions.

papers_seen.author: Zuniga
papers_seen.title: Large scale distributed neural network training through online distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Techniques such as ensembling and distillation promise model quality improvements when paired with almost any base model. However, due to increased test-time cost (for ensembles) and increased complexity of the training pipeline (for distillation), these techniques are challenging to use in industrial settings. In this paper we explore a variant of distillation which is relatively straightforward to use as it does not require a complicated multi-stage setup or many new hyperparameters. Our first claim is that online distillation enables us to use extra parallelism to fit very large datasets about twice as fast. Crucially, we can still speed up training even after we have already reached the point at which additional parallelism provides no benefit for synchronous or asynchronous stochastic gradient descent. Two neural networks trained on disjoint subsets of the data can share knowledge by encouraging each model to agree with the predictions the other model would have made. These predictions can come from a stale version of the other model so they can be safely computed using weights that only rarely get transmitted. Our second claim is that online distillation is a cost-effective way to make the exact predictions of a model dramatically more reproducible. We support our claims using experiments on the Criteo Display Ad Challenge dataset, ImageNet, and the largest to-date dataset used for neural language modeling, containing $6\times 10^{11}$ tokens and based on the Common Crawl repository of web data.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Recommendations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile method for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD works across modalities (vision, language, graphs, and generative models) by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from teachers to students. When applied thoughtfully—selecting appropriate distillation signals, aligning internal representations, and integrating complementary compression techniques—KD reliably yields compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is not a plug-and-play cure: its success depends on teacher quality, data strategy, optimization choices, and architecture alignment, so practitioners should pair KD with task-aware curricula, representation-level objectives, and other compression tools to realize robust deployment.

papers_seen.author: Cherry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Practical Recipes, and Open Issues
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, faster student models by transferring information beyond hard labels. Across modalities and tasks, KD methods include soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate feature or attention alignment, layer-mapping strategies, and combined pipelines that integrate pruning, quantization, or architecture-aware design. Empirically, KD routinely improves compact models relative to training from scratch and enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, but success depends on student capacity, the choice of distilled signals, data availability and quality, and careful alignment of teacher and student architectures. Ongoing challenges include robustly preserving teacher properties (robustness, fairness), operating under data scarcity or privacy limits, and automating architecture and signal selection for effective transfer.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Distilled Semantics for Comprehensive Scene Understanding from Videos
papers_seen.abstract: Whole understanding of the surroundings is paramount to autonomous systems. Recent works have shown that deep neural networks can learn geometry (depth) and motion (optical flow) from a monocular video without any explicit supervision from ground truth annotations, particularly hard to source for these two tasks. In this paper, we take an additional step toward holistic scene understanding with monocular cameras by learning depth and motion alongside with semantics, with supervision for the latter provided by a pre-trained network distilling proxy ground truth images. We address the three tasks jointly by a) a novel training protocol based on knowledge distillation and self-supervision and b) a compact network architecture which enables efficient scene understanding on both power hungry GPUs and low-power embedded platforms. We thoroughly assess the performance of our framework and show that it yields state-of-the-art results for monocular depth estimation, optical flow and motion segmentation.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Highlight Every Step: Knowledge Distillation via Collaborative Teaching
papers_seen.abstract: High storage and computational costs obstruct deep neural networks to be deployed on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation aims to train a compact student network by transferring knowledge from a larger pre-trained teacher model. However, most existing methods on knowledge distillation ignore the valuable information among training process associated with training results. In this paper, we provide a new Collaborative Teaching Knowledge Distillation (CTKD) strategy which employs two special teachers. Specifically, one teacher trained from scratch (i.e., scratch teacher) assists the student step by step using its temporary outputs. It forces the student to approach the optimal path towards the final logits with high accuracy. The other pre-trained teacher (i.e., expert teacher) guides the student to focus on a critical region which is more useful for the task. The combination of the knowledge from two special teachers can significantly improve the performance of the student network in knowledge distillation. The results of experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, SVHN and Tiny ImageNet datasets verify that the proposed knowledge distillation method is efficient and achieves state-of-the-art performance.

papers_seen.author: Bowers
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, efficient students by transferring behavioral and representational knowledge from teacher models. A rich family of distillation techniques—ranging from soft-target (logit) matching to intermediate feature imitation, layer-mapping, projector-based transforms, and meta-learned teachers—enables practical trade-offs between accuracy, latency, and deployability across vision and language tasks. Practical success depends on choosing appropriate distillation signals, adapting teacher behavior to student capacity, and addressing data or deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Garrison
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly adopted approach to compress large neural models into smaller, faster students for deployment in resource- and privacy-constrained settings. A rich set of practical variants has emerged — from matching teacher logits to aligning intermediate representations, multi-teacher and self-distillation schemes, and data-free or synthesized-data approaches — and KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression methods and deployment-aware design. Remaining challenges include optimization mismatch between teacher and student, distribution shift, rare-token or low-frequency behavior degradation, and the potential transfer of teacher biases; addressing these requires task-aware choices about what to transfer, how to build students and teachers, and how to handle limited or private data.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Imperative for Deploying Large NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained models have driven major NLP advances but are often impractical for real-world deployment because of size, latency, privacy, and data-distribution constraints. Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression strategies enable retaining most of a large model's performance while producing models that meet latency, memory, and regulatory requirements. Effective KD encompasses diverse techniques — task-adaptive compression, feature mimicking, data-free distillation, teacher meta-learning, privacy-aware distillation, and distributed/continual distillation — which together form a practical toolkit for making state-of-the-art NLP useful at scale.

papers_seen.author: Blair
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of techniques for transferring behavior from large, expensive teacher models into smaller, faster students so models can be deployed under compute, latency, memory, or privacy constraints. KD methods extend beyond simple logit matching to include intermediate representation matching, layer mapping, adversarial or decision-boundary focused sample selection, data-free generation of training examples, meta-learned teachers, and divergence-aware training objectives. Empirical work shows KD often preserves much of a teacher's performance when adapted to task and deployment constraints; theoretical and empirical analyses reveal optimization limits, distributional fragilities, and conditions under which distillation succeeds or fails. Combining KD with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and tailoring the distillation signal to student capacity and available data produces the most reliable compression outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Beck
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses larger teacher models into smaller student models by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. Approaches include matching softened logits, aligning intermediate representations or attention maps, mapping or projecting teacher layers to student layers, and operating in offline, online, federated, or data-free regimes. Distillation is commonly combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and task-aware data strategies. Practical success depends on choosing which signals to transfer, aligning teacher and student capacity, managing data or privacy constraints, and designing curricula or multi-stage pipelines that reflect deployment needs. While distillation routinely produces compact models that retain much of teacher performance, open challenges remain in representation mismatch, amplifying teacher biases, and ensuring robustness and fairness under compression.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature and flexible approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable ones. When combined with careful choices—such as pre-training compact students, data-free distillation for privacy, adaptive multi-teacher strategies, feature-level imitation, and teacher-side learning—KD can deliver strong task performance with much smaller inference cost. However, KD is not a panacea: optimization gaps between teacher and student, propagation of teacher biases, and dataset mismatches can limit gains unless explicitly addressed. A pragmatic KD pipeline therefore integrates algorithmic innovations and fairness/optimization checks to realize both efficiency and reliable behavior in production NLP and deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Understanding and Improving Lexical Choice in Non-Autoregressive Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is essential for training non-autoregressive translation (NAT) models by reducing the complexity of the raw data with an autoregressive teacher model. In this study, we empirically show that as a side effect of this training, the lexical choice errors on low-frequency words are propagated to the NAT model from the teacher model. To alleviate this problem, we propose to expose the raw data to NAT models to restore the useful information of low-frequency words, which are missed in the distilled data. To this end, we introduce an extra Kullback-Leibler divergence term derived by comparing the lexical choice of NAT model and that embedded in the raw data. Experimental results across language pairs and model architectures demonstrate the effectiveness and universality of the proposed approach. Extensive analyses confirm our claim that our approach improves performance by reducing the lexical choice errors on low-frequency words. Encouragingly, our approach pushes the SOTA NAT performance on the WMT14 English-German and WMT16 Romanian-English datasets up to 27.8 and 33.8 BLEU points, respectively. The source code will be released.

papers_seen.author: Hoffman
papers_seen.title: Federated Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Distributed learning frameworks often rely on exchanging model parameters across workers, instead of revealing their raw data. A prime example is federated learning that exchanges the gradients or weights of each neural network model. Under limited communication resources, however, such a method becomes extremely costly particularly for modern deep neural networks having a huge number of model parameters. In this regard, federated distillation (FD) is a compelling distributed learning solution that only exchanges the model outputs whose dimensions are commonly much smaller than the model sizes (e.g., 10 labels in the MNIST dataset). The goal of this chapter is to provide a deep understanding of FD while demonstrating its communication efficiency and applicability to a variety of tasks. To this end, towards demystifying the operational principle of FD, the first part of this chapter provides a novel asymptotic analysis for two foundational algorithms of FD, namely knowledge distillation (KD) and co-distillation (CD), by exploiting the theory of neural tangent kernel (NTK). Next, the second part elaborates on a baseline implementation of FD for a classification task, and illustrates its performance in terms of accuracy and communication efficiency compared to FL. Lastly, to demonstrate the applicability of FD to various distributed learning tasks and environments, the third part presents two selected applications, namely FD over asymmetric uplink-and-downlink wireless channels and FD for reinforcement learning.

papers_seen.author: Warner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Model Compression and Adaptation in NLP and Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as a central, practical technique for compressing and adapting large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD is versatile: it transfers predictive behavior, intermediate representations, and ensemble knowledge; supports data-free or privacy-sensitive settings; and can improve robustness and calibration when combined with complementary methods. Realizing KD’s full potential requires matching the distillation recipe to deployment goals and addressing failure modes such as optimization mismatches, bias transfer, and poor handling of low-frequency phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Cannon
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression aim to transfer knowledge from large or ensemble teacher models to smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained student models while preserving predictive performance. Approaches span soft-label imitation, intermediate feature matching, architecture-aware compression, data-centric augmentations, online and distributed schemes, and teacher-design strategies. Applications include NLP (BERT compression and task-specific distillation), speech recognition, graph neural networks, and vision tasks. Empirical results across benchmarks show that carefully chosen distillation objectives, alignment mechanisms, and data strategies can yield compact models that approach teacher performance while enabling substantial speed and memory gains. Open challenges remain in automating architecture search for compression, preserving robustness and domain generalization, and scaling distillation to very large datasets and model families.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: DINE: Domain Adaptation from Single and Multiple Black-box Predictors
papers_seen.abstract: To ease the burden of labeling, unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) aims to transfer knowledge in previous and related labeled datasets (sources) to a new unlabeled dataset (target). Despite impressive progress, prior methods always need to access the raw source data and develop data-dependent alignment approaches to recognize the target samples in a transductive learning manner, which may raise privacy concerns from source individuals. Several recent studies resort to an alternative solution by exploiting the well-trained white-box model from the source domain, yet, it may still leak the raw data through generative adversarial learning. This paper studies a practical and interesting setting for UDA, where only black-box source models (i.e., only network predictions are available) are provided during adaptation in the target domain. To solve this problem, we propose a new two-step knowledge adaptation framework called DIstill and fine-tuNE (DINE). Taking into consideration the target data structure, DINE first distills the knowledge from the source predictor to a customized target model, then fine-tunes the distilled model to further fit the target domain. Besides, neural networks are not required to be identical across domains in DINE, even allowing effective adaptation on a low-resource device. Empirical results on three UDA scenarios (i.e., single-source, multi-source, and partial-set) confirm that DINE achieves highly competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art data-dependent approaches. Code is available at \url{https://github.com/tim-learn/DINE/}.

papers_seen.author: Phillips
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation transfers knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models so students retain much of the teacher’s performance while reducing inference cost, memory, and latency. The literature has expanded from simple soft-label matching to a broad toolbox that includes intermediate-feature and attention matching, self-distillation, multi-teacher schemes, data-free and zero-shot approaches, curriculum and sample-selection strategies, and combinations with pruning/quantization or architecture search. Empirical work shows that careful choices about what to transfer, how to align architectures, and how to handle data or privacy constraints determine success; outstanding challenges include optimization dynamics, distribution shift, rare-token behaviors, and guaranteeing robust or fair behavior after compression.

papers_seen.author: Young
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Trade-offs, and Practical Recipes
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. KD operates across levels—from soft output (logit) imitation to intermediate-feature and layer-wise alignment—and is often combined with architecture search, pruning, or data-synthesis to meet deployment constraints. Beyond pure compression, KD can act as a regularizer that improves generalization and robustness, but its effectiveness depends on student capacity, the choice of distillation signal, data availability or privacy constraints, and careful matching of teacher and student objectives.

papers_seen.author: Diaz
papers_seen.title: Model Compression with Two-stage Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation for Web Question Answering System
papers_seen.abstract: Deep pre-training and fine-tuning models (such as BERT and OpenAI GPT) have demonstrated excellent results in question answering areas. However, due to the sheer amount of model parameters, the inference speed of these models is very slow. How to apply these complex models to real business scenarios becomes a challenging but practical problem. Previous model compression methods usually suffer from information loss during the model compression procedure, leading to inferior models compared with the original one. To tackle this challenge, we propose a Two-stage Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation (TMKD for short) method for web Question Answering system. We first develop a general Q\&A distillation task for student model pre-training, and further fine-tune this pre-trained student model with multi-teacher knowledge distillation on downstream tasks (like Web Q\&A task, MNLI, SNLI, RTE tasks from GLUE), which effectively reduces the overfitting bias in individual teacher models, and transfers more general knowledge to the student model. The experiment results show that our method can significantly outperform the baseline methods and even achieve comparable results with the original teacher models, along with substantial speedup of model inference.

papers_seen.author: Whitehead
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, flexible, and empirically effective approach for compressing large deep learning and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD operates through multiple mechanisms — soft-target regularization, transfer of intermediate representations, and alignment of optimization/inductive bias — and is most reliable when integrated into engineering pipelines that account for data availability, teacher-student mismatch, and deployment constraints. While KD is not a silver bullet, its versatility and compatibility with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data-centric strategies make it the natural default for production-focused compression.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Adapt-and-Distill: Developing Small, Fast and Effective Pretrained Language Models for Domains
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained models have achieved great success in many natural language processing tasks. However, when they are applied in specific domains, these models suffer from domain shift and bring challenges in fine-tuning and online serving for latency and capacity constraints. In this paper, we present a general approach to developing small, fast and effective pre-trained models for specific domains. This is achieved by adapting the off-the-shelf general pre-trained models and performing task-agnostic knowledge distillation in target domains. Specifically, we propose domain-specific vocabulary expansion in the adaptation stage and employ corpus level occurrence probability to choose the size of incremental vocabulary automatically. Then we systematically explore different strategies to compress the large pre-trained models for specific domains. We conduct our experiments in the biomedical and computer science domain. The experimental results demonstrate that our approach achieves better performance over the BERT BASE model in domain-specific tasks while 3.3x smaller and 5.1x faster than BERT BASE. The code and pre-trained models are available at https://aka.ms/adalm.

papers_seen.author: Powell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable, empirically effective approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. It supports multiple transfer signals (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps), operates with or without original training data, and composes naturally with complementary methods (pre-training of compact models, pruning, quantization, architecture search). KD enables substantial reductions in inference cost while retaining much teacher performance, but it is not a panacea: practitioners must address capacity mismatch, data or distributional heterogeneity, and the risk of transferring undesirable behaviors (biases or adversarial vulnerabilities). A pragmatic deployment pipeline treats KD as one component in a compression strategy, matched to task constraints and combined with targeted mitigations for fairness, robustness, and heterogeneous-data scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Learning Compact Metrics for MT
papers_seen.abstract: Recent developments in machine translation and multilingual text generation have led researchers to adopt trained metrics such as COMET or BLEURT, which treat evaluation as a regression problem and use representations from multilingual pre-trained models such as XLM-RoBERTa or mBERT. Yet studies on related tasks suggest that these models are most efficient when they are large, which is costly and impractical for evaluation. We investigate the trade-off between multilinguality and model capacity with RemBERT, a state-of-the-art multilingual language model, using data from the WMT Metrics Shared Task. We present a series of experiments which show that model size is indeed a bottleneck for cross-lingual transfer, then demonstrate how distillation can help addressing this bottleneck, by leveraging synthetic data generation and transferring knowledge from one teacher to multiple students trained on related languages. Our method yields up to 10.5% improvement over vanilla fine-tuning and reaches 92.6% of RemBERT's performance using only a third of its parameters.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Recommendations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile method for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD works across modalities (vision, language, graphs, and generative models) by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from teachers to students. When applied thoughtfully—selecting appropriate distillation signals, aligning internal representations, and integrating complementary compression techniques—KD reliably yields compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is not a plug-and-play cure: its success depends on teacher quality, data strategy, optimization choices, and architecture alignment, so practitioners should pair KD with task-aware curricula, representation-level objectives, and other compression tools to realize robust deployment.

papers_seen.author: Bass
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach to producing small, fast models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. When combined with complementary techniques (e.g., layer mapping, multi-stage curricula, data augmentation, and hardware-aware compression), KD enables deployable NLP and deep-learning systems across constrained environments while admitting clear failure modes that demand targeted remedies.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Tool for Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is more than a compression trick: it is a flexible training paradigm that enables deployment of high-performing models under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. By choosing what to transfer (soft targets, intermediate features, or relational signals), how to generate or select data (real, public, or synthesized), and how to schedule and regularize student training, practitioners can shape trade-offs among accuracy, robustness, interpretability, and privacy. KD’s effectiveness depends on careful alignment of teacher signals, student capacity, and data regime; when combined with multi-teacher strategies, adversarial data synthesis, or differential-privacy mechanisms, KD supports practical deployment across vision, language, graph, and multimodal tasks.

papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: Ensemble Knowledge Distillation for CTR Prediction
papers_seen.abstract: Recently, deep learning-based models have been widely studied for click-through rate (CTR) prediction and lead to improved prediction accuracy in many industrial applications. However, current research focuses primarily on building complex network architectures to better capture sophisticated feature interactions and dynamic user behaviors. The increased model complexity may slow down online inference and hinder its adoption in real-time applications. Instead, our work targets at a new model training strategy based on knowledge distillation (KD). KD is a teacher-student learning framework to transfer knowledge learned from a teacher model to a student model. The KD strategy not only allows us to simplify the student model as a vanilla DNN model but also achieves significant accuracy improvements over the state-of-the-art teacher models. The benefits thus motivate us to further explore the use of a powerful ensemble of teachers for more accurate student model training. We also propose some novel techniques to facilitate ensembled CTR prediction, including teacher gating and early stopping by distillation loss. We conduct comprehensive experiments against 12 existing models and across three industrial datasets. Both offline and online A/B testing results show the effectiveness of our KD-based training strategy.

papers_seen.author: Oliver
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of techniques that transfer information from large, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, efficient student models to enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD methods go beyond simple logit-matching to include feature- and relation-level imitation, data-free and zero-shot strategies, multi-teacher and self-distillation schemes, and combinations with other compression tools. Empirical work across vision, language, graph, and generative modeling domains demonstrates substantial size and latency reductions with modest performance loss when methods are adapted to task, data availability, and deployment constraints. Important open challenges include matching internal representations across architectures, avoiding transfer of undesirable biases, and ensuring robustness and privacy in constrained or federated settings.

papers_seen.author: Welch
papers_seen.title: Distillation as Default: A Practical Position on Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a necessary and practical core technique for compressing large deep models into deployable, efficient students. When combined with representation-level matching, careful pre-training of compact students, and attention to privacy and deployment constraints, KD preserves much of teacher performance while enabling low-latency, on-device, and federated use. However, naive soft-label matching is insufficient: best practice integrates intermediate-feature supervision, data- and architecture-aware pipelines, and multi-stage or multi-teacher strategies to handle domain shift, rare phenomena, and heterogeneous architectures.

papers_seen.author: Walls
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile approach for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large or ensemble teacher models into smaller student models. Across vision, language, graphs, and multimodal problems, KD is used alone or combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data-centric strategies to produce compact models that preserve much of teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints. Empirical and analytical work highlights mechanisms behind KD’s success, practical recipes for improving student fidelity, and persistent challenges (data mismatch, rare-token behavior, robustness, and optimization). This synthesis summarizes methods, applications, practical recommendations, and key open problems reported in recent literature.

papers_seen.author: Figueroa
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly adopted family of techniques for compressing high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, or inductive biases. Across vision, language, and multimodal tasks, KD methods aim to preserve teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and compute. Practical pipelines combine distillation with architecture adaptations, data strategies, and complementary compression (pruning, quantization) and must address failure modes related to data mismatch, rare-token fidelity, teacher–student capacity gaps, and privacy or domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Variants, and Practical Insights
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models into smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained student models. KD methods range from soft-label (logit) matching to feature- and layer-level imitation, self-distillation, multi-teacher schemes, and data- or privacy-aware variants that synthesize or reuse surrogate data. Applied across vision, speech, recommender systems, and NLP, KD supports deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints while enabling domain adaptation and robustness-focused objectives. Practical success depends on careful choices about what signals to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, how to handle limited or private data, and how to combine distillation with complementary compression methods.

papers_seen.author: Powers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a flexible, deployment-oriented family of techniques that transfer information from larger or multiple teachers into smaller students. KD can be applied at the level of logits, intermediate representations, or task-specific modules and is readily combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data-synthesis methods to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. While KD often preserves much of a teacher's performance in compressed models, realizing its benefits in NLP requires careful choices about what signals to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, and how to mitigate optimization and data-shift issues. With thoughtful protocol design, KD enables wide deployment of powerful language models under realistic resource limits, but it remains important to pair distillation with representation-aware objectives and engineering practices to avoid degrading rare-token behavior or amplifying teacher artifacts.

papers_seen.author: Mueller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a central, pragmatic approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD delivers strong empirical gains across domains by transferring soft outputs, intermediate representations, or task-specific behaviors from teachers to students. Its strengths are practical: it supports deployment on constrained hardware, enables multi-teacher and cross-model transfer, and integrates with other compression tools. At the same time, KD is not a plug-and-play solution: theoretical and empirical work shows limits under data heterogeneity, imperfect teachers, and mismatched architectures, so KD must be applied with task-aware choices (signal type, layer alignment, teacher selection, and curricula) and often combined with complementary methods to realize reliable, high-fidelity compression.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical, flexible approach for turning large, high-performing deep and pretrained NLP models into smaller, faster models suitable for real-world deployment. The literature shows KD operates via multiple signals (soft targets, intermediate features, attention or relational structure), multiple workflows (data-driven, data-free, multi-stage, multi-teacher), and often in combination with orthogonal compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical work demonstrates that properly designed distillation pipelines can recover most of a teacher's utility in a much smaller footprint, but success depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity, addressing data limitations and privacy constraints, and engineering choices such as layer mapping, augmentation, and progressive or curriculum-driven training.

papers_seen.author: Parsons
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Compressing NLP and Deep Learning Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a practical and flexible route to compress large neural models for real-world deployment. When applied carefully — via multi-stage pipelines, layer-aware mappings, internal-representation transfer, self-distillation, or even without original data — KD can preserve much of the teacher performance while reducing latency and memory. KD also composes effectively with orthogonal compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to meet diverse resource constraints. These properties make KD a central technique for bringing large pretrained models into production in NLP and other domains.

papers_seen.author: Decker
papers_seen.title: Practical and Principled Knowledge Distillation for Compressing NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature and versatile approach for compressing large deep learning and NLP models into smaller, faster students while preserving much of the teacher’s performance. Effective compression in practice requires matching the distillation technique to the deployment objective: using self-distillation or multi-teacher strategies to extract richer supervisory signals, combining KD with architecture search or pruning for task-specific efficiency, applying appropriate soft/hard label mixing informed by bias–variance tradeoffs, and controlling data and privacy considerations during distillation. When these elements are combined, KD can deliver substantial runtime and memory savings with minimal accuracy loss, making it central to deploying modern NLP systems under resource constraints.

papers_seen.author: Pham
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential but Context-Sensitive Tool for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical suite of techniques that transfers information from large teacher models into smaller student models so that compact systems approach teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints. When combined with representation-level objectives, multi-teacher schedules, data-aware strategies, and architecture-aware design, KD enables substantial reductions in compute, memory, and latency. Its effectiveness depends on careful handling of data availability, teacher-student mismatch, and ethical or robustness considerations.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Towards Model Agnostic Federated Learning Using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Is it possible to design an universal API for federated learning using which an ad-hoc group of data-holders (agents) collaborate with each other and perform federated learning? Such an API would necessarily need to be model-agnostic i.e. make no assumption about the model architecture being used by the agents, and also cannot rely on having representative public data at hand. Knowledge distillation (KD) is the obvious tool of choice to design such protocols. However, surprisingly, we show that most natural KD-based federated learning protocols have poor performance.   To investigate this, we propose a new theoretical framework, Federated Kernel ridge regression, which can capture both model heterogeneity as well as data heterogeneity. Our analysis shows that the degradation is largely due to a fundamental limitation of knowledge distillation under data heterogeneity. We further validate our framework by analyzing and designing new protocols based on KD. Their performance on real world experiments using neural networks, though still unsatisfactory, closely matches our theoretical predictions.

papers_seen.author: Cohen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Strategy for Model Compression and Adaptation in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible approach to produce compact models that retain much of the performance of larger models. Beyond simple compression, KD can transfer inductive biases, enable domain adaptation and vocabulary specialization, support privacy-preserving and federated scenarios, work without access to original data, and improve robustness and feature quality when carefully applied. When combined with targeted techniques — feature mimicking, weighted soft labels, projector layers, or adversarial robustness objectives — KD becomes a unifying toolkit to meet latency, capacity, and privacy constraints in real-world NLP and deep learning deployments.
