papers_seen.author: Wolfe
papers_seen.title: Robust and Resource-Efficient Data-Free Knowledge Distillation by Generative Pseudo Replay
papers_seen.abstract: Data-Free Knowledge Distillation (KD) allows knowledge transfer from a trained neural network (teacher) to a more compact one (student) in the absence of original training data. Existing works use a validation set to monitor the accuracy of the student over real data and report the highest performance throughout the entire process. However, validation data may not be available at distillation time either, making it infeasible to record the student snapshot that achieved the peak accuracy. Therefore, a practical data-free KD method should be robust and ideally provide monotonically increasing student accuracy during distillation. This is challenging because the student experiences knowledge degradation due to the distribution shift of the synthetic data. A straightforward approach to overcome this issue is to store and rehearse the generated samples periodically, which increases the memory footprint and creates privacy concerns. We propose to model the distribution of the previously observed synthetic samples with a generative network. In particular, we design a Variational Autoencoder (VAE) with a training objective that is customized to learn the synthetic data representations optimally. The student is rehearsed by the generative pseudo replay technique, with samples produced by the VAE. Hence knowledge degradation can be prevented without storing any samples. Experiments on image classification benchmarks show that our method optimizes the expected value of the distilled model accuracy while eliminating the large memory overhead incurred by the sample-storing methods.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques provide practical routes to deploy large, high-performance neural models in resource- constrained or latency-sensitive settings. Methods vary in what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, relational structure), how training data is used or synthesized, and whether compression is task-agnostic or task-adaptive. In natural language tasks, KD has enabled dramatic size and speed gains for large pretrained models (e.g., BERT) as well as the feasibility of simple architectures that retain most of the original performance. Despite empirical success, challenges remain: choosing what to transfer for maximal utility, constructing or selecting suitable training examples, handling heterogeneous or private data (federated or data-free settings), and designing teacher-student curricula or architectures that improve transfer. Emerging directions include task-adaptive compression, many-to-many layer alignment, multi-teacher and teacher-aware training, and principled approaches to data selection or generation during distillation.

papers_seen.author: Frost
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, versatile approach for turning large pre-trained models into smaller, deployable ones. By transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from teachers to students, KD enables substantial reductions in size and inference cost while retaining much of the original performance. Practical KD pipelines combine choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to supplement distillation with complementary compression and data strategies. Despite clear practical benefits, KD requires careful method selection to handle capacity mismatch, data scarcity, distribution shift, and risks of transferring teacher biases; a disciplined pipeline and evaluation strategy are therefore essential for reliable deployment.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression strategies enable smaller, faster models to inherit performance from larger teachers by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or ensemble knowledge. Techniques range from logit-based soft-target distillation to feature- and attention-level mimicry, multi-teacher and task-adaptive pipelines, and methods that relax the need for original training data or strong teachers. Across computer vision and natural language processing tasks, distilled students can approach teacher accuracy while drastically reducing parameters and latency; complementary strategies such as careful pre-training of compact models and architecture search further improve trade-offs between efficiency and effectiveness. Key challenges remain in preserving rare-token behavior, aligning heterogeneous teacher–student inputs, and ensuring privacy and robustness during compression.

papers_seen.author: Maldonado
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques reduce model size or communication cost by transferring knowledge from larger or multiple models (teachers) to smaller or otherwise constrained models (students). Methods vary from matching soft outputs to transferring intermediate features, training teachers to be student-friendly, coordinating multiple teachers, and combining distillation with pruning or federated/online schemes. Empirical and theoretical work highlights how distilled "dark knowledge" improves student generalization, how architectural components (e.g., projectors) shape transfer, and how distillation can be adapted for privacy, heterogeneity, and large-scale or multi-task NLP applications.

papers_seen.author: Chavez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Compression: Effective but Context-Sensitive
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful and practical approach to compress large neural models into smaller, faster, or more hardware-friendly students while retaining much of teacher performance. Its effectiveness spans supervised, self-supervised, and cross-modal settings, but the choice of what to transfer (logits, features, intermediate representations, attention), how to measure discrepancy, and how to combine KD with pruning or quantization critically determines success. I argue that KD should be treated as a toolbox of complementary techniques whose components must be matched to task, teacher quality, and deployment constraints to obtain reliable and robust compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Context-Sensitive Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and widely applicable method for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search, or data augmentation), and when adapted to task and data constraints, KD enables large reductions in size and latency while retaining much of a teacher's performance. At the same time, KD’s success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how teachers and students are matched, and how to handle domain shift or limited data.

papers_seen.author: Lopez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical Core Tool with Clear Limits and Complementary Needs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely used approach to compressing large deep and language models into smaller, faster students suitable for deployment. KD reliably reduces inference cost and model size while often preserving much of teacher performance, but success depends on what is transferred, how the student is initialized and trained, and how data and robustness constraints are handled. Effective compression therefore treats KD as one component in a pipeline that includes pre-training of compact architectures, architecture-aware alignment or progressive replacement, and data strategies (including data-free or synthesized data) to meet privacy and domain needs.

papers_seen.author: Kennedy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of teacher performance. KD encompasses techniques that transfer predictive behavior (soft logits), intermediate representations, and relational or structural signals; it can be combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet latency and memory constraints. Practical deployments extend KD to privacy-preserving, federated, and data-poor scenarios, and leverage online or multi-teacher protocols. Empirical and theoretical work highlights clear strengths in producing compact models for NLP and vision, while also identifying limits related to optimization, teacher imperfection, data mismatch, and distributional shifts that must be addressed by careful engineering and complementary compression strategies.

papers_seen.author: Bass
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach to producing small, fast models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. When combined with complementary techniques (e.g., layer mapping, multi-stage curricula, data augmentation, and hardware-aware compression), KD enables deployable NLP and deep-learning systems across constrained environments while admitting clear failure modes that demand targeted remedies.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Is Label Smoothing Truly Incompatible with Knowledge Distillation: An Empirical Study
papers_seen.abstract: This work aims to empirically clarify a recently discovered perspective that label smoothing is incompatible with knowledge distillation. We begin by introducing the motivation behind on how this incompatibility is raised, i.e., label smoothing erases relative information between teacher logits. We provide a novel connection on how label smoothing affects distributions of semantically similar and dissimilar classes. Then we propose a metric to quantitatively measure the degree of erased information in sample's representation. After that, we study its one-sidedness and imperfection of the incompatibility view through massive analyses, visualizations and comprehensive experiments on Image Classification, Binary Networks, and Neural Machine Translation. Finally, we broadly discuss several circumstances wherein label smoothing will indeed lose its effectiveness. Project page: http://zhiqiangshen.com/projects/LS_and_KD/index.html.

papers_seen.author: Nguyen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical and Multifaceted Tool for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students. Across vision, speech, graph, and language tasks, KD enables substantial reductions in memory and inference cost while retaining much of the teacher's performance. However, KD is not a silver bullet: its effectiveness depends on choices of teacher/student architecture, what is distilled (logits, layers, attention, representations), the optimization and data used for distillation, and constraints such as privacy or fairness. Carefully combining KD with techniques like multi-teacher schedules, layer-mapping strategies, task-adaptive compression, and privacy-preserving perturbations yields the best trade-offs for real-world deployment.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Recent Findings
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information from teacher models. Across vision, language, and cross-modal tasks, KD is used both as a stand-alone compression method and in combination with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Practical strategies include logit (soft-label) matching, feature-level imitation, multi-teacher schemes, and data- or label-synthesis when original training data are unavailable. Empirical work shows that distillation can recover most of a teacher's performance while enabling much smaller and faster models, but outcomes depend strongly on choices such as teacher quality, the form of distilled signals, augmentation and synthetic-data generation, and whether low-precision or domain-specific constraints apply.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression methods transfer behavior from large teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models. Across vision and language, practitioners match softened outputs, align internal representations, or transfer relational signals, often combining distillation with quantization, architecture adaptation, or data selection to meet deployment constraints. KD enables substantial reductions in model size and latency while retaining much of teacher performance, but success depends on student capacity, the distilled signals chosen, data availability or synthesis, and strategies for aligning heterogeneous architectures and preserving robustness.

papers_seen.author: Obrien
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Composable Core of Model Compression: Practical Benefits, Limits, and Recommendations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated not simply as a single recipe for compression but as the composable core of real-world model-compression pipelines. KD reliably reduces inference cost while preserving much of a teacher’s performance across modalities, and it naturally composes with pruning, quantization, architecture search, data synthesis, and domain-adaptive procedures. To deploy reliable compressed models practitioners must pair KD with careful teacher/student design, data and sample-selection strategies (including data-free synthesis where necessary), evaluation for robustness and fairness, and complementary compression steps that meet hardware constraints. This paper argues for a pragmatic, pipeline-oriented view of KD and outlines targeted practices to maximize utility while mitigating known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Leonard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Compressing Deep and NLP Models: Strengths, Limits, and How to Apply It
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. When applied thoughtfully—combining logits and representation matching, adapting teacher and student designs, and addressing data- or privacy-constrained settings—KD enables substantial reductions in model size and latency while retaining much of teacher performance. However, KD is not a cure-all: optimization difficulties, teacher imperfections, data mismatch, and distributional limits require targeted strategies (e.g., feature-aware losses, data-free synthesis, online or multi-teacher schemes) to make distillation robust and production-ready.

papers_seen.author: Diaz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, broadly applicable approach to compressing large models for deployment in resource-constrained settings. KD enables model-size and compute reductions while preserving task performance, and it integrates naturally with other compression techniques, privacy-preserving releases, federated and heterogeneous-device training, and domain/continual adaptation. However, its success depends on careful choices: how teacher signals are generated and weighted, which data (or synthetic/meta-data) drive distillation, and how KD interacts with data heterogeneity and fairness constraints. When combined with complementary methods (pruning, architecture search, data augmentation, selective sample weighting), KD yields efficient models that retain much of the teacher’s capabilities across vision, generative, and language tasks.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Tool for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a flexible, high-impact way to compress large models into smaller, efficient ones while retaining most task performance. Modern KD methods extend beyond matching final logits to include layer- and feature-level imitation, task-aware selection of distilled information, data-free or few-shot regimes, and multi-teacher or self-distillation strategies. When combined with architecture-aware compression or search, KD enables task-adaptive, privacy-conscious, and efficient deployment of deep models in real-world NLP and vision applications.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Understanding BERT Rankers Under Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep language models such as BERT pre-trained on large corpus have given a huge performance boost to the state-of-the-art information retrieval ranking systems. Knowledge embedded in such models allows them to pick up complex matching signals between passages and queries. However, the high computation cost during inference limits their deployment in real-world search scenarios. In this paper, we study if and how the knowledge for search within BERT can be transferred to a smaller ranker through distillation. Our experiments demonstrate that it is crucial to use a proper distillation procedure, which produces up to nine times speedup while preserving the state-of-the-art performance.

papers_seen.author: Warner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Model Compression and Adaptation in NLP and Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as a central, practical technique for compressing and adapting large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD is versatile: it transfers predictive behavior, intermediate representations, and ensemble knowledge; supports data-free or privacy-sensitive settings; and can improve robustness and calibration when combined with complementary methods. Realizing KD’s full potential requires matching the distillation recipe to deployment goals and addressing failure modes such as optimization mismatches, bias transfer, and poor handling of low-frequency phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Liu
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Strategy for Compressing NLP Models: Benefits, Limits, and Practical Recipes
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable ones. In NLP, KD enables retaining much of the teacher model's linguistic capability while reducing storage and inference cost. Effective compression with KD requires more than mimicking final outputs: it benefits from aligning internal representations, task-aware layer mapping, and handling data or privacy constraints with synthetic or metadata-driven techniques. However, KD is not a panacea — distributional heterogeneity, privacy, and mismatches between teacher and student capacity pose real limits that must be mitigated by careful method design and evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Heath
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical and flexible approach for producing smaller, faster models from larger teachers across vision, language, speech, and multimodal settings. Methods range from matching teacher logits to aligning intermediate representations, ensembling or self-teaching, and combining distillation with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Empirical work shows KD can preserve much of a teacher's performance while enabling deployment under compute, memory, privacy, and latency constraints, but effectiveness depends on choices of distilled signals, data and augmentations, teacher–student alignment, and task-aware pipeline design.

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Path for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Power, Pitfalls, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical and widely applicable approach to compress large neural models into smaller, faster, and often more deployable students while retaining much of the teacher's performance. KD enables dramatic inference speedups, parameter reduction, privacy-preserving transfer, and flexible deployment across device and domain constraints. However, distillation is not a panacea: it can introduce systematic errors (e.g., on low-frequency phenomena), struggle under data heterogeneity, and depends critically on teacher design and the distillation procedure. Combining KD with careful teacher selection or training, multi-teacher and ensemble strategies, data-free synthesis, architecture search for task-adaptive compression, and device-aware pruning yields a pragmatic toolkit for real-world compression and adaptation needs. The body of this paper lays out evidence for these claims and recommends concrete practices for deploying KD effectively in NLP and broader deep learning tasks.

papers_seen.author: Pacheco
papers_seen.title: Practical Principles for Knowledge Distillation and Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and model compression are essential for deploying large pretrained models in resource-constrained or privacy-sensitive settings. Effective distillation requires more than copying logits: combining domain adaptation, intermediate representation alignment, task-aware architecture search, and privacy-preserving or data-free techniques produces compact models that retain much of the teacher's utility across modalities and tasks.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical Core for Model Compression with Design-Sensitive Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and broadly applicable approach for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD can transfer predictive behavior, internal representations, and inductive biases to students so they recover much of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and deployment cost. In practice KD succeeds when paired with careful choices about what to transfer (logits, features, or layer-wise signals), teacher-student co-design, data strategies (including synthetic or unlabeled data), and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). KD is not a turnkey fix: optimization mismatch, data scarcity or mismatch, and certain fine-grained behaviors (e.g., low-frequency tokens) remain challenges that require targeted remedies.

papers_seen.author: Cortez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach that enables deployment of large deep models by training smaller students to retain much of teacher performance. KD supports a wide range of transfer signals (logits, features, attention), training protocols (multi-stage, multi-teacher, federated), and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design). When applied carefully and combined with appropriate data, alignment, and robustness strategies, KD yields substantial runtime and memory savings with modest accuracy loss, making it central to production model compression in NLP and related domains.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: Understanding Knowledge Distillation in Non-autoregressive Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Non-autoregressive machine translation (NAT) systems predict a sequence of output tokens in parallel, achieving substantial improvements in generation speed compared to autoregressive models. Existing NAT models usually rely on the technique of knowledge distillation, which creates the training data from a pretrained autoregressive model for better performance. Knowledge distillation is empirically useful, leading to large gains in accuracy for NAT models, but the reason for this success has, as of yet, been unclear. In this paper, we first design systematic experiments to investigate why knowledge distillation is crucial to NAT training. We find that knowledge distillation can reduce the complexity of data sets and help NAT to model the variations in the output data. Furthermore, a strong correlation is observed between the capacity of an NAT model and the optimal complexity of the distilled data for the best translation quality. Based on these findings, we further propose several approaches that can alter the complexity of data sets to improve the performance of NAT models. We achieve the state-of-the-art performance for the NAT-based models, and close the gap with the autoregressive baseline on WMT14 En-De benchmark.

papers_seen.author: Harris
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students while retaining much of the teacher's behavior. A growing literature shows KD can act via soft-target matching, intermediate representation transfer, attention- or relation-based losses, self-distillation, online and data-free variants, and can be combined with pruning, layer-skipping, quantization, or architecture search. KD delivers strong empirical gains across modalities (vision, language, recommendation, and graphs) when its signal, data strategy, and optimization schedule are chosen to match the deployment constraints. Important open issues remain — handling rare or low-frequency behaviors, adapting across domains and heterogeneous architectures, and operating under strict privacy or data-availability constraints — but pragmatic pipelines that mix KD with complementary compression tools offer the most reliable path to deployable compact models.

papers_seen.author: Blair
papers_seen.title: Distilling Policy Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The transfer of knowledge from one policy to another is an important tool in Deep Reinforcement Learning. This process, referred to as distillation, has been used to great success, for example, by enhancing the optimisation of agents, leading to stronger performance faster, on harder domains [26, 32, 5, 8]. Despite the widespread use and conceptual simplicity of distillation, many different formulations are used in practice, and the subtle variations between them can often drastically change the performance and the resulting objective that is being optimised. In this work, we rigorously explore the entire landscape of policy distillation, comparing the motivations and strengths of each variant through theoretical and empirical analysis. Our results point to three distillation techniques, that are preferred depending on specifics of the task. Specifically a newly proposed expected entropy regularised distillation allows for quicker learning in a wide range of situations, while still guaranteeing convergence.

papers_seen.author: Mckee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Model Compression: Power, Patterns, and Precautions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, flexible approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a toolkit rather than a single recipe, and combined with complementary compression methods and data strategies, KD enables substantial reductions in latency, memory, and energy while retaining much of teacher performance. However, distillation can transfer teacher weaknesses (biases, brittleness, low-frequency errors) and requires careful choices about what to transfer, how to align representations across heterogeneous architectures, and how to handle limited or private data. Practical deployment therefore calls for method selection tailored to task and constraints, plus safeguards for robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models so they meet real-world constraints on latency, memory, and deployment. Across vision, language, generative, and structured prediction tasks, KD has been adapted from simple soft-label matching into a rich toolbox that includes intermediate-layer supervision, multi-teacher schedules, student-aware teacher training, data- and augmentation-aware pipelines, and combinations with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). When applied with attention to student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints, KD reliably improves size–performance trade-offs, but its success depends on careful signal selection, teacher–student alignment, and strategies to mitigate capacity mismatch, distribution shift, and transferred teacher artifacts.

papers_seen.author: Pierce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a General-Purpose Paradigm: Beyond Compression to Adaptation, Robustness, and Inclusive Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) began as a technique to compress large models into smaller, faster ones. Over the past decade it has matured into a flexible training paradigm that can shape student behavior via soft targets, intermediate feature alignment, and multi-teacher or self-teaching schemes. When designed with task, data, and deployment constraints in mind, KD can enable domain specialization, interpretability, privacy-friendly federated learning, and improved robustness while still supporting efficient inference.

papers_seen.author: Doyle
papers_seen.title: DE-RRD: A Knowledge Distillation Framework for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: Recent recommender systems have started to employ knowledge distillation, which is a model compression technique distilling knowledge from a cumbersome model (teacher) to a compact model (student), to reduce inference latency while maintaining performance. The state-of-the-art methods have only focused on making the student model accurately imitate the predictions of the teacher model. They have a limitation in that the prediction results incompletely reveal the teacher's knowledge. In this paper, we propose a novel knowledge distillation framework for recommender system, called DE-RRD, which enables the student model to learn from the latent knowledge encoded in the teacher model as well as from the teacher's predictions. Concretely, DE-RRD consists of two methods: 1) Distillation Experts (DE) that directly transfers the latent knowledge from the teacher model. DE exploits "experts" and a novel expert selection strategy for effectively distilling the vast teacher's knowledge to the student with limited capacity. 2) Relaxed Ranking Distillation (RRD) that transfers the knowledge revealed from the teacher's prediction with consideration of the relaxed ranking orders among items. Our extensive experiments show that DE-RRD outperforms the state-of-the-art competitors and achieves comparable or even better performance to that of the teacher model with faster inference time.

papers_seen.author: Richards
papers_seen.title: TextKD-GAN: Text Generation using KnowledgeDistillation and Generative Adversarial Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Text generation is of particular interest in many NLP applications such as machine translation, language modeling, and text summarization. Generative adversarial networks (GANs) achieved a remarkable success in high quality image generation in computer vision,and recently, GANs have gained lots of interest from the NLP community as well. However, achieving similar success in NLP would be more challenging due to the discrete nature of text. In this work, we introduce a method using knowledge distillation to effectively exploit GAN setup for text generation. We demonstrate how autoencoders (AEs) can be used for providing a continuous representation of sentences, which is a smooth representation that assign non-zero probabilities to more than one word. We distill this representation to train the generator to synthesize similar smooth representations. We perform a number of experiments to validate our idea using different datasets and show that our proposed approach yields better performance in terms of the BLEU score and Jensen-Shannon distance (JSD) measure compared to traditional GAN-based text generation approaches without pre-training.

papers_seen.author: Scott
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques transfer information from larger teacher models into smaller student models to reduce computation, memory, and latency while attempting to preserve predictive performance. The field encompasses a range of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational signals), training workflows (single- and multi-stage, multi-teacher, self-distillation, data-free), and practical integrations with pruning, quantization, and architecture adaptation. Empirical and conceptual work points to several mechanisms that make distillation effective (soft-target regularization, representation alignment, and inductive-bias transfer) and identifies recurring deployment concerns such as architecture mismatch, data availability, domain shift, and robustness. Best practices emphasize matching distillation signals to student capacity, using layer-aware objectives when internal alignment matters, and combining distillation with complementary compression methods for realistic constraints.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Revisiting Knowledge Distillation via Label Smoothing Regularization
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge Distillation (KD) aims to distill the knowledge of a cumbersome teacher model into a lightweight student model. Its success is generally attributed to the privileged information on similarities among categories provided by the teacher model, and in this sense, only strong teacher models are deployed to teach weaker students in practice. In this work, we challenge this common belief by following experimental observations: 1) beyond the acknowledgment that the teacher can improve the student, the student can also enhance the teacher significantly by reversing the KD procedure; 2) a poorly-trained teacher with much lower accuracy than the student can still improve the latter significantly. To explain these observations, we provide a theoretical analysis of the relationships between KD and label smoothing regularization. We prove that 1) KD is a type of learned label smoothing regularization and 2) label smoothing regularization provides a virtual teacher model for KD. From these results, we argue that the success of KD is not fully due to the similarity information between categories from teachers, but also to the regularization of soft targets, which is equally or even more important.   Based on these analyses, we further propose a novel Teacher-free Knowledge Distillation (Tf-KD) framework, where a student model learns from itself or manuallydesigned regularization distribution. The Tf-KD achieves comparable performance with normal KD from a superior teacher, which is well applied when a stronger teacher model is unavailable. Meanwhile, Tf-KD is generic and can be directly deployed for training deep neural networks. Without any extra computation cost, Tf-KD achieves up to 0.65\% improvement on ImageNet over well-established baseline models, which is superior to label smoothing regularization.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature and flexible approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable ones. When combined with careful choices—such as pre-training compact students, data-free distillation for privacy, adaptive multi-teacher strategies, feature-level imitation, and teacher-side learning—KD can deliver strong task performance with much smaller inference cost. However, KD is not a panacea: optimization gaps between teacher and student, propagation of teacher biases, and dataset mismatches can limit gains unless explicitly addressed. A pragmatic KD pipeline therefore integrates algorithmic innovations and fairness/optimization checks to realize both efficiency and reliable behavior in production NLP and deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Domains, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques aim to transfer knowledge from larger, costly models (teachers) into smaller, faster models (students) so that the students retain much of the teachers' accuracy while meeting deployment constraints. Across vision, language, graphs, and generative models, researchers have developed complementary approaches — from matching soft logits to aligning intermediate representations, attention maps, channels, and global embedding topologies — and combined distillation with architecture search, pruning, and continual adaptation. Empirical work shows distillation can produce compact models that preserve or even improve task performance, but success depends on careful alignment of teacher-student inputs/representations, task- and domain-specific strategies, and trade-offs such as bias–variance effects introduced by soft labels. Important challenges remain around layer mismatches, low-frequency token handling, domain shift, and fundamental limits of compressibility for certain model families.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Ensemble Distillation for Neural Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation describes a method for training a student network to perform better by learning from a stronger teacher network. Translating a sentence with an Neural Machine Translation (NMT) engine is time expensive and having a smaller model speeds up this process. We demonstrate how to transfer the translation quality of an ensemble and an oracle BLEU teacher network into a single NMT system. Further, we present translation improvements from a teacher network that has the same architecture and dimensions of the student network. As the training of the student model is still expensive, we introduce a data filtering method based on the knowledge of the teacher model that not only speeds up the training, but also leads to better translation quality. Our techniques need no code change and can be easily reproduced with any NMT architecture to speed up the decoding process.

papers_seen.author: House
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Principled, Practical, and Context-Sensitive Toolbox for NLP Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an essential approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable systems. When treated as a flexible framework rather than a single recipe, KD can preserve much of teacher performance while meeting constraints of latency, memory, privacy, and domain heterogeneity. However, its success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to adapt to new domains or architectures, and how to select or synthesize training signals for the student.

papers_seen.author: Valencia
papers_seen.title: Practical and Robust Knowledge Distillation for Deployable Deep Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a central tool for compressing large deep models so they can be deployed under latency, memory, and power constraints. Beyond matching teacher output probabilities, modern distillation should transfer internal structure, be tailored to domain and modality differences, and integrate with quantization, privacy, and data-limited settings. When applied with methods that address representation mismatch, optimization challenges, and curriculum of supervisory signals, distillation enables small models that approach teacher performance while meeting real-world deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Fletcher
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Practical Methods, Mechanisms, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central technique for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. Practitioners use KD to transfer predictive behavior and internal representations, enabling reduced latency, memory footprint, and energy use while retaining much of teacher performance. Effective KD combines choices about what signals to transfer (soft logits, intermediate features, relational signals), how to align teacher and student architectures, how to supply or synthesize training data, and when to integrate complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization). Success depends on task- and data-aware engineering: careful teacher selection or synthesis, student capacity matching, and mitigation of distributional and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Ray
papers_seen.title: Transferring Inductive Biases through Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Having the right inductive biases can be crucial in many tasks or scenarios where data or computing resources are a limiting factor, or where training data is not perfectly representative of the conditions at test time. However, defining, designing and efficiently adapting inductive biases is not necessarily straightforward. In this paper, we explore the power of knowledge distillation for transferring the effect of inductive biases from one model to another. We consider families of models with different inductive biases, LSTMs vs. Transformers and CNNs vs. MLPs, in the context of tasks and scenarios where having the right inductive biases is critical. We study the effect of inductive biases on the solutions the models converge to and investigate how and to what extent the effect of inductive biases is transferred through knowledge distillation, in terms of not only performance but also different aspects of converged solutions.

papers_seen.author: Farmer
papers_seen.title: Towards Efficient 3D Object Detection with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite substantial progress in 3D object detection, advanced 3D detectors often suffer from heavy computation overheads. To this end, we explore the potential of knowledge distillation (KD) for developing efficient 3D object detectors, focusing on popular pillar- and voxel-based detectors.In the absence of well-developed teacher-student pairs, we first study how to obtain student models with good trade offs between accuracy and efficiency from the perspectives of model compression and input resolution reduction. Then, we build a benchmark to assess existing KD methods developed in the 2D domain for 3D object detection upon six well-constructed teacher-student pairs. Further, we propose an improved KD pipeline incorporating an enhanced logit KD method that performs KD on only a few pivotal positions determined by teacher classification response, and a teacher-guided student model initialization to facilitate transferring teacher model's feature extraction ability to students through weight inheritance. Finally, we conduct extensive experiments on the Waymo dataset. Our best performing model achieves $65.75\%$ LEVEL 2 mAPH, surpassing its teacher model and requiring only $44\%$ of teacher flops. Our most efficient model runs 51 FPS on an NVIDIA A100, which is $2.2\times$ faster than PointPillar with even higher accuracy. Code is available at \url{https://github.com/CVMI-Lab/SparseKD}.

papers_seen.author: Burton
papers_seen.title: What is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile set of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger or more informed models (teachers) into smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained models (students). KD has been used to (1) transfer inductive biases across architectures, (2) compress large pretrained language and vision models into task- or deployment-aware students, (3) combine and condense ensembles into single models, (4) enable privacy- or data-constrained distillation, and (5) improve student generalization via richer supervision beyond hard labels. Practical KD systems balance fidelity to the teacher, student capacity and architecture, data availability, privacy constraints, and deployment budgets; recent work addresses these trade-offs through architecture search, meta-learning teachers, multi-teacher designs, data-free synthesis, and specialized intermediate-feature matching losses. Despite broad empirical success, theoretical work highlights conditions where soft labels help (and when hard labels correct imperfect teachers), pointing to ongoing research directions in teacher design, student architecture search, privacy guarantees, and robust data-efficient distillation.

papers_seen.author: Charles
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, broadly applicable approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers information from high-capacity teachers to compact students via outputs, intermediate representations, or relational signals, and integrates naturally with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and deployment workflows (on-device inference, federated learning, and data-limited regimes). While KD reliably improves efficiency while preserving much of teacher performance, robust application requires careful choices about what signals to transfer, how to handle imperfect teachers and low-frequency behaviors, and how to combine KD with data strategies and architecture design to meet real-world constraints.

papers_seen.author: Hodges
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical Pillar for Compressing Deep Models in NLP and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical, flexible toolkit for compressing large neural networks while retaining much of their performance. Across NLP and other domains, KD enables deployment on resource-limited devices, supports privacy-preserving and federated scenarios, and combines effectively with pre-training, data augmentation, and structured compression. I argue that KD should be a default component of any production-aware model compression pipeline, augmented by task- and data-aware techniques to preserve robustness and accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a practical cornerstone for compressing large deep models into deployable, lower-latency students while retaining much of their predictive capacity. KD methods span simple soft-target matching to feature- and layer-level transfer, and they can operate in constrained settings (limited data, heterogeneous architectures, cross-modal scenarios). However, the effectiveness of KD depends on what is transferred, how teachers and students are matched, and how KD is combined with complementary compression strategies. Careful design—addressing teacher errors, domain shift, data availability, and architecture mismatch—yields compact models that meet real deployment constraints without disproportionate loss in quality.

papers_seen.author: Diaz
papers_seen.title: Model Compression with Two-stage Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation for Web Question Answering System
papers_seen.abstract: Deep pre-training and fine-tuning models (such as BERT and OpenAI GPT) have demonstrated excellent results in question answering areas. However, due to the sheer amount of model parameters, the inference speed of these models is very slow. How to apply these complex models to real business scenarios becomes a challenging but practical problem. Previous model compression methods usually suffer from information loss during the model compression procedure, leading to inferior models compared with the original one. To tackle this challenge, we propose a Two-stage Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation (TMKD for short) method for web Question Answering system. We first develop a general Q\&A distillation task for student model pre-training, and further fine-tune this pre-trained student model with multi-teacher knowledge distillation on downstream tasks (like Web Q\&A task, MNLI, SNLI, RTE tasks from GLUE), which effectively reduces the overfitting bias in individual teacher models, and transfers more general knowledge to the student model. The experiment results show that our method can significantly outperform the baseline methods and even achieve comparable results with the original teacher models, along with substantial speedup of model inference.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation in Practical Model Compression for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a niche training trick into a broad, practically necessary toolkit for compressing large deep models for deployment in resource-constrained settings. KD variants enable compressing Transformer-based and convolutional architectures, transferring useful inductive biases, operating with limited or no access to original training data, and even addressing downstream concerns such as fairness. At the same time, KD has limitations in certain distributed or heterogeneous-data settings that require complementary methods or careful protocol design. A targeted combination of task-aware layer-wise methods, feature-level mimicking, adversarial/data-free generation, and attention to distributional heterogeneity yields the best practical results for NLP and other deep learning applications.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses high-capacity models into smaller, faster models by transferring learned behavior from a teacher to a student. Techniques range from matching soft outputs to mimicking internal representations, and they address goals including latency reduction, domain adaptation, privacy, and scalability. Recent work expands classical teacher-student pipelines with self-distillation, data-free approaches, ensemble-to-singleton transfer, and scalable online schemes, while theoretical analyses reframe distillation as a form of label smoothing and regularization. Practical deployments show that careful choice of distilled signal (logits, features, attention, or ensembles) and training protocols can yield compact models that approach or match teacher performance in many settings, but open issues remain around low-frequency token handling, domain shift, and privacy-aware data constraints.

papers_seen.author: Alvarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Challenges, and Trends
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques aim to produce smaller, faster models that retain much of the predictive power of larger teachers. Across modalities (vision, language, speech, graphs, and generation), practitioners balance trade-offs among accuracy, efficiency, data availability, privacy, and fairness. Recent work extends classical logits-based distillation with feature- and layer-level objectives, projector modules, adversarial data generation for data-free settings, multi-teacher and meta-learned teachers, and privacy-aware perturbations. Empirical and theoretical analyses highlight both practical gains and persistent issues—optimization barriers that prevent perfect teacher matching, data-mismatch effects, and modality-specific alignment problems—guiding current best practices for deploying distilled models in resource- and privacy-constrained scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Donovan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Practical Compression: Essential, Effective, but Context-Sensitive
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students that retain much of teacher performance. KD can yield large speed, storage, and deployment gains across vision, speech, and language when combined with careful choices about what to transfer and how to train. However, success is not automatic: data regime, teacher-student mismatch, optimization dynamics, and downstream robustness or fairness constraints shape outcomes. I argue that KD should be treated as a core tool in model compression pipelines but one that must be adapted to the task, data availability, and deployment constraints through a set of best practices.

papers_seen.author: Daniel
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models to reduce compute, memory, and latency while preserving task performance. Across vision, speech, and language tasks, KD has been adapted into many forms—soft-target matching, intermediate representation alignment, attention and relational transfers, multi-teacher ensembles, online distillation, and task-adaptive pipelines—and combined with orthogonal compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to enable deployment in resource-constrained or privacy-sensitive settings. Empirical work shows KD often recovers most of a teacher's utility in a much smaller footprint, but success depends on teacher quality, the choice of distilled signals, data availability and domain shift, and robustness and privacy constraints. The field continues to refine objectives, layer-mapping strategies, and workflows that make distillation effective across modalities and large pretrained models in practical deployments.

papers_seen.author: Turner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a toolbox rather than a single recipe, KD can preserve much of teacher performance while meeting constraints of latency, memory, privacy, and heterogeneous deployment. Realizing KD's full value requires combining soft-target transfer with representation-level objectives, curriculum or staged training, teacher optimization, and architecture-aware mapping, and it also demands attention to distribution shift, rare-token fidelity, and teacher biases.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) offers a pragmatic pathway to produce compact, efficient models from large teachers while preserving much of their performance. When thoughtfully combined with complementary techniques—representation-level objectives, architecture-aware student design, data strategies including data-free or privacy-sensitive workflows, and targeted optimization—KD enables deployment under latency, memory, and heterogeneity constraints. However, realizing these gains requires attention to teacher quality, student capacity, optimization dynamics, and data issues; failures and trade-offs are documented and can be managed with targeted practices.

papers_seen.author: Daniel
papers_seen.title: Data-Free Adversarial Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge Distillation (KD) has made remarkable progress in the last few years and become a popular paradigm for model compression and knowledge transfer. However, almost all existing KD algorithms are data-driven, i.e., relying on a large amount of original training data or alternative data, which is usually unavailable in real-world scenarios. In this paper, we devote ourselves to this challenging problem and propose a novel adversarial distillation mechanism to craft a compact student model without any real-world data. We introduce a model discrepancy to quantificationally measure the difference between student and teacher models and construct an optimizable upper bound. In our work, the student and the teacher jointly act the role of the discriminator to reduce this discrepancy, when a generator adversarially produces some "hard samples" to enlarge it. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed data-free method yields comparable performance to existing data-driven methods. More strikingly, our approach can be directly extended to semantic segmentation, which is more complicated than classification, and our approach achieves state-of-the-art results. Code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/VainF/Data-Free-Adversarial-Distillation.

papers_seen.author: Hall
papers_seen.title: FedZKT: Zero-Shot Knowledge Transfer towards Resource-Constrained Federated Learning with Heterogeneous On-Device Models
papers_seen.abstract: Federated learning enables multiple distributed devices to collaboratively learn a shared prediction model without centralizing their on-device data. Most of the current algorithms require comparable individual efforts for local training with the same structure and size of on-device models, which, however, impedes participation from resource-constrained devices. Given the widespread yet heterogeneous devices nowadays, in this paper, we propose an innovative federated learning framework with heterogeneous on-device models through Zero-shot Knowledge Transfer, named by FedZKT. Specifically, FedZKT allows devices to independently determine the on-device models upon their local resources. To achieve knowledge transfer across these heterogeneous on-device models, a zero-shot distillation approach is designed without any prerequisites for private on-device data, which is contrary to certain prior research based on a public dataset or a pre-trained data generator. Moreover, this compute-intensive distillation task is assigned to the server to allow the participation of resource-constrained devices, where a generator is adversarially learned with the ensemble of collected on-device models. The distilled central knowledge is then sent back in the form of the corresponding on-device model parameters, which can be easily absorbed on the device side. Extensive experimental studies demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of FedZKT towards on-device knowledge agnostic, on-device model heterogeneity, and other challenging federated learning scenarios, such as heterogeneous on-device data and straggler effects.

papers_seen.author: Ferrell
papers_seen.title: AlphaNet: Improved Training of Supernets with Alpha-Divergence
papers_seen.abstract: Weight-sharing neural architecture search (NAS) is an effective technique for automating efficient neural architecture design. Weight-sharing NAS builds a supernet that assembles all the architectures as its sub-networks and jointly trains the supernet with the sub-networks. The success of weight-sharing NAS heavily relies on distilling the knowledge of the supernet to the sub-networks. However, we find that the widely used distillation divergence, i.e., KL divergence, may lead to student sub-networks that over-estimate or under-estimate the uncertainty of the teacher supernet, leading to inferior performance of the sub-networks. In this work, we propose to improve the supernet training with a more generalized alpha-divergence. By adaptively selecting the alpha-divergence, we simultaneously prevent the over-estimation or under-estimation of the uncertainty of the teacher model. We apply the proposed alpha-divergence based supernets training to both slimmable neural networks and weight-sharing NAS, and demonstrate significant improvements. Specifically, our discovered model family, AlphaNet, outperforms prior-art models on a wide range of FLOPs regimes, including BigNAS, Once-for-All networks, and AttentiveNAS. We achieve ImageNet top-1 accuracy of 80.0% with only 444M FLOPs. Our code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/facebookresearch/AlphaNet.
