papers_seen.author: Kennedy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of teacher performance. KD encompasses techniques that transfer predictive behavior (soft logits), intermediate representations, and relational or structural signals; it can be combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet latency and memory constraints. Practical deployments extend KD to privacy-preserving, federated, and data-poor scenarios, and leverage online or multi-teacher protocols. Empirical and theoretical work highlights clear strengths in producing compact models for NLP and vision, while also identifying limits related to optimization, teacher imperfection, data mismatch, and distributional shifts that must be addressed by careful engineering and complementary compression strategies.

papers_seen.author: Jackson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a primary practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, more efficient ones for deployment in constrained environments. KD techniques range from matching softened output distributions to aligning intermediate representations, transferring relational signals, and operating in data-limited or privacy-sensitive regimes via synthesized or public data. When combined with complementary compression methods (quantization, pruning, architecture search), KD enables substantial reductions in latency and memory while often retaining most of the teacher’s performance. Persistent challenges include understanding the mechanisms of transfer, handling student–teacher capacity mismatch, preserving rare-token or long-tail behaviors, and ensuring robustness and fairness under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Maddox
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Tool for Compression, Bias Transfer, and Robust Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is more than a model compression trick: it is a practical mechanism for transferring inductive biases, regularizing students, enabling privacy- and data-constrained deployments, and adapting architectures or modalities. When paired with complementary techniques—data augmentation, curriculum schedules, teacher ensembles, or generative replay—KD consistently narrows the gap between compact students and large teachers while addressing real-world constraints such as limited labeled data, compute, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Oliver
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of techniques that transfer information from large, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, efficient student models to enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD methods go beyond simple logit-matching to include feature- and relation-level imitation, data-free and zero-shot strategies, multi-teacher and self-distillation schemes, and combinations with other compression tools. Empirical work across vision, language, graph, and generative modeling domains demonstrates substantial size and latency reductions with modest performance loss when methods are adapted to task, data availability, and deployment constraints. Important open challenges include matching internal representations across architectures, avoiding transfer of undesirable biases, and ensuring robustness and privacy in constrained or federated settings.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: The Case for Versatile Knowledge Distillation: Compression, Adaptation, and Robustness in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical and flexible paradigm for transferring information from large, high-capacity models into smaller, more efficient ones. Beyond simple logit matching, distillation techniques can be adapted to operate without original training data, guide architecture search, improve generalization under limited data, support cross-modal and multi-task transfer, and preserve or even enhance downstream performance on specialized tasks. When combined with task-aware search, feature-level imitation, and data augmentation strategies, distillation enables deployment of compact models that remain competitive with their teachers while meeting real-world constraints such as privacy, compute, and latency.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Multi-Level Branched Regularization for Federated Learning
papers_seen.abstract: A critical challenge of federated learning is data heterogeneity and imbalance across clients, which leads to inconsistency between local networks and unstable convergence of global models. To alleviate the limitations, we propose a novel architectural regularization technique that constructs multiple auxiliary branches in each local model by grafting local and global subnetworks at several different levels and that learns the representations of the main pathway in the local model congruent to the auxiliary hybrid pathways via online knowledge distillation. The proposed technique is effective to robustify the global model even in the non-iid setting and is applicable to various federated learning frameworks conveniently without incurring extra communication costs. We perform comprehensive empirical studies and demonstrate remarkable performance gains in terms of accuracy and efficiency compared to existing methods. The source code is available at our project page.

papers_seen.author: Maldonado
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques reduce model size or communication cost by transferring knowledge from larger or multiple models (teachers) to smaller or otherwise constrained models (students). Methods vary from matching soft outputs to transferring intermediate features, training teachers to be student-friendly, coordinating multiple teachers, and combining distillation with pruning or federated/online schemes. Empirical and theoretical work highlights how distilled "dark knowledge" improves student generalization, how architectural components (e.g., projectors) shape transfer, and how distillation can be adapted for privacy, heterogeneity, and large-scale or multi-task NLP applications.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: The Case for Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Compressing and Adapting NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a principled way to produce small, fast models that retain much of the performance of larger networks. In natural language processing, where modern pretrained models are large and domain shifts are common, KD enables domain adaptation, latency- and memory-constrained deployment, continual learning, and improved robustness when applied with the right strategies. Practical success relies on combining methods — e.g., multi-stage distillation, selective or curriculum-driven example selection, leveraging soft targets as regularizers, and using adversarial or synthetic data when original data are unavailable. When applied thoughtfully, KD is not merely an implementation detail of model compression but a versatile lever for engineering efficient, accurate, and robust NLP systems.

papers_seen.author: Arnold
papers_seen.title: Does Knowledge Distillation Really Work?
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular technique for training a small student network to emulate a larger teacher model, such as an ensemble of networks. We show that while knowledge distillation can improve student generalization, it does not typically work as it is commonly understood: there often remains a surprisingly large discrepancy between the predictive distributions of the teacher and the student, even in cases when the student has the capacity to perfectly match the teacher. We identify difficulties in optimization as a key reason for why the student is unable to match the teacher. We also show how the details of the dataset used for distillation play a role in how closely the student matches the teacher -- and that more closely matching the teacher paradoxically does not always lead to better student generalization.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central approach to compress large deep models into smaller, faster, and often more deployable student models. KD techniques range from classic teacher-to-student soft-target training to recent advances including data-free distillation, multi-teacher strategies, meta-learned teachers, and compression combined with pruning or structural sparsity. In NLP applications KD is used to shrink pre-trained transformers, accelerate inference for production systems, enable non-autoregressive generation, and adapt large models to resource-constrained or heterogeneous environments. Empirical work shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance while producing models with far lower latency and storage cost, but theoretical understanding, sensitivity to data and teacher quality, and robustness under distributional shifts remain active research areas.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression encompass a family of methods that transfer information from larger, high-capacity models (teachers) to smaller, efficient models (students). These approaches aim to retain predictive performance while reducing model size, latency, or enabling deployment under privacy or communication constraints. Recent work broadens distillation beyond logits to intermediate features, attention maps, multi-teacher setups, and data-limited or privacy-preserving regimes, producing task- and domain-aware compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Daniels
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, faster students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. Methods range from matching softened logits to imitating internal representations, attention maps, or channel-wise activations, and can be combined with quantization, low-precision numerics, architecture-aware design, and data- or teacher-aware training regimes. In practice, distillation is a multifaceted toolkit that must be tailored to deployment goals (latency, memory, domain adaptation, privacy, robustness), and remaining challenges include principled sample selection, representation alignment across heterogeneous architectures, and preserving robustness and fairness under compression.

papers_seen.author: Kim
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, flexible approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When paired with representation-aware objectives, careful pre-training of compact models, and safeguards for robustness and privacy, KD enables production-ready reductions in latency, memory, and energy while retaining much of a teacher's performance. I argue that KD should be treated as a central tool in model-compression pipelines, not as a single recipe but as a family of methods to be combined with task-aware design choices for reliable deployment.

papers_seen.author: Gaines
papers_seen.title: AdaBERT: Task-Adaptive BERT Compression with Differentiable Neural Architecture Search
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained language models such as BERT have shown their effectiveness in various natural language processing tasks. However, the huge parameter size makes them difficult to be deployed in real-time applications that require quick inference with limited resources. Existing methods compress BERT into small models while such compression is task-independent, i.e., the same compressed BERT for all different downstream tasks. Motivated by the necessity and benefits of task-oriented BERT compression, we propose a novel compression method, AdaBERT, that leverages differentiable Neural Architecture Search to automatically compress BERT into task-adaptive small models for specific tasks. We incorporate a task-oriented knowledge distillation loss to provide search hints and an efficiency-aware loss as search constraints, which enables a good trade-off between efficiency and effectiveness for task-adaptive BERT compression. We evaluate AdaBERT on several NLP tasks, and the results demonstrate that those task-adaptive compressed models are 12.7x to 29.3x faster than BERT in inference time and 11.5x to 17.0x smaller in terms of parameter size, while comparable performance is maintained.

papers_seen.author: Tran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practical Patterns
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring predictive behavior or intermediate representations. Across vision, speech, and natural language tasks, practitioners apply KD to reduce model size, latency, and resource cost while retaining much of the teacher's performance. Variants of KD extend beyond soft-label matching to feature- and layer-level alignment, multi-teacher and online schemes, cross-modal transfer, and data-limited or privacy-sensitive settings. Effective distillation typically combines careful choice of transfer target, student architecture and pre-training, and complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization). Open challenges include principled data selection or synthesis for distillation, handling imperfect or heterogeneous teachers, preserving robustness and fairness, and scaling distillation to large distributed training scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Mckee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Model Compression: Power, Patterns, and Precautions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, flexible approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a toolkit rather than a single recipe, and combined with complementary compression methods and data strategies, KD enables substantial reductions in latency, memory, and energy while retaining much of teacher performance. However, distillation can transfer teacher weaknesses (biases, brittleness, low-frequency errors) and requires careful choices about what to transfer, how to align representations across heterogeneous architectures, and how to handle limited or private data. Practical deployment therefore calls for method selection tailored to task and constraints, plus safeguards for robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques transfer predictive behavior and internal structure from larger teacher models to smaller student models to reduce computation, memory, and latency while preserving performance. The literature documents a spectrum of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention or channel maps, and relational signals), a variety of optimization and architectural practices (layer mapping, projectors, multi-stage training, and student-friendly teacher design), and deployment workflows for constrained settings (data-free, federated, and domain-adaptive distillation). Empirical and theoretical work highlights multiple mechanisms that make KD effective (regularization via soft targets, representation alignment, and optimization/inductive-bias transfer), while also identifying persistent challenges such as aligning heterogeneous architectures, preserving low-frequency behavior, and selecting what and when to transfer. Practical recommendations center on matching distillation signals to student capacity, using feature- or layer-aware objectives when internal alignment matters, and combining KD with complementary compression techniques for robust deployment.

papers_seen.author: Mayo
papers_seen.title: Rethinking Soft Labels for Knowledge Distillation: A Bias-Variance Tradeoff Perspective
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is an effective approach to leverage a well-trained network or an ensemble of them, named as the teacher, to guide the training of a student network. The outputs from the teacher network are used as soft labels for supervising the training of a new network. Recent studies \citep{muller2019does,yuan2020revisiting} revealed an intriguing property of the soft labels that making labels soft serves as a good regularization to the student network. From the perspective of statistical learning, regularization aims to reduce the variance, however how bias and variance change is not clear for training with soft labels. In this paper, we investigate the bias-variance tradeoff brought by distillation with soft labels. Specifically, we observe that during training the bias-variance tradeoff varies sample-wisely. Further, under the same distillation temperature setting, we observe that the distillation performance is negatively associated with the number of some specific samples, which are named as regularization samples since these samples lead to bias increasing and variance decreasing. Nevertheless, we empirically find that completely filtering out regularization samples also deteriorates distillation performance. Our discoveries inspired us to propose the novel weighted soft labels to help the network adaptively handle the sample-wise bias-variance tradeoff. Experiments on standard evaluation benchmarks validate the effectiveness of our method. Our code is available at \url{https://github.com/bellymonster/Weighted-Soft-Label-Distillation}.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques have matured into a diverse set of approaches that trade off capacity, latency, and privacy to deploy high-performing deep models in constrained settings. Methods operate at different places in the training pipeline: compressing via soft-targets, transferring intermediate representations, searching or adapting compact architectures, or avoiding access to original data. Work across modalities (vision, language, graphs, generative models, and medical imaging) shows that careful choice of what to transfer (logits, relations, feature directions, layer mappings) and how to transfer it (attention, contrastive alignment, adversarial generators, or task-aware filters) determines final student performance. Practical concerns such as domain adaptation, federated and heterogeneous-device settings, and data augmentation interact strongly with distillation design choices. The literature suggests a clear pattern: representation-level and layer-aware transfers often outperform naive logits-only approaches for structured or pre-trained models, while teacher-free, data-free, and communication-efficient variants enable distillation under realistic deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Humphrey
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Versatile Path to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) offers a pragmatic route to compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. Across modalities and tasks, KD can transfer predictive behavior, representations, or task-specific inductive biases; when combined with pre-training, architecture search, or careful data handling, it enables compact models that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: its effectiveness depends on the choice of what is distilled (logits vs. features), how teachers and students are chosen or trained, the availability and quality of data (including synthetic or unlabeled public data), and auxiliary techniques such as projectors, multi-teacher weighting, or meta-learning to adapt the teaching process. I argue that with these design choices attended to, KD is a broadly applicable and cost-effective strategy for model compression in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Shaffer
papers_seen.title: Selective Knowledge Distillation for Neural Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Neural Machine Translation (NMT) models achieve state-of-the-art performance on many translation benchmarks. As an active research field in NMT, knowledge distillation is widely applied to enhance the model's performance by transferring teacher model's knowledge on each training sample. However, previous work rarely discusses the different impacts and connections among these samples, which serve as the medium for transferring teacher knowledge. In this paper, we design a novel protocol that can effectively analyze the different impacts of samples by comparing various samples' partitions. Based on above protocol, we conduct extensive experiments and find that the teacher's knowledge is not the more, the better. Knowledge over specific samples may even hurt the whole performance of knowledge distillation. Finally, to address these issues, we propose two simple yet effective strategies, i.e., batch-level and global-level selections, to pick suitable samples for distillation. We evaluate our approaches on two large-scale machine translation tasks, WMT'14 English->German and WMT'19 Chinese->English. Experimental results show that our approaches yield up to +1.28 and +0.89 BLEU points improvements over the Transformer baseline, respectively.

papers_seen.author: Hensley
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques form a broadly applicable toolkit for transferring capability from large, expensive teacher models to smaller, faster, or more privacy-friendly student models. Methods range from transferring softened output distributions to aligning intermediate representations, using synthetic or augmented data when original data are unavailable, and combining distillation with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search). KD is used both as a deployment-oriented compression strategy and as a general training paradigm that can improve regularization, robustness, and domain adaptation. Practical success requires careful matching of distillation objectives, teacher-student alignment, and data strategies; persistent challenges include theoretical understanding of when distillation helps, preserving rare-token behavior in NLP, and avoiding artifacts introduced by synthetic data.

papers_seen.author: Richards
papers_seen.title: TextKD-GAN: Text Generation using KnowledgeDistillation and Generative Adversarial Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Text generation is of particular interest in many NLP applications such as machine translation, language modeling, and text summarization. Generative adversarial networks (GANs) achieved a remarkable success in high quality image generation in computer vision,and recently, GANs have gained lots of interest from the NLP community as well. However, achieving similar success in NLP would be more challenging due to the discrete nature of text. In this work, we introduce a method using knowledge distillation to effectively exploit GAN setup for text generation. We demonstrate how autoencoders (AEs) can be used for providing a continuous representation of sentences, which is a smooth representation that assign non-zero probabilities to more than one word. We distill this representation to train the generator to synthesize similar smooth representations. We perform a number of experiments to validate our idea using different datasets and show that our proposed approach yields better performance in terms of the BLEU score and Jensen-Shannon distance (JSD) measure compared to traditional GAN-based text generation approaches without pre-training.

papers_seen.author: Pierce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Practical Tool for Compression — Capabilities, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practically indispensable approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable ones. KD enables large reductions in inference cost while preserving much of a teacher model’s performance, and it composes well with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. At the same time, distillation is not a turnkey solution: optimization difficulties, data dependence, heterogeneous deployment constraints, and distributional or robustness concerns mean practitioners must design distillation pipelines carefully and combine KD with complementary techniques to meet real-world requirements.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: On Representation Knowledge Distillation for Graph Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a learning paradigm for boosting resource-efficient graph neural networks (GNNs) using more expressive yet cumbersome teacher models. Past work on distillation for GNNs proposed the Local Structure Preserving loss (LSP), which matches local structural relationships defined over edges across the student and teacher's node embeddings. This paper studies whether preserving the global topology of how the teacher embeds graph data can be a more effective distillation objective for GNNs, as real-world graphs often contain latent interactions and noisy edges. We propose Graph Contrastive Representation Distillation (G-CRD), which uses contrastive learning to implicitly preserve global topology by aligning the student node embeddings to those of the teacher in a shared representation space. Additionally, we introduce an expanded set of benchmarks on large-scale real-world datasets where the performance gap between teacher and student GNNs is non-negligible. Experiments across 4 datasets and 14 heterogeneous GNN architectures show that G-CRD consistently boosts the performance and robustness of lightweight GNNs, outperforming LSP (and a global structure preserving variant of LSP) as well as baselines from 2D computer vision. An analysis of the representational similarity among teacher and student embedding spaces reveals that G-CRD balances preserving local and global relationships, while structure preserving approaches are best at preserving one or the other. Our code is available at https://github.com/chaitjo/efficient-gnns

papers_seen.author: Mills
papers_seen.title: Why Knowledge Distillation Should Be the Central Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, adaptable technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of their performance. When combined with careful pre-training of compact architectures, representation-level transfer, augmentation or synthesized data, and orthogonal compression methods (pruning, quantization), KD delivers strong trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy. However, realizing those gains in practice requires attention to optimization dynamics, data availability, privacy, and known failure modes (e.g., low-frequency token degradation), and so KD should be applied as part of an integrated, responsible compression pipeline.

papers_seen.author: Harrell
papers_seen.title: No One Left Behind: Inclusive Federated Learning over Heterogeneous Devices
papers_seen.abstract: Federated learning (FL) is an important paradigm for training global models from decentralized data in a privacy-preserving way. Existing FL methods usually assume the global model can be trained on any participating client. However, in real applications, the devices of clients are usually heterogeneous, and have different computing power. Although big models like BERT have achieved huge success in AI, it is difficult to apply them to heterogeneous FL with weak clients. The straightforward solutions like removing the weak clients or using a small model to fit all clients will lead to some problems, such as under-representation of dropped clients and inferior accuracy due to data loss or limited model representation ability. In this work, we propose InclusiveFL, a client-inclusive federated learning method to handle this problem. The core idea of InclusiveFL is to assign models of different sizes to clients with different computing capabilities, bigger models for powerful clients and smaller ones for weak clients. We also propose an effective method to share the knowledge among multiple local models with different sizes. In this way, all the clients can participate in the model learning in FL, and the final model can be big and powerful enough. Besides, we propose a momentum knowledge distillation method to better transfer knowledge in big models on powerful clients to the small models on weak clients. Extensive experiments on many real-world benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in learning accurate models from clients with heterogeneous devices under the FL framework.

papers_seen.author: Zuniga
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Composable Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable and practical technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster, and more deployable student models. KD is effective across modalities (vision, speech, language, graphs) and settings (task-specific compression, data-limited or data-free transfer), and its strengths are amplified when combined with complementary methods such as architecture-aware replacement, pruning, low-precision numerics, adaptive teacher design, and careful input-side practices. To realize robust and fair compressed models, practitioners should treat KD as one tool within a pipeline: design student-friendly teachers, account for data constraints, use augmentation and curriculum where helpful, and combine KD with orthogonal compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Novak
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Strategy for Compressing NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, production-ready approach that enables compact models to inherit much of the performance of large teachers while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. When applied thoughtfully—using representation-level targets, projector layers, multi-teacher or curriculum schedules, and data-aware workflows—KD consistently outperforms training small models from scratch for many NLP tasks. However, KD is not a panacea: mismatches in capacity, teacher imperfections, data heterogeneity, and distributional shifts require targeted remedies and careful evaluation. This essay argues that KD should be treated as the practical core of model compression in deep learning and NLP, paired with specific design choices to mitigate its limits.

papers_seen.author: Lawrence
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge From a Deep Pose Regressor Network
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a novel method to distill knowledge from a deep pose regressor network for efficient Visual Odometry (VO). Standard distillation relies on "dark knowledge" for successful knowledge transfer. As this knowledge is not available in pose regression and the teacher prediction is not always accurate, we propose to emphasize the knowledge transfer only when we trust the teacher. We achieve this by using teacher loss as a confidence score which places variable relative importance on the teacher prediction. We inject this confidence score to the main training task via Attentive Imitation Loss (AIL) and when learning the intermediate representation of the teacher through Attentive Hint Training (AHT) approach. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work which successfully distill the knowledge from a deep pose regression network. Our evaluation on the KITTI and Malaga dataset shows that we can keep the student prediction close to the teacher with up to 92.95% parameter reduction and 2.12x faster in computation time.

papers_seen.author: Dudley
papers_seen.title: Attention-Guided Answer Distillation for Machine Reading Comprehension
papers_seen.abstract: Despite that current reading comprehension systems have achieved significant advancements, their promising performances are often obtained at the cost of making an ensemble of numerous models. Besides, existing approaches are also vulnerable to adversarial attacks. This paper tackles these problems by leveraging knowledge distillation, which aims to transfer knowledge from an ensemble model to a single model. We first demonstrate that vanilla knowledge distillation applied to answer span prediction is effective for reading comprehension systems. We then propose two novel approaches that not only penalize the prediction on confusing answers but also guide the training with alignment information distilled from the ensemble. Experiments show that our best student model has only a slight drop of 0.4% F1 on the SQuAD test set compared to the ensemble teacher, while running 12x faster during inference. It even outperforms the teacher on adversarial SQuAD datasets and NarrativeQA benchmark.

papers_seen.author: Chambers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practices, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performance models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, or relational structure. A broad family of techniques—soft-target matching, feature and attention alignment, multi-stage and multi-teacher curricula, data synthesis or augmentation, and complementary compression steps (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation)—enables practical trade-offs among accuracy, latency, and resource constraints. Empirical and theoretical work indicates distillation often acts both as an information transfer mechanism and a regularizer; success depends on student capacity, data availability, choice of distilled signals, and careful handling of robustness and privacy concerns.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Recommendations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile method for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD works across modalities (vision, language, graphs, and generative models) by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from teachers to students. When applied thoughtfully—selecting appropriate distillation signals, aligning internal representations, and integrating complementary compression techniques—KD reliably yields compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is not a plug-and-play cure: its success depends on teacher quality, data strategy, optimization choices, and architecture alignment, so practitioners should pair KD with task-aware curricula, representation-level objectives, and other compression tools to realize robust deployment.

papers_seen.author: Rocha
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practical Trends
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques aim to transfer predictive power from large teacher models into smaller, faster, or more private student models while retaining most of the original performance. Work across vision and language has expanded KD beyond simple logit matching into data-centric methods (augmentation and mixup), layer- and representation-level transfers, task-adaptive architecture search, data-free and privacy-aware distillation, and unified pipelines that combine pruning or structural compression with distillation. The field blends empirical engineering (speed/size trade-offs) with emerging theoretical analyses that help explain when and why distillation helps.

papers_seen.author: Cochran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses high-capacity models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure. A broad family of KD methods—ranging from matching softened output distributions to aligning intermediate representations, attention patterns, or relational signals—enables practitioners to trade model size and latency for retained performance. In practice, KD is combined with data-aware strategies, teacher adaptation, and complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to meet deployment constraints. While KD is effective across vision and language tasks, success depends on careful choices about distilled signals, student capacity, data availability, and handling of domain shifts or low-frequency behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Farmer
papers_seen.title: The Practical Case for Feature- and Representation-Aware Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile strategy for compressing large models into efficient students while retaining much of their accuracy. Beyond the classical logit-matching formulation, modern KD practices that match internal representations, use tailored projectors or selective sample strategies, and account for deployment constraints (e.g., no access to original data or adversarial threats) yield better student models across modalities and tasks. Combining these advances—feature mimicking, projector ensembles, selective distillation, data-free techniques, and robustness-aware training—produces compact models that are both performant and deployable.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Path to Deployable Deep Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical framework for producing compact, faster models that retain much of the capability of larger teachers. Beyond simple logit matching, modern KD leverages internal representation transfer, selective data strategies, and integration with pruning, architecture search, or federated protocols to meet latency, privacy, and device-heterogeneity constraints. When applied thoughtfully, KD enables efficient deployment across modalities while posing clear methodological trade-offs and open challenges that guide future research.

papers_seen.author: Harrell
papers_seen.title: No One Left Behind: Inclusive Federated Learning over Heterogeneous Devices
papers_seen.abstract: Federated learning (FL) is an important paradigm for training global models from decentralized data in a privacy-preserving way. Existing FL methods usually assume the global model can be trained on any participating client. However, in real applications, the devices of clients are usually heterogeneous, and have different computing power. Although big models like BERT have achieved huge success in AI, it is difficult to apply them to heterogeneous FL with weak clients. The straightforward solutions like removing the weak clients or using a small model to fit all clients will lead to some problems, such as under-representation of dropped clients and inferior accuracy due to data loss or limited model representation ability. In this work, we propose InclusiveFL, a client-inclusive federated learning method to handle this problem. The core idea of InclusiveFL is to assign models of different sizes to clients with different computing capabilities, bigger models for powerful clients and smaller ones for weak clients. We also propose an effective method to share the knowledge among multiple local models with different sizes. In this way, all the clients can participate in the model learning in FL, and the final model can be big and powerful enough. Besides, we propose a momentum knowledge distillation method to better transfer knowledge in big models on powerful clients to the small models on weak clients. Extensive experiments on many real-world benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in learning accurate models from clients with heterogeneous devices under the FL framework.

papers_seen.author: Munoz
papers_seen.title: Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation in Deep Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation deals with the problem of training a smaller model (Student) from a high capacity source model (Teacher) so as to retain most of its performance. Existing approaches use either the training data or meta-data extracted from it in order to train the Student. However, accessing the dataset on which the Teacher has been trained may not always be feasible if the dataset is very large or it poses privacy or safety concerns (e.g., bio-metric or medical data). Hence, in this paper, we propose a novel data-free method to train the Student from the Teacher. Without even using any meta-data, we synthesize the Data Impressions from the complex Teacher model and utilize these as surrogates for the original training data samples to transfer its learning to Student via knowledge distillation. We, therefore, dub our method "Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation" and demonstrate that our framework results in competitive generalization performance as achieved by distillation using the actual training data samples on multiple benchmark datasets.

papers_seen.author: Gaines
papers_seen.title: AdaBERT: Task-Adaptive BERT Compression with Differentiable Neural Architecture Search
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained language models such as BERT have shown their effectiveness in various natural language processing tasks. However, the huge parameter size makes them difficult to be deployed in real-time applications that require quick inference with limited resources. Existing methods compress BERT into small models while such compression is task-independent, i.e., the same compressed BERT for all different downstream tasks. Motivated by the necessity and benefits of task-oriented BERT compression, we propose a novel compression method, AdaBERT, that leverages differentiable Neural Architecture Search to automatically compress BERT into task-adaptive small models for specific tasks. We incorporate a task-oriented knowledge distillation loss to provide search hints and an efficiency-aware loss as search constraints, which enables a good trade-off between efficiency and effectiveness for task-adaptive BERT compression. We evaluate AdaBERT on several NLP tasks, and the results demonstrate that those task-adaptive compressed models are 12.7x to 29.3x faster than BERT in inference time and 11.5x to 17.0x smaller in terms of parameter size, while comparable performance is maintained.

papers_seen.author: Beck
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses larger teacher models into smaller student models by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. Approaches include matching softened logits, aligning intermediate representations or attention maps, mapping or projecting teacher layers to student layers, and operating in offline, online, federated, or data-free regimes. Distillation is commonly combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and task-aware data strategies. Practical success depends on choosing which signals to transfer, aligning teacher and student capacity, managing data or privacy constraints, and designing curricula or multi-stage pipelines that reflect deployment needs. While distillation routinely produces compact models that retain much of teacher performance, open challenges remain in representation mismatch, amplifying teacher biases, and ensuring robustness and fairness under compression.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Wide Neural Networks: Risk Bound, Data Efficiency and Imperfect Teacher
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a strategy of training a student network with guide of the soft output from a teacher network. It has been a successful method of model compression and knowledge transfer. However, currently knowledge distillation lacks a convincing theoretical understanding. On the other hand, recent finding on neural tangent kernel enables us to approximate a wide neural network with a linear model of the network's random features. In this paper, we theoretically analyze the knowledge distillation of a wide neural network. First we provide a transfer risk bound for the linearized model of the network. Then we propose a metric of the task's training difficulty, called data inefficiency. Based on this metric, we show that for a perfect teacher, a high ratio of teacher's soft labels can be beneficial. Finally, for the case of imperfect teacher, we find that hard labels can correct teacher's wrong prediction, which explains the practice of mixing hard and soft labels.

papers_seen.author: Nolan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, or relational structure. Across vision, speech, and natural language tasks, distillation enables large reductions in model size and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance when combined with careful choices of transfer target, student architecture, and complementary compression techniques. Practical success depends on data strategies, layer-matching or projector design, and attention to optimization dynamics and teacher–student capacity mismatch; open problems include principled data synthesis or selection, preserving robustness and fairness, and scaling to heterogeneous or privacy-sensitive deployments.

papers_seen.author: Carr
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Cornerstone for Compressing Deep Models in NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, versatile mechanism for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable ones in NLP and related modalities. When paired with targeted choices—what signals to transfer (logits versus features), how to align layers, teacher design, and data strategies—KD preserves much of the teacher’s capability while reducing compute, memory, and latency. However, KD is not a universal remedy: its success depends on optimization details, data availability, and careful engineering to handle distribution shift, rare behaviors, and student–teacher mismatches.

papers_seen.author: Harrell
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques have become central tools to deploy high-capacity deep models in latency-, memory-, privacy-, and compute-constrained settings. Across vision, language, graph, and multimodal domains, practitioners use teacher-student training, feature-level transfer, data-free distillation, and hybrid pipelines that combine pruning or architecture search with distillation. Work in this area balances fidelity to teacher models, robustness, and efficiency, and explores trade-offs such as reliance on original training data, communication overhead in federated settings, and the benefits of designing students or student-friendly teachers. The literature shows repeated success of KD when tailored to the task and constraints, while also revealing limitations under severe data heterogeneity or adversarial settings.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Extensions, and Practical Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a core approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. Research over the past decade has expanded KD from simple teacher–student logit matching to a rich set of strategies that address data availability, privacy, distributed settings, architecture mismatches, and task-specific compression needs. Advances include data-free and zero-shot distillation, federated and privacy-aware distillation, representational and layer-mapping techniques for pre-trained language models, and practical combinations with quantization and architecture search to enable deployment on resource-constrained devices.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression methods aim to transfer performance and representational properties from large, expensive models to smaller, efficient ones. Across tasks in vision, language, graph learning, and generative modeling, researchers have developed strategies that extend beyond matching final logits: layer-wise and representation matching, many-to-many layer alignment, data-free distillation, private/distilled deployment, multi-teacher and self-distillation schemes, and task-adaptive compression. These approaches trade off fidelity, privacy, and computational cost, and they have been shown to enable real-world deployment of pretrained language models and other deep systems while revealing open challenges in distribution shift, heterogeneous data, and preserving inductive biases.

papers_seen.author: Harvey
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Practical, and Composable Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students that remain useful for deployment in resource-constrained or data-limited settings. KD works across modalities and deployment scenarios when combined with complementary compression techniques and careful design choices. To realize its benefits practitioners should treat KD as a component of a compression pipeline: design student-friendly teachers, choose what to transfer (logits, features, layers) based on task needs, address data constraints with augmentation or data-free methods, and pair distillation with pruning, quantization, or architecture search to meet latency and memory goals.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Unified Visual Transformer Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Vision transformers (ViTs) have gained popularity recently. Even without customized image operators such as convolutions, ViTs can yield competitive performance when properly trained on massive data. However, the computational overhead of ViTs remains prohibitive, due to stacking multi-head self-attention modules and else. Compared to the vast literature and prevailing success in compressing convolutional neural networks, the study of Vision Transformer compression has also just emerged, and existing works focused on one or two aspects of compression. This paper proposes a unified ViT compression framework that seamlessly assembles three effective techniques: pruning, layer skipping, and knowledge distillation. We formulate a budget-constrained, end-to-end optimization framework, targeting jointly learning model weights, layer-wise pruning ratios/masks, and skip configurations, under a distillation loss. The optimization problem is then solved using the primal-dual algorithm. Experiments are conducted with several ViT variants, e.g. DeiT and T2T-ViT backbones on the ImageNet dataset, and our approach consistently outperforms recent competitors. For example, DeiT-Tiny can be trimmed down to 50\% of the original FLOPs almost without losing accuracy. Codes are available online:~\url{https://github.com/VITA-Group/UVC}.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Understanding BERT Rankers Under Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep language models such as BERT pre-trained on large corpus have given a huge performance boost to the state-of-the-art information retrieval ranking systems. Knowledge embedded in such models allows them to pick up complex matching signals between passages and queries. However, the high computation cost during inference limits their deployment in real-world search scenarios. In this paper, we study if and how the knowledge for search within BERT can be transferred to a smaller ranker through distillation. Our experiments demonstrate that it is crucial to use a proper distillation procedure, which produces up to nine times speedup while preserving the state-of-the-art performance.

papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: Ensemble Knowledge Distillation for CTR Prediction
papers_seen.abstract: Recently, deep learning-based models have been widely studied for click-through rate (CTR) prediction and lead to improved prediction accuracy in many industrial applications. However, current research focuses primarily on building complex network architectures to better capture sophisticated feature interactions and dynamic user behaviors. The increased model complexity may slow down online inference and hinder its adoption in real-time applications. Instead, our work targets at a new model training strategy based on knowledge distillation (KD). KD is a teacher-student learning framework to transfer knowledge learned from a teacher model to a student model. The KD strategy not only allows us to simplify the student model as a vanilla DNN model but also achieves significant accuracy improvements over the state-of-the-art teacher models. The benefits thus motivate us to further explore the use of a powerful ensemble of teachers for more accurate student model training. We also propose some novel techniques to facilitate ensembled CTR prediction, including teacher gating and early stopping by distillation loss. We conduct comprehensive experiments against 12 existing models and across three industrial datasets. Both offline and online A/B testing results show the effectiveness of our KD-based training strategy.

papers_seen.author: Montgomery
papers_seen.title: Object DGCNN: 3D Object Detection using Dynamic Graphs
papers_seen.abstract: 3D object detection often involves complicated training and testing pipelines, which require substantial domain knowledge about individual datasets. Inspired by recent non-maximum suppression-free 2D object detection models, we propose a 3D object detection architecture on point clouds. Our method models 3D object detection as message passing on a dynamic graph, generalizing the DGCNN framework to predict a set of objects. In our construction, we remove the necessity of post-processing via object confidence aggregation or non-maximum suppression. To facilitate object detection from sparse point clouds, we also propose a set-to-set distillation approach customized to 3D detection. This approach aligns the outputs of the teacher model and the student model in a permutation-invariant fashion, significantly simplifying knowledge distillation for the 3D detection task. Our method achieves state-of-the-art performance on autonomous driving benchmarks. We also provide abundant analysis of the detection model and distillation framework.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Beyond Soft Labels: A Practical Position on Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a crucial technique for shrinking large deep models to meet real-world latency, memory and privacy constraints while retaining much of their performance. However, naive distillation that only matches teacher soft-labels is often insufficient. A more reliable strategy combines distillation of internal representations and features, task- or domain-adaptive compression, and architecture-aware search or adaptation. When applied with care — addressing optimization issues, data or privacy limits, and mismatch between teacher and student capacities — distillation enables compact, fast models that approach teacher performance across speech, NLP and vision tasks.

papers_seen.author: Davidson
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad family of techniques that transfer knowledge from larger, more expensive models (teachers) into smaller, efficient models (students) to improve inference speed, reduce memory, or enable deployment in resource-constrained settings. Across vision, language, graph, and generative modeling, KD has been instantiated as matching soft outputs, aligning internal representations, or supervising task-specific components. Practical work has shown KD can produce compact models with strong empirical performance, but success depends on many factors including student capacity, the choice of distilled signals, availability of data, training efficiency, and privacy constraints. Recent research has focused on richer teacher-to-student signals (intermediate layers, attention-based fusion), teacher adaptation strategies, data and augmentation strategies for better transfer, and integrating KD with pruning and other compression methods. Important open issues remain around optimization limits, data heterogeneity, and privacy-preserving distillation protocols.

papers_seen.author: Roberts
papers_seen.title: Improving the Interpretability of Deep Neural Networks with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep Neural Networks have achieved huge success at a wide spectrum of applications from language modeling, computer vision to speech recognition. However, nowadays, good performance alone is not sufficient to satisfy the needs of practical deployment where interpretability is demanded for cases involving ethics and mission critical applications. The complex models of Deep Neural Networks make it hard to understand and reason the predictions, which hinders its further progress. To tackle this problem, we apply the Knowledge Distillation technique to distill Deep Neural Networks into decision trees in order to attain good performance and interpretability simultaneously. We formulate the problem at hand as a multi-output regression problem and the experiments demonstrate that the student model achieves significantly better accuracy performance (about 1\% to 5\%) than vanilla decision trees at the same level of tree depth. The experiments are implemented on the TensorFlow platform to make it scalable to big datasets. To the best of our knowledge, we are the first to distill Deep Neural Networks into vanilla decision trees on multi-class datasets.

papers_seen.author: Ray
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses or transfers knowledge from larger or multiple models into smaller, faster models by leveraging softer training signals, intermediate representations, or alternate training protocols. Research has explored KD’s theoretical underpinnings, practical training strategies (including teacher-ensemble and teacher-free variants), privacy- and communication-aware settings, and extensions beyond classification to generation and structured prediction. Empirical work demonstrates KD’s ability to reduce deployment cost while retaining or sometimes even improving downstream performance, but trade-offs remain around data availability, representation matching, and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Charles
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, broadly applicable approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers information from high-capacity teachers to compact students via outputs, intermediate representations, or relational signals, and integrates naturally with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and deployment workflows (on-device inference, federated learning, and data-limited regimes). While KD reliably improves efficiency while preserving much of teacher performance, robust application requires careful choices about what signals to transfer, how to handle imperfect teachers and low-frequency behaviors, and how to combine KD with data strategies and architecture design to meet real-world constraints.

papers_seen.author: Walters
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and inductive biases from large teacher models to smaller student models so they can meet real-world constraints (latency, memory, privacy). Methods vary by what is transferred (soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention, relational signals), how data are used or synthesized, and whether distillation is combined with other compression tools or automated search. Empirically, KD often preserves much of teacher performance while enabling substantial reductions in size and inference cost, but practical success depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity, addressing data or privacy limits, and adapting teachers or objectives to propagate desired properties such as robustness and generalization.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Variants, and Practical Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, faster ones by transferring information from a teacher to a student. Research has explored diverse transfer signals (soft outputs, internal representations, layer mappings), different training regimes (data-driven, data-free, adversarial, federated), and task- or resource-aware designs that trade accuracy for latency and memory. Methods have been applied across vision, language, multimodal, and distributed settings, producing widely varying compression ratios and runtime improvements while raising challenges in alignment, stability, and privacy. The field continues to diversify through architecture-aware searches, self-distillation, and mechanisms that adapt teachers to be more student-friendly.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential but Context‑Sensitive Toolbox for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical centerpiece for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When used thoughtfully — selecting what to transfer, adapting objectives to teacher and student capacities, and combining distillation with complementary methods like pruning, quantization, or data synthesis — KD enables substantial reductions in inference cost while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. However, distillation’s effectiveness varies with task, data regime, and deployment constraints, so practitioners should treat it as a flexible set of techniques rather than a single plug‑and‑play algorithm.
