papers_seen.author: Aguirre
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques transfer information from large, high-capacity teacher models to smaller student models to reduce model size, latency, and deployment cost while retaining much of the teacher's utility. Methods vary in what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, ensembles), how training data is used or synthesized, and whether distillation is combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Across vision and NLP tasks, distillation enables practical deployment of compact models but requires careful handling of representation mismatch, data availability, optimization schedules, and potential amplification of teacher errors or biases.

papers_seen.author: Harrell
papers_seen.title: No One Left Behind: Inclusive Federated Learning over Heterogeneous Devices
papers_seen.abstract: Federated learning (FL) is an important paradigm for training global models from decentralized data in a privacy-preserving way. Existing FL methods usually assume the global model can be trained on any participating client. However, in real applications, the devices of clients are usually heterogeneous, and have different computing power. Although big models like BERT have achieved huge success in AI, it is difficult to apply them to heterogeneous FL with weak clients. The straightforward solutions like removing the weak clients or using a small model to fit all clients will lead to some problems, such as under-representation of dropped clients and inferior accuracy due to data loss or limited model representation ability. In this work, we propose InclusiveFL, a client-inclusive federated learning method to handle this problem. The core idea of InclusiveFL is to assign models of different sizes to clients with different computing capabilities, bigger models for powerful clients and smaller ones for weak clients. We also propose an effective method to share the knowledge among multiple local models with different sizes. In this way, all the clients can participate in the model learning in FL, and the final model can be big and powerful enough. Besides, we propose a momentum knowledge distillation method to better transfer knowledge in big models on powerful clients to the small models on weak clients. Extensive experiments on many real-world benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in learning accurate models from clients with heterogeneous devices under the FL framework.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a practical cornerstone for compressing large deep models into deployable, lower-latency students while retaining much of their predictive capacity. KD methods span simple soft-target matching to feature- and layer-level transfer, and they can operate in constrained settings (limited data, heterogeneous architectures, cross-modal scenarios). However, the effectiveness of KD depends on what is transferred, how teachers and students are matched, and how KD is combined with complementary compression strategies. Careful design—addressing teacher errors, domain shift, data availability, and architecture mismatch—yields compact models that meet real deployment constraints without disproportionate loss in quality.

papers_seen.author: Byrd
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Complementary Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. KD can preserve much of teacher performance while reducing inference cost, but it is not a standalone solution: its best results arise when combined with task-aware layer alignment, data strategies (augmentation or synthesis), architecture-aware compression, and careful teacher design. This position argues KD should be treated as the core of compression pipelines while acknowledging its failure modes and articulating practical mitigations.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical and Versatile Tool for Compression in NLP: Promise, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, faster students that retain much of the teacher's performance. In natural language processing, KD can operate at multiple granularities — from logits to intermediate representations or entire modules — and can be combined with pre-training, pruning, and low-precision inference to meet real-world deployment constraints. However, distillation is not a turnkey solution: optimization difficulties, mismatches in internal representations, and task-specific redundancies can limit benefits unless methods are adapted to the model size, pre-training regimen, and downstream objectives. When applied thoughtfully (e.g., pre-training compact students, selectively transferring internal features, and using task-aware layer-wise matching), KD yields efficient models that generalize well across tasks and settings.

papers_seen.author: Maddox
papers_seen.title: BERT-EMD: Many-to-Many Layer Mapping for BERT Compression with Earth Mover's Distance
papers_seen.abstract: Pre-trained language models (e.g., BERT) have achieved significant success in various natural language processing (NLP) tasks. However, high storage and computational costs obstruct pre-trained language models to be effectively deployed on resource-constrained devices. In this paper, we propose a novel BERT distillation method based on many-to-many layer mapping, which allows each intermediate student layer to learn from any intermediate teacher layers. In this way, our model can learn from different teacher layers adaptively for various NLP tasks. %motivated by the intuition that different NLP tasks require different levels of linguistic knowledge contained in the intermediate layers of BERT. In addition, we leverage Earth Mover's Distance (EMD) to compute the minimum cumulative cost that must be paid to transform knowledge from teacher network to student network. EMD enables the effective matching for many-to-many layer mapping. %EMD can be applied to network layers with different sizes and effectively measures semantic distance between the teacher network and student network. Furthermore, we propose a cost attention mechanism to learn the layer weights used in EMD automatically, which is supposed to further improve the model's performance and accelerate convergence time. Extensive experiments on GLUE benchmark demonstrate that our model achieves competitive performance compared to strong competitors in terms of both accuracy and model compression.

papers_seen.author: Waller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core of Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible technique for compressing large models into smaller, deployable ones for deep learning and NLP. When applied as part of an integrated compression pipeline it reduces inference cost and memory while retaining much of teacher performance. Achieving robust, fair, and private deployments requires combining KD with architecture-aware design, appropriate data strategies (including data-free alternatives), careful choice of distilled signals, and systematic evaluation of robustness and bias.

papers_seen.author: Munoz
papers_seen.title: Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation in Deep Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation deals with the problem of training a smaller model (Student) from a high capacity source model (Teacher) so as to retain most of its performance. Existing approaches use either the training data or meta-data extracted from it in order to train the Student. However, accessing the dataset on which the Teacher has been trained may not always be feasible if the dataset is very large or it poses privacy or safety concerns (e.g., bio-metric or medical data). Hence, in this paper, we propose a novel data-free method to train the Student from the Teacher. Without even using any meta-data, we synthesize the Data Impressions from the complex Teacher model and utilize these as surrogates for the original training data samples to transfer its learning to Student via knowledge distillation. We, therefore, dub our method "Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation" and demonstrate that our framework results in competitive generalization performance as achieved by distillation using the actual training data samples on multiple benchmark datasets.

papers_seen.author: Diaz
papers_seen.title: Model Compression with Two-stage Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation for Web Question Answering System
papers_seen.abstract: Deep pre-training and fine-tuning models (such as BERT and OpenAI GPT) have demonstrated excellent results in question answering areas. However, due to the sheer amount of model parameters, the inference speed of these models is very slow. How to apply these complex models to real business scenarios becomes a challenging but practical problem. Previous model compression methods usually suffer from information loss during the model compression procedure, leading to inferior models compared with the original one. To tackle this challenge, we propose a Two-stage Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation (TMKD for short) method for web Question Answering system. We first develop a general Q\&A distillation task for student model pre-training, and further fine-tune this pre-trained student model with multi-teacher knowledge distillation on downstream tasks (like Web Q\&A task, MNLI, SNLI, RTE tasks from GLUE), which effectively reduces the overfitting bias in individual teacher models, and transfers more general knowledge to the student model. The experiment results show that our method can significantly outperform the baseline methods and even achieve comparable results with the original teacher models, along with substantial speedup of model inference.

papers_seen.author: Orr
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information beyond hard labels. KD has evolved from simple soft-target matching into a flexible toolkit that includes intermediate-representation alignment, self- and multi-teacher schemes, data-free and online protocols, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Practical application of KD requires matching the distilled signals and workflows to student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints; addressing failure modes such as transferred biases or poor handling of low-frequency phenomena; and integrating distillation into a broader compression pipeline to meet latency, memory, and privacy goals.

papers_seen.author: Kelley
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performance models into smaller, deployable students by transferring useful behavior or representations. Across vision, language, generative, and graph domains, KD operates via multiple signals (soft logits, intermediate features, relational or ensemble knowledge) and is typically combined with complementary techniques such as pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation, and data strategies. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can both convey additional task signal and act as a regularizer that improves student generalization relative to training from scratch, but its effectiveness depends on choices about what to transfer, data availability or synthesis, teacher quality, and deployment constraints. Practical use requires tailoring distillation recipes to student capacity and application-specific constraints (latency, privacy, domain shift), and open problems remain around optimization mismatches, rare-token or low-frequency behavior, and privacy-sensitive or heterogeneous-data settings.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: The Case for Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Model Compression in NLP and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable ones while retaining much of their performance. Across NLP, speech, vision-language, and multimodal tasks, distillation techniques—including self-distillation, layer-wise/task-aware distillation, and teacher adaptation—enable substantial reductions in model size and compute with limited accuracy loss. KD is complementary to other compression strategies (e.g., pruning and architecture search) and benefits from careful choices in intermediate-target selection, data augmentation, and teacher-student alignment. When combined thoughtfully with task adaptation and hardware-aware techniques, KD unlocks feasible deployment of advanced models in resource-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression encompass a family of methods that transfer information from larger, high-capacity models (teachers) to smaller, efficient models (students). These approaches aim to retain predictive performance while reducing model size, latency, or enabling deployment under privacy or communication constraints. Recent work broadens distillation beyond logits to intermediate features, attention maps, multi-teacher setups, and data-limited or privacy-preserving regimes, producing task- and domain-aware compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP — Promise, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from larger teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. When paired with representation-level objectives, data strategies (including synthetic or privacy-preserving generation), and architecture-aware design, KD routinely yields models that meet latency, memory, and deployment constraints while retaining much of teacher performance. Success is engineering-dependent: the distillation signal, student capacity and pre-training, data availability, and explicit mitigation for harms such as bias or distributional fragility determine whether compressed models meet real-world needs.

papers_seen.author: Ray
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses or transfers knowledge from larger or multiple models into smaller, faster models by leveraging softer training signals, intermediate representations, or alternate training protocols. Research has explored KD’s theoretical underpinnings, practical training strategies (including teacher-ensemble and teacher-free variants), privacy- and communication-aware settings, and extensions beyond classification to generation and structured prediction. Empirical work demonstrates KD’s ability to reduce deployment cost while retaining or sometimes even improving downstream performance, but trade-offs remain around data availability, representation matching, and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Hicks
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Adaptation: Teaching to Adapt
papers_seen.abstract: Domain adaptation is crucial in many real-world applications where the distribution of the training data differs from the distribution of the test data. Previous Deep Learning-based approaches to domain adaptation need to be trained jointly on source and target domain data and are therefore unappealing in scenarios where models need to be adapted to a large number of domains or where a domain is evolving, e.g. spam detection where attackers continuously change their tactics.   To fill this gap, we propose Knowledge Adaptation, an extension of Knowledge Distillation (Bucilua et al., 2006; Hinton et al., 2015) to the domain adaptation scenario. We show how a student model achieves state-of-the-art results on unsupervised domain adaptation from multiple sources on a standard sentiment analysis benchmark by taking into account the domain-specific expertise of multiple teachers and the similarities between their domains.   When learning from a single teacher, using domain similarity to gauge trustworthiness is inadequate. To this end, we propose a simple metric that correlates well with the teacher's accuracy in the target domain. We demonstrate that incorporating high-confidence examples selected by this metric enables the student model to achieve state-of-the-art performance in the single-source scenario.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Releasing Graph Neural Networks with Differential Privacy Guarantees
papers_seen.abstract: With the increasing popularity of graph neural networks (GNNs) in several sensitive applications like healthcare and medicine, concerns have been raised over the privacy aspects of trained GNNs. More notably, GNNs are vulnerable to privacy attacks, such as membership inference attacks, even if only black-box access to the trained model is granted. We propose PrivGNN, a privacy-preserving framework for releasing GNN models in a centralized setting. Assuming an access to a public unlabeled graph, PrivGNN provides a framework to release GNN models trained explicitly on public data along with knowledge obtained from the private data in a privacy preserving manner. PrivGNN combines the knowledge-distillation framework with the two noise mechanisms, random subsampling, and noisy labeling, to ensure rigorous privacy guarantees. We theoretically analyze our approach in the Renyi differential privacy framework. Besides, we show the solid experimental performance of our method compared to several baselines adapted for graph-structured data. Our code is available at https://github.com/iyempissy/privGnn.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation in Practical Model Compression for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a niche training trick into a broad, practically necessary toolkit for compressing large deep models for deployment in resource-constrained settings. KD variants enable compressing Transformer-based and convolutional architectures, transferring useful inductive biases, operating with limited or no access to original training data, and even addressing downstream concerns such as fairness. At the same time, KD has limitations in certain distributed or heterogeneous-data settings that require complementary methods or careful protocol design. A targeted combination of task-aware layer-wise methods, feature-level mimicking, adversarial/data-free generation, and attention to distributional heterogeneity yields the best practical results for NLP and other deep learning applications.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Task-Aware Path to Model Compression in NLP and Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a flexible and practical framework for compressing large models and transferring capabilities to smaller ones. When applied thoughtfully — using layer-aware alignment, attention-guided feature matching, dynamic multi-teacher strategies, and privacy- or deployment-aware protocols — distillation enables substantial speedups, reduced footprint, and cross-modal or cross-device applicability with small drops (or even gains) in task performance. Distillation is not a plug-and-play cure: optimization challenges, teacher-student mismatch, and task-specific redundancy mean methods must be adapted to the target architecture and data regime to realize consistent benefits.

papers_seen.author: Collins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Strengths, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from a heuristic training trick into a broadly applicable, practical toolkit for compressing large models for deployment in constrained environments. KD enables substantial size and latency reductions while retaining much of teacher performance; it supports different transfer signals (logits, features, attention), works with or without original training data, and can be adapted to preserve robustness or meet privacy constraints. However, its success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to prepare students (including pre-training), how to handle limited or heterogeneous data, and how to mitigate transferred biases or adversarial vulnerability. Combining distillation with complementary strategies—layer-aware matching, feature-level mimicry, data synthesis or augmentation, teacher optimization, and robustness-aware objectives—gives the most reliable practical outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques transfer predictive behavior and internal structure from larger teacher models to smaller student models to reduce computation, memory, and latency while preserving performance. The literature documents a spectrum of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention or channel maps, and relational signals), a variety of optimization and architectural practices (layer mapping, projectors, multi-stage training, and student-friendly teacher design), and deployment workflows for constrained settings (data-free, federated, and domain-adaptive distillation). Empirical and theoretical work highlights multiple mechanisms that make KD effective (regularization via soft targets, representation alignment, and optimization/inductive-bias transfer), while also identifying persistent challenges such as aligning heterogeneous architectures, preserving low-frequency behavior, and selecting what and when to transfer. Practical recommendations center on matching distillation signals to student capacity, using feature- or layer-aware objectives when internal alignment matters, and combining KD with complementary compression techniques for robust deployment.

papers_seen.author: Nunez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical but Engineering-Dependent Route to Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile set of methods for transferring behavior from large teacher models to smaller students, enabling reduced inference cost and deployment on constrained devices. KD can match final outputs or internal representations and is often combined with complementary compression techniques; however, its success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align architectures, and how to handle data and optimization mismatches. I argue that KD should be treated as an essential, task-aware component of compression pipelines rather than a plug-and-play solution, and I offer practical directions to maximize its benefits while mitigating common failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Valdez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Pragmatic Tool for Compressing Deep and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is not merely one technique among many for model compression: when applied thoughtfully it is a central, practical lever for producing small, fast models that retain much of the performance, robustness, and task-specific behavior of large teachers. Best practice couples KD with representation-level supervision, teacher-student co-design, data and privacy strategies, and complementary compression methods so that compact models meet real-world latency, memory and heterogeneity constraints.

papers_seen.author: Galvan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Design-Sensitive Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely applicable approach for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. When implemented thoughtfully—choosing what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, and which data and augmentation strategies to use—KD can recover much of a teacher’s performance while substantially reducing inference cost and memory. However, distillation also has limits: it can propagate teacher biases, struggle with low-data or low-capacity students, and requires complementary techniques (e.g., layer mapping, pruning, or synthetic-data schemes) and careful evaluation to meet real-world deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Understanding and Improving Lexical Choice in Non-Autoregressive Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is essential for training non-autoregressive translation (NAT) models by reducing the complexity of the raw data with an autoregressive teacher model. In this study, we empirically show that as a side effect of this training, the lexical choice errors on low-frequency words are propagated to the NAT model from the teacher model. To alleviate this problem, we propose to expose the raw data to NAT models to restore the useful information of low-frequency words, which are missed in the distilled data. To this end, we introduce an extra Kullback-Leibler divergence term derived by comparing the lexical choice of NAT model and that embedded in the raw data. Experimental results across language pairs and model architectures demonstrate the effectiveness and universality of the proposed approach. Extensive analyses confirm our claim that our approach improves performance by reducing the lexical choice errors on low-frequency words. Encouragingly, our approach pushes the SOTA NAT performance on the WMT14 English-German and WMT16 Romanian-English datasets up to 27.8 and 33.8 BLEU points, respectively. The source code will be released.

papers_seen.author: Taylor
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller models by transferring predictive and representational information from teachers to students. Across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks, KD enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Practical pipelines combine soft-target matching, representation-level imitation, architecture-aware design and search, and data strategies (including data-free or privacy-preserving synthesis). While KD often recovers much of a teacher's performance and can enable students that are substantially faster and smaller, success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align representations, and how to manage data and teacher quality; important open problems remain in robustness, domain shift, and theoretical explanation.

papers_seen.author: Moreno
papers_seen.title: Reframing Knowledge Distillation: Beyond Compression to Regularization, Robustness, and Generalization
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is often presented primarily as a model compression technique. Emerging work shows KD is also a flexible training paradigm that provides regularization, transfers internal representations, improves robustness to adversaries and domain shifts, and can be applied without a stronger teacher. This essay argues KD should be treated as a general-purpose tool for shaping student learning — one that can and should be combined with teacher-free methods, internal-representation alignment, multi-teacher aggregation, careful data augmentation, and principled mixing of hard and soft targets to maximize performance in NLP and broader deep learning applications.

papers_seen.author: Walter
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression methods reduce the computational and memory cost of large neural models by transferring information from larger or ensemble teachers to smaller students. Approaches vary from using soft logits to matching internal representations, attention maps, or generator outputs; they have been adapted for modality transfer, privacy- or bandwidth-constrained settings, and specialized architectures (e.g., transformers, GANs). Empirical work shows that representation-level objectives, architectural design of the student/bridge modules, and careful training protocols can preserve most of the teacher’s performance while dramatically reducing size and runtime. Ongoing challenges include preserving rare-token or fine-grained behaviors, deploying under strict privacy/bandwidth constraints, and automating architecture search for compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Marshall
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely used approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Across modalities, KD transfers predictive behavior and internal representations using a variety of targets and protocols (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, multi-stage or online schemes) and composes well with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, and how to handle data or privacy constraints. KD enables many deployment goals (reduced latency/memory, domain adaptation, privacy-aware training), but its effectiveness is limited by optimization dynamics, teacher–student mismatch, distribution shift for synthetic data, and the potential transfer of undesirable biases.

papers_seen.author: Alvarado
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques compress large neural networks into smaller, faster models for practical deployment. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD succeeds through multiple mechanisms — not solely by copying a stronger teacher — enabling many practical variants (logit-based soft targets, feature- and layer-level matching, multi-teacher and online schemes, data-free and privacy-preserving protocols). Effective application depends on choosing what and how to transfer, handling data or device constraints, and combining distillation with other compression tools. Key limitations include optimization dynamics, distribution shift for synthetic data, and heterogeneity in federated or privacy-sensitive settings; current research points toward deeper study of representation transfer, optimization effects, and task-aware distillation pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Zavala
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. Over the past decade researchers have extended KD from simple soft-target matching to a diverse toolkit that includes intermediate-feature matching, progressive module replacement, data-augmentation-aware distillation, and federated or heterogeneous-device formulations. Empirical work shows KD often yields substantial gains in latency and memory while preserving much of teacher performance, but practical success requires careful choices about what to transfer, how to select or synthesize data, and how to align teacher and student architectures under constraints such as privacy, communication, and device heterogeneity.

papers_seen.author: Rhodes
papers_seen.title: Lifelong Language Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: It is challenging to perform lifelong language learning (LLL) on a stream of different tasks without any performance degradation comparing to the multi-task counterparts. To address this issue, we present Lifelong Language Knowledge Distillation (L2KD), a simple but efficient method that can be easily applied to existing LLL architectures in order to mitigate the degradation. Specifically, when the LLL model is trained on a new task, we assign a teacher model to first learn the new task, and pass the knowledge to the LLL model via knowledge distillation. Therefore, the LLL model can better adapt to the new task while keeping the previously learned knowledge. Experiments show that the proposed L2KD consistently improves previous state-of-the-art models, and the degradation comparing to multi-task models in LLL tasks is well mitigated for both sequence generation and text classification tasks.

papers_seen.author: Pierce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a General-Purpose Paradigm: Beyond Compression to Adaptation, Robustness, and Inclusive Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) began as a technique to compress large models into smaller, faster ones. Over the past decade it has matured into a flexible training paradigm that can shape student behavior via soft targets, intermediate feature alignment, and multi-teacher or self-teaching schemes. When designed with task, data, and deployment constraints in mind, KD can enable domain specialization, interpretability, privacy-friendly federated learning, and improved robustness while still supporting efficient inference.

papers_seen.author: Cook
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Benefits, Limits, and Engineering Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile foundation for compressing deep and language models: it enables much smaller, faster students to capture substantial teacher performance while supporting deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD excels when combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and careful engineering (choice of transferred signals, data augmentation, teacher selection). However, KD is not a plug-and-play solution: it can propagate teacher imperfections, struggle with rare-token or low-frequency behaviors, and face difficulties under heterogeneous or privacy-constrained data regimes. Treating KD as the central tool in a compression pipeline — but one that requires task-aware design and diagnostics — yields the best practical outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Byrd
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Complementary Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. KD can preserve much of teacher performance while reducing inference cost, but it is not a standalone solution: its best results arise when combined with task-aware layer alignment, data strategies (augmentation or synthesis), architecture-aware compression, and careful teacher design. This position argues KD should be treated as the core of compression pipelines while acknowledging its failure modes and articulating practical mitigations.

papers_seen.author: Higgins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Context-Sensitive Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely applicable approach for compressing large models into smaller ones that meet deployment constraints. KD reduces storage, latency, and energy while preserving much of teacher performance, but its success depends on what knowledge is transferred, how teacher signals are generated and trusted, and how distillation is combined with other compression methods and fairness or robustness constraints. Effective deployment requires task-aware decisions about targets (logits vs. features), data (original, augmented, or synthetic), architectural alignment, and additional safeguards for bias and domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Releasing Graph Neural Networks with Differential Privacy Guarantees
papers_seen.abstract: With the increasing popularity of graph neural networks (GNNs) in several sensitive applications like healthcare and medicine, concerns have been raised over the privacy aspects of trained GNNs. More notably, GNNs are vulnerable to privacy attacks, such as membership inference attacks, even if only black-box access to the trained model is granted. We propose PrivGNN, a privacy-preserving framework for releasing GNN models in a centralized setting. Assuming an access to a public unlabeled graph, PrivGNN provides a framework to release GNN models trained explicitly on public data along with knowledge obtained from the private data in a privacy preserving manner. PrivGNN combines the knowledge-distillation framework with the two noise mechanisms, random subsampling, and noisy labeling, to ensure rigorous privacy guarantees. We theoretically analyze our approach in the Renyi differential privacy framework. Besides, we show the solid experimental performance of our method compared to several baselines adapted for graph-structured data. Our code is available at https://github.com/iyempissy/privGnn.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Linkless Link Prediction via Relational Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have shown exceptional performance in the task of link prediction. Despite their effectiveness, the high latency brought by non-trivial neighborhood data dependency limits GNNs in practical deployments. Conversely, the known efficient MLPs are much less effective than GNNs due to the lack of relational knowledge. In this work, to combine the advantages of GNNs and MLPs, we start with exploring direct knowledge distillation (KD) methods for link prediction, i.e., predicted logit-based matching and node representation-based matching. Upon observing direct KD analogs do not perform well for link prediction, we propose a relational KD framework, Linkless Link Prediction (LLP), to distill knowledge for link prediction with MLPs. Unlike simple KD methods that match independent link logits or node representations, LLP distills relational knowledge that is centered around each (anchor) node to the student MLP. Specifically, we propose rank-based matching and distribution-based matching strategies that complement each other. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LLP boosts the link prediction performance of MLPs with significant margins, and even outperforms the teacher GNNs on 7 out of 8 benchmarks. LLP also achieves a 70.68x speedup in link prediction inference compared to GNNs on the large-scale OGB dataset.

papers_seen.author: Wise
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, production-ready approach for compressing large models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students. KD supports multiple transfer signals (logits, features, attention or relational structure), composes with other compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search), and can be adapted to domain- or data-constrained settings. Its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints; therefore KD should be treated as a toolbox of methods and workflows rather than a single recipe.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile method for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. It is applied across modalities and deployment constraints and is most effective when combined with complementary compression techniques, careful data and teacher design, and methods that address representation mismatch and optimization. This synthesis summarizes practical techniques, common challenges, and recommended practices for using KD in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Morales
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Practical Tool for Compressing and Adapting Deep and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated approach for producing smaller models that retain much of the performance and useful behavior of larger teachers. KD supports a spectrum of deployment goals — reduced latency and memory, domain adaptation, privacy-aware training, and robustness improvements — and works best when combined with complementary techniques (e.g., layer mapping, feature matching, synthetic-data generation, pruning, or quantization). However, KD is not a universal solution: outcomes depend on teacher quality, what signals are transferred, data fidelity, and design choices that align distilled knowledge to the downstream task. Practical adoption therefore requires principled pipeline choices and awareness of KD failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers information from larger teacher models to smaller student models to reduce inference cost while retaining much of the teacher's performance. KD methods operate at multiple granularities (soft-label/logit matching, intermediate-feature imitation, module- or layer-wise mapping) and appear across domains including NLP, vision, multimodal, federated, and graph settings. Practical pipelines combine KD with data strategies, teacher adaptation, and complementary compression (pruning, quantization, architecture search), but open challenges remain around data heterogeneity, teacher imperfections, and preserving properties such as low-frequency token fidelity, robustness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: On Representation Knowledge Distillation for Graph Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a learning paradigm for boosting resource-efficient graph neural networks (GNNs) using more expressive yet cumbersome teacher models. Past work on distillation for GNNs proposed the Local Structure Preserving loss (LSP), which matches local structural relationships defined over edges across the student and teacher's node embeddings. This paper studies whether preserving the global topology of how the teacher embeds graph data can be a more effective distillation objective for GNNs, as real-world graphs often contain latent interactions and noisy edges. We propose Graph Contrastive Representation Distillation (G-CRD), which uses contrastive learning to implicitly preserve global topology by aligning the student node embeddings to those of the teacher in a shared representation space. Additionally, we introduce an expanded set of benchmarks on large-scale real-world datasets where the performance gap between teacher and student GNNs is non-negligible. Experiments across 4 datasets and 14 heterogeneous GNN architectures show that G-CRD consistently boosts the performance and robustness of lightweight GNNs, outperforming LSP (and a global structure preserving variant of LSP) as well as baselines from 2D computer vision. An analysis of the representational similarity among teacher and student embedding spaces reveals that G-CRD balances preserving local and global relationships, while structure preserving approaches are best at preserving one or the other. Our code is available at https://github.com/chaitjo/efficient-gnns

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Multifaceted Tool: Beyond Compression to Fairness, Robustness, and Adaptation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is commonly used to compress large models into smaller, faster students, but its potential extends much further. When applied thoughtfully—via feature-level mimicking, progressive module replacement, teacher selection and confidence-weighting, and by combining with automated search or divergence choices—KD can improve fairness, domain adaptation, generative model compression, and student robustness while preserving or even improving task performance. This essay argues that KD is not a single recipe but a family of techniques that should be matched to specific goals (efficiency, fairness, transferability, or generation), and gives concrete methodological recommendations informed by empirical and theoretical work.

papers_seen.author: Ferrell
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation transfers information from large teacher models to smaller students to reduce inference cost and memory while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. Modern distillation expands beyond matching teacher logits to include intermediate representation matching, self-supervised and contrastive objectives, data-free and synthetic-data schemes, curriculum and augmentation strategies, and privacy- and deployment-aware protocols. These variants enable application across vision, speech, graph-structured data, and NLP, but practical deployment requires care about data availability, optimization dynamics, robustness, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Patterson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Effective, Flexible, and Context-Sensitive
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, widely applicable approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When used thoughtfully—matching what is transferred to student capacity, combining logits- and feature-level objectives, and integrating complementary techniques like low-precision numerics or architectural redesign—KD consistently yields compact models that approach teacher performance while reducing inference cost. However, KD is not a one-size-fits-all solution: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints such as privacy or heterogeneity, so practitioners must adapt KD components and pipelines to the task and environment.

papers_seen.author: Gardner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Essential, Versatile, and Context-Sensitive for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable technique for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students that retain much of teacher performance. KD can be applied across modalities and settings to reduce inference cost, enable deployment under resource or privacy constraints, and serve as a core component of broader compression pipelines. However, its effectiveness depends on careful design choices about what to transfer, data regimes, and alignment between teacher and student.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. The field has broadened from soft-logit matching to include feature- and layer-level alignment, relational and attention-aware transfers, data-free synthesis, adversarially-aware objectives, and curriculum or multi-teacher schemes. Practical success depends on choices about the distillation signal, data availability or synthesis, teacher–student architectural alignment, and training curricula; open challenges include preserving rare or long-tail behaviors, maintaining robustness and privacy, and adapting distillation to domain shifts and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. KD variants—soft-target matching, intermediate-representation matching, self- and online-distillation, and data-free (zero-shot) synthesis—enable latency, memory, and privacy gains across vision and language tasks. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: its success depends on what signals are distilled, teacher quality, data availability or synthesis, and pipeline choices (layer mapping, curricula, and complementary compression). I argue KD should be treated as the central component of compression pipelines, applied with task-aware design and combined with other methods to manage its limitations and maximize deployment utility.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central approach to compress large deep models into smaller, faster, and often more deployable student models. KD techniques range from classic teacher-to-student soft-target training to recent advances including data-free distillation, multi-teacher strategies, meta-learned teachers, and compression combined with pruning or structural sparsity. In NLP applications KD is used to shrink pre-trained transformers, accelerate inference for production systems, enable non-autoregressive generation, and adapt large models to resource-constrained or heterogeneous environments. Empirical work shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance while producing models with far lower latency and storage cost, but theoretical understanding, sensitivity to data and teacher quality, and robustness under distributional shifts remain active research areas.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Improved Accuracy in Spoken Question Answering
papers_seen.abstract: Spoken question answering (SQA) is a challenging task that requires the machine to fully understand the complex spoken documents. Automatic speech recognition (ASR) plays a significant role in the development of QA systems. However, the recent work shows that ASR systems generate highly noisy transcripts, which critically limit the capability of machine comprehension on the SQA task. To address the issue, we present a novel distillation framework. Specifically, we devise a training strategy to perform knowledge distillation (KD) from spoken documents and written counterparts. Our work makes a step towards distilling knowledge from the language model as a supervision signal to lead to better student accuracy by reducing the misalignment between automatic and manual transcriptions. Experiments demonstrate that our approach outperforms several state-of-the-art language models on the Spoken-SQuAD dataset.

papers_seen.author: Hoffman
papers_seen.title: Federated Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Distributed learning frameworks often rely on exchanging model parameters across workers, instead of revealing their raw data. A prime example is federated learning that exchanges the gradients or weights of each neural network model. Under limited communication resources, however, such a method becomes extremely costly particularly for modern deep neural networks having a huge number of model parameters. In this regard, federated distillation (FD) is a compelling distributed learning solution that only exchanges the model outputs whose dimensions are commonly much smaller than the model sizes (e.g., 10 labels in the MNIST dataset). The goal of this chapter is to provide a deep understanding of FD while demonstrating its communication efficiency and applicability to a variety of tasks. To this end, towards demystifying the operational principle of FD, the first part of this chapter provides a novel asymptotic analysis for two foundational algorithms of FD, namely knowledge distillation (KD) and co-distillation (CD), by exploiting the theory of neural tangent kernel (NTK). Next, the second part elaborates on a baseline implementation of FD for a classification task, and illustrates its performance in terms of accuracy and communication efficiency compared to FL. Lastly, to demonstrate the applicability of FD to various distributed learning tasks and environments, the third part presents two selected applications, namely FD over asymmetric uplink-and-downlink wireless channels and FD for reinforcement learning.

papers_seen.author: Gilbert
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Composable Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as a central, composable component of model-compression pipelines for deep learning and NLP. KD is versatile—able to transfer logits, intermediate representations, and relational signals—and can be combined with pruning, quantization, architecture redesign, or data-synthesis techniques to produce deployable students that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Its practical success requires matching distilled signals to student capacity, handling data and distributional constraints, and explicitly addressing fairness and robustness concerns. When designed and evaluated carefully, KD enables effective trade-offs between efficiency and task performance across modalities.

papers_seen.author: Tucker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Efficient and Responsible NLP and Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical, versatile approach for compressing large models and enabling deployment in resource-constrained environments. Beyond raw compression, KD supports domain adaptation, data-free scenarios, improved inference speed, and novel training regimes for specialized tasks. However, distillation is not a panacea: it can amplify teacher biases, interact with regularization techniques in subtle ways, and benefits most when combined with complementary methods such as architecture-aware training, generator-based sample synthesis, or instance-aware losses.

papers_seen.author: Potter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core of Practical Model Compression in NLP: Benefits, Techniques, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible method for transferring the capabilities of large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. When combined with complementary techniques (architecture-aware design, quantization, data synthesis, or curriculum learning), KD enables substantial reductions in inference cost, memory, and latency while retaining much of the original performance. However, its success depends on careful choice of what signals to transfer, availability or synthesis of training data, and explicit handling of domain shift, student capacity mismatches, and potential amplification of teacher biases.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Rejuvenating Low-Frequency Words: Making the Most of Parallel Data in Non-Autoregressive Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is commonly used to construct synthetic data for training non-autoregressive translation (NAT) models. However, there exists a discrepancy on low-frequency words between the distilled and the original data, leading to more errors on predicting low-frequency words. To alleviate the problem, we directly expose the raw data into NAT by leveraging pretraining. By analyzing directed alignments, we found that KD makes low-frequency source words aligned with targets more deterministically but fails to align sufficient low-frequency words from target to source. Accordingly, we propose reverse KD to rejuvenate more alignments for low-frequency target words. To make the most of authentic and synthetic data, we combine these complementary approaches as a new training strategy for further boosting NAT performance. We conduct experiments on five translation benchmarks over two advanced architectures. Results demonstrate that the proposed approach can significantly and universally improve translation quality by reducing translation errors on low-frequency words. Encouragingly, our approach achieves 28.2 and 33.9 BLEU points on the WMT14 English-German and WMT16 Romanian-English datasets, respectively. Our code, data, and trained models are available at \url{https://github.com/alphadl/RLFW-NAT}.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical but Design-Sensitive Path to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly useful family of techniques for transferring behavior from large teacher models to smaller students to reduce inference cost and enable deployment. KD has been instantiated as matching soft targets, aligning intermediate representations, progressive module replacement, and selective or multi-teacher schemes. While KD often yields strong empirical gains and enables domain- and task-specific compression, its success depends on optimization dynamics, the choice of distilled signal, data quality and selection, and teacher–student alignment. Careful method choices make KD a reliable, production-ready compression strategy, but it is not a universal shortcut: practitioners must tailor KD objectives and protocols to their constraints and goals.

papers_seen.author: Harmon
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, more deployable students by transferring information beyond hard labels. Over the past decade KD has evolved from simple soft-target (logit) matching to a broad toolkit that includes internal representation alignment, self-distillation, multi-teacher and data-free methods, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Practical distillation success depends on aligning transferred signals to student capacity, handling data and privacy constraints, and designing optimization and evaluation protocols that preserve accuracy and robustness in deployment settings.

papers_seen.author: Mayo
papers_seen.title: Rethinking Soft Labels for Knowledge Distillation: A Bias-Variance Tradeoff Perspective
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is an effective approach to leverage a well-trained network or an ensemble of them, named as the teacher, to guide the training of a student network. The outputs from the teacher network are used as soft labels for supervising the training of a new network. Recent studies \citep{muller2019does,yuan2020revisiting} revealed an intriguing property of the soft labels that making labels soft serves as a good regularization to the student network. From the perspective of statistical learning, regularization aims to reduce the variance, however how bias and variance change is not clear for training with soft labels. In this paper, we investigate the bias-variance tradeoff brought by distillation with soft labels. Specifically, we observe that during training the bias-variance tradeoff varies sample-wisely. Further, under the same distillation temperature setting, we observe that the distillation performance is negatively associated with the number of some specific samples, which are named as regularization samples since these samples lead to bias increasing and variance decreasing. Nevertheless, we empirically find that completely filtering out regularization samples also deteriorates distillation performance. Our discoveries inspired us to propose the novel weighted soft labels to help the network adaptively handle the sample-wise bias-variance tradeoff. Experiments on standard evaluation benchmarks validate the effectiveness of our method. Our code is available at \url{https://github.com/bellymonster/Weighted-Soft-Label-Distillation}.

papers_seen.author: Cobb
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, faster students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels. Over the past decade KD has evolved from simple soft-target matching to a diverse toolkit that includes intermediate-representation matching, layerwise alignment, multi-teacher and self-distillation, curriculum and augmentation strategies, and privacy- or data-free procedures. When combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) and task-aware choices about what and how to transfer, KD enables practical deployment of high-performing models across modalities while raising open issues in robustness, fairness, and distributional generalization.
