papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: Ensemble Knowledge Distillation for CTR Prediction
papers_seen.abstract: Recently, deep learning-based models have been widely studied for click-through rate (CTR) prediction and lead to improved prediction accuracy in many industrial applications. However, current research focuses primarily on building complex network architectures to better capture sophisticated feature interactions and dynamic user behaviors. The increased model complexity may slow down online inference and hinder its adoption in real-time applications. Instead, our work targets at a new model training strategy based on knowledge distillation (KD). KD is a teacher-student learning framework to transfer knowledge learned from a teacher model to a student model. The KD strategy not only allows us to simplify the student model as a vanilla DNN model but also achieves significant accuracy improvements over the state-of-the-art teacher models. The benefits thus motivate us to further explore the use of a powerful ensemble of teachers for more accurate student model training. We also propose some novel techniques to facilitate ensembled CTR prediction, including teacher gating and early stopping by distillation loss. We conduct comprehensive experiments against 12 existing models and across three industrial datasets. Both offline and online A/B testing results show the effectiveness of our KD-based training strategy.

papers_seen.author: May
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a suite of methods for transferring information from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller student models so they can be deployed under compute, memory, and privacy constraints. KD encompasses matching teacher outputs, aligning intermediate representations, online and multi-teacher workflows, and data-aware or data-free strategies. Empirically KD often yields compact students that approach teacher performance and can improve generalization, but practical success hinges on teacher-student alignment, data strategy, and addressing robustness and distribution-shift issues. Open directions include distillation without original data, preserving fine-grained sequence behavior, and adapting KD to heterogeneous or privacy-sensitive settings.

papers_seen.author: Davenport
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically proven approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of large teachers. KD methods—ranging from soft-label/logit matching to feature- and relation-level imitation—work across modalities and tasks and integrate naturally with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. However, maximizing KD’s benefits requires deliberate choices about what signals to transfer, how to supply or synthesize data, and how to align teacher and student architectures; left unaddressed, challenges such as representation misalignment, degraded rare-token behavior, and robustness or privacy losses can limit gains.

papers_seen.author: Walton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential, Practical Strategy for Compressing Deep Models in NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques are indispensable for deploying high-capacity deep and language models in resource-constrained settings. By transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teachers to smaller students, practitioners can achieve large reductions in model size and latency while retaining most task performance. However, realizing these gains reliably requires attention to what is transferred (logits, features, relations), how teachers and data are chosen, and hardware- or deployment-aware compression strategies.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Practical Recommendations for NLP and Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely applicable approach to compress large deep models into smaller, deployable ones. Across language models, speech encoders, and vision systems, distillation reduces model size and inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance. However, success is not automatic: distillation interacts with dataset availability, model heterogeneity, optimization dynamics, robustness, and fairness. Careful choices of what to transfer (logits, features, layer-wise representations), how to handle missing data, and how to address heterogeneous or privacy-sensitive settings are essential for reliable compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Burton
papers_seen.title: Efficient Transformer-based Large Scale Language Representations using Hardware-friendly Block Structured Pruning
papers_seen.abstract: Pre-trained large-scale language models have increasingly demonstrated high accuracy on many natural language processing (NLP) tasks. However, the limited weight storage and computational speed on hardware platforms have impeded the popularity of pre-trained models, especially in the era of edge computing. In this work, we propose an efficient transformer-based large-scale language representation using hardware-friendly block structure pruning. We incorporate the reweighted group Lasso into block-structured pruning for optimization. Besides the significantly reduced weight storage and computation, the proposed approach achieves high compression rates. Experimental results on different models (BERT, RoBERTa, and DistilBERT) on the General Language Understanding Evaluation (GLUE) benchmark tasks show that we achieve up to 5.0x with zero or minor accuracy degradation on certain task(s). Our proposed method is also orthogonal to existing compact pre-trained language models such as DistilBERT using knowledge distillation, since a further 1.79x average compression rate can be achieved on top of DistilBERT with zero or minor accuracy degradation. It is suitable to deploy the final compressed model on resource-constrained edge devices.

papers_seen.author: Caldwell
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer information from larger, expensive teacher models to smaller, deployable students to reduce inference cost while preserving much of the teacher’s behavior. Across modalities and tasks, KD methods vary by the form of transferred signal (soft targets, intermediate features, attention maps, or module behaviors), training setting (offline, online, federated, or data-free), and complementary techniques (architecture design, pruning, quantization, and data augmentation). Practical success depends on aligning teacher and student inputs/representations, selecting appropriate distillation objectives for the task and data regime, and mitigating distributional or token-frequency artifacts introduced during distillation. This synthesis summarizes major approaches, empirical findings, limitations, and practical strategies for applying KD in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Mckee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Model Compression: Power, Patterns, and Precautions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, flexible approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a toolkit rather than a single recipe, and combined with complementary compression methods and data strategies, KD enables substantial reductions in latency, memory, and energy while retaining much of teacher performance. However, distillation can transfer teacher weaknesses (biases, brittleness, low-frequency errors) and requires careful choices about what to transfer, how to align representations across heterogeneous architectures, and how to handle limited or private data. Practical deployment therefore calls for method selection tailored to task and constraints, plus safeguards for robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer predictive behavior and internal structure from larger, often pre-trained teacher models into smaller, efficient student models in order to reduce latency, memory, and deployment cost while retaining task performance. Methods span matching soft outputs, aligning intermediate representations, attention- or relation-based feature matching, curriculum strategies for progressively harder supervision, and task- or data-aware architecture search. Practical success depends on student capacity, availability and quality of data, whether the student itself is pre-trained, and choices about what to transfer; open challenges include preserving fairness and robustness, aligning heterogeneous architectures, and operating under privacy or data-limited conditions.

papers_seen.author: Hensley
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques form a broadly applicable toolkit for transferring capability from large, expensive teacher models to smaller, faster, or more privacy-friendly student models. Methods range from transferring softened output distributions to aligning intermediate representations, using synthetic or augmented data when original data are unavailable, and combining distillation with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search). KD is used both as a deployment-oriented compression strategy and as a general training paradigm that can improve regularization, robustness, and domain adaptation. Practical success requires careful matching of distillation objectives, teacher-student alignment, and data strategies; persistent challenges include theoretical understanding of when distillation helps, preserving rare-token behavior in NLP, and avoiding artifacts introduced by synthetic data.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Multi-Level Branched Regularization for Federated Learning
papers_seen.abstract: A critical challenge of federated learning is data heterogeneity and imbalance across clients, which leads to inconsistency between local networks and unstable convergence of global models. To alleviate the limitations, we propose a novel architectural regularization technique that constructs multiple auxiliary branches in each local model by grafting local and global subnetworks at several different levels and that learns the representations of the main pathway in the local model congruent to the auxiliary hybrid pathways via online knowledge distillation. The proposed technique is effective to robustify the global model even in the non-iid setting and is applicable to various federated learning frameworks conveniently without incurring extra communication costs. We perform comprehensive empirical studies and demonstrate remarkable performance gains in terms of accuracy and efficiency compared to existing methods. The source code is available at our project page.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques transfer predictive behavior and internal structure from larger teacher models to smaller student models to reduce computation, memory, and latency while preserving performance. The literature documents a spectrum of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention or channel maps, and relational signals), a variety of optimization and architectural practices (layer mapping, projectors, multi-stage training, and student-friendly teacher design), and deployment workflows for constrained settings (data-free, federated, and domain-adaptive distillation). Empirical and theoretical work highlights multiple mechanisms that make KD effective (regularization via soft targets, representation alignment, and optimization/inductive-bias transfer), while also identifying persistent challenges such as aligning heterogeneous architectures, preserving low-frequency behavior, and selecting what and when to transfer. Practical recommendations center on matching distillation signals to student capacity, using feature- or layer-aware objectives when internal alignment matters, and combining KD with complementary compression techniques for robust deployment.

papers_seen.author: Harris
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical, and Composable Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly practical approach for turning large, high-performing models into smaller, efficient models suitable for deployment. Across vision and language tasks, KD enables substantial reductions in parameter count and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance. Its strengths come from flexibility in what to transfer (logits, intermediate features, optimization signals), its compatibility with architecture search and other compression primitives, and its ability to operate under constrained or private-data scenarios. KD is not a one-size-fits-all remedy: practitioners should select KD variants and complementary techniques guided by task requirements, data availability, and deployment constraints to balance fidelity, robustness, and efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature and flexible approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable ones. When combined with careful choices—such as pre-training compact students, data-free distillation for privacy, adaptive multi-teacher strategies, feature-level imitation, and teacher-side learning—KD can deliver strong task performance with much smaller inference cost. However, KD is not a panacea: optimization gaps between teacher and student, propagation of teacher biases, and dataset mismatches can limit gains unless explicitly addressed. A pragmatic KD pipeline therefore integrates algorithmic innovations and fairness/optimization checks to realize both efficiency and reliable behavior in production NLP and deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile method for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. It is applied across modalities and deployment constraints and is most effective when combined with complementary compression techniques, careful data and teacher design, and methods that address representation mismatch and optimization. This synthesis summarizes practical techniques, common challenges, and recommended practices for using KD in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Zuniga
papers_seen.title: Large scale distributed neural network training through online distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Techniques such as ensembling and distillation promise model quality improvements when paired with almost any base model. However, due to increased test-time cost (for ensembles) and increased complexity of the training pipeline (for distillation), these techniques are challenging to use in industrial settings. In this paper we explore a variant of distillation which is relatively straightforward to use as it does not require a complicated multi-stage setup or many new hyperparameters. Our first claim is that online distillation enables us to use extra parallelism to fit very large datasets about twice as fast. Crucially, we can still speed up training even after we have already reached the point at which additional parallelism provides no benefit for synchronous or asynchronous stochastic gradient descent. Two neural networks trained on disjoint subsets of the data can share knowledge by encouraging each model to agree with the predictions the other model would have made. These predictions can come from a stale version of the other model so they can be safely computed using weights that only rarely get transmitted. Our second claim is that online distillation is a cost-effective way to make the exact predictions of a model dramatically more reproducible. We support our claims using experiments on the Criteo Display Ad Challenge dataset, ImageNet, and the largest to-date dataset used for neural language modeling, containing $6\times 10^{11}$ tokens and based on the Common Crawl repository of web data.

papers_seen.author: Gibson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression methods transfer predictive behavior and internal representations from larger or more informed teacher models into smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained students. These methods are applied to reduce latency and memory, enable deployment on heterogeneous or private devices, and to retain teacher performance through tailored losses, intermediate-feature matching, multi-stage pipelines, and combinations with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Empirical work shows KD succeeds across modalities (language, vision, multimodal, and generative models) when design choices — what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and which data to use — are matched to the task and constraints. Ongoing challenges include distilling rare-token behaviors, handling severe data heterogeneity, ensuring privacy and fairness, and automating student architecture design.

papers_seen.author: Morgan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: The Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile technique for turning large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable ones. By transferring richer supervision than hard labels—soft outputs, intermediate representations, or relational signals—KD reduces inference cost while preserving much of teacher behavior. KD is not a single recipe but a flexible toolbox: its success depends on teacher design, the choice of distilled signal, data availability, and combination with complementary compression methods. When matched to task and deployment constraints, KD enables real-world use of pretrained models across vision, language, speech, graphs, and structured prediction, while open challenges remain around distribution shift, rare-token fidelity, and privacy-sensitive scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression techniques aim to transfer predictive capacity from large, expensive models into smaller, faster models while preserving performance. Approaches vary in what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate representations, attention maps, feature projectors), how teachers are constructed (single teacher, multi-teacher, self-teaching, or meta-learned teachers), and what resources are available (original data, public data, or no data). Practical extensions address domain-specific needs (e.g., BERT compression, low-precision deployment, privacy-preserving and federated settings) and include strategies such as progressive module replacement, multi-stage distillation, adversarially generated synthetic data, and self-supervised distillation. Empirical and theoretical work highlights both the power of soft targets as a regularizer and the importance of aligning internal representations and layer correspondences to improve student generalization.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Beyond Soft Labels: A Practical Position on Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a crucial technique for shrinking large deep models to meet real-world latency, memory and privacy constraints while retaining much of their performance. However, naive distillation that only matches teacher soft-labels is often insufficient. A more reliable strategy combines distillation of internal representations and features, task- or domain-adaptive compression, and architecture-aware search or adaptation. When applied with care — addressing optimization issues, data or privacy limits, and mismatch between teacher and student capacities — distillation enables compact, fast models that approach teacher performance across speech, NLP and vision tasks.

papers_seen.author: James
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a heuristic for compressing large models into a broadly applicable set of techniques that enable smaller, faster, and in some cases fairer or more interpretable models. Its effectiveness depends on choices about what to transfer (logits, features, structure), how to prepare training data, and how to reconcile teacher imperfections with student capacity. When these design choices are matched to the task and constraints, KD enables substantial compression with small performance loss and can address privacy and resource limitations.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Path to Compact, Deployable Deep Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, flexible set of techniques for transferring behavior from large, expensive teacher models into smaller, faster students. In deep learning and NLP, KD enables practical deployment by reducing latency, memory, and power requirements while retaining much of teacher performance. Effective application requires: (1) combining KD with domain-aware pretraining of compact models, (2) adapting distillation to data-constrained or privacy-sensitive settings, and (3) integrating architectural and optimization improvements (e.g., feature projectors, mixed-precision) to close remaining gaps. When applied thoughtfully, KD is a key tool for making state-of-the-art models useful in real-world, resource-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Mechanisms, Variants, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, more deployable students by transferring information beyond hard labels. Across modalities and settings, KD methods range from matching teacher soft targets (logits) to aligning intermediate representations, combining multiple teachers, synthesizing training data when originals are unavailable, and integrating with other compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Practical distillation must balance student capacity, the form of transferred knowledge, data availability and privacy constraints, and optimization strategies to produce compact models that preserve accuracy, robustness, and deployment requirements.

papers_seen.author: Velasquez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Context-Sensitive Argument
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, deployment-oriented approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, efficient students. When applied with careful choices about what to transfer (logits, features, attention), how to align teacher and student architectures, and how to handle data and privacy constraints, KD routinely yields compact models that approach teacher performance across vision and language tasks. KD is most effective when combined with complementary techniques—feature projectors, adversarial objectives, student-aware teacher training, and privacy-preserving mechanisms—so that compressed models meet real-world latency, robustness, and deployment requirements.

papers_seen.author: Jackson
papers_seen.title: Online Knowledge Distillation via Mutual Contrastive Learning for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: The teacher-free online Knowledge Distillation (KD) aims to train an ensemble of multiple student models collaboratively and distill knowledge from each other. Although existing online KD methods achieve desirable performance, they often focus on class probabilities as the core knowledge type, ignoring the valuable feature representational information. We present a Mutual Contrastive Learning (MCL) framework for online KD. The core idea of MCL is to perform mutual interaction and transfer of contrastive distributions among a cohort of networks in an online manner. Our MCL can aggregate cross-network embedding information and maximize the lower bound to the mutual information between two networks. This enables each network to learn extra contrastive knowledge from others, leading to better feature representations, thus improving the performance of visual recognition tasks. Beyond the final layer, we extend MCL to intermediate layers and perform an adaptive layer-matching mechanism trained by meta-optimization. Experiments on image classification and transfer learning to visual recognition tasks show that layer-wise MCL can lead to consistent performance gains against state-of-the-art online KD approaches. The superiority demonstrates that layer-wise MCL can guide the network to generate better feature representations. Our code is publicly avaliable at https://github.com/winycg/L-MCL.

papers_seen.author: Cannon
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression aim to transfer knowledge from large or ensemble teacher models to smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained student models while preserving predictive performance. Approaches span soft-label imitation, intermediate feature matching, architecture-aware compression, data-centric augmentations, online and distributed schemes, and teacher-design strategies. Applications include NLP (BERT compression and task-specific distillation), speech recognition, graph neural networks, and vision tasks. Empirical results across benchmarks show that carefully chosen distillation objectives, alignment mechanisms, and data strategies can yield compact models that approach teacher performance while enabling substantial speed and memory gains. Open challenges remain in automating architecture search for compression, preserving robustness and domain generalization, and scaling distillation to very large datasets and model families.

papers_seen.author: Mason
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression strategies have become core methods for deploying large deep models in resource-constrained settings. Across vision, speech, and language tasks, practitioners compress models by transferring teacher behavior to smaller students, by architectural replacement, or by searching for task-specific compact architectures. Techniques differ in what is transferred (logits, intermediate representations, inter-class relations), how training data are used (original data, distilled targets, or synthetic data), and how robustness and task-specificity are preserved. Empirical work shows strong trade-offs between model size, runtime, and task performance; recent advances focus on task-adaptive compression, improved layer-mapping, data-free approaches, and preserving robustness under adversarial or distributional shifts. Important open challenges remain in handling domain shift, low-frequency phenomena, heterogeneous teacher ensembles, and reliable data-free distillation.

papers_seen.author: Lin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, faster student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. KD is applied across modalities and deployment contexts to reduce inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance. Practical KD pipelines combine choice of distillation target, teacher and student preparation, data strategies, and complementary compression methods to meet constraints such as latency, memory, privacy, and domain shift. While KD is highly effective in many settings, it has known limits—capacity mismatch, distributional heterogeneity, and transferred biases—that require careful method and evaluation design.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Variants, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses or transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller students by providing richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. Across vision, speech, graph, and language tasks, KD appears to work through a mix of mechanisms — soft targets acting as regularizers, matching intermediate representations, and reducing effective data complexity — and can be combined with data augmentation, privacy-preserving noise, and architecture-aware projectors. Practical research highlights trade-offs related to teacher quality, which samples to transfer, robustness, and device heterogeneity; current methods address these by selective sample transfer, contrastive or feature-level alignment, adversarial objectives, and pre-training compact students before distillation. Key open directions include principled selection of distilled samples, theoretical characterization of when distilled soft targets help versus hurt, and integrating KD with pruning and other compression approaches for deployment on constrained devices.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Rejuvenating Low-Frequency Words: Making the Most of Parallel Data in Non-Autoregressive Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is commonly used to construct synthetic data for training non-autoregressive translation (NAT) models. However, there exists a discrepancy on low-frequency words between the distilled and the original data, leading to more errors on predicting low-frequency words. To alleviate the problem, we directly expose the raw data into NAT by leveraging pretraining. By analyzing directed alignments, we found that KD makes low-frequency source words aligned with targets more deterministically but fails to align sufficient low-frequency words from target to source. Accordingly, we propose reverse KD to rejuvenate more alignments for low-frequency target words. To make the most of authentic and synthetic data, we combine these complementary approaches as a new training strategy for further boosting NAT performance. We conduct experiments on five translation benchmarks over two advanced architectures. Results demonstrate that the proposed approach can significantly and universally improve translation quality by reducing translation errors on low-frequency words. Encouragingly, our approach achieves 28.2 and 33.9 BLEU points on the WMT14 English-German and WMT16 Romanian-English datasets, respectively. Our code, data, and trained models are available at \url{https://github.com/alphadl/RLFW-NAT}.

papers_seen.author: Roman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Tool for Practical Model Compression in NLP and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-purpose strategy for compressing large deep models while preserving performance. KD can be adapted to constraints common in NLP deployment—limited compute, privacy restrictions, low-latency requirements, and robustness demands—by pairing standard teacher-student training with techniques such as feature-level matching, data augmentation, multi-teacher supervision, and teacher adaptation. Across domains (transformers for NLP, speech embeddings, graph models, generative models), KD consistently enables large reductions in model size or latency with modest accuracy loss, making it a primary method for productionization of deep models.

papers_seen.author: Tucker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Efficient and Responsible NLP and Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical, versatile approach for compressing large models and enabling deployment in resource-constrained environments. Beyond raw compression, KD supports domain adaptation, data-free scenarios, improved inference speed, and novel training regimes for specialized tasks. However, distillation is not a panacea: it can amplify teacher biases, interact with regularization techniques in subtle ways, and benefits most when combined with complementary methods such as architecture-aware training, generator-based sample synthesis, or instance-aware losses.

papers_seen.author: Cohen
papers_seen.title: ALP-KD: Attention-Based Layer Projection for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is considered as a training and compression strategy in which two neural networks, namely a teacher and a student, are coupled together during training. The teacher network is supposed to be a trustworthy predictor and the student tries to mimic its predictions. Usually, a student with a lighter architecture is selected so we can achieve compression and yet deliver high-quality results. In such a setting, distillation only happens for final predictions whereas the student could also benefit from teacher's supervision for internal components.   Motivated by this, we studied the problem of distillation for intermediate layers. Since there might not be a one-to-one alignment between student and teacher layers, existing techniques skip some teacher layers and only distill from a subset of them. This shortcoming directly impacts quality, so we instead propose a combinatorial technique which relies on attention. Our model fuses teacher-side information and takes each layer's significance into consideration, then performs distillation between combined teacher layers and those of the student. Using our technique, we distilled a 12-layer BERT (Devlin et al. 2019) into 6-, 4-, and 2-layer counterparts and evaluated them on GLUE tasks (Wang et al. 2018). Experimental results show that our combinatorial approach is able to outperform other existing techniques.

papers_seen.author: Kidd
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable approach for compressing large deep learning models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students. Modern KD goes beyond matching logits: it includes feature- and representation-level transfers, multi-teacher and self-distillation strategies, and workflows that integrate augmentation, data-free synthesis, pruning, and quantization to meet latency, memory, and privacy requirements. Practical success depends on matching distillation technique to deployment objectives, careful design of layer mappings and loss terms, attention to teacher quality and data availability, and combinations with other compression tools to preserve robustness and generalization.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques transfer knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models to reduce computation, memory, and latency while preserving performance. Research has developed multiple distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, and relational signals), architectural and optimization strategies (projectors, multi-teacher weighting, student-friendly teacher training), and workflows for constrained scenarios (data-free distillation, federated or black-box settings, and task-adaptive compression). Empirical and theoretical work highlights when distillation succeeds, the key role of representation alignment, and persistent challenges such as data heterogeneity, low-frequency token behavior in sequence models, and designing teacher signals that the student can effectively absorb.

papers_seen.author: Rhodes
papers_seen.title: Lifelong Language Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: It is challenging to perform lifelong language learning (LLL) on a stream of different tasks without any performance degradation comparing to the multi-task counterparts. To address this issue, we present Lifelong Language Knowledge Distillation (L2KD), a simple but efficient method that can be easily applied to existing LLL architectures in order to mitigate the degradation. Specifically, when the LLL model is trained on a new task, we assign a teacher model to first learn the new task, and pass the knowledge to the LLL model via knowledge distillation. Therefore, the LLL model can better adapt to the new task while keeping the previously learned knowledge. Experiments show that the proposed L2KD consistently improves previous state-of-the-art models, and the degradation comparing to multi-task models in LLL tasks is well mitigated for both sequence generation and text classification tasks.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models by transferring information from a high-capacity teacher to a smaller student so the student retains much of the teacher’s predictive power while using less compute, memory, or latency. The literature has expanded KD beyond matching teacher soft-labels to include intermediate-feature and layer-wise matching, online/self-distillation, data-free and privacy-aware methods, and combinations with architectural compression (pruning, quantization, and architecture search). Empirical results across vision, NLP, speech, graphs, and ranking show that distilled students often recover a large fraction of teacher performance, but practical success depends on choices like teacher design, student capacity, layer alignment, data availability, and training schedules. Remaining challenges include handling low-frequency or fine-grained behaviors, optimization and capacity mismatch, matching heterogeneous architectures, and distilling under privacy or data-scarce constraints.

papers_seen.author: Roberts
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Cornerstone for Compressing Deep Models in NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic and broadly applicable strategy for compressing large deep models so they can be deployed under real-world constraints. By transferring predictive behavior or intermediate representations from a high-capacity teacher to a smaller student, KD enables substantial reductions in model size and latency while preserving much of the original performance. When combined with architectural replacements, meta-learning, or task-aware layer matching, KD can be adapted to diverse settings (on-device inference, federated systems, data-scarce environments) and modalities. However, its effectiveness depends on choices such as which signals to transfer, how to handle imperfect teachers, and how to preserve rare or low-frequency behaviors; addressing these challenges is necessary for robust practical adoption.

papers_seen.author: Pacheco
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation with Adversarial Samples Supporting Decision Boundary
papers_seen.abstract: Many recent works on knowledge distillation have provided ways to transfer the knowledge of a trained network for improving the learning process of a new one, but finding a good technique for knowledge distillation is still an open problem. In this paper, we provide a new perspective based on a decision boundary, which is one of the most important component of a classifier. The generalization performance of a classifier is closely related to the adequacy of its decision boundary, so a good classifier bears a good decision boundary. Therefore, transferring information closely related to the decision boundary can be a good attempt for knowledge distillation. To realize this goal, we utilize an adversarial attack to discover samples supporting a decision boundary. Based on this idea, to transfer more accurate information about the decision boundary, the proposed algorithm trains a student classifier based on the adversarial samples supporting the decision boundary. Experiments show that the proposed method indeed improves knowledge distillation and achieves the state-of-the-arts performance.

papers_seen.author: Moran
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of methods for transferring predictive capacity from larger teacher models into smaller, more efficient students so models can be deployed under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. Research over the past decade has expanded simple logit-matching into a rich set of variants—feature and layer alignment, progressive module replacement, self-distillation, data-free synthesis, and privacy-aware ensembles—making KD a cornerstone of modern model-compression toolkits.

papers_seen.author: Powers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a flexible, deployment-oriented family of techniques that transfer information from larger or multiple teachers into smaller students. KD can be applied at the level of logits, intermediate representations, or task-specific modules and is readily combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data-synthesis methods to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. While KD often preserves much of a teacher's performance in compressed models, realizing its benefits in NLP requires careful choices about what signals to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, and how to mitigate optimization and data-shift issues. With thoughtful protocol design, KD enables wide deployment of powerful language models under realistic resource limits, but it remains important to pair distillation with representation-aware objectives and engineering practices to avoid degrading rare-token behavior or amplifying teacher artifacts.

papers_seen.author: Byrd
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Complementary Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. KD can preserve much of teacher performance while reducing inference cost, but it is not a standalone solution: its best results arise when combined with task-aware layer alignment, data strategies (augmentation or synthesis), architecture-aware compression, and careful teacher design. This position argues KD should be treated as the core of compression pipelines while acknowledging its failure modes and articulating practical mitigations.

papers_seen.author: Walton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential, Practical Strategy for Compressing Deep Models in NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques are indispensable for deploying high-capacity deep and language models in resource-constrained settings. By transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teachers to smaller students, practitioners can achieve large reductions in model size and latency while retaining most task performance. However, realizing these gains reliably requires attention to what is transferred (logits, features, relations), how teachers and data are chosen, and hardware- or deployment-aware compression strategies.

papers_seen.author: Lopez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical Core Tool with Clear Limits and Complementary Needs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely used approach to compressing large deep and language models into smaller, faster students suitable for deployment. KD reliably reduces inference cost and model size while often preserving much of teacher performance, but success depends on what is transferred, how the student is initialized and trained, and how data and robustness constraints are handled. Effective compression therefore treats KD as one component in a pipeline that includes pre-training of compact architectures, architecture-aware alignment or progressive replacement, and data strategies (including data-free or synthesized data) to meet privacy and domain needs.

papers_seen.author: Hickman
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques aim to transfer the predictive power of large, expensive models into smaller, faster models while retaining performance. Approaches vary from matching teacher outputs (soft labels) to aligning intermediate representations, leveraging data augmentation or synthesized data when real data are limited, and jointly optimizing architecture and distillation losses for task-adaptive compression. Advances address student–teacher capacity gaps, multi-teacher transfer, and domain or data scarcity; remaining challenges include transferring internal structure efficiently, generalization under distribution shifts, and designing teacher models that are optimized for downstream distillation.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: Understanding Knowledge Distillation in Non-autoregressive Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Non-autoregressive machine translation (NAT) systems predict a sequence of output tokens in parallel, achieving substantial improvements in generation speed compared to autoregressive models. Existing NAT models usually rely on the technique of knowledge distillation, which creates the training data from a pretrained autoregressive model for better performance. Knowledge distillation is empirically useful, leading to large gains in accuracy for NAT models, but the reason for this success has, as of yet, been unclear. In this paper, we first design systematic experiments to investigate why knowledge distillation is crucial to NAT training. We find that knowledge distillation can reduce the complexity of data sets and help NAT to model the variations in the output data. Furthermore, a strong correlation is observed between the capacity of an NAT model and the optimal complexity of the distilled data for the best translation quality. Based on these findings, we further propose several approaches that can alter the complexity of data sets to improve the performance of NAT models. We achieve the state-of-the-art performance for the NAT-based models, and close the gap with the autoregressive baseline on WMT14 En-De benchmark.

papers_seen.author: Jordan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Across vision and language tasks, KD transfers information from teachers to students using softened outputs, intermediate representations, or auxiliary signals; it is commonly combined with data augmentation, architecture adaptation, and privacy-preserving or data-free procedures. When applied with care to teacher signals, data selection, and student capacity, KD enables large reductions in size and latency while retaining much of a teacher’s performance, but meaningful limitations remain (optimization difficulty, capacity mismatch, and potential transfer of biases) that must be managed in deployment.

papers_seen.author: Walter
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression methods reduce the computational and memory cost of large neural models by transferring information from larger or ensemble teachers to smaller students. Approaches vary from using soft logits to matching internal representations, attention maps, or generator outputs; they have been adapted for modality transfer, privacy- or bandwidth-constrained settings, and specialized architectures (e.g., transformers, GANs). Empirical work shows that representation-level objectives, architectural design of the student/bridge modules, and careful training protocols can preserve most of the teacher’s performance while dramatically reducing size and runtime. Ongoing challenges include preserving rare-token or fine-grained behaviors, deploying under strict privacy/bandwidth constraints, and automating architecture search for compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Rios
papers_seen.title: Improving Neural Topic Models using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Topic models are often used to identify human-interpretable topics to help make sense of large document collections. We use knowledge distillation to combine the best attributes of probabilistic topic models and pretrained transformers. Our modular method can be straightforwardly applied with any neural topic model to improve topic quality, which we demonstrate using two models having disparate architectures, obtaining state-of-the-art topic coherence. We show that our adaptable framework not only improves performance in the aggregate over all estimated topics, as is commonly reported, but also in head-to-head comparisons of aligned topics.

papers_seen.author: Alvarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Challenges, and Trends
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques aim to produce smaller, faster models that retain much of the predictive power of larger teachers. Across modalities (vision, language, speech, graphs, and generation), practitioners balance trade-offs among accuracy, efficiency, data availability, privacy, and fairness. Recent work extends classical logits-based distillation with feature- and layer-level objectives, projector modules, adversarial data generation for data-free settings, multi-teacher and meta-learned teachers, and privacy-aware perturbations. Empirical and theoretical analyses highlight both practical gains and persistent issues—optimization barriers that prevent perfect teacher matching, data-mismatch effects, and modality-specific alignment problems—guiding current best practices for deploying distilled models in resource- and privacy-constrained scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Ortiz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Context-Sensitive Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic strategy for compressing large deep and NLP models into compact, deployable students. Rather than a single recipe, KD functions as a toolbox: it can transfer softened outputs, intermediate representations, attention maps, or relational signals; be combined with architecture search, pruning, or quantization; and operate with or without original training data. KD delivers substantial reductions in size and latency with modest performance loss when methods and signals are chosen to match student capacity, task requirements, and deployment constraints. However, KD is context-sensitive: success depends on handling teacher–student mismatch, robustness and fairness concerns, data availability, and optimization choices. The most reliable pipelines therefore combine multiple distillation signals, data-aware strategies, and targeted remedies for limits such as bias transfer and rare-token degradation.

papers_seen.author: Wise
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, production-ready approach for compressing large models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students. KD supports multiple transfer signals (logits, features, attention or relational structure), composes with other compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search), and can be adapted to domain- or data-constrained settings. Its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints; therefore KD should be treated as a toolbox of methods and workflows rather than a single recipe.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Insights
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques enable deployment of large deep models by transferring knowledge to smaller, faster, or lower-precision models. Existing work spans pre-training compact models, teacher-to-student soft-target transfer, data-free and teacher-free approaches, self-distillation, architecture- and task-specific adaptations, and combinations with quantization or pruning. Empirical results show that distilled students can approach teacher performance across classification, ranking, speech, and generation tasks, while specialized strategies address limited task data, privacy constraints, and heterogeneous deployment settings. Open challenges include handling domain shift, designing teacher-student curricula, and developing universally effective objectives for diverse architectures and tasks.

papers_seen.author: Doyle
papers_seen.title: DE-RRD: A Knowledge Distillation Framework for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: Recent recommender systems have started to employ knowledge distillation, which is a model compression technique distilling knowledge from a cumbersome model (teacher) to a compact model (student), to reduce inference latency while maintaining performance. The state-of-the-art methods have only focused on making the student model accurately imitate the predictions of the teacher model. They have a limitation in that the prediction results incompletely reveal the teacher's knowledge. In this paper, we propose a novel knowledge distillation framework for recommender system, called DE-RRD, which enables the student model to learn from the latent knowledge encoded in the teacher model as well as from the teacher's predictions. Concretely, DE-RRD consists of two methods: 1) Distillation Experts (DE) that directly transfers the latent knowledge from the teacher model. DE exploits "experts" and a novel expert selection strategy for effectively distilling the vast teacher's knowledge to the student with limited capacity. 2) Relaxed Ranking Distillation (RRD) that transfers the knowledge revealed from the teacher's prediction with consideration of the relaxed ranking orders among items. Our extensive experiments show that DE-RRD outperforms the state-of-the-art competitors and achieves comparable or even better performance to that of the teacher model with faster inference time.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Ensemble Distillation for Neural Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation describes a method for training a student network to perform better by learning from a stronger teacher network. Translating a sentence with an Neural Machine Translation (NMT) engine is time expensive and having a smaller model speeds up this process. We demonstrate how to transfer the translation quality of an ensemble and an oracle BLEU teacher network into a single NMT system. Further, we present translation improvements from a teacher network that has the same architecture and dimensions of the student network. As the training of the student model is still expensive, we introduce a data filtering method based on the knowledge of the teacher model that not only speeds up the training, but also leads to better translation quality. Our techniques need no code change and can be easily reproduced with any NMT architecture to speed up the decoding process.

papers_seen.author: Rios
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques transform large, high-performing models into smaller or more usable forms while attempting to retain performance. Methods range from transferring soft targets to matching intermediate representations, to data-free and federated protocols that address privacy and communication constraints. These approaches have been applied across computer vision, speech, and natural language tasks and are used both for deployment efficiency and for secondary goals such as interpretability or domain generalization.

papers_seen.author: Welch
papers_seen.title: Distillation as Default: A Practical Position on Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a necessary and practical core technique for compressing large deep models into deployable, efficient students. When combined with representation-level matching, careful pre-training of compact students, and attention to privacy and deployment constraints, KD preserves much of teacher performance while enabling low-latency, on-device, and federated use. However, naive soft-label matching is insufficient: best practice integrates intermediate-feature supervision, data- and architecture-aware pipelines, and multi-stage or multi-teacher strategies to handle domain shift, rare phenomena, and heterogeneous architectures.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Context-Sensitive Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and widely applicable method for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search, or data augmentation), and when adapted to task and data constraints, KD enables large reductions in size and latency while retaining much of a teacher's performance. At the same time, KD’s success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how teachers and students are matched, and how to handle domain shift or limited data.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core of Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practical approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a flexible toolbox rather than a single recipe, KD enables retention of teacher capabilities across modalities and tasks by transferring logits, intermediate representations, attention patterns, or relational signals. Effective deployment requires matching distillation targets to student capacity, addressing data availability or privacy limits, and combining KD with complementary compression methods such as pruning or architecture search. This paper argues that KD should be the central component of modern compression pipelines and outlines practical principles to maximize its benefits and mitigate common failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques transfer information from larger, ensemble, or otherwise expensive teacher models into smaller, cheaper student models so that deployed systems meet latency, memory, and power constraints while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. Over the past decade researchers have developed a family of approaches — soft-target matching, intermediate representation and relation matching, online and self-distillation, curriculum and data-aware strategies, and combinations with pruning/quantization or architecture search — that together form a practical toolkit for compressing models used in vision and language tasks. Empirical work shows KD can produce dramatic inference-speed and memory gains with modest accuracy loss when methods are chosen to match task, data, and deployment constraints; important open problems remain around optimization mismatches, robustness to distribution shift, and how best to distill under limited or sensitive data conditions.
