papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing neural models by transferring information from a teacher to a smaller student so the student preserves much of the teacher’s behavior while using less compute, memory, or latency. The literature shows a family of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention or relational signals), multiple training regimes (offline, online/self-distillation, data-free), and many practical integrations (pre-training compact students, combining with pruning/quantization, and curriculum or data selection). Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, availability and selection of data, and deployment constraints; remaining challenges include capacity/optimization mismatch, preserving rare or fine-grained behaviors, and distillation under privacy or data-scarce settings.

papers_seen.author: Cochran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses high-capacity models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure. A broad family of KD methods—ranging from matching softened output distributions to aligning intermediate representations, attention patterns, or relational signals—enables practitioners to trade model size and latency for retained performance. In practice, KD is combined with data-aware strategies, teacher adaptation, and complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to meet deployment constraints. While KD is effective across vision and language tasks, success depends on careful choices about distilled signals, student capacity, data availability, and handling of domain shifts or low-frequency behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Maldonado
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge by Mimicking Features
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a popular method to train efficient networks ("student") with the help of high-capacity networks ("teacher"). Traditional methods use the teacher's soft logits as extra supervision to train the student network. In this paper, we argue that it is more advantageous to make the student mimic the teacher's features in the penultimate layer. Not only the student can directly learn more effective information from the teacher feature, feature mimicking can also be applied for teachers trained without a softmax layer. Experiments show that it can achieve higher accuracy than traditional KD. To further facilitate feature mimicking, we decompose a feature vector into the magnitude and the direction. We argue that the teacher should give more freedom to the student feature's magnitude, and let the student pay more attention on mimicking the feature direction. To meet this requirement, we propose a loss term based on locality-sensitive hashing (LSH). With the help of this new loss, our method indeed mimics feature directions more accurately, relaxes constraints on feature magnitudes, and achieves state-of-the-art distillation accuracy. We provide theoretical analyses of how LSH facilitates feature direction mimicking, and further extend feature mimicking to multi-label recognition and object detection.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Compressing Visual-linguistic Model via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite exciting progress in pre-training for visual-linguistic (VL) representations, very few aspire to a small VL model. In this paper, we study knowledge distillation (KD) to effectively compress a transformer-based large VL model into a small VL model. The major challenge arises from the inconsistent regional visual tokens extracted from different detectors of Teacher and Student, resulting in the misalignment of hidden representations and attention distributions. To address the problem, we retrain and adapt the Teacher by using the same region proposals from Student's detector while the features are from Teacher's own object detector. With aligned network inputs, the adapted Teacher is capable of transferring the knowledge through the intermediate representations. Specifically, we use the mean square error loss to mimic the attention distribution inside the transformer block and present a token-wise noise contrastive loss to align the hidden state by contrasting with negative representations stored in a sample queue. To this end, we show that our proposed distillation significantly improves the performance of small VL models on image captioning and visual question answering tasks. It reaches 120.8 in CIDEr score on COCO captioning, an improvement of 5.1 over its non-distilled counterpart; and an accuracy of 69.8 on VQA 2.0, a 0.8 gain from the baseline. Our extensive experiments and ablations confirm the effectiveness of VL distillation in both pre-training and fine-tuning stages.

papers_seen.author: Galloway
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical but Context-Sensitive Path to Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly effective toolkit for compressing large deep models into smaller, faster students for deployment in resource-constrained settings. KD methods span matching output distributions, aligning internal representations, synthesizing surrogate data when originals are unavailable, and co-designing compact architectures for target tasks. While KD often preserves much of a teacher’s performance and enables trade-offs among accuracy, latency, and memory, success depends on the distillation signal, data regime, robustness and privacy needs, and architecture alignment between teacher and student.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Highlight Every Step: Knowledge Distillation via Collaborative Teaching
papers_seen.abstract: High storage and computational costs obstruct deep neural networks to be deployed on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation aims to train a compact student network by transferring knowledge from a larger pre-trained teacher model. However, most existing methods on knowledge distillation ignore the valuable information among training process associated with training results. In this paper, we provide a new Collaborative Teaching Knowledge Distillation (CTKD) strategy which employs two special teachers. Specifically, one teacher trained from scratch (i.e., scratch teacher) assists the student step by step using its temporary outputs. It forces the student to approach the optimal path towards the final logits with high accuracy. The other pre-trained teacher (i.e., expert teacher) guides the student to focus on a critical region which is more useful for the task. The combination of the knowledge from two special teachers can significantly improve the performance of the student network in knowledge distillation. The results of experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, SVHN and Tiny ImageNet datasets verify that the proposed knowledge distillation method is efficient and achieves state-of-the-art performance.

papers_seen.author: Zamora
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, cheaper students by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations. The family of KD methods includes soft-target (logit) matching, feature- and layer-wise alignment, relational and module-level transfer, data-free or zero-shot synthesis, and integration with architecture search or federated training. Practical deployments balance what is transferred with student capacity, data availability, privacy constraints, and device heterogeneity; empirical work shows KD often preserves much of teacher performance while enabling lower latency, smaller models, and domain specialization, but open challenges remain around robustness, domain shift, and principled selection of distilled signals.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a practical cornerstone for compressing large deep models into deployable, lower-latency students while retaining much of their predictive capacity. KD methods span simple soft-target matching to feature- and layer-level transfer, and they can operate in constrained settings (limited data, heterogeneous architectures, cross-modal scenarios). However, the effectiveness of KD depends on what is transferred, how teachers and students are matched, and how KD is combined with complementary compression strategies. Careful design—addressing teacher errors, domain shift, data availability, and architecture mismatch—yields compact models that meet real deployment constraints without disproportionate loss in quality.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Collaborative Distillation for Ultra-Resolution Universal Style Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Universal style transfer methods typically leverage rich representations from deep Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models (e.g., VGG-19) pre-trained on large collections of images. Despite the effectiveness, its application is heavily constrained by the large model size to handle ultra-resolution images given limited memory. In this work, we present a new knowledge distillation method (named Collaborative Distillation) for encoder-decoder based neural style transfer to reduce the convolutional filters. The main idea is underpinned by a finding that the encoder-decoder pairs construct an exclusive collaborative relationship, which is regarded as a new kind of knowledge for style transfer models. Moreover, to overcome the feature size mismatch when applying collaborative distillation, a linear embedding loss is introduced to drive the student network to learn a linear embedding of the teacher's features. Extensive experiments show the effectiveness of our method when applied to different universal style transfer approaches (WCT and AdaIN), even if the model size is reduced by 15.5 times. Especially, on WCT with the compressed models, we achieve ultra-resolution (over 40 megapixels) universal style transfer on a 12GB GPU for the first time. Further experiments on optimization-based stylization scheme show the generality of our algorithm on different stylization paradigms. Our code and trained models are available at https://github.com/mingsun-tse/collaborative-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Mckay
papers_seen.title: MixKD: Towards Efficient Distillation of Large-scale Language Models
papers_seen.abstract: Large-scale language models have recently demonstrated impressive empirical performance. Nevertheless, the improved results are attained at the price of bigger models, more power consumption, and slower inference, which hinder their applicability to low-resource (both memory and computation) platforms. Knowledge distillation (KD) has been demonstrated as an effective framework for compressing such big models. However, large-scale neural network systems are prone to memorize training instances, and thus tend to make inconsistent predictions when the data distribution is altered slightly. Moreover, the student model has few opportunities to request useful information from the teacher model when there is limited task-specific data available. To address these issues, we propose MixKD, a data-agnostic distillation framework that leverages mixup, a simple yet efficient data augmentation approach, to endow the resulting model with stronger generalization ability. Concretely, in addition to the original training examples, the student model is encouraged to mimic the teacher's behavior on the linear interpolation of example pairs as well. We prove from a theoretical perspective that under reasonable conditions MixKD gives rise to a smaller gap between the generalization error and the empirical error. To verify its effectiveness, we conduct experiments on the GLUE benchmark, where MixKD consistently leads to significant gains over the standard KD training, and outperforms several competitive baselines. Experiments under a limited-data setting and ablation studies further demonstrate the advantages of the proposed approach.

papers_seen.author: Pacheco
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation with Adversarial Samples Supporting Decision Boundary
papers_seen.abstract: Many recent works on knowledge distillation have provided ways to transfer the knowledge of a trained network for improving the learning process of a new one, but finding a good technique for knowledge distillation is still an open problem. In this paper, we provide a new perspective based on a decision boundary, which is one of the most important component of a classifier. The generalization performance of a classifier is closely related to the adequacy of its decision boundary, so a good classifier bears a good decision boundary. Therefore, transferring information closely related to the decision boundary can be a good attempt for knowledge distillation. To realize this goal, we utilize an adversarial attack to discover samples supporting a decision boundary. Based on this idea, to transfer more accurate information about the decision boundary, the proposed algorithm trains a student classifier based on the adversarial samples supporting the decision boundary. Experiments show that the proposed method indeed improves knowledge distillation and achieves the state-of-the-arts performance.

papers_seen.author: Rios
papers_seen.title: Improving Neural Topic Models using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Topic models are often used to identify human-interpretable topics to help make sense of large document collections. We use knowledge distillation to combine the best attributes of probabilistic topic models and pretrained transformers. Our modular method can be straightforwardly applied with any neural topic model to improve topic quality, which we demonstrate using two models having disparate architectures, obtaining state-of-the-art topic coherence. We show that our adaptable framework not only improves performance in the aggregate over all estimated topics, as is commonly reported, but also in head-to-head comparisons of aligned topics.

papers_seen.author: Byrd
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Complementary Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. KD can preserve much of teacher performance while reducing inference cost, but it is not a standalone solution: its best results arise when combined with task-aware layer alignment, data strategies (augmentation or synthesis), architecture-aware compression, and careful teacher design. This position argues KD should be treated as the core of compression pipelines while acknowledging its failure modes and articulating practical mitigations.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: A Deep Hierarchical Approach to Lifelong Learning in Minecraft
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a lifelong learning system that has the ability to reuse and transfer knowledge from one task to another while efficiently retaining the previously learned knowledge-base. Knowledge is transferred by learning reusable skills to solve tasks in Minecraft, a popular video game which is an unsolved and high-dimensional lifelong learning problem. These reusable skills, which we refer to as Deep Skill Networks, are then incorporated into our novel Hierarchical Deep Reinforcement Learning Network (H-DRLN) architecture using two techniques: (1) a deep skill array and (2) skill distillation, our novel variation of policy distillation (Rusu et. al. 2015) for learning skills. Skill distillation enables the HDRLN to efficiently retain knowledge and therefore scale in lifelong learning, by accumulating knowledge and encapsulating multiple reusable skills into a single distilled network. The H-DRLN exhibits superior performance and lower learning sample complexity compared to the regular Deep Q Network (Mnih et. al. 2015) in sub-domains of Minecraft.

papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: Effective Knowledge Distillation: Representation, Selection, and Practical Constraints
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach to compress and adapt large deep models for deployment in resource- or privacy-constrained settings. Effective distillation goes beyond matching teacher logits: transferring internal representations, choosing which teacher signals to trust, and accommodating deployment constraints (limited data, communication, low-precision hardware) are all decisive. I argue that the most reliable distillation pipelines combine representation-level objectives, selective/sample-aware strategies, and engineering choices that address privacy and efficiency, yielding compact students that retain teacher strengths across NLP, vision, and graph domains.

papers_seen.author: Cherry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Practical Recipes, and Open Issues
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, faster student models by transferring information beyond hard labels. Across modalities and tasks, KD methods include soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate feature or attention alignment, layer-mapping strategies, and combined pipelines that integrate pruning, quantization, or architecture-aware design. Empirically, KD routinely improves compact models relative to training from scratch and enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, but success depends on student capacity, the choice of distilled signals, data availability and quality, and careful alignment of teacher and student architectures. Ongoing challenges include robustly preserving teacher properties (robustness, fairness), operating under data scarcity or privacy limits, and automating architecture and signal selection for effective transfer.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Unifying Paradigm for Compression, Adaptation, and Robust Training
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be considered not merely as a compression trick but as a general and practical training paradigm. Across modalities and tasks, KD transfers information about function, structure, and uncertainty from one model (or ensemble) to another, enabling smaller, faster, or more adaptable models while improving generalization, interpretability, and domain transfer. Success depends on how teacher knowledge is selected, represented, and combined with data-side techniques; thoughtful design choices (layer mapping, sample selection, augmentation, and teacher trust) determine whether KD yields compression, robustness, or better task-specific performance.

papers_seen.author: Novak
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Strategy for Compressing NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, production-ready approach that enables compact models to inherit much of the performance of large teachers while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. When applied thoughtfully—using representation-level targets, projector layers, multi-teacher or curriculum schedules, and data-aware workflows—KD consistently outperforms training small models from scratch for many NLP tasks. However, KD is not a panacea: mismatches in capacity, teacher imperfections, data heterogeneity, and distributional shifts require targeted remedies and careful evaluation. This essay argues that KD should be treated as the practical core of model compression in deep learning and NLP, paired with specific design choices to mitigate its limits.

papers_seen.author: Hensley
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques form a broadly applicable toolkit for transferring capability from large, expensive teacher models to smaller, faster, or more privacy-friendly student models. Methods range from transferring softened output distributions to aligning intermediate representations, using synthetic or augmented data when original data are unavailable, and combining distillation with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search). KD is used both as a deployment-oriented compression strategy and as a general training paradigm that can improve regularization, robustness, and domain adaptation. Practical success requires careful matching of distillation objectives, teacher-student alignment, and data strategies; persistent challenges include theoretical understanding of when distillation helps, preserving rare-token behavior in NLP, and avoiding artifacts introduced by synthetic data.

papers_seen.author: Harmon
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, more deployable students by transferring information beyond hard labels. Over the past decade KD has evolved from simple soft-target (logit) matching to a broad toolkit that includes internal representation alignment, self-distillation, multi-teacher and data-free methods, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Practical distillation success depends on aligning transferred signals to student capacity, handling data and privacy constraints, and designing optimization and evaluation protocols that preserve accuracy and robustness in deployment settings.

papers_seen.author: Hensley
papers_seen.title: Apprentice: Using Knowledge Distillation Techniques To Improve Low-Precision Network Accuracy
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning networks have achieved state-of-the-art accuracies on computer vision workloads like image classification and object detection. The performant systems, however, typically involve big models with numerous parameters. Once trained, a challenging aspect for such top performing models is deployment on resource constrained inference systems - the models (often deep networks or wide networks or both) are compute and memory intensive. Low-precision numerics and model compression using knowledge distillation are popular techniques to lower both the compute requirements and memory footprint of these deployed models. In this paper, we study the combination of these two techniques and show that the performance of low-precision networks can be significantly improved by using knowledge distillation techniques. Our approach, Apprentice, achieves state-of-the-art accuracies using ternary precision and 4-bit precision for variants of ResNet architecture on ImageNet dataset. We present three schemes using which one can apply knowledge distillation techniques to various stages of the train-and-deploy pipeline.

papers_seen.author: Parsons
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Compressing NLP and Deep Learning Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a practical and flexible route to compress large neural models for real-world deployment. When applied carefully — via multi-stage pipelines, layer-aware mappings, internal-representation transfer, self-distillation, or even without original data — KD can preserve much of the teacher performance while reducing latency and memory. KD also composes effectively with orthogonal compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to meet diverse resource constraints. These properties make KD a central technique for bringing large pretrained models into production in NLP and other domains.

papers_seen.author: Maddox
papers_seen.title: BERT-EMD: Many-to-Many Layer Mapping for BERT Compression with Earth Mover's Distance
papers_seen.abstract: Pre-trained language models (e.g., BERT) have achieved significant success in various natural language processing (NLP) tasks. However, high storage and computational costs obstruct pre-trained language models to be effectively deployed on resource-constrained devices. In this paper, we propose a novel BERT distillation method based on many-to-many layer mapping, which allows each intermediate student layer to learn from any intermediate teacher layers. In this way, our model can learn from different teacher layers adaptively for various NLP tasks. %motivated by the intuition that different NLP tasks require different levels of linguistic knowledge contained in the intermediate layers of BERT. In addition, we leverage Earth Mover's Distance (EMD) to compute the minimum cumulative cost that must be paid to transform knowledge from teacher network to student network. EMD enables the effective matching for many-to-many layer mapping. %EMD can be applied to network layers with different sizes and effectively measures semantic distance between the teacher network and student network. Furthermore, we propose a cost attention mechanism to learn the layer weights used in EMD automatically, which is supposed to further improve the model's performance and accelerate convergence time. Extensive experiments on GLUE benchmark demonstrate that our model achieves competitive performance compared to strong competitors in terms of both accuracy and model compression.

papers_seen.author: Warner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Model Compression and Adaptation in NLP and Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as a central, practical technique for compressing and adapting large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD is versatile: it transfers predictive behavior, intermediate representations, and ensemble knowledge; supports data-free or privacy-sensitive settings; and can improve robustness and calibration when combined with complementary methods. Realizing KD’s full potential requires matching the distillation recipe to deployment goals and addressing failure modes such as optimization mismatches, bias transfer, and poor handling of low-frequency phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Figueroa
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly adopted family of techniques for compressing high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, or inductive biases. Across vision, language, and multimodal tasks, KD methods aim to preserve teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and compute. Practical pipelines combine distillation with architecture adaptations, data strategies, and complementary compression (pruning, quantization) and must address failure modes related to data mismatch, rare-token fidelity, teacher–student capacity gaps, and privacy or domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Pena
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, production-oriented paradigm for turning large, high-performing models into smaller, faster students suitable for deployment. Beyond pure compression, KD can act as a regularizer and a mechanism for transferring internal representations, enabling trade-offs among accuracy, latency, privacy, and robustness. Effective KD pipelines combine multiple signals (soft targets, intermediate features, attention maps), data strategies (including data-free synthesis), and deployment-aware techniques (privacy-preserving queries, architecture adaptation). I argue that KD should be treated as the central, organizing method in any practical compression workflow, but that realizing its benefits requires task-aware choices about what to transfer and how to mitigate known failure modes such as teacher–student mismatch and degraded modeling of rare phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Green
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and internal information from teacher models. Across vision, language, graph, and detection tasks, distillation techniques range from matching softened output distributions to aligning intermediate features or relational structures, and they are frequently combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) and data strategies (augmentation, synthetic-data or no-data approaches). Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, how to supply or synthesize training data, and how to mitigate capacity, distributional, and bias-related limits. Continued progress centers on principled transfer objectives, data-aware workflows, and integration with other compression primitives to produce deployable, robust compact models.

papers_seen.author: Donovan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Practical Compression: Essential, Effective, but Context-Sensitive
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students that retain much of teacher performance. KD can yield large speed, storage, and deployment gains across vision, speech, and language when combined with careful choices about what to transfer and how to train. However, success is not automatic: data regime, teacher-student mismatch, optimization dynamics, and downstream robustness or fairness constraints shape outcomes. I argue that KD should be treated as a core tool in model compression pipelines but one that must be adapted to the task, data availability, and deployment constraints through a set of best practices.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Across computer vision and NLP, practitioners use KD to reduce inference cost, enable on-device deployment, and adapt large pretrained models to constrained settings. KD techniques vary in what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, attention or relational signals), how training data are handled (real, augmented, synthesized, or none), and how teachers and students are aligned architecturally and procedurally. When design choices are matched to the task and constraints, KD enables substantial compression with modest performance loss; however, challenges remain for heterogeneous architectures, generative tasks, privacy-sensitive settings, and preserving rare-token or low-frequency behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Hall
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large models by transferring useful information from one or more teacher models to a smaller student model, enabling faster inference, lower memory use, and domain- or deployment-specific adaptation. Research has developed multiple distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational signals), teacher-management strategies (ensembles, multi-teacher weighting, teacher-training), data strategies (data-aware curricula, data-free synthesis), and complementary techniques (projector layers, adversarial objectives, curriculum schedules). Empirical work shows that careful selection of what to transfer and how to align teacher and student—balanced with attention to optimization dynamics and data constraints—produces compact models that preserve much of the teacher’s performance while meeting real-world latency, privacy, and robustness requirements.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information beyond hard labels. Over the past decade this has grown from simple logit-matching into a toolkit that includes internal representation alignment, layer-mapping strategies, data and privacy-aware procedures, adversarial and robustness-aware objectives, online and distributed schemes, and methods tailored for specific architectures such as pre-trained language models. Distillation often recovers much of a teacher’s performance when deliberately designed (choice of signals, data, and architecture), but it faces limits from optimization difficulties, capacity mismatch, distributional shift, and the risk of transferring undesirable teacher behaviors such as bias. Practical success therefore depends on combining multiple transfer signals, handling data constraints, and adapting both teacher and student to the deployment context.

papers_seen.author: Mason
papers_seen.title: Learning Student Networks via Feature Embedding
papers_seen.abstract: Deep convolutional neural networks have been widely used in numerous applications, but their demanding storage and computational resource requirements prevent their applications on mobile devices. Knowledge distillation aims to optimize a portable student network by taking the knowledge from a well-trained heavy teacher network. Traditional teacher-student based methods used to rely on additional fully-connected layers to bridge intermediate layers of teacher and student networks, which brings in a large number of auxiliary parameters. In contrast, this paper aims to propagate information from teacher to student without introducing new variables which need to be optimized. We regard the teacher-student paradigm from a new perspective of feature embedding. By introducing the locality preserving loss, the student network is encouraged to generate the low-dimensional features which could inherit intrinsic properties of their corresponding high-dimensional features from teacher network. The resulting portable network thus can naturally maintain the performance as that of the teacher network. Theoretical analysis is provided to justify the lower computation complexity of the proposed method. Experiments on benchmark datasets and well-trained networks suggest that the proposed algorithm is superior to state-of-the-art teacher-student learning methods in terms of computational and storage complexity.

papers_seen.author: Allison
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a core strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable ones by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from teacher models to students. The field has diversified from logits-only matching to richer targets (intermediate features, attention maps, relational signals), multiple training regimes (data-free, online, federated, multi-teacher), and task-aware techniques that address capacity mismatch and deployment constraints. KD is widely applicable across modalities (vision, speech, multimodal, graphs, NLP) and is most effective when combined with data- and architecture-aware practices, but practical limits remain around representation alignment, rare-token behavior, privacy, and domain transfer.

papers_seen.author: Crosby
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible family of techniques for transferring information from large teacher models to smaller student models so that students approach teacher performance while using less compute, memory, and energy. Modern KD extends beyond soft-label matching to include intermediate-feature, layer-wise, and structural transfer, and is most effective when integrated with architecture-aware design, pre-training of compact models, and complementary compression methods. Implementation choices—what signals to transfer, how to align layers, which data to use, and how to mitigate bias or domain shift—determine practical success.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Path to Deployable Deep Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical framework for producing compact, faster models that retain much of the capability of larger teachers. Beyond simple logit matching, modern KD leverages internal representation transfer, selective data strategies, and integration with pruning, architecture search, or federated protocols to meet latency, privacy, and device-heterogeneity constraints. When applied thoughtfully, KD enables efficient deployment across modalities while posing clear methodological trade-offs and open challenges that guide future research.

papers_seen.author: Welch
papers_seen.title: Distillation as Default: A Practical Position on Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a necessary and practical core technique for compressing large deep models into deployable, efficient students. When combined with representation-level matching, careful pre-training of compact students, and attention to privacy and deployment constraints, KD preserves much of teacher performance while enabling low-latency, on-device, and federated use. However, naive soft-label matching is insufficient: best practice integrates intermediate-feature supervision, data- and architecture-aware pipelines, and multi-stage or multi-teacher strategies to handle domain shift, rare phenomena, and heterogeneous architectures.

papers_seen.author: Hahn
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression strategies are widely used to produce smaller, faster models by transferring knowledge from larger or ensemble teachers to compact students. These techniques span supervised distillation, self-distillation, data-free and adversarial approaches, layer- and task-aware mappings, and distributed/online schemes. Empirical work shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance across modalities (classification, detection, generation, and language tasks) while enabling practical deployment; theoretical and practical challenges remain around data dependence, teacher imperfection, robustness, and optimal student–teacher alignment.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Survey of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical and flexible approach to compress large models and transfer knowledge across models, modalities, and tasks. Practitioners use KD to produce smaller, faster student models that retain much of a teacher's performance, to regularize training via self-distillation, and to enable multi-task or resource-heterogeneous deployment. Despite strong empirical results across vision, speech, translation, and question answering, distillation exhibits failure modes—e.g., propagation of teacher errors or poor handling of low-frequency phenomena—that motivate variants such as multi-teacher schemes, feature-level objectives, projector layers, and teacher-student co-training. The literature combines empirical recipes and growing theoretical analysis to guide when and how to mix soft teacher signals and hard labels, design teacher architectures, and choose representation vs. logit distillation for best trade-offs between accuracy, efficiency, and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Yu
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable ones by transferring predictive behavior or internal structure. A range of techniques — from matching teacher soft outputs to aligning intermediate representations, synthesizing or augmenting data, and coordinating multi-teacher or online protocols — enable practical trade-offs between accuracy, latency, and resource constraints. Success depends on task-aware design choices, student capacity, data availability, and careful handling of robustness and social-impact concerns.

papers_seen.author: Turner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a toolbox rather than a single recipe, KD can preserve much of teacher performance while meeting constraints of latency, memory, privacy, and heterogeneous deployment. Realizing KD's full value requires combining soft-target transfer with representation-level objectives, curriculum or staged training, teacher optimization, and architecture-aware mapping, and it also demands attention to distribution shift, rare-token fidelity, and teacher biases.

papers_seen.author: Callahan
papers_seen.title: A Practical Position on Knowledge Distillation: Go Beyond Soft Labels
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a necessary tool for compressing large deep and NLP models into efficient students suitable for deployment. However, naive KD that only matches teacher soft-labels is often insufficient. Effective distillation combines richer knowledge targets (internal features, attention, and layerwise signals), data-aware augmentations, selective sample strategies, and privacy- or domain-aware procedures. The best practical pipelines treat KD as a toolbox: choose which knowledge to transfer based on student capacity and task needs, use augmentation or self-distillation to improve generalization when data are scarce, and apply selective or privacy-preserving queries where constraints require it.

papers_seen.author: Scott
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques transfer information from larger teacher models into smaller student models to reduce computation, memory, and latency while attempting to preserve predictive performance. The field encompasses a range of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational signals), training workflows (single- and multi-stage, multi-teacher, self-distillation, data-free), and practical integrations with pruning, quantization, and architecture adaptation. Empirical and conceptual work points to several mechanisms that make distillation effective (soft-target regularization, representation alignment, and inductive-bias transfer) and identifies recurring deployment concerns such as architecture mismatch, data availability, domain shift, and robustness. Best practices emphasize matching distillation signals to student capacity, using layer-aware objectives when internal alignment matters, and combining distillation with complementary compression methods for realistic constraints.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Preserving Privacy in Federated Learning with Ensemble Cross-Domain Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) is a machine learning paradigm where local nodes collaboratively train a central model while the training data remains decentralized. Existing FL methods typically share model parameters or employ co-distillation to address the issue of unbalanced data distribution. However, they suffer from communication bottlenecks. More importantly, they risk privacy leakage. In this work, we develop a privacy preserving and communication efficient method in a FL framework with one-shot offline knowledge distillation using unlabeled, cross-domain public data. We propose a quantized and noisy ensemble of local predictions from completely trained local models for stronger privacy guarantees without sacrificing accuracy. Based on extensive experiments on image classification and text classification tasks, we show that our privacy-preserving method outperforms baseline FL algorithms with superior performance in both accuracy and communication efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Stevens
papers_seen.title: Representation- and Deployment-Aware Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is most effective for real-world model compression when it goes beyond logits to transfer internal representations, adapts to data availability, and explicitly preserves robustness and deployment constraints. Combining feature- and layer-aware objectives, adaptive layer mapping, data-free synthesis when needed, and robustness-aware training yields compact students that better match teacher behavior across tasks and modalities while meeting latency, memory, and privacy requirements.

papers_seen.author: Calderon
papers_seen.title: Learning Generalizable Models for Vehicle Routing Problems via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Recent neural methods for vehicle routing problems always train and test the deep models on the same instance distribution (i.e., uniform). To tackle the consequent cross-distribution generalization concerns, we bring the knowledge distillation to this field and propose an Adaptive Multi-Distribution Knowledge Distillation (AMDKD) scheme for learning more generalizable deep models. Particularly, our AMDKD leverages various knowledge from multiple teachers trained on exemplar distributions to yield a light-weight yet generalist student model. Meanwhile, we equip AMDKD with an adaptive strategy that allows the student to concentrate on difficult distributions, so as to absorb hard-to-master knowledge more effectively. Extensive experimental results show that, compared with the baseline neural methods, our AMDKD is able to achieve competitive results on both unseen in-distribution and out-of-distribution instances, which are either randomly synthesized or adopted from benchmark datasets (i.e., TSPLIB and CVRPLIB). Notably, our AMDKD is generic, and consumes less computational resources for inference.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Versatile Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely applicable approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable ones while retaining much of their effectiveness. When combined with task-specific adaptations (layer mapping, data-free synthesis, federated protocols, quantization, or self-supervision), KD enables deployment in low-resource, privacy-sensitive, and domain-specific settings. Success depends on designing appropriate alignment mechanisms, data strategies, and fairness safeguards.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques reduce computation, memory and latency of large deep models by transferring information from high-capacity "teacher" models to smaller "student" models. A range of approaches have been developed: soft-target (logit) distillation, feature- and layer-wise matching, data-augmentation and data-free synthesis, multi-teacher and curriculum strategies, and teacher-aware or teacher-training modifications. These methods are applied across modalities (NLP, vision, multimodal) and settings (limited data, federated or resource-constrained deployments), and combine naturally with quantization and low-precision inference. Empirical and theoretical work shows gains arise both from conveying inter-class similarities (dark knowledge) and from the regularization effect of softened targets; more recent work focuses on selecting or synthesizing the most useful knowledge for a given student and task.

papers_seen.author: Young
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Trade-offs, and Practical Recipes
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. KD operates across levels—from soft output (logit) imitation to intermediate-feature and layer-wise alignment—and is often combined with architecture search, pruning, or data-synthesis to meet deployment constraints. Beyond pure compression, KD can act as a regularizer that improves generalization and robustness, but its effectiveness depends on student capacity, the choice of distillation signal, data availability or privacy constraints, and careful matching of teacher and student objectives.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Domains, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques aim to transfer knowledge from larger, costly models (teachers) into smaller, faster models (students) so that the students retain much of the teachers' accuracy while meeting deployment constraints. Across vision, language, graphs, and generative models, researchers have developed complementary approaches — from matching soft logits to aligning intermediate representations, attention maps, channels, and global embedding topologies — and combined distillation with architecture search, pruning, and continual adaptation. Empirical work shows distillation can produce compact models that preserve or even improve task performance, but success depends on careful alignment of teacher-student inputs/representations, task- and domain-specific strategies, and trade-offs such as bias–variance effects introduced by soft labels. Important challenges remain around layer mismatches, low-frequency token handling, domain shift, and fundamental limits of compressibility for certain model families.

papers_seen.author: Charles
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, broadly applicable approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers information from high-capacity teachers to compact students via outputs, intermediate representations, or relational signals, and integrates naturally with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and deployment workflows (on-device inference, federated learning, and data-limited regimes). While KD reliably improves efficiency while preserving much of teacher performance, robust application requires careful choices about what signals to transfer, how to handle imperfect teachers and low-frequency behaviors, and how to combine KD with data strategies and architecture design to meet real-world constraints.

papers_seen.author: Hensley
papers_seen.title: Apprentice: Using Knowledge Distillation Techniques To Improve Low-Precision Network Accuracy
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning networks have achieved state-of-the-art accuracies on computer vision workloads like image classification and object detection. The performant systems, however, typically involve big models with numerous parameters. Once trained, a challenging aspect for such top performing models is deployment on resource constrained inference systems - the models (often deep networks or wide networks or both) are compute and memory intensive. Low-precision numerics and model compression using knowledge distillation are popular techniques to lower both the compute requirements and memory footprint of these deployed models. In this paper, we study the combination of these two techniques and show that the performance of low-precision networks can be significantly improved by using knowledge distillation techniques. Our approach, Apprentice, achieves state-of-the-art accuracies using ternary precision and 4-bit precision for variants of ResNet architecture on ImageNet dataset. We present three schemes using which one can apply knowledge distillation techniques to various stages of the train-and-deploy pipeline.

papers_seen.author: House
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Principled, Practical, and Context-Sensitive Toolbox for NLP Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an essential approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable systems. When treated as a flexible framework rather than a single recipe, KD can preserve much of teacher performance while meeting constraints of latency, memory, privacy, and domain heterogeneity. However, its success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to adapt to new domains or architectures, and how to select or synthesize training signals for the student.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: DINE: Domain Adaptation from Single and Multiple Black-box Predictors
papers_seen.abstract: To ease the burden of labeling, unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) aims to transfer knowledge in previous and related labeled datasets (sources) to a new unlabeled dataset (target). Despite impressive progress, prior methods always need to access the raw source data and develop data-dependent alignment approaches to recognize the target samples in a transductive learning manner, which may raise privacy concerns from source individuals. Several recent studies resort to an alternative solution by exploiting the well-trained white-box model from the source domain, yet, it may still leak the raw data through generative adversarial learning. This paper studies a practical and interesting setting for UDA, where only black-box source models (i.e., only network predictions are available) are provided during adaptation in the target domain. To solve this problem, we propose a new two-step knowledge adaptation framework called DIstill and fine-tuNE (DINE). Taking into consideration the target data structure, DINE first distills the knowledge from the source predictor to a customized target model, then fine-tunes the distilled model to further fit the target domain. Besides, neural networks are not required to be identical across domains in DINE, even allowing effective adaptation on a low-resource device. Empirical results on three UDA scenarios (i.e., single-source, multi-source, and partial-set) confirm that DINE achieves highly competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art data-dependent approaches. Code is available at \url{https://github.com/tim-learn/DINE/}.

papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: Private Model Compression via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The soaring demand for intelligent mobile applications calls for deploying powerful deep neural networks (DNNs) on mobile devices. However, the outstanding performance of DNNs notoriously relies on increasingly complex models, which in turn is associated with an increase in computational expense far surpassing mobile devices' capacity. What is worse, app service providers need to collect and utilize a large volume of users' data, which contain sensitive information, to build the sophisticated DNN models. Directly deploying these models on public mobile devices presents prohibitive privacy risk. To benefit from the on-device deep learning without the capacity and privacy concerns, we design a private model compression framework RONA. Following the knowledge distillation paradigm, we jointly use hint learning, distillation learning, and self learning to train a compact and fast neural network. The knowledge distilled from the cumbersome model is adaptively bounded and carefully perturbed to enforce differential privacy. We further propose an elegant query sample selection method to reduce the number of queries and control the privacy loss. A series of empirical evaluations as well as the implementation on an Android mobile device show that RONA can not only compress cumbersome models efficiently but also provide a strong privacy guarantee. For example, on SVHN, when a meaningful $(9.83,10^{-6})$-differential privacy is guaranteed, the compact model trained by RONA can obtain 20$\times$ compression ratio and 19$\times$ speed-up with merely 0.97% accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Cook
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Benefits, Limits, and Engineering Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile foundation for compressing deep and language models: it enables much smaller, faster students to capture substantial teacher performance while supporting deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD excels when combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and careful engineering (choice of transferred signals, data augmentation, teacher selection). However, KD is not a plug-and-play solution: it can propagate teacher imperfections, struggle with rare-token or low-frequency behaviors, and face difficulties under heterogeneous or privacy-constrained data regimes. Treating KD as the central tool in a compression pipeline — but one that requires task-aware design and diagnostics — yields the best practical outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Walls
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile approach for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large or ensemble teacher models into smaller student models. Across vision, language, graphs, and multimodal problems, KD is used alone or combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data-centric strategies to produce compact models that preserve much of teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints. Empirical and analytical work highlights mechanisms behind KD’s success, practical recipes for improving student fidelity, and persistent challenges (data mismatch, rare-token behavior, robustness, and optimization). This synthesis summarizes methods, applications, practical recommendations, and key open problems reported in recent literature.

papers_seen.author: Ray
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses or transfers knowledge from larger or multiple models into smaller, faster models by leveraging softer training signals, intermediate representations, or alternate training protocols. Research has explored KD’s theoretical underpinnings, practical training strategies (including teacher-ensemble and teacher-free variants), privacy- and communication-aware settings, and extensions beyond classification to generation and structured prediction. Empirical work demonstrates KD’s ability to reduce deployment cost while retaining or sometimes even improving downstream performance, but trade-offs remain around data availability, representation matching, and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Zuniga
papers_seen.title: Large scale distributed neural network training through online distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Techniques such as ensembling and distillation promise model quality improvements when paired with almost any base model. However, due to increased test-time cost (for ensembles) and increased complexity of the training pipeline (for distillation), these techniques are challenging to use in industrial settings. In this paper we explore a variant of distillation which is relatively straightforward to use as it does not require a complicated multi-stage setup or many new hyperparameters. Our first claim is that online distillation enables us to use extra parallelism to fit very large datasets about twice as fast. Crucially, we can still speed up training even after we have already reached the point at which additional parallelism provides no benefit for synchronous or asynchronous stochastic gradient descent. Two neural networks trained on disjoint subsets of the data can share knowledge by encouraging each model to agree with the predictions the other model would have made. These predictions can come from a stale version of the other model so they can be safely computed using weights that only rarely get transmitted. Our second claim is that online distillation is a cost-effective way to make the exact predictions of a model dramatically more reproducible. We support our claims using experiments on the Criteo Display Ad Challenge dataset, ImageNet, and the largest to-date dataset used for neural language modeling, containing $6\times 10^{11}$ tokens and based on the Common Crawl repository of web data.

papers_seen.author: Hawkins
papers_seen.title: A Fast Knowledge Distillation Framework for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: While Knowledge Distillation (KD) has been recognized as a useful tool in many visual tasks, such as supervised classification and self-supervised representation learning, the main drawback of a vanilla KD framework is its mechanism, which consumes the majority of the computational overhead on forwarding through the giant teacher networks, making the entire learning procedure inefficient and costly. ReLabel, a recently proposed solution, suggests creating a label map for the entire image. During training, it receives the cropped region-level label by RoI aligning on a pre-generated entire label map, allowing for efficient supervision generation without having to pass through the teachers many times. However, as the KD teachers are from conventional multi-crop training, there are various mismatches between the global label-map and region-level label in this technique, resulting in performance deterioration. In this study, we present a Fast Knowledge Distillation (FKD) framework that replicates the distillation training phase and generates soft labels using the multi-crop KD approach, while training faster than ReLabel since no post-processes such as RoI align and softmax operations are used. When conducting multi-crop in the same image for data loading, our FKD is even more efficient than the traditional image classification framework. On ImageNet-1K, we obtain 79.8% with ResNet-50, outperforming ReLabel by ~1.0% while being faster. On the self-supervised learning task, we also show that FKD has an efficiency advantage. Our project page: http://zhiqiangshen.com/projects/FKD/index.html, source code and models are available at: https://github.com/szq0214/FKD.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical but Design-Sensitive Path to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly useful family of techniques for transferring behavior from large teacher models to smaller students to reduce inference cost and enable deployment. KD has been instantiated as matching soft targets, aligning intermediate representations, progressive module replacement, and selective or multi-teacher schemes. While KD often yields strong empirical gains and enables domain- and task-specific compression, its success depends on optimization dynamics, the choice of distilled signal, data quality and selection, and teacher–student alignment. Careful method choices make KD a reliable, production-ready compression strategy, but it is not a universal shortcut: practitioners must tailor KD objectives and protocols to their constraints and goals.
